jobs.title: Product Design Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Who We Are HP IQ is HP’s new AI innovation lab. Combining startup agility with HP’s global scale, we’re building intelligent technologies that redefine how the world works, creates, and collaborates. We’re assembling a diverse, world-class team—engineers, designers, researchers, and product minds—focused on creating an intelligent ecosystem across HP’s portfolio. Together, we’re developing intuitive, adaptive solutions that spark creativity, boost productivity, and make collaboration seamless. We create breakthrough solutions that make complex tasks feel effortless, teamwork more natural, and ideas more impactful—always with a human-centric mindset. By embedding AI advancements into every HP product and service, we’re expanding what’s possible for individuals, organisations, and the future of work. Join us as we reinvent work, so people everywhere can do their best work. About The Role HP IQ's Hardware Design team is responsible for materializing product vision into manufacturable hardware systems. Working closely with Industrial Design, System Software, Electrical Engineering, and Manufacturing partners, this role drives the design and integration of complete hardware products from early architecture and prototype phases through production ramp. The position offers the opportunity to own the mechanical and systems integration challenges that transform concepts into shipping products. What You Might Do Collaborate with Industrial Design to translate product vision into mechanical design, enclosure layout, and form factor feasibility Integrate multiple subsystems (microphone, speaker, antenna, battery, PCB, sensors, buttons) into a cohesive hardware architecture Produce CAD models, component placement studies, and tolerance analysis to guide manufacturing Work with contract manufacturers and vendors to validate design feasibility, manage drawing releases, and troubleshoot production issues Participate in hands-on prototype builds, design validation, and iterative refinement across development cycles Apply design of experiments methodology to validate material selection, assembly processes, and design assumptions Collaborate with Electrical Engineering on PCB layout, flexible PCB integration, and component placement constraints Define assembly processes, fixturing strategies, and datuming schemes to ensure manufacturability Own design documentation including 2D drawings, specifications, and design rationale for internal and vendor communication Essential Qualifications Solid understanding of material science fundamentals including stress-strain relationships, thermal properties, and material selection rationale Proficiency with CAD tools and component placement within constrained form factors Familiarity with tolerance analysis, tolerance stacks, and design for manufacturability principles Experience or demonstrated knowledge of manufacturing processes including injection molding, CNC machining, extrusion, and assembly processes Experience with PCB design, flexible PCB, or electrical component integration Ability to operate effectively in ambiguous, prototype-heavy environments; resourcefulness and self-direction essential Strong communication skills with ability to partner across Industrial Design, Engineering, and Manufacturing teams Comfort with hands-on prototyping, lab work, and iterative design refinement Demonstrated ability to work without extensive documentation or rigid structure; thrives in startup-like, fast-moving environments Preferred Skills Minimum 1-2 years of hardware product design or related experience; prior internship at a consumer electronics company is preferred Experience communicating with contract manufacturers or FATP (final assembly) partners Exposure to design of experiments (DOE) or design validation methodologies Portfolio demonstrating complete hardware projects from design through prototype or production Experience with assembly process design, datuming, and fixturing Familiarity with cross-functional product development from concept through production ramp Hourly Pay Range: $40.00–$50.00 per hour. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as skills, qualifications, and experience. 2027 Internship Program Dates: May/June–August/September 2027. Final dates will be based on student schedules. Compensation & Benefits (Full-Time Employees) The salary range for this role is listed above. Final salary offered is based upon multiple factors including individual job-related qualifications, education, experience, knowledge and skills. At HP IQ, we offer a competitive and comprehensive benefits package, including: Health insurance Dental insurance Vision insurance Long term/short term disability insurance Employee assistance program Flexible spending account Life insurance Generous time off policies, including; 4-12 weeks fully paid parental leave based on tenure 11 paid holidays Additional flexible paid vacation and sick leave ( US benefits overview ) Why HP IQ? HP IQ is HP’s new AI innovation lab, building the intelligence to empower humanity—reimagining how we work, create, and connect to shape the future of work. Innovative Work Help shape the future of intelligent computing and workplace transformation. Autonomy and Agility Work with the speed and focus of a startup, backed by HP’s scale. Meaningful Impact Build AI-powered solutions that help people and organisations thrive. Flexible Work Environment Freedom and flexibility to do your best work. Forward-Thinking Culture We learn fast, stay future-focused, and imagine what comes next—together. jobs.title: Electromechanical Design Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: ABOUT US Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world. The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone. This is a general application used to fill multiple internship openings across our Electrical Hardware teams. If selected, you will be matched to a specific team based on your background and interests during the interview process. - Electrical Design Engineering Intern - Electrical Engineering Design Intern - Electrical Functional Safety Engineering Intern - Embedded Software Engineering Intern - Mechanical Design Engineering Intern - Product Launch Engineering Intern - Reliability Engineering Intern - Software Engineering Intern, Vehicle Lab - Supplier Excellence Engineering Intern - Test Automation Systems Engineering Intern ROLE SUMMARY Every Electronic Control Unit goes through a full lifecycle of design, validation, manufacturing readiness, and release. As an Electromechanical Design Engineering intern, you will be involved in one part of that lifecycle, which may include circuit design, mechanical packaging, hardware validation and test, reliability and functional safety analysis, or supplier and manufacturing readiness work. Specific project areas vary by team and may include: - Designing and developing analog, digital, or mixed signal circuits, including schematic capture and component selection - Supporting mechanical packaging design or structural and thermal simulation for ECU enclosures - Building or running hardware validation tests and test automation systems - Contributing to hardware functional safety analyses such as FMEA or FMEDA - Supporting supplier quality, product launch, or manufacturing readiness activities for ECU programs RESPONSIBILITIES - Support proof of concept, design, or validation work for an assigned hardware project - Debug and troubleshoot hardware issues at the board or system level - Document component release information and maintain accurate design records - Collaborate with cross functional engineering and design teams to understand requirements - Communicate progress and findings to your team throughout the internship QUALIFICATIONS Minimum: - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at an accredited US university - Proficient in electrical engineering fundamentals Preferred: - Actively pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Hardware Engineering, or a closely related field, with intent to return to school after the internship - Understanding of electronics, packaging, and hardware design - Familiarity with communication protocols such as CAN, Ethernet, USB, I2C, or SPI - Coursework or project experience with PCB design tools, CAD tools, or simulation software - Familiarity with product lifecycle management and component release processes TOTAL REWARDS We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. In addition to a competitive base salary, full-time positions may be is eligible to participate in our annual company performance bonus program. Payments are discretionary and not guaranteed; actual amounts depend on company results and the terms of the plan in effect, and require active employment at the time of payout. This role is also eligible for equity in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), subject to board approval and the terms of our equity incentive plans, including applicable vesting requirements. In addition to our compensation programs, we invest in our people with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, wellbeing, and financial future for full-time employees — including health coverage, retirement savings, time off, and family planning programs. Offerings vary by country. Learn more about our global benefit programs https://rvtech.mybenefits.life/. If you are a current employee, please apply through our internal job board https://app.ashbyhq.com/internal/job-board/b10a9912-eb45-4a84-9a34-84b2a459923a. jobs.title: Summer 2027 - Mechanical Engineering Intern
jobs.body: Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. Our Summer Internship program is a wonderful opportunity for Fall and Spring graduates to immerse themselves in an innovative and mission driven culture. Our paid internship program will provide you with hands on mentorship, an opportunity to add real contribution to our company via your internship project, and a possible job offer at the end. You will have the chance to make lifelong friendships, expand your network, and learn all about what it's like to work in a high-growth, fast scaling tech unicorn. You'll take part in company sponsored events and enjoy exploring a new city. Read on below to learn more about this unique internship! Job Description: The mechanical engineering team is responsible for mechanical design and development projects for Shield AI's autonomous UAV products. We follow a rigorous design process, as we innovate, prototype, test, and release creative design solutions. We work with cross-functional teams to ensure the successful development and launch of new products. Intern Project Scope & Description: - - Own requirements gathering, design, and validation of multiple test stands used to test components and subsystems on X-BAT or V-BAT - Design tooling to hold devices-under-test (DUTs) during environmental testing. - Design test stands and test fixtures that interface with engines, electric motors, circuit boards, and various other aeronautical components. - Specify facilities requirements (electrical, plumbing, etc…) for environmental test chambers. - Contribute to and attend cross-functional design reviews. Advocate for design changes that result in simpler testing processes. - Other duties as assigned. Required qualifications: - - You are an undergraduate, graduate or PhD student pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering or related STEM field. - Strong understanding of fundamental engineering concepts, including EE, Mech E, Programming, Physics, and Mathematics. - Experience working on multidisciplinary hardware development projects, which can be from an internship, job, club, team, personal project, etc. - Great written and verbal communication. - Demonstrated history of showing ownership of project outcomes and delivering exceptional results. - Record of working hard, being a trustworthy teammate, holding yourself and others to high standards, and being kind to others. Preferred qualifications: - - Experience with CAD tools such as SolidWorks, NX, CATIA, etc… (NX preferred). - Ability to rapidly manufacture your designs in a machine shop. - Experience working with internal combustion engines. This could be in design, tuning, and/or assembly. - Familiarity with designing mechanical tooling or test fixtures. - Demonstrated adaptability, agility, and the ability to innovate under pressure to meet dynamic project demands and drive successful #intern Shield AI is proud to offer competitive pay and a housing stipend for qualified hires. While our People Experience team provides resources and assistance, interns are responsible to find their own housing and travel to and from their office location. ### Shield AI is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

jobs.title: Test Engineering Intern
jobs.body: ABOUT US: Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures. WHO WE ARE: We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy. WHO YOU ARE: Astro Mechanica is seeking an intern to join our Test Team for the summer of 2027 (program begins on June 7, 2027 for semester schools and June 27, 2027 for quarter schools). The ideal candidate is excited to help design, fabricate, operate, and improve the test infrastructure supporting our jet engine and subsystems. As an intern, you’ll be embedded with the test team in Antioch or Alameda, working on real test stands and hardware alongside full-time engineers. Your work will help keep test operations running smoothly while expanding and improving our test capabilities. In this role, your mission will be to help create and operate test infrastructure for hardware research and development, with mentorship from senior engineers along the way. You’ll see firsthand how new designs are rigorously tested to meet quality and performance targets before they’re integrated into the aircraft. You embody the test-like-you-fly philosophy. WHAT YOU’LL DO: - Help design test stands, fixtures, and supporting hardware to enable new test capabilities - Support development of test plans, instrumentation schemes, and data collection methods that capture high-quality, decision-driving data - Create and update documentation, including P&IDs, electrical schematics, and test procedures, while working with stakeholders to make sure stand requirements are met - Assist with fabrication, assembly, and activation of test stands and fixtures - Support test operations, including setup, instrumentation, execution, and teardown - Analyze test data and compare results with analytical models or simulations - Help troubleshoot test facility problems and find ways to improve test throughput and reliability - Own a scoped project through the summer and present your results to the team at the end of the internship WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR: - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline - Club, project, research, or internship hands-on experience with fluidic, mechanical, or electrical systems - Exposure to instrumentation and test hardware (pressure transducers, thermocouples, load cells, relays, solenoids, pneumatics) - Familiarity with CAD and the ability to design simple test hardware, fixtures, or modifications - Experience with Python, MATLAB, or similar tools for data analysis - Exposure to data acquisition systems (e.g., LabVIEW, NI hardware) is a plus - Hands-on fabrication skills (machining, wiring, soldering, plumbing) are a plus - Respect for safety when working around pressurized systems, flammables, and high voltage - Attentive to detail and committed to a high level of quality in all work - Flexibility to work in a fast-paced environment - Available for a full-time, in-person internship in San Francisco during Summer 2027 (approximately 10–12 weeks) PERKS & BENEFITS: - Competitive hourly pay - Hands-on mentorship from experienced engineers - Company-funded perks, including team lunches, game nights, and other activities ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: At Astro Mechanica, we highly value in-office work to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. We consider working in the office five days a week an essential part of the employee's role. Astro Mechanica is an equal opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Pay range: $40 – $55 per hour.

jobs.title: Intern, Haptic Metrology & Stylus Tablet Development - Summer 2027
jobs.body: > Requisition Number: 79110 The company built on breakthroughs. ​ Join us.​ Corning is one of the world’s leading innovators in glass, ceramic, and materials science. From the depths of the ocean to the farthest reaches of space, our technologies push the boundaries of what’s possible. ​ How do we do this? With our people. They break through limitations and expectations – not once in a career, but every day. They help move our company, and the world, forward. ​ ​ At Corning, there are endless possibilities for making an impact. You can help connect the unconnected, drive the future of automobiles, transform at-home entertainment, and ensure the delivery of lifesaving medicines. And so much more.​ ​ Come break through with us. Role Purpose We are seeking a motivated Summer Intern to support the development of haptic metrology methods and tools for stylus-enabled tablet applications. This rotational internship provides hands-on exposure to the interdisciplinary work involved in evaluating, measuring, and improving stylus haptic experiences. The intern will collaborate with engineering, product, research, and quality teams to help characterize haptic performance, develop repeatable measurement approaches, analyze test data, and translate findings into recommendations for product development. This role is well suited to a student interested in hardware, sensing, human-computer interaction, mechanical or electrical engineering, embedded systems, or experimental measurement. Program Perks: Competitive salaries Assistance with housing and travel Meaningful project and final project presentation Intern Activities: Social and networking opportunities Weekly tech talks Community involvement Key Responsibilities Support development and validation of metrology methods for measuring haptic performance in stylus and tablet systems. Assist with test setup design, fixture development, calibration, and documentation of measurement procedures. Conduct repeatable experiments to evaluate variables such as vibration, force, latency, frequency response, contact behavior, pressure sensitivity, and user-perceived haptic quality. Collect, clean, analyze, and visualize experimental data; identify trends, variation, and potential sources of error. Help define performance metrics, test protocols, acceptance criteria, and reporting formats for haptic features. Collaborate with hardware, firmware, software, mechanical, UX research, and quality teams to understand product requirements and test results. Investigate measurement equipment, sensors, data-acquisition tools, and industry practices relevant to haptic characterization. Support root-cause investigations for performance issues and help propose improvements to test methods, designs, or processes. Maintain organized lab records, test reports, experiment logs, and technical presentations. Participate in professional-development programming and present a final project summary to technical stakeholders. Experiences/Education - Required Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Robotics, Human-Computer Interaction, Materials Science, or a related technical discipline. Interest in haptics, sensing, precision measurement, stylus input, consumer electronics, or human-device interaction. Familiarity with experimental methods, data collection, and basic statistical analysis. Experience with one or more of the following is preferred: Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, Excel, data visualization, signal processing, microcontrollers, sensors, or data-acquisition systems. Ability to interpret technical drawings, test plans, specifications, and engineering documentation is a plus. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and a commitment to measurement repeatability. Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively on a cross-functional team. Ability to work safely and responsibly in a laboratory or prototyping environment. Experiences/Education - Desired Coursework or projects involving vibrations, controls, mechatronics, instrumentation, signal processing, embedded systems, or human factors. Familiarity with accelerometers, force sensors, strain gauges, oscilloscopes, motion measurement, or other test instrumentation. Experience building prototypes, test fixtures, scripts, or automated data-analysis workflows. Experience conducting user studies or evaluating subjective product experiences is beneficial. This position does not support immigration sponsorship. ​The range for this position is $1,635.00 - $3,185.00 biweekly. Starting pay for the successful applicant is prescribed based on geographic location, nature of position, and year in school. A job that shapes a life. We prohibit discrimination on the basis of race, color, gender, age, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, veteran status or any other legally protected status. Corning is committed to providing equal employment opportunities and considers requests for reasonable accommodations in accordance with applicable laws. Individuals with disabilities or sincerely held religious beliefs may request reasonable accommodations to participate in the application or interview process, perform essential job functions, or access other benefits and privileges of employment. jobs.title: Manufacturing Test Engineer Co-Op
jobs.body: Boston Dynamics is a world leader in mobile robots, tackling some of the toughest robotics challenges. For years, our awe-inspiring viral videos on YouTube have shown the world what remarkably capable robots can do. We embody cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence in advanced robotics, quickly moving from the research lab into increasingly impactful roles across industrial spaces. The Manufacturing Test Engineering team seeks a Test Engineering Co-Op to design, document and deploy test equipment to build some of the most capable and amazing robots.This role provides hands-on design and technical support to a peer group of Manufacturing Test Engineers. You will work alongside the Technical Operations team to deploy test equipment, software, and procedures for both in-line and end-of-line production testing. You will be paired with a senior mentor to guide your project work and ensure a strong learning experience throughout your term. Logistics: Duration: 6 months Schedule: 40 hours per week How you will make an impact: Working within a team of engineers to design, construct, document, and run test sets on electromechanical parts and assemblies. Conduct troubleshooting and failure analysis efforts on the production floor to improve engineering and assemblies design as well as supplier quality. Collect, analyze, and present test performance data to both operations and engineering stakeholders for continuous improvement. Support station duplication, maintenance, and deployments for repair and service teams. Required Skills & Experience: Familiarity with test software development using programming languages such as Python in both Windows or Linux environments. In progress Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering or a related field. Preferred Skills & Experience: Solid mechatronics fundamentals with hands-on experience designing, building, and testing PCBAs or subsystem test stands used for hardware and software validation. Experience in the test and debugging of complex electromechanical systems. General experience in firmware, automation, and controls, utilizing software tools including Python, C++, Raspberry Pi, and Arduino. Data analysis and visualization. Experience working with manufacturing team members to create test plans and procedures for complex electromechanical assemblies on final assembly lines. Experience working with software and control teams in robotics manufacturing test development. Experience with lean manufacturing and/or six sigma. Familiarity with using a PLM (e.g. Arena). The pay range for this position is between $32 to $37 per hour. This range represents a good faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Internship: Mechanical Engineering
jobs.body: SUMMER 2027 INTERNSHIP/CO-OP: MECHANICAL ENGINEERING Kirkland, WA · Full-time · Onsite ABOUT SKYBAND GPS jamming and spoofing affect thousands of flights every day (GPSThreatMap.com http://GPSThreatMap.com). Skyband Systems has built the M100, a certified avionics system to overcome this threat to safety and operational reliability. The M100 fuses satellite signals from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) with inertial sensing to give pilots a trusted position source that doesn't depend on GPS. We're a VC-backed, fast-paced team based in Kirkland, WA, made up of engineers who built and scaled Starlink Aviation at SpaceX. We design, build, test, and fly our own hardware in our own aircraft. Everyone on the team has significant ownership over product areas or problem spaces. THE ROLE You'll join our mechanical team and assist in design and operational engineering scope for the M100 and subsequent products. You will work to improve M100 performance, reliability, and cost throughout its life cycle - from concept to physical aircraft installation, flight test, and fleet operation. You will also help conceptualize and design the next generation of Skyband products. Your products will integrate into a wide variety of airframes, enabling wireless connections to satellites, data bus connections to aircraft, and IP networking to store and analyze data. You will design the future of pilot-focused navigation equipment, and stand up the production line to build it. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Help design the future of aviation PNT with new Skyband products - Build, test, and refine production M100 avionics assemblies - Design and build test fixtures and automated test setups for development and production - Support environmental and EMI/EMC qualification testing to DO-160: planning, execution, and data review - Build and expand production equipment and tooling - Support aircraft integration and flight test, including installation and mounting, harnessing, instrumentation, and airframe modifications BASIC QUALIFICATIONS - Bachelor's degree or equivalent in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, manufacturing engineering, or a related field - 3+ months of hands-on engineering experience from internships, research labs, or student project teams - Comfortable with basic shop processes: torque and measurement tools, manual machining, adhesives, surface cleaning and finishing - Authorized to work in the United States PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE - You've designed, built, and tested something yourself (such as project teams, research, or personal projects) - CAD experience (Solidworks, Fusion, or similar) - CAM experience is a plus (MasterCAM, HSMWorks, Fusion CAM, etc) - Python or similar scripting experience for automation and analysis - Finite Element Analysis experience and understanding of core principles - Familiarity with structural and mechanical strength margins, mechanism designs - Exposure to environmental, material, or destructive testing - Interest in aviation, navigation, or GNSS; a pilot's license or flight test experience is a plus - Clear written communication and the discipline to document what you did and what you found ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS - Full-time, onsite in Kirkland, WA for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning June-July 2027 - Able to lift up to 25 lbs. and work in lab and hangar environments - Occasional travel for aircraft integration and flight test will be required COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS - $50.00/hour - $2500 relocation bonus - Paid holidays based on company holiday schedule - Direct mentorship from engineers who have shipped flight hardware at scale EEO STATEMENT Skyband Systems is an Equal Opportunity Employer employment with Skyband is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.body: Who We Are Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology. What We Offer Location: Santa Clara,CA You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more. At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits . Position Overview We are seeking a highly motivated Mechanical Engineering Intern to join our Hardware Engineering team. This role provides an opportunity to work alongside experienced engineers on the development, analysis, testing, and improvement of semiconductor equipment and subsystems. The intern will gain hands-on experience in mechanical design, product development, experimental validation, and failure analysis while contributing to real-world engineering projects that impact customer performance and product reliability. Key Responsibilities Work as a Mechanical Design Engineer of Critical Chamber Hardware of Capital Equipment Product Lines, with following additional responsibilities: ​ Support mechanical design and development activities for semiconductor manufacturing equipment and related hardware. Assist in creating and modifying 3D CAD models, drawings, and engineering documentation. Design and execute engineering experiments, collect and analyze data, and present findings to project teams. Participate in prototype development, testing, and validation activities. Conduct root cause investigations and support failure analysis efforts. Collaborate with cross-functional teams including manufacturing, quality, sourcing, and suppliers. Contribute to design reviews and recommend improvements for performance, reliability, manufacturability, and cost. Prepare technical reports and presentations to communicate project results and recommendations. Preferred Technical Skills Fundamentals of mechanics, materials, heat transfer, fluid mechanics, and machine design. Experience with CAD software such as Siemens NX, SolidWorks, Creo, or similar platforms. Basic knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T). Familiarity with Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and engineering simulation tools. Knowledge of Design of Experiments (DOE), statistical analysis, or data analytics is a plus. Strong problem-solving, analytical, and communication skills. Ability to work effectively in a team environment and manage multiple priorities. Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline. Good academic standing with a preferred GPA of 3.0 or higher preferred Available for a full-time internship during the summer or designated internship period. Strong interest in product design, mechanical systems, and semiconductor manufacturing technologies. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Please apply by December 31, 2026. Note: This position may close early based on application volume or candidate selection. Additional Information Time Type: Full time Employee Type: Intern / Student Travel: No Relocation Eligible: Yes The salary offered to a selected candidate will be based on multiple factors including location, hire grade, job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and with consideration of internal equity of our current team members. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer Intern
jobs.body: To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology. Group/Division The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The e-Beam division plays a critical role in KLA’s inspection ecosystem, with tools that deliver high-resolution, timely insights into defects and critical locations on the wafer. Used alongside KLA’s patterned and bare wafer inspectors, e-Beam systems help our customers quickly identify and understand yield-impacting issues—enabling faster, more effective actions to correct the manufacturing process. What You'll Do In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise. Mechanical engineering is fundamental to the semiconductor industry. Every wafer inspection and metrology system depends on precise and reliable mechanical design. As a Mechanical Engineering Intern at KLA, you'll learn how advanced semiconductor tools work from the inside out. You'll also own a real design project that ships to the team. What you'll do Design, model and document a functional subsystem for an e-beam tool, or tooling and fixtures that support tool build, alignment, test or service. Create 3D CAD models and production-ready 2D drawings using GD&T. Run engineering analysis (tolerance stack-ups, structural, thermal or vibration) to validate your design. Work with suppliers and the machine shop on prototypes, then assemble, test and iterate. Present your design and results to the engineering team at the end of the internship. What we're looking for Pursuing a BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field. Strong foundation in mechanical design, materials and manufacturing processes. Experience with 3D CAD (e.g., SolidWorks, Creo or NX). Hands-on build experience, such as a lab, a design team or personal projects. Clear communication and a curiosity to learn how complex systems work. Minimum Qualifications Requires less than 1 year of related experience About KLA We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us. Total Rewards Base Pay Range: $0.00 - $0.00 Primary Location: USA-CA-Milpitas-KLA KLA’s total rewards package for employees may also include participation in performance incentive programs and eligibility for additional benefits including but not limited to: medical, dental, vision, life, and other voluntary benefits, 401(K) including company matching, employee stock purchase program (ESPP), student debt assistance, tuition reimbursement program, development and career growth opportunities and programs, financial planning benefits, wellness benefits including an employee assistance program (EAP), paid time off and paid company holidays, and family care and bonding leave. Interns are eligible for some of the benefits listed. Our pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. The range displayed reflects the pay for this position in the primary location identified in this posting. Actual pay depends on several factors, including state minimum pay wage rates, location, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education level or training. We are committed to complying with all applicable federal and state minimum wage requirements where applicable. If applicable, your recruiter can share more about the specific pay range for your preferred location during the hiring process. To ensure a fair and consistent evaluation, the use of AI, recording tools or other technologies to generate, suggest or provide responses during interviews—whether virtual or in person—is not permitted unless explicitly approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation or invited by the interviewer. Use of these tools may interfere with our ability to evaluate your individual qualifications and affect your candidacy. KLA is committed to advancing innovation through responsible AI, and we value candidates who share this mindset. Equal Opportunity Statement KLA is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.title: Summer 2027 Intern - Hardware Engineering
jobs.body: WD is building the infrastructure behind the AI-driven data economy. As AI scales, so does data. Every interaction, every model, every system generates data that must be stored, managed, and made accessible over time. That’s where we come in. We combine deep engineering expertise with global-scale manufacturing to deliver the storage systems that make AI possible, powering hyperscale data centers, cloud platforms, and enterprise infrastructure worldwide. This isn’t theoretical work. It’s real systems, at real scale, people solving some of the hardest challenges in technology today. We’re looking for people who want to build, solve, and operate at that level. Join us and let’s shape the future of data. This posting supports current and anticipated early-career hiring needs. Applying allows our recruiting team to consider you for opportunities that align with your qualifications, preferences, and availability. An immediate opening or interview is not guaranteed. Where are these roles located? You’ll have the opportunity to work with teams in: Colorado Springs, Colorado Irvine, California Longmont, Colorado Fremont, California Rochester, Minnesota San Jose, California ASIC Engineering Design the silicon powering the future of data storage. As an ASIC Engineer, you’ll help create the custom chips that power next-generation hard disk drives (HDDs). Working alongside experienced engineers, you’ll contribute to digital design, verification, simulation, and optimization to deliver high-performance, energy-efficient products at global scale. What you’ll do Design and verify ASIC architectures and digital logic Build simulations and validate complex hardware designs Support the ASIC development lifecycle—from architecture through synthesis, place-and-route, and timing closure Optimize performance, power, and reliability Collaborate across hardware, firmware, and systems engineering teams Technologies you’ll use ASIC Design • RTL • Verilog/SystemVerilog • Digital Logic • Verification • Simulation • Timing Analysis • Low-Power Design Why you’ll love this role Help build technology that stores the world’s data. Learn from experienced semiconductor engineers. Work on cutting-edge silicon development. Solve challenging engineering problems with cross-functional teams. Build highly transferable chip design skills. Hardware Development Engineering Build the hardware behind the world’s data. As a Hardware Development Engineer, you’ll help develop the technologies that make modern data storage faster, more reliable, and higher capacity. You’ll design, prototype, validate, and improve hardware while solving real engineering challenges alongside multidisciplinary teams. What you’ll do Design and develop electronic hardware and magnetic recording systems Create validation strategies and automated test solutions Perform reliability, stress, and performance testing Analyze circuit boards, processors, sensors, and other hardware components Improve products from prototype through manufacturing Technologies you’ll use Electronics • PCB Design • Signal Integrity • Hardware Validation • Reliability Engineering • Test Engineering • Data Analysis Why you’ll love this role Design products used around the world. Work with advanced recording technologies. Gain hands-on laboratory experience. Collaborate with experts across multiple engineering disciplines. See your designs move from concept to production. Firmware Engineering Bring hardware to life through software. As a Firmware Engineer, you’ll develop the embedded software that controls advanced storage devices. You’ll work at the intersection of hardware and software, building reliable, high-performance firmware that enables world-class products. What you’ll do Design, develop, and debug embedded firmware Write software in C, C++, Assembly, and other low-level languages Integrate firmware with analog and digital hardware Troubleshoot hardware-software interactions Improve system performance, functionality, and reliability Technologies you’ll use Embedded Systems • C • C++ • Assembly • RTOS • Hardware Interfaces • Firmware Validation • Debugging Why you’ll love this role Build software that directly controls hardware. Solve complex engineering challenges. Work closely with both hardware and software engineers. Learn how products operate at the lowest level. Develop highly sought-after embedded systems skills. Systems Design & Integration Engineering Connect hardware and software into complete products. As a Systems Design & Integration Engineer, you’ll bring together hardware, firmware, and software to create reliable, high-performing storage systems. You’ll solve integration challenges and ensure every subsystem works seamlessly together. What you’ll do Define system requirements and technical specifications Integrate hardware, firmware, and software components Coordinate subsystem development across engineering teams Troubleshoot complex system-level issues Improve product performance, compatibility, and reliability Technologies you’ll use Systems Engineering • Integration • Validation • Root Cause Analysis • Product Development • Cross-Functional Engineering Why you’ll love this role Work across multiple engineering disciplines. Understand how complete products come together. Solve challenging integration problems. Gain broad technical exposure. Build systems-level engineering expertise. Mechanical Design Engineering Engineer the mechanics behind breakthrough technology. As a Mechanical Design Engineer, you’ll design the precision mechanical systems that support advanced storage products. From concept through manufacturing, you’ll help create innovative, reliable, and manufacturable solutions. What you’ll do Design mechanical components, assemblies, and packaging Develop prototypes and evaluate new concepts Perform engineering analysis and design validation Conduct testing to improve performance and reliability Partner with manufacturing teams to prepare products for production Technologies you’ll use CAD • Mechanical Design • Product Development • Prototype Testing • Design Validation • Manufacturing Engineering Why you’ll love this role Turn ideas into real products. Design precision mechanical systems. Build and test prototypes. Collaborate across engineering teams. See your designs manufactured at scale. Equipment Engineering Build smarter manufacturing. As an Equipment Engineer, you’ll optimize the advanced manufacturing equipment used to build world-class storage technology. You’ll improve equipment performance, increase reliability, and help solve complex production challenges. What you’ll do Install, upgrade, and optimize manufacturing equipment Improve equipment uptime, reliability, and process performance Investigate equipment failures and implement corrective actions Develop preventive maintenance strategies Partner with manufacturing and process engineers to drive continuous improvement Technologies you’ll use Automation • Manufacturing Engineering • Preventive Maintenance • Root Cause Analysis • Reliability Engineering • Continuous Improvement Why you’ll love this role Work with advanced manufacturing technology. Solve real-world production challenges. Improve efficiency through engineering. Learn automation and industrial systems. Help build products used around the world. System-on-Chip (SoC) Engineering Design the brains behind next-generation storage technology. As a System-on-Chip (SoC) Engineer, you’ll help develop the intelligent controllers that power advanced storage products. Working at the intersection of hardware, firmware, and silicon, you’ll design, integrate, verify, and validate complex SoC solutions that deliver high performance, reliability, and efficiency. What you’ll do Design, integrate, and validate SoC components and subsystems Develop and verify digital logic, interfaces, and IP blocks Support simulation, debugging, and hardware bring-up Analyze system performance, power, timing, and reliability Collaborate with ASIC, firmware, hardware, and systems engineering teams Technologies you’ll use SoC Architecture • RTL • Verilog/SystemVerilog • FPGA • Digital Design • Verification • Embedded Systems • Hardware Validation • Performance Optimization Why you’ll love this role Build the controllers that power modern storage technology. Work across silicon, firmware, hardware, and systems engineering. Experience the complete chip development lifecycle. Solve complex semiconductor design challenges. Develop highly marketable SoC engineering skills. This role is part of WD's early career development program. WD's early career development program is ideal for individuals at the early stages of their professional career. Participants receive foundational training through structured onboarding, mentorship, and a curated development curriculum. The responsibilities of this role are typically aligned with candidates who have approximately 0–2+ years of relevant professional experience, though candidates of all experience levels are encouraged to apply. Required: Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Software Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechatronics, Materials Engineering, Data Science, or a related engineering or technical discipline. Experience developing technical skills through coursework, internships, co-ops, research, laboratory work, capstone projects, hackathons, or personal projects in one or more areas such as software development, embedded systems, firmware, ASIC/SoC design, hardware development, systems engineering, mechanical design, manufacturing, automation, data analysis, testing, validation, or related engineering disciplines. Demonstrated analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively in a cross-functional engineering environment. Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills with a passion for learning new technologies. Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment. jobs.title: Internship - Mechanical Design Engineer
jobs.body: Internship – Mechanical Design Engineer Introduction to the job ASML US, including its affiliates and subsidiaries, bring together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, Netherlands and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon. Roles and Responsibilities As a Summer Intern in Mechanical Design Engineering, you will participate in developing hardware solutions for the lithography system and/or associated tooling. You will work on the Level Sensor Lens sub-system involving precision mechanics and/or opto-mechanics. Precision machine design at ASML starts with understanding the functional requirements and deriving specifications. You will collaborate with design engineers and sub-system architects in a multidiscipline project team to develop concepts, perform engineering analysis, build and test prototypes, generate detailed CAD designs, create engineering drawings, partner with suppliers, and support system integration and testing. This position is located on-site in Wilton, CT. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation. Must be available for 12 weeks for one of these sessions starting with the following dates: 6/2/2027 or 6/14/2027 Education and Experience Seeking an individual with a strong background in mechanical design and engineering. A background in mechanical design of mechatronics, precision design, or complex optical systems is desirable, as well as good complex mechanical system intuition. · Must be pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Optical Engineering, Optics, or related Engineering discipline and completed 2 years. Mechanical design exposure to kinematics, dynamics, material properties and behavior, and structural analysis. Experience with 3D solid modelling for design conceptualization and realization. Familiar with thermal and structural engineering fundamentals Basic experience with mechanical analytical techniques, including “first principle” engineering equations and Finite Element Analysis such as stress, strain, deformation, modal response, etc. Demonstrated ability to derive conclusions from analysis and make practical recommendations. Strong technical writing, communication and presentations skills. Skills Working at the cutting edge of tech, you will always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You will not work in a silo. Instead, you will be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you will collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer, Atlas Hardware Co-Op
jobs.body: We’re looking for an ambitious, self-starting, hands-on mechanical engineering co-op to join the team building Atlas, our humanoid robot. Our co-ops design, build, and test prototypes; they investigate weird problems; and they run experiments of all kinds. Boston Dynamics is a world leader in mobile robots, tackling some of the toughest robotics challenges. For years, our awe-inspiring viral videos on YouTube have shown the world what remarkably capable robots can do. Now we are quickly becoming a recognized leader in automation solutions for industrial applications , warehouse logistics and general purpose labor . What our co-ops do Work with mechanical, electrical, and software engineers to help design and support complex robotic systems Plan and perform verification and validation testing on prototype and production systems Design and develop new features for existing products Troubleshoot issues, perform root cause failure analysis and design/implement corrective actions to sustain existing products Design and release parts and assemblies using Catia CAD software Develop and maintain product support documentation including bills of material (BOMs) and detailed part/assembly drawings Support system design analyses, including reliability, DFM / DFA, cost-reduction What we want to see in our co-ops: A demonstrated passion for robotics and mechanical design Design experience w/ 3D CAD tools (CATIA, Solidworks, Onshape, &c.) That you’re hands-on. Our best co-ops can and want to build, assemble, and troubleshoot stuff That you can write well. A poorly written test plan, report, or spec robs the team of the knowledge we need to make our robots even better. That you’re working toward a BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, or similar Nice to Have: You know Python, LabView, MATLAB, or similar You know some FEA/CFD tools You have designed stuff for manufacturing (eg injection molding, castings, extrusions, sheet metal, weldments, &c.) You’re acquainted with ASME drafting standards including GD&T, (Y14.5-2018) You’ve worked systems comprising sensors, actuators and mechanisms Additional Info: Public transportation is accessible from Boston/Alewife.
