jobs.title: Systems Test Engineer - Co-Op
jobs.body: Boston Dynamics is a world leader in mobile robots, tackling some of the toughest robotics challenges. For years, our awe-inspiring viral videos on YouTube have shown the world what remarkably capable robots can do. We embody cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence in advanced robotics, quickly moving from the research lab into increasingly impactful roles across industrial spaces. The Systems Engineering, Integration, and Test (SEIT) Department of Boston Dynamics (BD) seeks a Systems Test Engineer Co-op to help verify and validate the most capable humanoid robot system in the world. This role provides hands-on technical support to a peer group of test engineers and technicians. The team will include mechanical, electrical, and software expertise. The Systems Test Engineer Co-op reports to the Verification, Validation, & Test Associate Director on the Atlas team and helps BD continue the development of the most capable full-body-manipulating mobile robots in the world. How you will make an impact: Work across electrical, mechanical, firmware, and technician teams to validate and integrate robot systems into test stands for reliability, verification, and software testing. Oversee and execute the integration of testing fixtures, including instrumentation, wiring, and configurations. Test and validate assemblies and firmware for critical components of our robot, such as actuators, grippers, power distribution boards, battery management systems, sensing boards, motor controllers, or compute boards. Contribute to the definition of our test system design and test process. Support system integration and test activities by contributing to test execution and debugging. Work alongside test engineers to develop and execute accelerated life reliability test specifications for actuators, batteries, structures, bushings, wirings, sensors, and the full system. Support failure analysis efforts for failures resulting from reliability testing. Required Skills & Experience: In progress Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related field. Desirable Skills & Experience: Solid mechatronics fundamentals with hands-on experience designing, building, and testing PCBAs or subsystem test stands used for hardware and software validation. Experience using 3D Modeling SW or Altium (or similar EDA tools). Experience in the test and debugging of complex electromechanical systems. General experience in firmware, automation, and controls. Data analysis and visualization. Software tools including: Python, C++, Jama, Jira, Google Suite, Matlab, Arena, Altium, Solidworks, Catia v6, Raspberry Pi, Arduino.

jobs.title: General Internship Application 2027
jobs.location: Santa Clara, CA or Any Office Location
jobs.body: We are excited to announce an open call for talented interns to join Oklo's dynamic team! Below are multiple positions across various disciplines that may be available, offering the chance to work on innovative projects for Summer 2027. If you're passionate about solving complex challenges, thrive in a collaborative environment, and are eager to contribute to groundbreaking solutions, we encourage you to apply. Requirements Oklo interns are required to: Relocate or be available to work out of Santa Clara CA where Oklo Headquarters is located for the duration of the internship or out of one of our satellite locations in Denver, CO, Brooklyn, NY, Idaho Falls, ID, or Washington D.C. Be available to work 30-40 hours per week between June 7, 2027 - August 20, 2027 (depending on the scope of work) Be currently enrolled or recently (2027) graduated with a Bachelor's or Master's Degree from an accredited university Intern Position Descriptions Thermal Hydraulics Intern The TH Intern will develop intermediate fidelity (IF) subchannel and high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models for applications in sodium fast reactors (SFRs). The project will involve comparisons between simulation results and experimental data. The exact topic will depend on interest and company needs but could cover fluid-structure interaction, turbulence model development, uncertainty quantification, or surrogate modeling. Required Qualifications Coursework in fluid mechanics and heat transfer General reactor physics and systems analysis Statistical methods and uncertainty quantification Experience with 3-D CFD and meshing workflows Proficiency in Python Bonus Qualifications Experience with advanced 3-D CFD concepts (large eddy simulation, fluid-structure interaction) Familiarity with high-performance computing workflows and tools Experience with MOOSE framework (SAS, RELAP, MOOSE subchannel) Experience with legacy codes in FORTRAN or similar Familiarity with statistics and reduced order modeling Materials Intern Working with members of Oklo’s Materials Team, will help with the selection and qualification of materials for use in nuclear reactor systems. Typical work duties include computational model development and implementation, engineering analysis, documentation, and interfacing with our fuel fabrication and engineering teams. Key Responsibilities Analyzing material performance across expected operating conditions Developing new analysis methods to predict material behavior in service Performing engineering analyses, including assessments of thermal performance, mechanical performance, safety performance, manufacturability, and cost. Collaborating cross-functionally to provide technical feedback to quick-iterating computational teams. Authoring technical reports using modern documentation tools and techniques Required Qualifications Experience working with and developing material behavior models Experience with material characterization (material testing, metallography) Background in nuclear, chemical, materials engineering, or equivalent Motivated learner who is adept at efficiently summarizing literature Bonus Qualifications Experience with engineering simulation software, such as ANSYS or COMSOL Coding or data analysis experience (e.g., Python or similar tools) Mechanical Analyst Intern This intern will contribute to the evaluation and optimization of mechanical components that are critical to Oklo’s advanced power plant designs. This position offers hands-on experience in applying engineering fundamentals, performing structural analysis, and integrating results into design iterations. Key Responsibilities Apply first-principles mechanics and strength of materials to support analysis of structural components Assist in summarizing mechanical analysis results for design teams, highlighting key findings such as peak stresses, margins of safety, and potential design revisions Support the development of technical documentation, ensuring clear and concise communication of assumptions, methods, and results Collaborate with design, manufacturing, and testing teams to help inform design improvements Required Qualifications Working toward a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Materials Science, or a related discipline Strong foundation in mechanics of materials, dynamics, and heat transfer Exposure to FEA tools (e.g., Ansys, Abaqus, COMSOL, or similar) through coursework or projects Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, or another programming language for basic data analysis or workflow automation Strong communication skills with the ability to clearly document and present technical findings Bonus Qualifications Prior research or project experience involving creep, fatigue, or thermal-mechanical problems Familiarity with engineering codes and standards (e.g., ASME, AISC, or similar) Experience using Git or another version control system Instrumentation and Controls Intern This intern will contribute to the development, integration, and testing of measurement and control systems that support advanced reactor operation and power generation. This position provides hands-on exposure to sensors, automation, and control strategies, while giving interns the opportunity to apply classroom knowledge to real-world engineering challenges. Key Responsibilities Assist in developing and testing sensors, instrumentation, and actuators under real design constraints Help design and implement control algorithms for equipment and processes Support the integration of I&C components into reactor systems and analysis workflows Contribute to documenting methods, results, and system designs in a clear and professional manner Collaborate with design and analysis teams to provide feedback that supports rapid iteration and improvement Required Qualifications Working toward a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field Familiarity with measurement techniques, data acquisition, and signal processing Exposure to control theory and feedback systems through coursework or projects Basic programming skills in Python (or similar) for data analysis and automation Strong communication skills and an eagerness to learn in a collaborative environment Bonus Qualifications Experience with circuit design (analog or digital) from labs, research, or projects Exposure to communication protocols and digital networks Familiarity with Git version control Neutronics Methodologies Intern This intern will assist in updating and streamlining neutronic methodologies to align with the latest format and standards. They will ensure that the methodologies match the way the code base builds the model, verifying consistency across both. This position also involves identifying and documenting gaps or discrepancies in the review process for future improvements. Key Responsibilities Update and optimize neutronic methodologies to the latest format and standards. Ensure methodologies align with the way the code base builds the model. Identify and document any gaps or discrepancies in the current processes. Collaborate with team members to ensure consistency and accuracy in modeling procedures. Required Qualifications Proficient in Python for scripting and automation. Familiar with AsciiDoc for documentation and formatting. Strong background in nuclear engineering and neutronics. Attention to detail with an ability to identify gaps in methodologies and processes. Process Intern This intern will support the design and analysis of fluid and power systems that are essential to Oklo’s advanced reactors. This position provides hands-on experience with system modeling, equipment evaluation, and prototyping, offering interns a chance to apply classroom knowledge to real-world energy systems. Key Responsibilities Assist in designing fluid and process systems, including piping, valves, pumps, compressors, and heat exchangers Support definition of process equipment specifications, performance criteria, and operating conditions Contribute to prototype setup and testing activities for iterative system design and validation Help prepare technical documentation to support system layout, fabrication, installation, and operation Collaborate with engineers on analyses to evaluate performance and inform design refinements Document results and methods in a clear and professional manner for use across design and regulatory teams Required Qualifications Working toward a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a related discipline Background in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer through coursework or projects Familiarity with process or system modeling tools (e.g., MATLAB, Python, Aspen, or similar) Strong problem-solving skills with attention to detail Ability to clearly communicate technical findings through reports or presentations Bonus Qualifications Experience with lab work, prototyping, or experimental systems Exposure to piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs) or process design coursework Familiarity with pumps, heat exchangers, or thermal-fluid systems from research or internships Prototyping/Manufacturing Intern The prototyping engineering intern will be a part of the prototyping and visualization team. Key Responsibilities Assist in machining and general fabrication of prototypes and test setups Work with engineers to develop and execute testing procedures for mechanical systems Support assembly, troubleshooting, and optimization of electro-mechanical systems Conduct inspections and quality control on fabricated components Document test results, process improvements, and technical findings Collaborate with the engineering team to improve designs and manufacturing processes Maintain a safe and organized workspace Required qualifications Mechanical, manufacturing, electrical, nuclear, chemical, or similar engineering student graduating with bachelors, masters, or PhD within the following year Hands-on experience with mechanical fabrication, machining, or assembly Good understanding of mechanical design, materials, and manufacturing processes Familiarity with mechanical measurement tools (calipers, micrometers, etc.) Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and schematics Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work independently and in a team environment Good communication and technical documentation skills Bonus qualifications Experience with manual or CNC machining Exposure to electronics, sensors, and control systems (mechatronics experience) Experience with CAD software (SolidWorks, AutoCAD, or similar) Experience with welding, 3D printing, or other prototyping techniques Understanding of fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, or materials science Experience with data acquisition systems and programming (Python, LabVIEW, or MATLAB) Business Operations Intern This role provides an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in business operations, process improvement, and cross-functional collaboration. This role is ideal for someone looking to grow their operational skill set in core business operational functions and is passionate about contributing to initiatives that drive efficiency while supporting key compliance functions across the organization. Key Responsibilities Assist with day-to-day business operations, including process documentation, workflow optimization, and project coordination. Collect, organize, and analyze operational and financial data to generate insights and support decision-making. Prepare reports, presentations, and dashboards for internal stakeholders. Collaborate with cross-functional teams (finance, HR, marketing, product, etc.) to support operational initiatives. Conduct research on industry trends, competitors, and best practices to support strategic planning. Identify and recommend opportunities for process improvements and increased efficiency. Provide administrative and logistical support for team projects and meetings. Required Qualifications Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, Economics, or a related field. Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) or Google Workspace. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. Attention to detail and eagerness to learn. Competencies We are looking for interns that are: Passionate about making advanced fission a reality Willing and able to learn quickly Eager to work on a dynamic team, receive constructive feedback, and grow with us Willing to think differently and do things in new ways Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment Excited to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about the problems they are solving, while not leaning only on what has been done before Willing to propose novel and creative solutions to technical problems An excellent writer who can write in modern active voice, so make your cover letter compelling and write it well! Able to communicate technical content and results verbally Who you are: A startup person : You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that. Motivated : You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals. A team-player : Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team. An excellent communicator : We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator. Creative : Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day. Detail-oriented : This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward. About Oklo's Intern compensation: Oklo offers housing assistance, $35 - $44 per hour (compensation is determined based on education, skills, and experience), 1-on-1 mentorship, hands-on training, and the opportunity to engage in fun team-building activities as well as interactive workshops, enhancing both professional and personal growth. Due to the nature of Oklo's work, only U.S. citizens can be considered for these positions. About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories. #CHOP: Oklo’s Values Collaboration : We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes. Humility : We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition. Ownership : We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy. Pathfinding : We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity. Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws. Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address. All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process. If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

jobs.title: Hardware Test and Reliability Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.body: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions. About the role: We are seeking Summer 2027 interns or Co-ops for our Hardware Test & Reliability Team! Autonomous systems are a new breed of product that bring together electronics hardware and real-time AI software. The complexity of the systems combined with the fact they can move freely in the real world, makes the development and reliability testing strategy a key element of delivering a great product. We are seeking a driven and cross-functional engineering intern to help the development and execution of test plans and testing infrastructure to enable rapid design iteration and robust product validation for state-of-the-art autonomous flying machines servicing a broad range of consumer and commercial use cases. How you’ll make an impact: - Own the design and implementation of hardware and software systems to execute comprehensive performance and reliability validation for products performing in a wide array of use cases - Analyze data, calculate statistics, and carefully document results to explain trends and inform impactful design improvements - Perform failure analysis to identify root cause and help develop process/design mitigations to resolve system issues, collaborating with mechanical, electrical, software, manufacturing, and quality engineering teams - Participate in design reviews and provide key design for reliability inputs to mitigate risks at every stage of the product development lifecycle What makes you a good fit: - A sense of how to test, how not to test, and how to find vulnerabilities in processes and design - A systematic approach to problem solving, and a knack for rapidly identifying issues within electro-mechanical systems; strong desire to drive failure analyses to true root cause - Enthusiastic tendencies toward diving in and applying first principles to engineer creative solutions to complex problems - Experience with Python or other programming languages for test automation, data analysis and visualization - Strong desire to learn and contribute across multiple domains within a dynamic and growing organization - Excellent project management, written & verbal communication and cross-functional teamwork skills - Familiarity with testing equipment and basic knowledge of stress, environmental, and accelerated life testing methods to assess product durability and reliability. Our organization delivers features end-to-end from early requirements and architectural design through full vehicle integration, calibration, validation, and global program launch. Defining dashboards and performing data mining activities and analytics Develop scripting to automate testing in-vehicle and on benches Advanced Systems Integration Execute functional bring-up and system integration on development vehicles. Evaluate system interactions across compute platforms, ECUs, sensors, and actuators. Prepare and execute feature, sensor-level tests, and vehicle-level evaluation. Develop scripting to automate testing in-vehicle and on benches Develop calibrations both in vehicle and on the bench meet performance and regulatory requirements Execute performance and validation tests using simulation, bench (HIL/SIL) and on-road fleets. Document test results, consolidate findings, and support root-cause investigations. Develop scripting to automate testing in-vehicle and on benches Prepare prototype parts, tools, fixtures, harnesses, and work areas for vehicle builds; help establish repeatable installation methods that improve build efficiency, quality, and safety Troubleshoot hardware and software interface problems across mechanical, electrical, controls, and systems domains. With deep engineering expertise and leading design, emulation, and test solutions, our ~16,800 employees help customers in over 100 countries accelerate innovation across communications, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace and defense, semiconductor, and artificial intelligence markets. Responsibilities Support manufacturing and NPI projects for precision optical and laser interferometer products by assisting with product, process, and tooling improvements that enhance manufacturability, quality, and production readiness. Assist production teams in the assembly, alignment, testing, and release of optical and opto-mechanical products, including the transfer of new tooling, processes, and procedures into production. jobs.title: Undergraduate Engineering Internships 2027
jobs.body: Moog is a performance culture that empowers people to achieve great things. Our people enjoy solving interesting technical challenges in a culture where everyone trusts each other to do the right thing. For you, working with us can mean deeper job satisfaction, better rewards, and a great quality of life inside and outside of work. Job Title : Undergraduate Engineering Internships 2027 Work Schedule: Onsite – Tewkesbury, GBR With Headquarters in the US and a global reach, Moog Inc is a world-leading integrator of precision motion control systems for aerospace, defence, industrial and medical applications. Our engineers have developed the capability to design and manufacture the most advanced products for application where precise control of velocity, force, acceleration, and fluid flow are critical. Moog Inc. is split across the following operating groups: Military Aircraft Group, Commercial Aircraft Group, Industrial Group, and Space and Defence Group. We are proud that our people and products represent a culture where the opportunity to solve a challenging control problem is always welcomed. Our state-of-the-art facility in Tewkesbury focuses on the design and testing of our high-spec Servo valve products. We strive to foster a close relationship with our Interns from day one so that they can return to the business where possible as a member of our Graduate Engineering Programme. We are recruiting for a number of internships within the following areas of our business, these include: Product Engineering: The Product Engineering (PE) function is the focal point for resolving complex technical issues concerning the design, assembly, and test processes through the product life cycle. During the New Product Introduction (NPI) phase the team is responsible for developing effective build and test processes using tools such as PFMEA and Design for Assembly. We create the production documentation including Assembly and Test Work Instructions (ATW), Repair Work Instructions (RTW), test and nulling specifications, tooling concepts, and designs, all required to support the operations team. Following the completion of the NPI phase the PE team supports to ensure the operations team can deliver products safely, to the required quality standard, on time, and at the correct cost, utilizing lean philosophies throughout the sustainment/aftermarket phases. Product Development Engineering : The Product Development Engineering team leads new product development from initial concept design through to certification of hardware for use on an aircraft application. We work on a range of high-profile aerospace programs providing electrohydraulic servo valves for flight control and engine control applications. We have direct access to the latest design technologies such as 3D modeling and design simulation software, prototype manufacture and test environments, additive manufacture tools and techniques as well as opportunities for training and development within these areas. Assembly Systems Engineering: The ASE Intern will report to the Lead ASE on the Tewkesbury AG site, typically running 3–6-month projects with the objective of implementing assembly technology solutions in support of quality and productivity improvements in production operations. Projects will involve research, hands-on development, and integration of cutting-edge technologies to solve complex assembly process challenges. Project development will be based on-site but implementations will be considered for all AG sites, UK, USA, and Philippine facilities. Typical projects may include process/tooling design and 3D modeling, programming in C#/Python, database design and transactions in SQL Server, PLC programming, system build, and integration using pneumatics and electronic controls, as well as exposure to a variety of technologies such as robotics, vision systems with artificial intelligence, force-monitoring presses, automated torque tools and more. Quality Engineering: The Quality Engineering department works closely with all departments, technical and non-technical, within the business, from design all the way through to aftermarket, and supports the continual improvement of Moog products and processes. A Quality Engineering Intern will perform varied technical tasks related to project engineering which is non-routine such as product improvement studies, process improvement studies, and the development of new systems & procedures. The Quality Engineering Intern is responsible for conducting failure analyses by utilising their organisational skill, technical knowledge, and analytical and communication skills. The end result is to find the root cause and implement corrective and preventative actions, making sure that the problem never arises again. Manufacturing Engineering: The Manufacturing Engineering (ME) function is central to the production of complex technical components across various CNC Manufacturing Platforms, including mill turn, 5-axis mill, sliding head and conventional lathes, EDM, grinding, honing, and more. This role involves programming with software packages like NX CAD/CAM and Autodesk Partmaker, as well as validating and proving out the NC code on the machines. Additionally, ME provides daily operational support on manufacturing flowlines and resolves issues to maintain production output. During the New Product Introduction (NPI) phase, the ME team influences product designs using tools such as PFMEA and Design for Manufacture (DFM) and takes the initial concept design through to hardware certification for aircraft applications, all while achieving the proposed cost targets. The Manufacturing Engineers interface closely with many departments, such as: Operations, Quality, Design and Programme Management. Here are the skills and qualifications that will suit this internship: Working towards a relevant bachelor’s or master’s degree in engineering (e.g., Aerospace, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Systems) Excellent interpersonal and presentation skills, energetic and self-starter Resourceful Good at self-initiative Flair for practical, hands-on activities as well as analytical and theoretical Creative, problem-solving mentality Willing to embrace and effect change, with an eagerness to make a positive impact Next Steps: For your application to be considered please apply with a CV and Cover Letter. You must include your predicted grade for your degree, and where possible each grade attained for your completed modules thus far (our top tip is to go the extra mile and tell us all about your hobbies and projects which are relevant to this Internship!). You must be available for an assessment and site tour at our Tewkesbury facility during February 2027. The selection stages include attendance at an assessment and a 60-minute Team's interview. We will begin to review applications on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Vacancies will close once filled. All placements are available to penultimate/final year students and the paid internships will start between August and September 2027, for a duration of 12 months. In Return Moog can offer you: You'll have access to career progression opportunities and learning and development programs that will empower you to grow both personally and professionally. Enjoy a comprehensive Flexible Benefits Package, 33 Days Annual Leave (including Bank Holidays), Private Medical Insurance, access to mental health support and expert financial advice. You'll also benefit from free parking, access to electric car charging, an onsite gym, Life Assurance, a Company Pension Contribution starting at 6%, an Employee Share Option, and flexible working arrangements. You Matter at Moog – Our Mission and Vision At Moog, we prioritize diversity, equity, and inclusion. We aim to create a culture where everyone is valued, respected, and given equal opportunities. We strive to empower employees to bring their authentic selves to work, celebrating our differences to foster a welcoming environment for all. Embrace the journey and explore exciting possibilities!

jobs.title: Hardware Engineering Intern (Mechanical & Electrical)
jobs.body: Parallel Systems is pioneering autonomous battery-electric rail vehicles designed to transform freight transportation by shifting portions of the $900 billion U.S. trucking industry onto rail. Our innovative technology offers cleaner, safer, and more efficient logistics solutions. Join our dynamic team and help shape a smarter, greener future for global freight. Hardware Engineering Intern - Summer 2027 Internship The Hardware Engineering Intern will drive progress toward initial production and production ramp-up of our next generation vehicles. This is a hands-on role spanning design and analysis work, process development and improvement, field testing, troubleshooting, and failure analysis. You will own and deliver a production subsystem or process from concept through implementation. What You Will Work On Projects will be scoped based on team priorities during the internship, but may include: Design and implementation of end-of-line testing for Mk3 pneumatic and brake systems Design, analysis, and deployment of improved powertrain installation tooling Design, procurement, and deployment of LV harness checkout test bench Design, installation, and checkout of Mk3 drag-on instrumentation system Design, commissioning, and implementation of gearbox onboard sensor suite What to Expect Weeks 1-2: Onboarding, vehicle familiarization, facility visits, and pairing with an engineer on a small initial project Weeks 3-6: First project assignment with requirements gathering, benchmarking, concept design review, and prototype development Weeks 7-10: Final project assignment (new or continuation), full design cycle through implementation and field testing Weeks 11-12: Final presentation of outcomes, documentation, recommended next steps, and handover to the team Progress will be tracked through weekly check-ins, design reviews, field testing with data review and presentation, and feedback from the broader engineering team. Basic Requirements Currently pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field (rising junior, senior, or graduate student) Self-motivated problem solver who takes personal ownership of challenges and drives them to completion Comfortable applying first-principles thinking to find creative solutions beyond your usual scope Strong communication skills with the ability to present design work and field test results Preferred Requirements Leadership experience on a hands-on engineering team that solves real-world problems while balancing competing priorities (e.g., FSAE, solar car, Design Build Fly, Baja SAE, or similar) EE candidates: CAD proficiency to enable cross-functional contributions ME candidates: Experience with electronics, coding, or PCBA design Experience with design reviews, prototyping, and iterative hardware development cycles Please note the hourly range in the job posting reflects the new hire hourly range across levels that would be applicable to the position. jobs.title: Intern, Reliability and Inspection - Summer 2027
jobs.body: > Requisition Number: 79617 The company built on breakthroughs. ​ Join us.​ Corning is one of the world’s leading innovators in glass, ceramic, and materials science. From the depths of the ocean to the farthest reaches of space, our technologies push the boundaries of what’s possible. ​ How do we do this? With our people. They break through limitations and expectations – not once in a career, but every day. They help move our company, and the world, forward. ​ ​ At Corning, there are endless possibilities for making an impact. You can help connect the unconnected, drive the future of automobiles, transform at-home entertainment, and ensure the delivery of lifesaving medicines. And so much more.​ ​ Come break through with us. Scope of Position The Summer 2027 intern will support the development and validation of laboratory methods that detect and characterize small defects in brittle materials and multi-material structures, either as damage forms during thermal-mechanical reliability stresses or through inspection afterwards. The work will establish what each method can and cannot detect, and how those detections relate to underlying failure mechanisms. Under the guidance of technical staff, the intern will set up and calibrate sensing and inspection systems, run reliability experiments, analyze waveform and image data, and confirm detections against independent ground truth from microscopy, fractography, sectioning, materials and property characterization and failure analysis. Depending on interests and program needs, the project may focus on acoustic emission or ultrasonic monitoring during thermal cycling, on commissioning and applying an automated imaging and machine vision inspection system, or on a combination of both. Results will also help calibrate physics-based models and empirical reliability predictions. Program Benefits Competitive salaries Housing assistance Travel reimbursement Intern Activities Social and networking events Volunteer opportunities Community Involvement Key Responsibilities Review literature on non-destructive evaluation, acoustic emission and ultrasonic sensing, optical inspection, and reliability mechanisms in brittle materials and electronic packaging. Plan and run experiments, including building and calibrating sensors, data acquisition systems, and test or inspection setups. Apply acoustic emission or other ultrasonic methods to detect, locate and time damage during thermal cycling and other reliability-related stressors. Commission and apply a laboratory imaging system, including automated image analysis and machine vision for defect detection. Acquire, process and analyze sensor waveforms and image data using MATLAB, Python or similar data-analysis tools. Correlate detected events with independent ground truth from microscopy, sectioning, materials characterization and failure analysis; quantify detection thresholds, noise and false calls, and identify which damage mechanisms can and cannot be detected. Use collected data to help calibrate physics-based modeling predictions and develop empirical reliability predictions and associated models. Document methods so others can repeat them, follow laboratory safety practices, and communicate findings clearly in written reports and presentations. Requirements Currently pursuing a graduate degree (PhD preferred) in mechanical, materials, reliability, electrical or computer engineering, applied physics, optics, or a closely related field. Research, coursework, or hands-on laboratory experience in at least one of: acoustic emission, ultrasonics or non-destructive evaluation; optical imaging or machine vision; reliability testing, life modeling or failure analysis. Experience with signal or image processing using MATLAB, Python or similar tools. Ability to follow laboratory safety procedures, experimental protocols, and data-documentation practices. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and a willingness to learn new hands-on laboratory techniques. Ability to organize, analyze, and communicate experimental results clearly in written and verbal formats. Ability to work collaboratively with scientists and engineers while independently completing assigned tasks. Must be available for 10 weeks during Summer 2027 (May-August 2027) with a graduation date of December 2027 or later Be interested in working for Corning, Inc after graduation, if presented with a full-time job opportunity. Be willing to work at the posted job location Desired Skills PhD research in non-destructive evaluation, acoustics/ultrasonics, or imaging, applied to reliability of electronics and semiconductor packaging. Experience with acoustic emission sensors, waveguides, source location, waveform feature extraction, or laser vibrometry. Experience setting up cameras, optics, motion stages or automated inspection systems, including machine-learning-based image analysis. Experience with reliability testing of electronics or semiconductor packages, such as thermal cycling or environmental stress testing. Knowledge of brittle materials, glass, fracture mechanics, or thermal-mechanical modeling. Experience with microscopy, cross-sectioning, sample preparation, or other materials characterization methods. Familiarity with experimental design, statistical data analysis, and technical literature review. This position does not support immigration sponsorship. ​The range for this position is $1,635.00 - $3,185.00 biweekly. Starting pay for the successful applicant is prescribed based on geographic location, nature of position, and year in school. A job that shapes a life. jobs.title: Intern - Hardware Engineer
jobs.body: Who we are With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility. Timeframe: Summer (May-Aug 2027) At Symbotic, Early Career talent plays a meaningful role in helping us reimagine the future of supply chain automation. Through our Internship and Co-op programs, students have the opportunity to contribute to real projects, collaborate with experienced engineers and business leaders, and gain hands-on exposure to the technologies powering our end-to-end robotics and automation solutions. We are looking for curious, motivated students who are excited to solve complex problems, bring new perspectives to cross-functional teams, and see their work make an impact in a fast-moving, innovative environment. Along the way, Interns and Co-ops are supported through mentorship, professional development, networking opportunities, and a robust calendar of events designed to help them build community and grow their careers. Symbotic offers transportation and housing benefits for students who meet our relocation requirements. Continue reading below to learn more about this exciting opportunity! About the Opportunities Symbotic’s Hardware Engineering team is a dynamic community of innovators designing the technology that powers our integrated systems. Intern opportunities in our Hardware function include: Mechanical interns turn ideas into reality by designing and prototyping robotic components while gaining hands-on experience with CAD, SolidWorks, and other technologies that keep our robotics systems running. Electrical interns play a key role in sustaining and enhancing our system by managing cables, troubleshooting power issues, and testing and debugging circuit boards (PCBs). Testing interns will ensure seamless interaction between hardware and software systems through building test fixtures, developing test plans, and conducting root cause analyses. Industrial Controls interns support onsite installations, working hands-on with programmable logic controllers (PLC). What You’ll Do: Assist one of our various Hardware Engineering teams with designing, documenting, building, testing and debugging of the latest technologies and engineering designs. Design parts for various manufacturing processes, including machining, casting, sheet metal, plastics, and fabricated assemblies using CAD. Assemble electromechanical assemblies, fixtures utilizing hand tools, measurement equipment and machine tools. Assist in debugging issues with the bot Mechanical and Electro-mechanical systems and components. Develop and execute robot motion scripts (python) to control single-axis repetitive movements and coordinate complex multi-axis behaviors in support of test requirements. Create and manage Bills of Materials (BOMs) and Engineering Change Orders (ECOs). Contribute to the design and implementation of PLC hardware and software systems. Inform reliability test plans to identify failure modes early in development cycles. Conduct root cause analysis of system failures to support engineering development. What you’ll need Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in engineering required (Systems, Robotics, Mechanical, Electrical, Computer Science, or related engineering/technical field). Familiarity with developing tests for integrated systems with a high degree of hardware and software complexity, preferably robotics or automation. Familiarity with Python. Knowledge of complex electro-mechanical applications including technologies such as robotics, vision, safety-critical systems, multi-axis sensors, localization methods, actuators, and control algorithms. Strong analytical, creative problem solving, critical thinking, and organizational skills. Outstanding communication skills with demonstrated ability to organize and present data. Experience with programmable logic controllers (PLC) a plus Mechanical: Working knowledge of GD&T and other drawing standards. Experience using SolidWorks or equivalent 3D design software. Familiarity with manufacturing processes: machining, casting, sheet metal, plastics, fabricated assemblies, etc. Our Environment Up to 10% of travel may be required. Employees must have a valid driver’s license and the ability to drive and/or fly to client and other customer locations. The employee is responsible for owning a credit card and managing expenses personally to be reimbursed on a bi-weekly basis. #LI-JK2 #LI-Onsite About Symbotic Symbotic is an automation technology leader reimagining the supply chain with its end-to-end, AI-powered robotic and software platform. Symbotic reinvents the warehouse as a strategic asset for the world’s largest retail, wholesale, and food & beverage companies. Applying next-gen technology, high-density storage and machine learning to solve today's complex distribution challenges, Symbotic enables companies to move goods with unmatched speed, agility, accuracy and efficiency. As the backbone of commerce the Symbotic platform transforms the flow of goods and the economics of supply chain for its customers. For more information, visit www.symbotic.com . We are a community of innovators, collaborators and pioneers who embrace our differences, because we know unique perspectives make us stronger and smarter. Every perspective matters. We depend on the collective voices of our employees, customers and community to help guide us as we build a better place to work – for you and the world. That’s why we’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, or genetic information. The base range for this position in the posted location is $29.00 - $40.00 however, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The compensation package includes medical, dental, vision, disability, 401K, PTO and/or other benefits.

jobs.title: Quality & Manufacturing Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Quality and Manufacturing Team At Zipline, the Quality and Manufacturing team is essential to delivering safe, reliable, and scalable products that power our global operations. The team is made up of two key disciplines: Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) and Manufacturing Quality Engineering (MQE) . Together, they drive excellence across the entire product lifecycle — from early design and prototyping to high-volume production and field performance. AME ensures our manufacturing processes are innovative, efficient, and scalable, while MQE safeguards product integrity and compliance through rigorous quality standards and continuous improvement. This team plays a mission-critical role in Zipline’s success by ensuring that every product we build can perform flawlessly in the real world — whether it’s delivering life-saving medical supplies or supporting our expanding logistics network. Their work directly enables Zipline’s ability to scale globally, operate with precision, and fulfill our promise of fast, reliable service to the communities we serve. About the Role As an AME Intern, you will be focused on maintaining assembly lines & designing equipment for Zipline’s Top Level Assemblies (TLAs) that will be manufactured at Zipline's Final Assembly and End of Line Testing. This involves working with internal & external cross-functional stakeholders on design for manufacturing & assembly, assembly process and equipment design, assembly line commissioning, validation & continuous improvement to ensure Zipline can continue to serve its customers with better operational efficiency. As an MQE Intern, you will be focused on the quality and reliability of Zipline’s in-house manufacturing. This involves tracking yield performance, performing root cause analysis and corrective action implementation on assembly and functional test failures, and helping to build a world class manufacturing organization by implementing innovative processes to improve performance during manufacturing and in the field What You'll Do As an AME Intern , you will: Dfx Discussion: Assist Design for X conversation with internal & external stakeholders for Zipline TLAs and sub-assemblies. Assembly Line Management: Assist planning, budgeting, design, procurement, commissioning & validation of Assembly Lines and associated equipment at Zipline for Product Validation Builds and at Zipline TLA CMs for Mass Production. Capacity Model Management: Conduct time studies for the various assemblies and maintain the Manufacturing Capacity Model Process Documentation: Develop & maintain Process Documentation (Manufacturing Process Flow, Process FMEA, Work Instructions, Setup Checklists, Training Plans, etc.) throughout the life of a program. jobs.title: Supplier Industrialization Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About The Supplier Industrialization Engineering Team Zipline is scaling drone production and flight operations by more than 20× over the next three years while maintaining best-in-class safety and reliability. You will own the entire supplier industrialization and supplier development engineering functions — building the team, processes, tools, and culture that make Zipline’s massive scale-up possible without compromising quality, delivery, or cost. The Role As an SIE Intern, the projects you undertake will be focused on the improvement of manufacturing operations & quality at critical Zipline suppliers. This involves working with internal & external cross-functional stakeholders on design for manufacturing & assembly, manufacturing process design & implementation, statistical quality control, and root cause analysis to ensure that Zipline suppliers can meet quality, cost & delivery targets set for them. What You'll Do Design for X (DfX) Discussions: Participate in DfX discussions with internal and external stakeholders to ensure designs are optimized for manufacturability, assembly, and efficiency across Zipline’s Top Level Assemblies (TLAs) and sub-assemblies. Assembly Line Management: Assist with the planning, budgeting, design, procurement, commissioning, and validation of assembly lines and associated equipment at Zipline for Product Validation Builds and mass production at contract manufacturers (CMs). Process Documentation & Training: Develop and maintain key process documentation such as Manufacturing Process Flows, FMEAs, Control Plans, and Work Instructions. Provide training to operators and quality teams to ensure consistent standards in manufacturing and assembly processes. Supplier Management & Qualification: Support in evaluating and qualifying new suppliers, ensuring they meet Zipline’s quality and production standards. Assist in implementing manufacturing processes at supplier facilities to meet the Zipline Approval Process (ZAP) requirements. Fixture Design & Automation: Design fixtures for assembly and inspection, and propose automation strategies to improve efficiency and reliability, both at Zipline and supplier facilities. Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Corrective Actions: Assist in performing root cause analysis and implementing corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to resolve quality issues, ensuring these actions are effectively implemented to prevent future occurrences. Supplier and Process Performance Tracking: Monitor and track Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) such as first-pass yield, on-time delivery, and cost of poor quality, generating regular reports for internal and external stakeholders to drive continuous improvements. Continuous Improvement Projects: Assist in Continuous Improvement (CI) projects to enhance manufacturing processes, reduce costs, and improve product quality at both Zipline and its supplier locations What You'll Bring Must have at least completed the second year of your Undergraduate studies. jobs.location: Milford, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.body: Job Description GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need GM immigration sponsorship now or in the future. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.) To help facilitate administration of relocation benefits if you are selected, please apply using the permanent address you would move from. Work Arrangement: On-Site: This internship is categorized as on-site. The selected intern is expected to report to the office 5 days a week. Locations: Milford, Michigan About the Team The Autonomous Vehicle (AV) Engineering organization supports the development of safe, reliable, and high-performing assisted and automated driving systems throughout the vehicle lifecycle. Our teams combine vehicle systems expertise, engineering analysis, data, hands-on execution, and disciplined documentation to accelerate learning and enable productive development testing. The Fleet Reliability Engineering and AV Test Engineering teams work closely with AV Operations, Service Operations, technicians, vehicle integration, software, systems, safety, and supplier teams. Together, they identify risks, plan and execute validation, analyze vehicle and fleet performance, resolve issues, and improve the processes that keep development vehicles safe, available, serviceable, and ready for testing. We are hiring interns across two complementary focus areas. Both opportunities offer hands-on experience with autonomous vehicle development, cross-functional problem-solving, data analysis, scripting, and real-world engineering execution. What You Will Do Fleet Reliability Engineering The Fleet Reliability Engineering team improves the health, availability, serviceability, and operational readiness of autonomous vehicle fleets. Define and improve fleet health, reliability, availability, uptime, and serviceability metrics. Analyze vehicle health data, telemetry, diagnostic information, service records, work orders, incidents, and operational data. Support dashboards, data-mining activities, and analytics that provide visibility into fleet condition and reliability trends. Investigate recurring vehicle, hardware, software, sensor, electrical, or operational issues by organizing symptoms, timelines, configurations, and supporting evidence. Support root-cause investigations, issue prioritization, corrective-action tracking, and communication of findings to technical and operational stakeholders. Partner with technicians and service teams to evaluate repairs, maintenance activities, return-to-service requirements, and opportunities to improve repeatability. Develop standard work, checklists, troubleshooting guides, and documentation that improve fleet reliability, service execution, and issue closure. Develop scripting and analysis tools to automate data processing, fleet reporting, reliability calculations, and engineering workflows. Support reliability testing and validation activities using vehicles, benches, diagnostic tools, simulation, and available fleet data. AV Test Engineering The AV Test Engineering team plans, executes, and analyzes testing of assisted and automated driving capabilities across simulation, benches, closed courses, and on-road development fleets. Translate engineering questions, feature requirements, and test requests into clear test cases, procedures, and acceptance criteria. Assess test feasibility and identify dependencies, including vehicles, routes, prototypes, software branches, tools, instrumentation, safety coverage, staffing, and operating approvals. Prepare and execute feature, sensor-level, system-level, regression, A/B comparison, and vehicle-level tests. Execute performance and validation tests using simulation, playback, bench, HIL/SIL, closed-course, and on-road fleets. Develop scripts to automate testing, data collection, result processing, and repeatable test workflows in vehicles and on benches. Analyze vehicle, sensor, software, and system data to evaluate performance, identify regressions, and improve validation efficiency. Document test results, consolidate findings, create defects or mitigations, and support root-cause investigations and re-test plans. Support the creation of test datasets, scenario libraries, regression suites, dashboards, and automated test pipelines. Coordinate with AV Operations and cross-functional engineering teams to schedule and execute testing safely and consistently. Shared Responsibilities Collaborate with cross-functional engineering and operations teams to deliver technical work and improve AV development processes. Apply structured problem-solving to organize technical evidence, identify trends, and recommend next steps. Prepare technical summaries and communicate findings clearly to technical and operational stakeholders. Draw in senior engineers or technical experts when needed. Manage multiple tasks while maintaining attention to detail and working toward defined deliverables. What We’re Looking For Strong interest in autonomous vehicles, vehicle systems, reliability, diagnostics, testing, embedded systems, simulation, data analysis, or related areas. A hands-on mindset—you enjoy building, testing, troubleshooting, debugging, analyzing, and learning through doing. Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail. Ability to communicate technical findings clearly, both verbally and in writing. Comfort working collaboratively in a team environment and managing multiple tasks toward a deliverable. Required Qualifications Pursuit of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, including Electrical, Computer, Mechatronics, Systems Design, Mechanical, Chemical, or an equivalent discipline. Coursework or project experience in Python, MATLAB, or embedded microcontrollers. Ability to work full time, 40 hours per week. Preferred Qualifications Basic understanding of automotive control systems, ADAS features, vehicle diagnostics, sensors, electronics, vehicle testing, fleet operations, or software validation. Familiarity with reliability methods, root-cause analysis, data analysis, model-based design tools such as MATLAB/Simulink, simulation, HIL/SIL, data logging, or test automation. Familiarity with automotive communication protocols such as CAN, LIN, or Ethernet. Proficiency in scripting or data-analysis languages such as Python, MATLAB, or SQL. Experience developing engineering tools, dashboards, automated workflows, test datasets, or regression suites. Intent to return to a degree program after completion of the internship. Expected graduation between December 2027 and August 2028. Compensation: The monthly salary range for this role is $8,100 – $8,700 per month GM will provide a one-time lump sum taxable stipend payment to eligible students selected for the 2027 Student Program. What you’ll get from us (Benefits): Paid US GM Holidays GM Family First Vehicle Discount Program Result-based potential for growth within GM Intern events to network with company leaders and peers About GM Our vision is a world with Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions and Zero Congestion and we embrace the responsibility to lead the change that will make our world better, safer and more equitable for all. Why Join Us We believe we all must make a choice every day – individually and collectively – to drive meaningful change through our words, our deeds and our culture. Every day, we want every employee to feel they belong to one General Motors team. Benefits Overview From day one, we're looking out for your well-being–at work and at home–so you can focus on realizing your ambitions. Learn how GM supports a rewarding career that rewards you personally by visiting Total Rewards resources . jobs.title: Product Design Engineer Intern
jobs.body: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions. About the role: As a member of the Product Design Team, you will work on meaningful projects that add value to Skydio and our users. You will solve complex, interesting problems and learn from a team of world-class engineers and researchers. How you'll make an impact: - Conquer challenges creatively with a scrappy mindset - Design parts for next generation prototypes - Chase down the root cause of mission critical issues on existing or developing products - Find solutions with engineering design or manufacturing process changes - Validate your solutions with hands-on prototyping, testing, and data collection - Communicate with a cross functional team of engineers and suppliers around the globe - Present your work in design reviews and learn from senior members of our team What makes you a good fit: - Relentless curiosity. - Ability to leverage rock solid fundamentals to create exceptional designs for complicated products. - Passion for elegant mechanical design at the highest and lowest levels of detail that will delight customers. - Experience with 3D CAD. Familiarity with CATIA is highly valued. - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions. Bonus skills for the job (This experience is great to have, but we are also happy to teach you): - How to design for a broad array of manufacturing processes including: injection molding, metal casting, CNC machining, sheet metal forming, and composites. - How to complete DFM (design-for-manufacturing) with local and foreign suppliers - How to design and integrate circuit boards, antennas, and connectors into mechanical assemblies Some examples of past projects include: - Gimbal Isolation: Design, simulate, re-design, DFM, and kick-off tooling for Skydio X10 gimbal vibration isolators - Scrappy Wind Tunnel: Exactly what it sounds like. Research what it takes to make a wind tunnel. Build a wind tunnel. Use the wind tunnel to learn about aerodynamic forces on a drone to inform design improvements. - Drone Battery Charger: Create prototypes for the battery charger for Skydio 2. Perform user studies, come up with a thermal solution, architect the product, and work on cosmetic surfacing. Compensation: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Graduate students, and $58/hr for PhD students*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends. *Compensation for certain positions may vary based on the position's location. #LI-ZD1 At Skydio we believe that diversity drives innovation. We have created a multidisciplinary environment that embraces the power of diverse perspectives to create elegant solutions for complex problems. We are committed to growing our network of people, programs, and resources to nurture an inclusive culture. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local anti-discrimination laws. jobs.title: 2027 Internship Hardware Engineer, Machine Integration & Test
jobs.body: JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs. In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks. This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us. ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM Getting an autonomy stack onto a 40-ton excavator is a hardware problem long before it's a software one — brackets, harnesses, enclosures, and interfaces that survive vibration, dust, and weather. As our Machine Integration intern, you'll design and build the physical interfaces between our system and the machine, plus the test stands we use to prove them out before they ever hit a jobsite. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Integrate sensors, compute, and wiring onto machines alongside the hardware team - Design brackets, enclosures, and interface hardware in CAD, then help fabricate and install them - Build test stands for validating subsystems on the bench instead of in the field - Run lab tests, capture data, and iterate on designs based on what breaks - Document build and install procedures so the next machine goes faster than the last - Close the loop with the field team on what's working and what isn't WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR REQUIRED - Currently pursuing a BS or MS in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, robotics, or a related field — or bringing equivalent hands-on experience - CAD proficiency (SolidWorks, Onshape, or similar) - Genuine hands-on shop skills — you've built physical things, not just modeled them - Basic electrical competence: harnessing, connectors, multimeter, reading a schematic - Willingness to work on and around heavy equipment in PPE PREFERRED - Wiring harness design or manufacturing experience - Exposure to off-highway, automotive, or industrial equipment - Machining, welding, or 3D printing experience About This Internship This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited." Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic. jobs.body: It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion—have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide. We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world. The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life. If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you’ll find your purpose here.
