jobs.title: Avionics Mechanical Engineer - Summer Internship 2027
jobs.body: Advanced Reentry Technologies Who We Are: Inversion is an aerospace and defense company pioneering advanced reentry technology to enable next-generation capabilities from space. By combining high-performance materials, precision aerodynamics, and mission-driven autonomy, Inversion is transforming reentry into an operational capability for an entirely new class of missions. The company’s highly maneuverable reentry spacecraft, Arc, is designed for rapid global cargo delivery, hypersonic testing, and other national security missions that require precise, controlled flight through the atmosphere. Arc creates an entirely new transportation domain, unlocking unprecedented speed and global reach. Headquartered in Los Angeles, Inversion designs, manufactures, and integrates its spacecraft under one roof, enabling the company to move rapidly from concept to flight. The company is backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, Spark Capital, and Lockheed Martin Ventures, with customers across the U.S. government and commercial space industry. Position Overview: As an Avionics Mechanical Engineering Intern, you will support the design, build, integration, and testing of mechanical hardware that enables Inversion’s flight avionics systems. You will sit within the Avionics team and work closely with electrical, RF, embedded software, manufacturing, and vehicle engineering teams to develop robust mechanical solutions for flight-critical electronics and avionics systems. You will gain hands-on experience taking hardware from early design concepts through detailed design, prototyping, fabrication, integration, and environmental testing. This is a practical, hardware-focused internship for students interested in aerospace structures, mechanical design, electronics packaging, thermal management, mechanisms, and rapid hardware development. Key Responsibilities: Work closely with avionics and mechanical engineers to design, build, integrate, and test mechanical hardware for flight avionics systems. Support the design and packaging of flight computers, electronics, RF systems, sensors, batteries, and other avionics components. Create and modify 3D CAD models, assemblies, drawings, and manufacturing documentation. Support mechanical design reviews, including tolerance analysis, fastener selection, interfaces, manufacturability, and assembly considerations. Build and evaluate prototypes and engineering test articles using machining, additive manufacturing, sheet metal, composites, or other fabrication processes. Support vehicle-level avionics integration, including mechanical interfaces, mounting, harness routing, connector access, grounding/bonding provisions, and serviceability. Participate in environmental testing such as vibration, shock, thermal cycling, and thermal-vacuum testing. Assist with troubleshooting mechanical integration issues and rapidly develop hardware solutions to unblock testing and vehicle integration. Collect, analyze, and document test data and support generation of engineering reports and design documentation. Required Qualifications: Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related engineering discipline. GPA of 3.0 or above. 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable). Coursework or project experience in mechanical design, structures, materials, manufacturing, thermal systems, or related disciplines. Experience using a 3D CAD package such as SolidWorks, Creo, NX, Fusion 360, or similar. Strong problem-solving, written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate technical results clearly to multidisciplinary teams. Desired Qualifications: Hands-on experience designing and building mechanical hardware. Experience creating engineering drawings with GD&T and appropriate manufacturing tolerances. Experience with machining, CNC, sheet metal, additive manufacturing, composites, or other fabrication processes. Familiarity with structural analysis, FEA, thermal analysis, or mechanical simulation tools. Experience designing mechanical hardware for electronics or embedded systems. Understanding of fasteners, joints, materials, tolerances, and mechanical interfaces. Experience with vibration, shock, thermal, or other environmental testing. Experience designing hardware through Formula SAE, student rocketry, CubeSat, robotics, or similar engineering projects. Experience working with PCBs, connectors, cables, harnesses, sensors, or other avionics hardware. Familiarity with aerospace hardware development, configuration control, or engineering change processes. Previous internship experience at a space, aerospace, or hardware startup. Our office headquarters is located in Playa Vista, CA. This position requires in-office presence. The California annual base hourly rate for this role is currently $38-$41. Pay Grades are determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Individual pay will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: interviews and an assessment of several factors that are unique to each candidate, job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and internal equity. ITAR Compliance: To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here . We are bringing together the best scientists, engineers, and operators from the fusion community, hard tech industry, and other sectors. jobs.title: 2027 Flight Test Engineer Intern
jobs.body: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. The Test and Evaluation team at Anduril works across the entire spectrum of products and business lines, as well as all flight operations and test range management. Our team conducts full system level development testing, new production acceptance testing, sub-component qualification testing and much more. This varies from Road Runner flight testing, Anvil checkouts, tower calibration, surrogate integrations and much more. In short, if it involves test, we support it. Experience with CAD modeling and PCB design. FAA Part 107 certification. Direct experience in the development, testing, and deployment of mission autonomy systems in a defense or aerospace context. Hands-on experience with simulation environments and tools used for testing autonomous systems. Ability to understand new concepts quickly; apply them accurately; organize, schedule, and coordinate work phases; and determine the appropriate approach at the task level or, with assistance, at the project level to provide solutions to a range of complex problems. jobs.title: Product Design Engineering Intern, Summer 2027
jobs.body: Mill is a waste prevention technology company reimagining what it means to eliminate waste, starting with food. Tens of thousands of Mill’s residential food recyclers are already helping households divert millions of pounds of food scraps every year, paving the way for our upcoming launch of Mill Commercial—the industry’s first end-to-end solution for managing, understanding, and preventing food waste in commercial environments (e.g. grocery, restaurants, food services). At Mill, we are passionate about building easy-to-use, beautifully designed technologies that keep food in the food system and out of landfills. As a Product Design Engineering intern at Mill, you’ll be working with a tight-knit, fast-paced team on a novel consumer product. Your day-to-day will include hands-on work with hardware components and lab equipment as well as CAD design tools like NX. jobs.title: NPI Engineering Intern
jobs.body: To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology. Group/Division The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The Film and Scatterometry Technology (FaST) division delivers industry-leading metrology solutions essential to advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Its portfolio includes systems for measuring film thickness, critical dimensions, composition, and resistivity—key to developing and scaling next-gen IC processes. FaST partners closely with customers from early R&D through high-volume production, ensuring performance and process alignment. Key responsibilities and skills: Own NPI deliverables, related to product BOMs, procedures, tooling, fixtures. Lead multi-functional team (project manager) to meet key milestones, while meeting project requirements. Key participant in the design and development process; Propose new ideas and improvements, determine and review requirements, and drives crucial project decisions. Experiencing, contributing to, and owning components in the critical PLC process. Coordinate prototype material, build, align, and test opto-mechanical, mechanical, and electrical assemblies for design validation and assembly procedure development. Generate and release the product Bill of Material (BOM) and work with technical writers to provide valuable input to generate assembly, integration, and test procedures. Drive the development of the alignment/test tooling and packaging that are required to build and ship assemblies from our vendors to our manufacturing facility and the field. Troubleshoot and resolve issues with new designs and prototypes through assembly, testing, and system integration in a cleanroom environment. Possess strong communication skills and make decisions based on data. A motivated self-starter who is fast-learning, capable of working independently, and can effectively coordinate with a globally distributed team. Minimum Qualifications NPI Engineer Intern minimum qualifications: Pursuing Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering (Industrial, Mechanical, Optical, Electrical or Manufacturing) or Physics or related technical field. Detailed, thorough with good troubleshooting skills and ability to think as a project manager. Experience with building and aligning opto-mechanical systems is desirable. Experience with Semiconductor Capital Equipment a plus. Familiarity using 3D CAD software, preferably ProE /CREO a plus. jobs.title: 2027 Internship Sensor Hardware Test Engineer
jobs.body: JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs. In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks. This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us. ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM As a Sensor Hardware Test intern, you'll work alongside our test engineering team to characterize and validate the sensors - cameras, lidar, and supporting hardware - that power Bedrock's autonomous excavators. You'll help build test fixtures, run structured lab test campaigns, and turn raw sensor data into clear conclusions that guide how we select and integrate hardware. You'll also get out to our field site to see how bench results hold up on a live construction machine. You’ll own a hands-on project involving sensor hardware testing end-to-end, and your results will directly shape what hardware ends up on the next generation of machines. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Build and iterate on test fixtures and benchtop setups - mechanical mounts, wiring harnesses, DAQ integration - used to characterize camera, lidar, and other sensor hardware - Run structured sensor test campaigns in the lab, following defined test procedures and capturing repeatable, well-documented data - Help safely deploy test setups and instrumentation out at our field site, and support live field test campaigns on active construction equipment - Develop tools to automate data collection, process raw sensor logs, and summarize results against pass/fail criteria - Help scope and select test equipment (light meters, targets, DAQ hardware, valves and actuators for environmental or fluid test rigs) for new test setups - Support electrical and mechanical debugging of test hardware, including wiring, sensor interfacing, and basic CAD work for fixture design - Document test methods, results, and findings, and present conclusions to the test engineering team to inform sensor selection and system design decisions WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR REQUIRED - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Optics, Mechatronics, or a related field - Hands-on experience building or testing hardware through coursework, personal projects, or a prior internship - Working proficiency in Python for data processing, scripting, or automation - Comfortable with basic lab equipment and electrical debugging (multimeters, oscilloscopes, DAQ systems) - Comfortable working outdoors and around active construction equipment, and willing to spend time on-site at our field test location for deployment and field testing - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document technical work clearly for a team PREFERRED - Exposure to cameras, lidar, radar, or other sensing hardware through coursework, internship experience, or personal projects - Experience with CAD tools for mechanical fixture design - Familiarity with Git and working within a shared codebase - Prior coursework, internship, or project experience in robotics, autonomous systems, or controls About This Internship This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited. Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic. jobs.title: New Product Introduction Engineering Intern
jobs.body: Job Title: New Product Introduction Engineering Intern Job Description: Here at Entegris, we use advanced science to enable technologies that transform the world, and we are seeking employees who have the drive to continue the mission. The Role: Our site in Colorado Springs, CO is seeking a New Product Introduction Engineering Intern to join our team for the Summer 2027 season. This assignment is intended to be 12-14 weeks in duration, beginning in May-August. We are seeking a curious, hands-on NPI Engineering Intern to support the introduction and scale-up of new products in a precision manufacturing environment. The intern will work alongside NPI Engineering, Product Development, Manufacturing, Quality, Operations, and other cross-functional partners to help transition products from engineering development through prototype and pilot builds toward stable manufacturing. This internship is designed to give a college student practical experience in new product introduction, manufacturing engineering, technical documentation, data collection and analysis, and structured problem solving. Assignments will be completed with guidance from experienced engineers and technical team members. What You’ll Do: Support prototype, engineering, pilot, qualification, and manufacturing builds for new products. Maintain a hands-on presence in manufacturing areas to observe processes, support planned builds, gather data, and learn how products transition into production. Assist with injection molding trials, molded-part evaluations, and plastic product assembly activities by documenting process conditions, measurements, defects, and observations. Assemble, inspect, test, label, clean, and package prototype or production-intent products using engineering drawings, bills of material, work instructions, and build plans. Collect and organize manufacturing data related to yield, cycle time, scrap, process capability, capacity, measurements, and build performance. Use Excel or similar tools to analyze, chart, summarize, and communicate technical data. Assist with dimensional and functional inspection using appropriate measurement and test equipment under guidance. Support basic manufacturing and industrial engineering activities such as process mapping, time studies, workflow analysis, work-cell layout, capacity calculations, line balancing, and ergonomic observations. Help create and update work instructions, process records, assembly instructions, inspection methods, training materials, project trackers, and lessons learned. Prepare concise technical summaries that communicate accomplishments, data, open issues, risks, action owners, due dates, and recommended next steps. Participate in structured troubleshooting and root-cause investigations by gathering data, documenting findings, and completing assigned experiments or evaluations. Support fixture, tooling, workstation, error-proofing, and process-flow improvement activities. Assist engineers with manufacturing-readiness activities, which may include design reviews, PFMEAs, control plans, qualification activities, change-control documentation, and manufacturing master data. Coordinate assigned materials, samples, documentation, measurements, or other resources required for planned engineering activities. Follow all environmental, health, safety, quality, contamination-control, and clean-manufacturing requirements. Communicate concerns promptly and complete assigned actions with attention to accuracy, traceability, and timing. What We Seek: Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Engineering Technology, Plastics or Polymer Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Ability to collect, organize, analyze, and clearly communicate technical data. Ability to create clear technical documentation and concise written summaries. Foundational understanding of engineering drawings, specifications, measurements, and manufacturing processes. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Willingness to work directly with manufacturing equipment, fixtures, tools, inspection systems, components, and production personnel. Strong interpersonal, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Preferred Qualifications: Interest in injection molding, plastic components, product assembly, tooling, fixtures, inspection, and precision manufacturing. Familiarity with statistical analysis, CAD, SAP, Minitab, JMP, SolidWorks, or other engineering and manufacturing systems.Hands-on project, laboratory, manufacturing, internship, or co-op experience. jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern - Research & Development - Energy and Propulsion Controls
jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.body: Job Description The Role: As a 2027 Summer Intern on the Energy and Propulsion Controls team, you will support researchers and engineers working on advanced vehicle energy-management, propulsion-control, and thermal-management technologies. A primary focus of this role will be the EVE Research Program, where thermal management is a core technical deliverable. You will help translate ongoing research into vehicle-level control concepts, models, simulations, and implementation activities that support efficient, safe, and high-performing electrified propulsion systems. You will gain experience connecting control strategies with batteries, power electronics, electric machines, propulsion systems, thermal loops, sensors, actuators, and vehicle-level energy requirements. GM’s thermal-control work includes coordinating battery, power-electronics, drive-unit, charging, HVAC-related, and front-end airflow requirements while balancing efficiency, performance, comfort, and component protection. The Team: The Research and Development organization explores technologies that can improve vehicle efficiency, propulsion performance, charging, thermal behavior, durability, and customer experience. The EVE Research Program includes work across advanced controls, thermal management, propulsion-energy conversion, fast charging, and vehicle health management. You will work in a multidisciplinary environment with controls researchers, thermal engineers, propulsion specialists, modeling and simulation experts, and vehicle-development teams. The team applies systems engineering, controls theory, experimentation, simulation, and data analysis to evaluate new concepts and transition promising research into vehicle applications. What You’ll Do: Support ongoing research assignments related to energy management, propulsion controls, thermal management, and vehicle-level control coordination. Help develop, evaluate, and document control strategies for battery, power electronics, electric machines, drive units, charging systems, and related thermal systems. Support the vehicle implementation of thermal-management research, including control logic for coolant pumps, valves, compressors, heaters, fans, shutters, and other thermal actuators. Develop or modify models used to study battery, propulsion, and thermal-system behavior under representative vehicle operating conditions. Run simulations and analyze system behavior across drive cycles, ambient conditions, charging conditions, operating modes, and component limits. Evaluate tradeoffs among energy consumption, range, component temperature, charging performance, propulsion capability, drive quality, efficiency, and occupant comfort. Support the development of interfaces between propulsion controls, energy-management functions, battery systems, thermal systems, HVAC-related systems, and vehicle-level controllers. Analyze sensor and actuator data to identify trends, control issues, performance limitations, and opportunities for improvement. Compare simulation results with laboratory, bench, hardware-in-the-loop, or vehicle-test data when available. Assist with control-strategy verification and validation through test-case development, test execution, data review, and issue investigation. Support the documentation of requirements, control logic, system assumptions, interfaces, calibration parameters, test procedures, and technical results. Create plots, dashboards, presentations, technical summaries, and other materials that communicate findings to engineering and research stakeholders. Collaborate with researchers and engineers to define technical questions, establish analysis plans, review results, and recommend next steps. Present progress and technical findings in team reviews and incorporate feedback into follow-on work. Required Qualifications: Pursuit of an advanced degree (MS or PhD) in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, controls engineering, computer engineering, chemical engineering, systems engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related engineering discipline. Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months. Must be willing to work in a laboratory, engineering test, or vehicle-development environment, as applicable to the assignment. Preferred Qualifications: Coursework, research, or project experience in control systems, thermal systems, energy management, vehicle dynamics, battery systems, power electronics, electric propulsion, or mechatronics. Experience with MATLAB/Simulink, Python, Modelica, GT-SUITE, or comparable modeling and simulation tools. Familiarity with feedback control, system identification, optimization, state estimation, calibration, or control-oriented modeling. Experience analyzing time-series data from simulations, laboratory testing, hardware-in-the-loop testing, or vehicle testing. Experience with sensors, actuators, data acquisition, embedded controls, or software development. Understanding of battery state of charge, battery power limits, thermal limits, energy consumption, regenerative braking, or propulsion-system operating modes. Familiarity with CAN, LIN, signal databases, vehicle data logging, or other automotive communication and measurement technologies. Ability to organize technical work, document assumptions, investigate unexpected results, and communicate conclusions clearly. Strong analytical, written, and verbal communication skills, along with curiosity and a willingness to learn. GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need GM immigration sponsorship now or in the future. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.). Work Arrangement: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Warren, MI three times per week, at minimum [or other frequency dictated by the business] GM will provide a one-time lump sum taxable stipend payment to eligible students selected for the 2027 Student Program - to help facilitate administration of relocation benefits, please apply using the permanent address you would move from. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: There was a time when all of America believed that the future of the physical world could be radically different. The engineers of the mid-1900s put a man on the moon in eight years, designed and built planes and submarines from scratch in under three, and conceived of building things we wouldn’t even be able to dream up today. Today, the last of the engineers who imagined and built these systems are retiring. As they go, we lose not only the engineering knowledge gained from their decades of imagination and trial-and-error, but also the spirit that made that imagination possible. Amca is working day-in and day-out to restore America’s ability to engineer anything that our critical systems depend on, and reinvigorate the cycle of creation that allows imagination to shape physical reality. We rapidly develop and manufacture new critical components and subsystems required to build and sustain the planes, military vehicles, and core infrastructure America needs. By restoring the capability of our antiquated supply chains, we increase the country’s capacity to imagine and realize new systems, and make a physical world that looks very different from today. Overview The Mechanical Design Engineering Intern works alongside our design team to develop flight hardware for new and existing airframes. You will own a scoped hardware project from concept through prototype and test, with a dedicated mentor and daily access to the engineers responsible for the systems around you. Your summer will consist of designing, analyzing, and building fluid and structural components, and learning how customer level requirements translate into parts that get built and qualified. This is not a shadowing program. Interns at Amca ship hardware. You should expect your work to be reviewed with the same rigor as a full-time engineer's, and to see your parts on the bench before you leave. Responsibilities Design and prototype mechanical hardware under the guidance of a mentor engineer Contribute to avionics hardware (buttons, switches, dials), flow control devices (valves, regulators, solenoids), or mechanisms (actuators, pistons) Question requirements, look for simplification, and help accelerate component deliveries Generate and maintain detailed drawings, component specifications, and supporting analysis We believe design engineers should perform their own concept design, technical analysis, and first unit builds, and we hold interns to the same expectation at an appropriate scope Support root cause investigations arising in development, production, and test, and help implement corrective actions Build and test your own prototypes in our in-house R&D lab Work with test engineering to help define and execute qualification plans for the components you own Work with build engineers to understand manufacturability constraints and incorporate DFM feedback into your designs Present your project and results to the engineering team at the end of the internship Basic Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD program in aerospace engineering, manufacturing engineering, materials engineering, mechanical engineering, or engineering physics Returning to school in Fall 2027, or graduating in Spring 2027 and interested in a full-time role Completed coursework in thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, or solid mechanics, and a working understanding of engineering first principles Hands-on design, analysis, or build experience through coursework, a student project team, personal projects, or a prior internship Preferred Skills and Experience Experience on a student project team building physical hardware, such as rocketry, Formula SAE, Baja, or a design build fly team Familiarity with GD&T concepts Experience with Siemens NX, SolidWorks, or a similar CAD package Exposure to finite element analysis (FEA) software Experience designing, building, testing, and troubleshooting mechanical systems Familiarity with pressurized components (valves, regulators, tubes, pipes) Experience using test instrumentation and control components such as pressure transducers, thermocouples, resistance temperature detectors, relays, and solenoid valves Machine shop, welding, or fabrication experience Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, enthusiasm for problem solving, and interest in modern aerospace production and design Additional Requirements This internship is on-site in El Segundo, California, five days a week. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology. jobs.title: Hardware Reliability Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Do you want to change how the world creates? At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before. We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us. We’re looking for a R&D Test Engineer who will play a key role in running tests and partner closely with the engineers to perform systemized tests on 3d printers and report your findings. The output of this work will determine future features and settings for our 3d printers. The Hardware Reliability Engineering team ensures that Formlabs products in development are reliable and ready to ship, as well as triaging reliability issues of current products already in the field. We work closely with design teams of all disciplines to find product flaws as fast as possible and then work on redesigns to make more robust systems. Are you a cross-functional engineer that is passionate about creating robust products? We want you as a Hardware Test Engineering Intern . Internship Term: Summer (May/June - August) Commitment: Full-time Location: Onsite in Somerville, MA Application Materials : A portfolio of your previous engineering work/projects is recommended. View our Portfolio FAQ ! The Job Develop, execute, and manage system, subsystem, and component level validation test plans to ensure products meet design and reliability requirements. Work with other teams to ensure a thorough system is completed. Perform hands-on and data-driven root cause analysis to triage field failures and electromechanical systems, utilizing common problem-solving methodologies and a "physics of failure" approach. Design, build, and implement automated testing equipment for subsystem characterization and reliability/environmental testing Collaborate with the design team throughout product development to perform risk assessments, manage continuous testing, and contribute to design reviews You Are well versed with complex electromechanical systems and are passionate about understanding what it takes to make them work reliably Have experience developing full system test plans and know how to execute them in fast-paced product development timelines Have experience with testing a wide range of sensors, actuators, and mechanical components Can prototype and run your own tests, from experimental setup to hardware and software implementation Bonus skills: Familiarity with Linux systems and scripting in various languages (Python preferred) Familiarity with HALT and HASS testing Intern Benefits & Perks: Flexible Out of Office Plan – take time when you need it Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits Catered on-site lunches (3x per week), snacks, beverages, & treats Cohort-based social and professional development experience for interns Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community And of course… unlimited 3D prints We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. jobs.title: 2027 Low Observables Engineer Intern
jobs.body: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. ABOUT THE TEAM The Air Dominance and Strike Low Observable Team are advancing into the next generation of LO Technology to enhance the survivability and effectiveness of unmanned air systems. Our Low Observables engineering team is responsible for designing, analyzing, testing, and sustaining stealth features that reduce radar (RCS) and infrared (IR) signatures, ensuring our systems remain undetectable in contested environments. ABOUT THE ROLE This is an intern role open to engineers finishing a degree in aerospace, electrical, or mechanical engineering. Low Observables work sits at the intersection of all three: the shape of the air vehicle, the electromagnetic behavior of its surfaces, and the materials and processes used to build it. You do not need prior stealth experience. Almost nobody arrives with it, because most of it cannot be taught outside a cleared program. We will teach you the LO-specific methods. What we are looking for is strong engineering fundamentals, comfort picking up unfamiliar analysis tools, and the judgment to tell a real result from a bad one. You will be paired with an LO engineer and start on a scoped piece of a live program, not a training exercise. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Run broadband Radar Cross Section (RCS) analysis on components and full air vehicles, and learn to judge when a prediction can be trusted Support the design and development of Low Observable unmanned air systems, from early configuration trades through detailed design Build and improve the analysis tools, scripts, and validation workflows the team runs on Model LO materials and treatments, and help select and optimize them for specific components Support manufacturing and validation planning, including tolerances, inspection methods, and what is actually producible at rate Help plan and execute RCS measurement campaigns in indoor chambers and on outdoor ranges, then reduce and interpret the data Compare measured results against predictions, chase down the disagreements, and feed what you learn back into the models REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field. Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester. Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. Ability to complete an in-person 12-week internship in one of our offices in summer 2027. jobs.body: To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology. What You'll Do In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise. Job Description/Responsibilities KLA is looking for high-energy interns for several exciting projects this coming summer in our Ann Arbor, Michigan location. This position provides an outstanding opportunity to learn about semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Specifically, this position provides an opportunity to perform hands-on work and contribute to the development of sub-components for KLA’s inspection and metrology tools. The individual in this role will work self-motivated in a team with other interns and engineers on a specific aspect of a larger project. In this position, the candidate would work on designing, documenting, and procuring parts for stand-alone test fixtures and tools. They would be working in a team environment and collaborating with engineers and other interns from different disciplines, such as electrical engineering, optical engineering, and computer science. The candidate will design 3D CAD models of parts and assemblies. Engineering documentation as well as basic analytical modeling will be required. Furthermore, it is expected that the candidate will assemble and test the designs in a laboratory environment. Qualifications/Education Desired The successful candidate should have taken classes in mechanical design and manufacturing and have basic knowledge in CAD software. Experience with PTC Creo and Ansys is a plus. The candidate should have strong analytical capabilities, written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills. jobs.title: Systems Integration and Test Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Peak Energy Job Title: Systems Integration and Test Engineering Intern Location: Burlingame, CA Department: ESS Engineering Reports To: Senior Manager, Test Engineering Position Type: Internship (Summer 2027 Term) About Peak Energy Peak Energy is the first American venture to advance globally proven Sodium-Ion battery systems as the storage standard for the new era of renewable energy on a resilient grid. Sodium-Ion is cheap, readily available and safe, making it the leading contender in a rapidly evolving market. Our leadership team is powered by decades of expertise in scaling gigawatt-level innovation at world-class companies such as Tesla, Northvolt, Apple, Powin, Enovix, Zipline, Solid Power, and Fluence. We are backed by strategic investment and product partners such as TDK Ventures and Eclipse Ventures. We are a team of engineers, operators, entrepreneurs, and partners driven by a shared ambition to set the new performance standard for renewable energy and grid resilience. About the Role – Systems Integration and Test Engineering Intern This intern will support integration testing and functional verification of Peak Energy's energy storage systems, working across BMS, inverters, and other systems from batteries to power electronics. As Peak Energy scales its ESS testing infrastructure, this role helps build out the benchtop and HIL test capabilities needed to validate systems ahead of production. You'll work closely with firmware, design, and simulation teams, gaining exposure to the full test lifecycle – from procedure development to execution to reporting. This role suits a hands-on, curious engineer who's eager to learn by doing and comfortable navigating ambiguity in a fast-moving startup environment. What You'll Do (Responsibilities) Support functional testing of BMS, inverters, and other systems across Peak Energy's energy storage product Help design, set up, and run benchtop and HIL test setups for validation of the BMS Develop and execute test scripts to support test automation efforts Assist in developing test plans and procedures across electrical and mechanical systems Interface with design, simulation, and manufacturing engineering partners to inform design decisions Help analyze test data and document findings for engineering teams Support troubleshooting and diagnosis of issues identified during testing Participate in a culture of rapid prototyping and testing What You'll Bring (Qualifications) Pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a closely related field Experience interfacing with microcontrollers and writing scripts for functional testing Basic familiarity with electromechanical test setups Proficiency in Python or similar Strong analytical and problem-solving skills Comfortable working hands-on with hardware and lab equipment Passion for renewable energy, sustainability, and driving positive environmental impact through technology innovation Eligible to work in the U.S. Preferred Qualifications Exposure to high voltage battery and power electronics systems Familiarity with battery management systems (BMS) architecture Coursework or project experience with hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test systems Peak Energy is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce. We strongly encourage women, people of color, and individuals from underrepresented groups to apply. We value skills, potential, and perspective over specific credentials. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t look perfect on paper, we still want to hear from you. Our Core Values Speed Through Focus - Move fast but understand why. Focus on the goal, don't sacrifice quality. Mission Over Self - It's about the greater good; confident humility. Take ownership and accountability. Face the Brutal Truth - Transparency, honesty, big picture curiosity. Fearless decision making. Be a Good Person - Kindness, collaboration and teamwork. Compensation & Benefits The hourly rate for this role is $35/hr. Join us to thrive in a supportive environment while making a meaningful impact in the energy sector! jobs.body: About Varda Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses. From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind. Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital. Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL. Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem. jobs.title: Space Mechanical Design Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.body: About Us At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space. The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy. About the Summer Internship Program Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater. Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else. We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer. We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules: Cohort #1 Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13 Cohort #2 Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10 All internship roles are based at our Torrance headquarters and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package. About the Role As a Space Mechanical Design Intern, you will contribute to the mechanical design and development of Antares reactor and power systems, with a particular focus on space applications. You will work on hardware ranging from space radiators and power conversion components to reactor mechanical systems, taking projects from early design and manufacturing concepts through integration and testing. You will also evaluate how Antares systems could be deployed across different applications, translating customer operating conditions into technical requirements and concepts of operation. This role offers exposure to both detailed hardware development and the system-level engineering required to deploy nuclear power systems in space and terrestrial applications. Roles and Responsibilities: - Design, develop, and test space radiator hardware - Develop manufacturing approaches for scaling radiator technology from small test coupons to full-scale hardware - Contribute to the development and integration of space power conversion systems - Own the design and development of power conversion components such as recuperators, primary heat exchangers, and piping - Support overall mechanical integration of space power conversion systems - Contribute to reactor mechanical design - Perform microgrid analyses, including identifying nominal customer load profiles, outage frequencies, integration with other energy sources, and power distribution requirements - Develop reactor deployment assessments and concepts of operation for candidate applications - Evaluate external markets, including process heat, to identify potential reactor deployment concepts and customer use cases - Translate potential customer applications into technical requirements - Expand technoeconomic analyses to evaluate potential reactor applications and deployment scenarios Basic Qualifications: - Enrolled in at least a bachelor’s degree program, and going into your Junior or Senior year of studies - Must have prior internship experience, or significant (>1yr) project team, laboratory, or research experience Preferred Skills & Experience: - GPA of 3.5 or above - Experience in a University club or organization, leadership role preferred - Strong interpersonal and technical communication skills (examples: leading a student project team, presenting research at conferences, etc.) - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail - Ability to work cross-departmentally with different groups and teams - Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements - Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively Location - We are located in Torrance, CA in a 322,000 square foot, brand new facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access to the 405, 105, and 110 freeways. Our facility is in the heart of Los Angeles' vibrant emerging tech ecosystem alongside many other high growth startups and enterprises. Culture At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful: - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done” - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption Equal Opportunity Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status. ITAR REQUIREMENTS To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987. Pay range: $34 per hour.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineering Intern
jobs.body: What we’re building The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now. Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water. The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it Who we’re looking for We’re looking for a curious, hands-on engineer who wants to understand how things are built and make the process better. You’ll join our Manufacturing Engineering team in Torrance, working alongside engineers, technicians, supervisors, and quality partners on real production challenges. With mentorship from a full-time engineer, you’ll own a scoped improvement project from observing the process and collecting data through implementing a solution and measuring the results. You should enjoy spending time on the production floor, listening to the people doing the work, and turning ideas into practical improvements. Internship Term - June 14–August 20, 2027, onsite at our Torrance headquarters. What You'll Do Observe production processes and perform time studies to identify bottlenecks, excess motion, rework, and opportunities to reduce build hours. Create and improve work instructions, process flows, and assembly sequences with input from technicians and engineers. Design, prototype, and validate tools, fixtures, and shop aids that improve repeatability, ergonomics, and build quality. Support root-cause investigations into production issues and help implement corrective actions. Partner with design engineering and quality to improve manufacturability and support the introduction of new parts or processes. jobs.title: Manufacturing Intern
jobs.body: Who we are At Atoms, we are building the machines that power the next era of progress. Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that. Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive. This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale. We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life. If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us. What you’ll do As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern, you won't just shadow—you'll own real projects alongside experienced engineers and technicians on our production floor. Process & Line Optimization: Conduct time-and-motion studies, line balancing, and cycle time analyses to identify bottlenecks in custom computer builds and retrofit kit manufacturing. Tooling & Fixtures: Design and fabricate production tooling, jigs, and fixtures to improve build quality, repeatability, and floor ergonomics. Layout & Material Flow: Assist in optimizing station layouts and material kitting flows across our San Francisco facility. Floor Collaboration: Work daily with build technicians to capture hands-on process knowledge and translate floor feedback into implemented physical or procedural improvements. Standardization: Draft and update version-controlled Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and work instructions in partnership with Hardware Engineering. Data Tracking: Collect and analyze key manufacturing metrics (cycle time, first-pass yield, defect rates) to help prioritize engineering fixes. What we’re looking for Education: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial, or Mechatronics Engineering (or a related field). Hands-on Mindset: Comfortable spending time on the shop floor working directly with technicians, tools, and hardware. Technical Fundamentals: Basic proficiency with 3D CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks, NX, or Onshape) for designing fixtures or workstation layouts. Analytical Skills: Familiarity with data analysis tools (Excel, Python, or similar) and an interest in Lean principles (5S, Root Cause Analysis, Kaizen). Communication: Strong communication skills and an eagerness to collaborate across engineering and technician teams. Preferred qualifications Prior internship or project experience in a hands-on manufacturing, robotics, automotive, or hardware environment. Experience running time-and-motion studies or drafting assembly instructions. Student team participation (e.g., Formula SAE, FIRST Robotics, Hyperloop, or similar hardware clubs). Why join us At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow. What else you need to know This role is based in our San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week. Program Dates: Our internship is a 12-weeks program. Cohort sessions run as follows: Winter 2027: January – April Summer 2027: Late May – September The base salary range for this role is $50.00 per hour. Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications. Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others? #LI-Onsite

jobs.body: Job Location BOSTON GO & TECH CENTER Job Description About P&G and Our Engineering Sites: P&G is a global leader in consumer goods, committed to innovation impacting 5 billion consumers daily. Our Product Supply (PS) team - of which includes our Engineering (ENG) experts - drives our creation process, offering a rewarding career path to build expertise and grow as a leader. These ENG roles are primarily located at our Business & Technical Centers, with some opportunities also available at our Manufacturing Sites across the United States. Explore our US ENG locations here: Business & Technical Centers and Manufacturing Sites . The Opportunity: Engineer the Future, Today Are you an aspiring engineer passionate about inventing, developing, and delivering groundbreaking solutions? This 12-week Engineering Internship offers a chance to contribute to P&G's global success in dynamic environments, from technical centers developing the latest innovations to plants optimizing advanced engineering systems . You'll be a key member of our engineering team, collaborating with R&D and Manufacturing, working with cutting-edge technologies, and gaining invaluable hands-on experience on projects that matter. What You Will Do: As an Engineering Intern , you'll contribute to specialized engineering domains tied to our central technical teams and future manufacturing visions. Projects may include: Intelligent Controls & Automation (ICA): Support design, development, and implementation of control systems, robotics, Industry 4.0 technologies, and AI/ML solutions for process control. Mechanical Design & Development (APS): Apply mechanical engineering mastery to develop innovative equipment (e.g., Blades & Metals, Plastics Systems, Equipment Design). Work from modeling/analysis to hands-on prototyping. Converting & Packing Engineering: Assist in refining technologies for material conversion and high-speed packaging, including packaging group projects. Manufacturing Process Development (MPD): Collaborate with R&D to scale up innovative processes, assist in material/format validation, optimize production lines, and support supplier management. Instrumentation & Metrology: Support design and maintenance of precision instrumentation and metrology systems for quality control and measurement accuracy. Robotics Engineering: Contribute to developing and integrating robotic solutions for manufacturing tasks. Environmental & Civil Engineering: Support sustainable solutions, site infrastructure, and environmental compliance projects. What We Offer: Meaningful Work & Ownership: Lead or significantly contribute to a real engineering projects with measurable impact from Day 1. Continuous Mentorship & Training: Receive formal training and daily coaching from experienced engineers. Click here to learn more about our approach to leadership & development . Dynamic & Encouraging Environment: Work on a diverse array of interesting and impactful problems in a collaborative setting. Click here to discover more about P&G's vibrant culture . jobs.body: Join us in our mission to commercialize fusion energy ⚡️ About Type One Energy Type One Energy Group is mission-driven to provide sustainable, affordable fusion power to the world. Established in 2019 and venture-backed in 2023, the company is led by a team of globally recognized fusion scientists with a strong track record of building state-of-the-art stellarator fusion machines, together with veteran business leaders experienced in scaling companies and commercializing energy technologies. If you are searching for the best new ideas and share our vision, join us as a ”. This is what you need to know: Location: Knoxville, TN Salary: $25-$30 per hour, 40 hours per week Contract: 12-week contract - Summer 2027 (May 24th Start Date) Reporting to: Engineering Resource Manager Your role in the mission: As a mechanical engineering Intern, you will contribute to the design and development of mechanical systems and components for our fusion energy projects. Working alongside experienced engineers and physicists, you’ll gain hands-on experience in 3D modeling and design documentation using Siemens NX, and in structural and thermal analysis using ANSYS and COMSOL Multiphysics, while learning about advanced fabrication, assembly, and integration processes in a cutting-edge R&D environment. Key responsibilities could include: Create and update 3D CAD models and detailed engineering drawings in Siemens NX Support mechanical design activities including concept generation, layout, and tolerance analysis Assist with mechanical assembly design, tooling design, and part integration efforts Work with CAD geometry from Siemens NX to prepare models for simulation (defeaturing, simplification, mesh-ready geometry) Perform structural and mechanical analyses in ANSYS (static, modal, buckling, and thermal-structural coupling) to support and validate design decisions Build and run thermal analyses in COMSOL Multiphysics, including conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer for components operating in extreme thermal environments Contribute to design reviews and documentation to ensure accuracy and manufacturability Correlate analysis results with hand calculations, test data, or prototype inspection results Collaborate with engineers across disciplines (mechanical, electrical, systems) to support ongoing development projects Participate in prototype fabrication, inspection, and testing as needed What you’ll need: Pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in mechanical engineering or related discipline Hands-on experience with Siemens NX (Or similar CAD Software) for modeling and drafting Strong understanding of mechanical design fundamentals and GD&T principles Familiarity with manufacturing methods such as machining, welding, or assembly Coursework or project experience with finite element analysis (FEA) using ANSYS (Mechanical or Workbench) for structural analysis Familiarity with COMSOL Multiphysics, or a strong desire to learn it, for thermal and heat transfer modeling Solid grounding in heat transfer, solid mechanics, and materials fundamentals Ability to critically evaluate simulation results, including checking for mesh convergence and reasonableness of boundary conditions Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary environment Strong attention to detail and solid problem-solving skills Nice to have: Scripting experience (Python, MATLAB, or APDL) to automate or post-process simulation runs Experience with ANSYS, SpaceClaim or Discovery for geometry preparation Familiarity with the CAD-to-simulation workflow between Siemens NX and ANSYS or COMSOL Type One Energy applies proven advanced manufacturing methods, modern computational physics and high-field superconducting magnets to develop its optimized stellarator fusion energy system. Our FusionDirect development program pursues the lowest-risk, shortest-schedule path to a fusion power plant over the coming decade, using a partner-intensive and capital-efficient strategy. jobs.title: R&D Intern (Shanghai)
jobs.body: At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com . As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit. Job Function: Career Programs Job Sub Function: Non-LDP Intern/Co-Op Job Category: Career Program All Job Posting Locations: Shanghai, China Job Description: Location: J&J Shanghai Office (Building A, 65 Guiqing Road, Xuhui) Report to : Principal Engineer, R&D Johnson & Johnson MedTech China R&D Shanghai team is seeking two motivated R&D interns to support the development, verification and lifecycle activities for Endomech and Energy medical devices. This role covers hands ‑ on product design, prototyping, test execution and maintenance of test equipment, as well as coordination with prototype and test service suppliers. Interns will work on feasibility and functional concept development, execute test programs, support embedded and UI development tasks where applicable, and contribute to technical documentation and data analysis. Key Responsibilities Support product design and engineering tasks: part and assembly modeling, concept sketches, breadboarding and prototyping under coaching. Work with design and test engineers to execute verification and validation tests using axial load frames and universal testers (e.g., MTS, Instron). Assist with embedded software tasks as needed (MCU, basic firmware or integration testing). Assist in programming or UI development tasks when required. Prepare and maintain technical documentation: test protocols, data collection, test reports and design change recommendations. Perform basic data analysis and support finite element or tolerance analysis activities when required. Coordinate with prototype suppliers and external test service providers (quoting, sample delivery, technical clarifications). Support cross ‑ functional activities with Manufacturing, Quality and Regulatory teams for technical reviews and audits. Requirements Majoring in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, sophomore year or above. Commit to a full ‑ time (5 days/week) internship for at least 4 consecutive months. Proactive, ownership mindset with strong drive for project delivery and personal growth. Basic programming skills (Python, C/C++, MATLAB) and comfortable using Windows ‑ based engineering toolchains. Experience or coursework in mechanical testing or materials testing, including familiarity with universal test frames and data analysis. (Preferred) Proficiency with 3D CAD tools (UG/NX or SolidWorks) for part and assembly modelling and drawing output. (Preferred) Ability to read schematics and BOMs. What You Will Gain Domain learning: deepen your understanding of medical device product lifecycle, verification data, and regulatory considerations in China. Hands‑on project experience: participate in real test and validation work, prototype activities and equipment setup/verification. Transferable skills: improve technical analysis, test planning, reporting, presentation & storytelling, project collaboration and English business communication. Mentorship & professional growth: receive regular coaching and feedback from experienced engineers and R&D leads. Cross‑functional collaboration & global exposure: work with R&D, Manufacturing, Quality, global stakeholders and external suppliers. Factory & operational exposure: opportunities to visit manufacturing or assembly areas and learn about prototyping and production processes. Required Skills: Preferred Skills:

jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Fluid Component Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to support the Components team in working to design second generation devices to achieve the next level of maturity and reliability for future missions. The Fluid Components team designs and manufactures valves and actuators which manage fluid handling on our oxidizer-rich staged combustion engine and medium-lift launch vehicle. Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.
