jobs.title: Co-op - Test and Measurement Facility Engineer (Internship)
jobs.body: Introduction to the job ASML US brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon. Role and responsibilities Through exposure to advanced test and measurement techniques, you will design and develop test systems and/or applications to support feasibility, robustness, reliability or lifetime testing of advanced semiconductor lithography mechatronic parts and modules. As a Co-op in the Test and Measurement Facility (TMF) within the Service and Enablers Department, you will participate in the following: Develop portions of the lithography system and/or associated tooling and test equipment. You will work on sub-systems involving robotics, mechatronics, precision mechanics and/or opto-mechanics You will need to consider engineering specifications and performance, lifetime, failure modes, root cause analysis, statistical analysis, reliability predictions, 6 sigma techniques, measurement system capability, etc. You will collaborate with system architects and engineers in a multidiscipline project team to develop concepts, perform engineering analysis, build and test prototypes, partner with suppliers, analyze data and support system integration and test This position is located on-site in Wilton, CT. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation. Must be available for 6 to 9 months Education and experience Pursuing a Bachelor's, Master’s or PhD Degree in Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering or Machine Controls with a minimum 2 years completed (Must be a current student and pursuing a degree) Prior use of LabVIEW preferred Prior use of CAD software (Siemens NX) preferred Prior use of measurement equipment, such as but not limited to the following: Accelerometers Data Acquisition systems National Instruments equipment Oscilloscopes Multimeters Hand tools Skills Working at the cutting edge of tech, you will always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way do that. You will not work in a silo. Instead, you will be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you will collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You will have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems. To thrive in this job, you will need the following skills: Hands-on attitude Capability to interface with multidisciplinary groups including senior leadership High energy self-motivated team player with strong desire to learn Customer oriented and willing to work with high level problem solvers on a daily basis Possess strong leadership and ownership characteristics with commitment to achieve results on time Other information Co-Ops typically work at ASML for a semester and a summer, 8 months total This position is located on-site in Wilton, Connecticut. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation While performing the duties of this job, the employee routinely is required to sit; walk; talk; hear; use hands to keyboard, finger, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, reach, and stretch The employee is occasionally required to move around the campus The employee may occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds May require travel dependent on company needs Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus Can work under deadlines The environment generally is moderate in temperature and noise level Must be able to read and interpret data, information, and documents Can observe and respond to people and situations and interact with others encountered in the course of work Can learn and apply new information or skills The current base hourly range for this role is currently: $18.00 to $48.00 per hour Pay scales are determined by role, level, location and alignment with market data. Individual pay is determined through interviews and an assessment of several factors that that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and pay relative to other team members This position may require access to controlled technology, as defined in the Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. § 730, et seq.). Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. Business demands may require the Company to proceed with candidates who are immediately eligible to access controlled technology. It is the policy of the company to recruit, hire, train and promote persons in all job titles without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. jobs.title: Global Sourcing Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Do you want to change how the world creates? At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before. We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us. Your Impact: The components we source from all over the world are essential to the success of our products and company. We must carefully balance our need to lower costs while ensuring high performance, reliability, and abundant supply. You’ll work with our team of engineers to build relationships with suppliers and expand the capabilities of Formlabs to directly improve our products. If you are focused and inspired with a passion for streamlining and optimization, we want you as a Global Sourcing Intern on our Global Sourcing Team. Internship Term: Summer 2027 (May/June - August) Commitment: Full-time Location: Onsite in Somerville, MA The Job: Work directly with current and potential suppliers to keep our material pipeline flowing Develop strategies to better optimize our suppliers for cost, quality, and supply resilience Assist in supply chain planning for future product rollout Conduct market analysis to provide deep and meaningful sourcing insights You: Have a technical or engineering background Excited to source, contact, and evaluate potential suppliers for quality, reliability, cost and capacity Able to work with a variety of teams, communicating effectively in-person and remotely Organized and focused, able to handle concurrent conversations and projects, documenting progress along the way Leadership experience and exposure to project management Bonus Skills (Optional): Manufacturing and procurement experience Advanced use of Microsoft Excel Product development experience Familiarity with part inspection and corrective action, i.e. Quality Control Experience with the manufacturing technologies used to make our printer parts: injection molding, machining, sheet metal stamping, bending, and forming, SMT etc. Intern Benefits & Perks: Flexible Out of Office Plan – take time when you need it Salaried bi-weekly pay schedule Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits Catered on-site lunches (3x per week), snacks, beverages, & treats Cohort-based social and professional development experience for interns Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community And of course… unlimited 3D prints We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing. Compensation: Interns at Formlabs are paid on a bi-weekly pay schedule. The pay range for this role will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, location and expected impact on the organization. This is a salaried role, so you will always be paid based on the assumed 40 hours per week as a full-time intern. This position does not offer housing or relocation assistance. The weekly pay range for this role is: $1,575 — $1,950 USD

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern, Radar Hardware Development Engineer,  ASD
jobs.body: Job Description GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need GM immigration sponsorship now or in the future. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.) To help facilitate administration of relocation benefits if you are selected, please apply using the permanent address you would move from. Work Arrangement: On-Site: This internship is categorized as on-site. The selected intern is expected to report to the office 5 days a week. Locations: Milford, Michigan Warren, Michigan About the Role General Motors is seeking a Radar Hardware Development Engineer Intern to support the development and evaluation of advanced radar hardware for next-generation vehicle safety and automated-driving capabilities. You will gain hands-on experience with radar electronics, RF signal chains, sensor architecture, hardware bring-up, laboratory testing, vehicle integration, and validation. Working with experienced hardware engineers, the Munich radar team, and cross-functional partners across GM, you will contribute to design reviews, bench testing, troubleshooting, data analysis, and technical documentation for complex automotive sensing systems. Key Responsibilities Support radar hardware development through requirements review, interface definition, design reviews, verification, validation, and issue tracking. Assist with reviews of schematics, PCB layouts, RF front ends, antennas, signal chains, power, embedded compute, thermal behavior, diagnostics, and hardware interfaces. Set up and execute bench, laboratory, environmental, simulation, and vehicle-integration tests using appropriate instrumentation and documented procedures. Support hardware bring-up and troubleshooting by taking measurements, analyzing results, reproducing issues, and documenting root-cause findings. Evaluate engineering data to assess hardware and sensor performance, identify trends, and support design or corrective-action decisions. Assist with investigations involving signal integrity, power, thermal performance, electromagnetic compatibility, reliability, interfaces, and other hardware behaviors. Collaborate with firmware, embedded software, mechanical, manufacturing, quality, supplier, and vehicle-integration teams to resolve issues and assess design maturity. Contribute to technical documentation, including requirements, design decisions, test results, validation evidence, risk assessments, issue logs, and lessons learned. Required Qualifications Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, systems engineering, or a related technical discipline. Available for an engineering internship or co-op during the applicable term. Coursework, project, research, or laboratory experience in electronics, RF engineering, radar, antennas, signal processing, embedded systems, circuit design, or automotive systems. Familiarity with circuits, technical requirements, hardware interfaces, testing, measurement, debugging, and data analysis. Experience with Python, MATLAB, or a similar scripting or analysis environment. Ability to interpret basic schematics, technical requirements, test procedures, or engineering drawings. Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to learn quickly, ask effective technical questions, and work hands-on in laboratory or test environments. Preferred Qualifications Experience with radar hardware, RF systems, antennas, mixed-signal electronics, embedded compute, power management, or related sensing technologies. Must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2028 Intent to return to degree-program after the completion of the internship. Familiarity with schematic capture, PCB layout or review, oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, or other electronic test equipment. Exposure to hardware/software interface debugging, signal integrity, power integrity, thermal analysis, electromagnetic compatibility, reliability testing, or failure-mode analysis. Familiarity with automotive network interfaces, embedded systems, hardware-in-the-loop, software-in-the-loop, or vehicle testing. Experience contributing to technical projects with distributed teams and an interest in radar, advanced-driver-assistance systems, automated driving, robotics, or automotive electronics. jobs.title: Robotics and Controls Engineering Intern
jobs.body: It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide. We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world. The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life. If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here. Primary Function of Position We are seeking a robotics and controls engineering intern to join the Future Forward development team working on a next generation medical robot. The focus of the internship will be on the development and testing of algorithms for controlling novel prototypes of robotic systems and instruments. jobs.title: Hardware Engineering Intern (EE)
jobs.body: Overview Keysight is a mission-critical design enablement partner for organizations solving the world’s most complex engineering challenges. With deep engineering expertise and leading design, emulation, and test solutions, our ~16,800 employees help customers in over 100 countries accelerate innovation across communications, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace and defense, semiconductor, and artificial intelligence markets. Learn more about what we do. At Keysight, people come together to explore new ideas, challenge what's possible, and advance the technologies defining the future. Here, you'll find opportunities to do your best work, take your career further, and thrive in an award-winning culture. Learn more about our benefits. This position is based in Santa Rosa, in the heart of California’s beautiful wine country and home to Keysight’s corporate headquarters and many product-development R&D labs. The Digital and Photonics R&D team develops and produces some of the world’s highest-performance oscilloscopes—giving early-career engineers the opportunity to learn from experienced specialists while contributing to real products and challenging measurement problems. You will join a collaborative environment where learning is part of the job. Experienced hardware, signal-integrity, FPGA, software, and measurement specialists will provide technical guidance, design feedback, and hands-on mentorship as you build confidence and depth. You’ll gain experience with advanced hardware, modern design and simulation tools, and state-of-the-art laboratory equipment while contributing to the communications-electronics measurement challenges of today and tomorrow. We are seeking an Electrical Engineer who is excited to grow their hardware-design skills while helping design, integrate, and validate high-performance electronic hardware for advanced instrumentation and measurement systems. This opportunity is especially well suited to a recent BS or MS graduate with strong fundamentals and meaningful hands-on experience from internships, university research, labs, or engineering projects. You do not need to arrive as an expert in every technology listed below. We are looking for curiosity, practical problem solving, a willingness to learn, and enthusiasm for working with experienced technical specialists who can help accelerate your development. Responsibilities What You’ll Do: Contribute to the design and development of high-speed board-level digital and mixed-signal hardware, including multi-GHz designs and applications approaching 10 GHz. Learn and participate across the hardware-development lifecycle, from architecture and component selection through schematic capture, PCB/PCA implementation, board bring-up, characterization, validation, and troubleshooting. Develop experience with circuits ranging from basic RLC networks to high-speed op-amps, filters, low-noise oscillators, microcontrollers, FPGAs, ADCs/DACs, memory, and power-supply conditioning. Design and evaluate clock and timing circuitry, including oscillators, PLLs, clock generators, buffers, synchronization, distribution, and jitter-sensitive circuits. Apply and deepen your understanding of high-speed signal-integrity and noise-control principles. Develop robust power architectures incorporating DC/DC converters, LDOs, sequencing, decoupling, grounding, and low-noise power distribution for sensitive analog, digital, FPGA, and clock circuitry. Partner with PCB and signal-integrity engineers on materials, stack-up, impedance targets, placement, high-speed routing, via structures, connectors, grounding, power planes, and return paths. Learn how PCB materials, packages, connectors, launches, vias, and other interconnects influence electrical behavior at multi-GHz frequencies. Participate in pre-layout and post-layout design reviews and, where applicable, use tools and models such as SPICE, IBIS/IBIS-AMI, S-parameters, and SI/PI simulation to predict and correlate hardware performance. Perform hands-on board bring-up and troubleshooting using advanced lab equipment such as high-bandwidth oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, VNAs where applicable, TDR/TDT techniques, logic analyzers, DMMs, and power supplies. Investigate and solve hardware challenges involving signal integrity, timing, jitter, clocks, power integrity, interfaces, FPGA behavior, embedded firmware, and PCB implementation—with support and mentorship from experienced engineers. Collaborate with software and FPGA engineers on device initialization, register configuration, diagnostics, communication interfaces, and hardware/software integration. Participate in multi-functional peer design reviews and use measurement results to improve subsequent hardware revisions. Support hardware verification, design documentation, design-for-manufacturability, EMI/EMC activities, and transition to production. How You’ll Grow: Learn directly from experienced engineers through collaborative design reviews, lab work, troubleshooting, and technical discussions. Build breadth across digital, analog, mixed-signal, signal-integrity, power-integrity, FPGA, and embedded-system domains while developing deeper expertise in the areas that interest you most. Take on increasing ownership as your skills grow—from contributing to individual circuits and measurements to driving larger pieces of a hardware design. Strengthen your engineering judgment by connecting simulation, design decisions, and real laboratory measurements on production-relevant hardware. Develop communication and collaboration skills by working across disciplines and participating in peer reviews with specialists throughout the development process. Qualifications BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline. Hands-on hardware experience gained through internships, university research, laboratory work, student teams, personal projects, or professional engineering experience. Strong digital-electronics fundamentals and a practical foundation in analog and mixed-signal circuitry. Some experience with schematic design, PCB/PCA development, board bring-up, measurement, troubleshooting, or root-cause analysis through academic, project, internship, or professional work. Foundational understanding of transmission lines, controlled impedance, termination, reflections, crosstalk, return paths, and PCB parasitics. Interest in developing deeper expertise in signal integrity and power integrity for high-performance hardware. Familiarity with high-speed digital interfaces through coursework, projects, research, internships, or professional experience. Familiarity with clock/timing concepts such as oscillators, PLLs, clock generation/distribution, synchronization, and jitter. Enthusiasm for hands-on laboratory work and systematic troubleshooting. Ability and willingness to work across hardware, software, and FPGA boundaries when diagnosing complex system behavior. Preferred Qualifications: We encourage you to apply even if you do not check every box below. These are areas you may already know or have the opportunity to develop on the job. Academic, project, internship, or professional exposure to multi-GHz signals, fast edge rates, high-speed serial interfaces, or design techniques relevant to approximately 10 GHz operation. Exposure to high-speed ADCs/DACs and FPGA-based acquisition or signal-processing hardware. Familiarity with SERDES or multi-gigabit serial links. Familiarity with S-parameters, VNA measurements, TDR/TDT, eye diagrams, jitter analysis, or channel characterization. Exposure to ADS, SystemVue, S-parameter models, or SI/PI simulation tools. Understanding of how PCB dielectric properties, insertion loss, copper loss, surface roughness, connectors, vias, and interconnect discontinuities affect high-frequency designs. Exposure to EMI/EMC design or troubleshooting. Experience with Python, C/C++, MATLAB, or similar languages for hardware characterization, diagnostics, data analysis, or test automation. Experience through coursework, research, internships, or projects involving electronic instrumentation, measurement systems, data-acquisition hardware, or other high-performance electronic products. Why This Role: This role is designed to help you grow from strong engineering fundamentals into confident, independent hardware design. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers who can coach you through unfamiliar technical challenges, provide constructive feedback, and help you understand not only how a design works, but why key engineering choices are made. As your experience develops, you’ll have opportunities to take increasing ownership, expand your technical depth, and follow your designs from concept and simulation through lab validation and into real products used by customers around the world. The level of the role will be based on applicable experience, education and skills; most offers will be between the minimum and the midpoint of the salary range listed below. jobs.title: Undergraduate Engineering Intern - Mechanical Design
jobs.body: This undergraduate internship is a full-time position Summer-Fall 2027 (May or June through December) on site in Rochester, Minnesota. The Mechanical Engineering Design intern will join the Mechanical Development Unit within the Division of Engineering (DOE). This unit is one of several specialized groups within DOE, similar to the Software and Electronics development units. The Mechanical Development Unit leverages mechanical engineering expertise as part of DOE's multidisciplinary approach to developing unique devices and systems for Mayo Clinic providers and researchers. The candidate will be assigned to projects alongside other Mechanical Engineers as well as other engineering disciplines. Some projects only require Mechanical Engineers, while other projects require multiple engineering disciplines. Project work for this candidate will include computer-aided design (CAD) work using SolidWorks, prototype development with both traditional and additive manufacturing technologies, verification testing, and engineering documentation. The candidate will be assigned one or more members to provide work direction and guidance on projects. The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of mechanical engineering principles, a working knowledge of SolidWorks, experience with design for manufacturing, and excellent written and verbal communication skills. The primary purpose of the Undergraduate Engineer Internship is to provide the student with relevant engineering experiences. One or more mentors will be assigned to the intern to provide instruction, guidance and to assess performance. The intern is responsible for learning the procedures and processes of the Division of Engineering and the assigned work unit. In addition, the intern will be given selected engineering work assignments to reinforce the learning experience and to provide benefit to the work unit. The engineering assignments may include designing components, developing a project strategy, gathering user needs, requirements and specifications, evaluating commercial components, assembling prototype systems, performing design verification and design validation, troubleshooting, and participating in design reviews. All assignments are within the context of the Division of Engineering Quality Management System (including safety risk management) and are performed in a multi-disciplinary development environment. The intern will be responsible for completing all internship-related assignments and reports for both Mayo and the participating educational facility (if applicable). The incumbent must be enrolled in an engineering, management information systems, or other technology-related degree program from an accredited college or university and have completed a minimum of four semesters – or the equivalent – of instruction toward their degree. ***To be considered for this position please attach the following to your application: 3.3 GPA or higher Current Transcript Resume or CV Applicants are strongly encouraged to include a Cover Letter Applicants are strongly encouraged to include current portfolio of sample work/writing

jobs.title: R&D Engineering Intern
jobs.body: About JLG, an Oshkosh company JLG began in 1969, when our founder, John L. Grove set out to resolve growing safety concerns in the construction industry. Since then we have been committed to understanding the challenges and delivering innovative solutions to the access market. We partner with customers to provide quality equipment, training opportunities and trusted support within the access industry. We are a global company, and our products—including mobile elevating work platforms, telehandlers, utility vehicles and accessories—can be found all over the world. As an R&D Engineering Intern with JLG, you will work alongside engineers and technicians in a hands-on research, development, and test environment supporting new and existing JLG products. This role provides exposure to the design, fabrication, assembly, testing, and modification of heavy equipment, vehicle systems, components, tooling, and test fixtures. You will spend significant time in the R&D shop working directly with technicians to support prototype builds, test setups, fabrication, machining, welding, and troubleshooting. The ideal candidate enjoys working in a heavy manufacturing environment and is interested in combining engineering design and analysis with hands-on problem solving. YOUR IMPACT Support the design, fabrication, assembly, testing, and modification of vehicles, subsystems, components, tooling, fixtures, and test stands. Work directly with R&D technicians and engineers to support prototype builds, test setups, equipment configuration changes, repairs, and troubleshooting. Create and revise engineering drawings, component layouts, tooling, and fixtures using CAD software such as Creo Parametric. Read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, specifications, and technical documentation to support shop activities. Support CAM programming and other computer-based manufacturing applications used for machining, fabrication, and R&D shop equipment. Assist with machining setups, tooling, welding, fabrication, and assembly activities while working closely with experienced technicians. Perform engineering calculations and analysis to support component design, test setups, vehicle modifications, and problem resolution. Assist with vehicle and component testing, including test setup, instrumentation, data collection, and evaluation of test results. Support validation of new product designs as part of new product development and assist with troubleshooting and resolution of issues on existing products. Develop practical solutions to shop and product challenges while considering safety, manufacturability, quality, cost, and performance. Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, technicians, suppliers, and other cross-functional teams to support project objectives. Follow applicable engineering procedures, safety requirements, standards, and specifications while working in the R&D shop and test environment. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Student pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or another related engineering field. Cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above. Ability to read and interpret basic engineering drawings, blueprints, and technical specifications. Interest in working in a hands-on heavy manufacturing, fabrication, or R&D shop environment. STANDOUT QUALIFICATIONS Previous internship, manufacturing, fabrication, machining, welding, or other hands-on technical experience. Experience with or exposure to CAM software and CNC machining processes. Experience using Creo Parametric, Pro/E, CATIA, SolidWorks, or a similar CAD system. Understanding of machining, tooling, steel fabrication, sheet metal fabrication, and/or welding principles. Experience with test instrumentation, data acquisition, vehicle testing, or component testing. Strong mechanical aptitude and an interest in working directly with technicians on equipment setups, tooling, fabrication, and troubleshooting. Experience with SAE teams, robotics, Formula SAE, Baja SAE, or other hands-on engineering activities. Knowledge of heavy equipment, construction equipment, automotive, agricultural equipment, or other heavy manufacturing industries. Strong written and verbal communication skills. WORKING CONDITIONS The following represents general working conditions for this role. Specific conditions may vary depending on business needs and individual circumstances. This role combines office-based administrative duties with physical activity in field or production environments. In the office setting, tasks may require extended computer use, sitting, and attending meetings. Field or floor work may involve walking across various terrains or shop floors, standing, moderate lifting (up to 50 pounds), climbing stairs, and exposure to varying temperatures or noise levels. Must be able to shift focus between detailed cognitive work and occasional physical tasks as needed. Reasonable accommodations will be provided for qualified individuals with disabilities to support performance across both office and field responsibilities. Pay Range: $18.00 - $37.00 The above pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target pay for the position across all U.S. locations. Within this range, individual pay is determined by various factors, including the scope and responsibilities of the role, the candidate's experience, education and skills, as well as the equity of pay among team members in similar positions. Beyond offering a competitive total rewards package, we prioritize a people-first culture and offer various opportunities to support team member growth and success. Oshkosh is committed to working with and offering reasonable accommodation to job applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to disability for any part of the employment process, please contact us at corporatetalentacquisition@oshkoshcorp.com. Oshkosh Corporation is a merit-based Equal Opportunity Employer. Job opportunities are open for application to all qualified individuals and selection decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected characteristic. To the extent that information is provided or collected regarding categories as provided by law it will in no way affect the decision regarding an employment application. Oshkosh Corporation will not discharge or in any manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with Oshkosh Corporation's legal duty to furnish information. Certain positions with Oshkosh Corporation require access to controlled goods and technologies subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations or the Export Administration Regulations. jobs.title: Test Engineering Intern (Summer)
jobs.body: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW The rhythm of this role changes constantly: prepping a test plan one day, monitoring a live run the next, and diving into post-event analysis the day after, because Paladin and Squire are both advancing toward manufacturing in parallel, and testing has to keep pace with both. You'll need a real engineering foundation to do this well, since understanding what a subsystem is supposed to do is what lets you write a test plan and recognize an anomaly instead of just a number. You don't need prior test experience. The team teaches how a test event runs, how to build a test card, and how to work a Data Room station, and you'll be on live tests early in the term. The Test Operations team cares deeply about getting that rigor right, because safe and effective testing is what lets REGENT build Seagliders and reinvent how coastal communities move. If you want a front-row seat to how a vehicle actually gets tested and moves toward certification, and you're energized by precision, fast shifts in focus, and learning from senior technical experts, this internship was built for you. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Help Build the Test Plans: You'll help write the test cards and test plans that tell the team exactly what to check and how, for both Paladin and Squire. Clear, well-structured plans are what keep a test event efficient and its data usable. - Learn the Live Watch: During test events, you'll sit in the Data Room alongside a test engineer tracking real-time telemetry as the vehicle operates, learning to catch something odd in the moment rather than after the fact. - Drive Issues to Resolution: After a test, you'll dig into the data alongside subject matter experts to understand what happened and why. You'll help carry open questions through to a real answer, not just a note in a file. - Move Between Modes Fast: Your week will shift between prepping the next test, running one live, and analyzing the last, often all within the same few days. Priorities on both vehicles move in parallel, and you'll move with them. - Work Indoors and On the Water: You'll operate in the Data Room for some tests and out on the water for others, adjusting to very different environments and requirements. Comfort in both settings is part of the job. - Partner Across Engineering: You'll work closely with engineers across electrical, mechanical, and aero/hydro disciplines to understand what a subsystem is supposed to be doing. That shared understanding is what makes a test plan, and an anomaly call, meaningful. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Engineering Coursework: You're currently pursuing a degree in engineering, with coursework in electrical, mechanical, or aero/hydro principles that gives you a working sense of what a system should be doing under normal conditions. That foundation is what lets you start recognizing when something isn't. - Curiosity About Live Data: You've worked with data or instrumentation in a lab, a project, or a class, and you want to learn to watch it stream in during a live test rather than only reviewing it afterward. - Clear Technical Writing: You write documentation someone else can follow, like lab reports or project write-ups, and you care about getting the details right. The team teaches the test card format; the writing habits are yours to bring. - Composure at Speed: You stay sharp and organized when things move fast, because live testing of air and water vehicles doesn't pause for you to catch up. High tempo doesn't rattle you. - Genuine Adaptability: You're comfortable moving between prep work, live execution, and analysis, and between indoor and on-water environments, sometimes within the same week. You don't need a fixed routine to do good work. - A Bonus in Aviation or Maritime: Coursework, projects, or club work in aerodynamics, aviation, or on the water gives you a head start, since Paladin and Squire blend both worlds. Familiarity with wind, water, or flight dynamics helps you get oriented faster. - A Bonus in Scripting or Data Tools: Some exposure to Python, MATLAB, or similar tools is a plus, since post-event analysis moves faster when you can pull patterns out of a dataset instead of scrolling through it by hand. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You're passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.body: Manufacturing Engineering Intern Location: Tuas, Singapore Duration: 20 weeks starting 11 January 2027 Role Summary At ResMed, the Manufacturing Engineering team plays a critical role in transforming innovative product designs into safe, high-quality, and scalable manufacturing solutions. jobs.body: About the Team DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. jobs.body: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. ABOUT THE JOB We are looking for Product Sourcing Engineer interns to join our rapidly growing teams. In this role, you will be responsible for driving the strategic supply network development and cost management of Anduril’s product hardware, across their lifecycles, by collaborating with suppliers and cross-functionally, including stakeholders in engineering, quality, and manufacturing. WHAT YOU’LL DO Conduct supplier selection for a specific product, leveraging approved supplier list. Partner with strategic suppliers to accelerate product development via activities such as: Concept scoping to quickly solidify requirements Feature trade-off / trade tables Total Cost of Ownership modeling Joint design development, via clear statements of work Simulation of mechanical & electronics designs Develop and execute on sourcing strategy via full market knowledge, supplier rationalization, commodity pricing plan and effective principles to drive efficiency and cost Drive the development and consolidation of a manufacturing BOM, working with Quality & Manufacturing, to ramp production internally and with our suppliers with high flexibility Be accountable for all NPI component procurement, on-time and correctly, to scale up manufacturing operations Manage the request for and associated verification of supplier related CAPEX throughout NPI Conduct value-stream mapping to optimize supply network lead time and flexibility Complete the BOM risk assessment and develop plan per part analysis Follow through completion of component qualifications by relevant stakeholders, ahead of production need dates Reduce complexity of supply chain through commonality optimization & component/supplier rationalization Lead all cost engineering activities to converge the bottoms-up cost curve to product cost, maximizing the total cost of ownership (TCO) across the product lifecycle Manage ad-hoc cost issues e.g., tariffs / import export cost, and cost inflation Drive the design and implementation of new supply chain processes and systems, ensuring they meet business requirements and are built for scale Manage project schedules, identify critical path activities, and proactively identify and mitigate risks to keep initiatives on track Hold project teams and stakeholders accountable for deliverables and deadlines, navigating organizational complexity to clear roadblocks and drive decisions Establish program structure, milestones, and operating rhythms to ensure accountability and drive results across the business Drive alignment across stakeholders and influence without formal authority in ambiguous, high-stakes situations REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Must Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: Benefits At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits . jobs.title: Innovations Engineering Co-op
jobs.body: > Requisition Number: 79067 The company built on breakthroughs. ​ Join us.​ Corning is one of the world’s leading innovators in glass, ceramic, and materials science. From the depths of the ocean to the farthest reaches of space, our technologies push the boundaries of what’s possible. ​ How do we do this? With our people. They break through limitations and expectations – not once in a career, but every day. They help move our company, and the world, forward. ​ ​At Corning, there are endless possibilities for making an impact. You can help connect the unconnected, drive the future of automobiles, transform at-home entertainment, and ensure the delivery of lifesaving medicines. And so much more.​ Come break through with us. Corning’s businesses are ever-evolving to best serve our customers, industries, and consumers. Today, we accelerate and transform life sciences, mobile consumer electronics, optical communications, display, automotive, and solar markets. We are changing the world with: Trusted products that accelerate drug discovery, development, and delivery to save lives Damage-resistant cover glass to enhance the devices that keep us connected Optical fiber, wireless technologies, and connectivity solutions to carry information and ideas at the speed of light Precision glass for advanced displays to deliver richer experiences Auto glass and ceramics to drive cleaner, safer, and smarter transportation Solar polysilicon, wafers, and innovative photovoltaic modules, enabling low-cost solar energy solutions Role Purpose The Emerging Innovations Group (EIG) transforms Corning’s materials, process, and technology expertise into new products, processes, and manufacturing capabilities. Our teams develop and scale emerging technologies from early concept through commercialization. As an Innovations Engineering Co-op, you will work alongside engineers, scientists, technicians, and operations teams on hands-on projects that advance technologies through laboratory, prototype, pilot, and manufacturing environments. Projects may include one or more of the following areas: Process Engineering - Support process development, experimentation, process characterization, scale-up, pilot operations, troubleshooting, technical documentation, and manufacturing-process improvement. Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering - Analyze workflows, process capacity, cycle time, equipment utilization, material flow, labor requirements, and operational performance. Support process mapping, Lean initiatives, standard work, and scalable operating-process design. Engineering Data Analytics - Analyze laboratory, pilot, equipment, sensor, manufacturing, or operational data. Develop reports, dashboards, visualizations, databases, automated workflows, or data pipelines that enable data-informed decisions. Automation, Controls, and Measurement - Support work involving sensors, instrumentation, controls, data acquisition, robotics, mechanical equipment automation, and connected manufacturing systems. What You’ll Gain Hands-on experience advancing early-stage technologies and new operational capabilities. Exposure to laboratory, prototype, pilot, manufacturing, automation, and data-rich technical environments. Mentorship from engineers, scientists, technical leaders, and operational professionals. Experience applying engineering, data analysis, experimentation, and continuous-improvement methods to real-world challenges. Direct contribution to meaningful projects with visible technical and business impact. Key Responsibilities Contribute to hands-on engineering projects that advance emerging technologies from laboratory and prototype development through pilot and manufacturing environments. Collect, analyze, and communicate experimental, equipment, manufacturing, or operational data to support technical decisions and project progress. Support testing, troubleshooting, process improvement, documentation, and implementation activities in collaboration with cross-functional teams. Familiarity with one or more of the following: Computer-Aided Design (CAD), process simulation, Python, SQL, R, MATLAB, JMP, Excel, Power BI, Tableau, Design of Experiments (DOE), Lean, Six Sigma, process mapping, root-cause analysis, sensors, instrumentation, controls, automation, or data acquisition. Experience working in a laboratory, research, pilot, manufacturing, operations, or other hands-on technical environment. Demonstrated initiative through student organizations, project teams, research groups, technical leadership activities, or prior work experience. jobs.title: Robotics Engineering Intern
jobs.body: It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide. We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world. The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life. If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here. Primary Function of Position The Robotics Engineering Intern will report to future forward research lad and contribute to creating a sim-to-real-to-sim platform for the Intuitive surgical robot system. The intern will enable rapid prototyping and de-risking of new controller architectures, particularly semi-supervised and supervised autonomous systems that are data-hungry and require extensive validation. Key functions include developing tools that systematically transfer and test controllers from simulation to robot hardware, building virtual models of the surgical field for simulation interaction, and closing the loop between simulation and reality to accelerate development and evaluation of autonomous controllers. Essential Job Duties Implement novel control architectures in high-level (e.g., MATLAB) and low-level (e.g., embedded C++) targets. Systematically test controller performance in simulation and on robot hardware. Create simulation environments that integrate constrained rigid-body dynamics (e.g., MuJoCo) and realistic texture and lighting (e.g., Isaac Sim). Synthesize simulated environments from video data, including geometry, texture, and inferred stiffness. Execute closed-loop round-trip tests: train a controller in simulation, test it experimentally, and use experimental data to construct new simulation environments. Required Skills and Experience University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements: University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship. Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process. Required Education and Training Current enrollment in a Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or related degree-seeking program at the Master's or Doctorate level. Working Conditions None. Preferred Skills and Experience Experience with MATLAB and/or Python for control system design and analysis. Experience with MuJoCo or similar constrained rigid-body dynamics simulators. Experience with sim-to-real transfer methods for robotic systems. Familiarity with NVIDIA Isaac Sim or similar platforms for realistic rendering and simulation. Familiarity with embedded C++ for low-level controller implementation. Awareness of video-based 3D reconstruction and environment synthesis techniques. Awareness of autonomous or semi-autonomous control architectures. Due to the nature of our business and the role, please note that Intuitive and/or your customer(s) may require that you show current proof of vaccination against certain diseases including COVID-19. Details can vary by role. Intuitive is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants and employees, and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any type, without regard to race, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, color, age, religion, protected veteran or disability status, genetic information or any other status protected under federal, state, or local applicable laws. Certain information you provide as part of the application will be used for purposes of determining whether Intuitive Surgical will need to (i) obtain an export license from the U.S. Government on your behalf (note: the government’s licensing process can take 3 to 6+ months) or (ii) implement a Technology Control Plan (“TCP”) (note: typically adds 2 weeks to the hiring process). For any Intuitive role subject to export controls, final offers are contingent upon obtaining an approved export license and/or an executed TCP prior to the prospective employee’s start date, which may or may not be flexible, and within a timeframe that does not unreasonably impede the hiring need. If applicable, candidates will be notified and instructed on any requirements for these purposes. We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with fair chance laws. Accommodation & Accessibility Notice: Intuitive is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you require assistance or an accommodation during any part of the application or interview process, please contact People Services at HRHelpNow@intusurg.com. We provide market-competitive compensation packages, inclusive of base pay (paid at an hourly rate), benefits, and a housing allowance. The hourly rate is prorated against the intern program salaries listed and total program compensation will be based on internship duration.

jobs.body: RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: No relocation assistance available CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No CLEARANCE TYPE: None TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. Northrop Grumman Mission Systems is a trusted provider of mission-enabling solutions for global security. We have a wide portfolio of secure, affordable, integrated, and multi-domain systems and technologies. Our differentiated battle management and cyber solutions deliver timely, mission-enabling information and provide superior situational awareness and understanding to protect the U.S. and its global allies. An internship at Northrop Grumman is unique. Sure, you’ll learn new skills, explore our enterprise, network with experts, connect with thought leaders, and finish with a resume that opens doors. But you’ll gain something even more valuable: pride in what you’ve done. Join us and launch your career. We’ll support you with training, professional development and networking opportunities, and our shared vision of global security. Northrop Grumman is seeking a Manufacturing Engineer for an internship opportunity. This position will be located at our Mission Systems sector in Charlottesville, VA. The qualified candidate will become part of Northrop Grumman’s Machining and Fabrication Manufacturing Engineering Team within the Multidomain Sensing, Targeting and Survivability Division and will develop and maintain technical solutions for the manufacturing of machined/fabricated components using milling, sheet metal manufacturing, welding, hydraulic assembly, painting, finishing and forming equipment. jobs.body: Company: Qualcomm Canada ULC Job Area: Interns Group, Interns Group > Interim Engineering Intern - Systems Qualcomm Overview: Qualcomm is a company of inventors that unlocked 5G ushering in an age of rapid acceleration in connectivity and new possibilities that will transform industries, create jobs, and enrich lives. But this is just the beginning. It takes inventive minds with diverse skills, backgrounds, and cultures to transform 5Gs potential into world-changing technologies and products. This is the Invention Age - and this is where you come in. General Summary: About Qualcomm Qualcomm relentlessly innovates transforming businesses, enriching lives and fortifying societies. Our solutions are pivotal in crafting a smarter, interconnected world. Building on our nearly 40-year history of era-defining technology breakthroughs, we deliver leading-edge AI, high performance, lower-power computing, and unrivaled connectivity. We’re proud to be the partner of choice to many of the world’s largest enterprises. Together with our ecosystem partners, we enable next-generation digital transformation. jobs.title: Engineering Intern to the Chief Engineer (Summer)
jobs.body: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW REGENT is looking for an Engineering Intern to work with the Chief Engineer - Viceroy, spending a summer at the center of Viceroy, our first manned certification program, working directly alongside the person responsible for how it all comes together. This isn't an internship built around one discipline or one team. You'll move across systems, mechanical, electrical, controls, and software work as the program demands it, picking up analysis, drawings, and integration tasks wherever the need is greatest during an intense and fast-moving stretch of the program. It's a rare chance to see how a complex vehicle program actually fits together end to end, rather than experiencing just one slice of it. You'll sit within our Engineering & Technology team and report directly to the Chief Engineer, who will actively coach and mentor you through the breadth of the role rather than narrowing it down to something more conventional. Because this is a newly created position, you'll have real input into shaping what it becomes, including helping define what a technically grounded systems engineering path looks like at REGENT going forward. If you're the kind of person who gets energized by variety, wants to understand how mechanical, electrical, controls, and software decisions interact to shape a vehicle's performance, cost, and schedule, and is excited by the idea of helping bring Seagliders into reality from the inside, this is a role where you'll thrive. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Float Across the Program: You'll move across systems, mechanical, electrical, controls, and software work on Viceroy, going wherever the program needs help most on a given week. - Dig Into Analysis and Drawings: You'll contribute to the analysis and drawing work driving Viceroy forward during a particularly active stretch of the program. - Lead a Cross-Discipline Trade Study: By the midpoint of the term, you'll complete a trade study that touches multiple disciplines from start to finish, building a real understanding of how system-level decisions affect performance, cost, and schedule. - Build Toward Integration: You'll work toward getting an integrated subsystem running in our hardware-in-the-loop environment by the end of the term, whether that's a VCC controlling an actuator or a sensor-fused solution providing feedback. - Learn Directly From the Chief Engineer: You'll get hands-on coaching and mentorship as you navigate the breadth of the role, with someone invested in helping you connect the dots across disciplines. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Multidisciplinary Technical Grounding: You have real experience or coursework in systems, mechanical, electrical, controls, or software engineering, and ideally more than one of these. - Mechatronics Curiosity: Exposure to mechanisms or electromechanical systems is a plus and will help you move comfortably between disciplines. - Genuine Enthusiasm for Seagliders: You're drawn to the idea of reinventing coastal transportation and want to understand how a real vehicle program comes together. - Comfort With Ambiguity: You're energized rather than overwhelmed by a role without a fixed lane, and you're ready to shape your own path alongside your manager. - Clear, Confident Communication: You can communicate well across teams and disciplines, translating what you're learning into useful updates and questions. - A Strong Appetite to Learn: You're ready to be taught almost everything, and you bring the curiosity and follow-through to make the most of that. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: System Test Automation Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the System Validation Team The System Validation Team ensures the performance, reliability, and safety of Zipline’s integrated system of systems, including the Zip, Droid, and Dock. We specialize in Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing, enabling us to validate complex interactions across hardware and software before real-world deployment. Our team builds and maintains automated pipelines that rigorously test software in a simulated environment, ensuring it meets high standards before being tested in flight. By catching potential issues early and refining system behavior, we play a critical role in delivering reliable, safe, and efficient solutions that power Zipline’s mission to transform global logistics. Our team owns automation of flight testing as well to capture issues before it happens in commercial flights. The Role As a System Validation Intern, you will contribute to testing and validating Zipline’s complete system of systems—spanning the Zip, Droid, and Dock. You’ll help build and refine automated testing pipelines, ensuring that software meets rigorous quality standards before being tested in flight. Working closely with a supportive and experienced team, you’ll develop hands-on experience with cutting-edge tools and technologies while solving meaningful challenges. Your work will play an essential role in ensuring the reliability of systems that deliver life-saving goods worldwide. This role offers a unique opportunity to learn, grow, and make an impact in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment. What You'll Do Assist in executing Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) tests and flight tests to validate the interaction between Zipline’s Zip, Droid, and Dock systems. Collaborate with a wide range of engineers from different teams to build and refine automated pipelines that test software before it is deployed in flight. Design and improve tools that stress-test the system in off-nominal cases. Analyze and troubleshoot hardware and software issues uncovered during testing, contributing to system improvements. Work alongside a multidisciplinary team to design and execute system-level validation plans. Develop and enhance scripts and tools to support automated testing workflows. Learn how to ensure reliability and quality in complex, safety-critical systems, gaining valuable insights into real-world engineering challenges. What You'll Bring You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies. Master's and PhD students are also eligible. Strong understanding of engineering design fundamentals and the ability to triage and identify root causes of technical issues. Experience writing Rust or Python scripts to automate tasks or tests, either through coursework or personal projects. Hands-on experience writing Python tests using tools like Pytest or Unittest. Familiarity with creating and executing test plans or validation plans for software or hardware systems. A hands-on approach to problem-solving, including debugging and triaging technical issues. General understanding of electrical systems such as motors, sensors, cameras, and onboard computers. Experience working in a Linux environment, including using command-line tools effectively. Familiarity with tools like Git for version control, bazel for build and test management and Jira for task tracking. Basic understanding of networking concepts such as RPC or sockets. Experience working with CI tools like GitHub Actions, Buildkite, or similar. Strong attention to detail and organizational skills to document test results and track issues effectively. What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September). jobs.title: Intern, Image Analysis - Summer 2027
jobs.body: > Requisition Number: 79593 The company built on breakthroughs. ​ Join us.​ Corning is one of the world’s leading innovators in glass, ceramic, and materials science. From the depths of the ocean to the farthest reaches of space, our technologies push the boundaries of what’s possible. ​ How do we do this? With our people. They break through limitations and expectations – not once in a career, but every day. They help move our company, and the world, forward. ​ ​ At Corning, there are endless possibilities for making an impact. You can help connect the unconnected, drive the future of automobiles, transform at-home entertainment, and ensure the delivery of lifesaving medicines. And so much more.​ ​ Come break through with us. Scope of Position Deep UV (DUV) photolithography depends on glass and crystalline optics that stay highly transparent under 193 nm laser irradiation. As semiconductor features shrink, the laser power passing through these optics continues to rise. This increases the need for materials with prolonged lifetime under UV irradiation. Under these conditions, microscopic material defects can lead to surface or bulk damage. Damage shortens the lifetime of optics in semiconductor process tools, which are highly sensitive to optical performance. A successful candidate will develop an image analysis algorithm that quantifies surface damage on crystalline DUV optics after laser irradiation. The results will improve the fundamental understanding of the underlying laser induced damage mechanisms. After the benchmarking of an image analysis algorithm the candidate will then apply this to historical laser damage features to correlate to the measured laser damage threshold of critical crystalline components. Program Benefits Competitive salaries Housing assistance Travel reimbursement Intern Activities Social and networking events Volunteer opportunities Community Involvement Key Responsibilities Develop an image analysis algorithm to quantify laser-induced damage on crystalline optic surfaces. Validate the algorithm's reliability and repeatability across image sets. Apply the algorithm to historical laser damage images to generate quantitative data. Correlate extracted damage features with laser damage lifetime and laser fluence. Summarize methodology and results in a report or poster presentation. Requirements Currently pursuing a degree in Physics, Materials Science, Computer Science, or an Engineering discipline. Exposure to coding languages and familiarity with basic computation and data analysis. Must be available for 10 weeks during Summer 2027 (May-August 2027) with a graduation date of December 2027 or later Be interested in working for Corning, Inc after graduation, if presented with a full-time job opportunity. Be willing to work at the posted job location Desired Skills Basic experience in any of the following: Java, Matlab, C, C+, C#, Python, or other high level programming languages. Data analysis using Excel, JMP, Origin, or similar tools. Introductory knowledge of optics and materials science of semiconductor materials. Laboratory or Research experience. Success Measures / End-of-Term Outcomes A reliable algorithm that quantifies laser damage on optic surfaces. Quantitative data generated from the historical image set. Documented correlations between damage features and lifetime and fluence. Skills / Competencies Translates raw optical images into quantitative, repeatable measurements. Documents methods and results so others can reproduce the analysis. Interprets data trends and explains findings clearly to technical teammates. Works with engineers and scientists to refine the approach based on feedback. This position does not support immigration sponsorship. ​The range for this position is $1,635.00 - $3,185.00 biweekly. Starting pay for the successful applicant is prescribed based on geographic location, nature of position, and year in school. A job that shapes a life. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Intern - Winter
jobs.body: About fab2 The fab2 team can build anything. We design all the hardware and software needed to make chips and we make the fabs, tools, and components ourselves. We're looking for exceptional, hands-on people who can iterate to the limits of what's possible. fab2 was founded by Sam Zeloof https://www.youtube.com/@SamZeloof and Jim Keller https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Keller_(engineer). Sam is best known for making chips in his garage, and Jim has been a leader in the semiconductor industry for the past 40 years. About the role We’re hiring full-stack Mechanical Engineering Interns for the winter term. The internship begins in January, with a preferred commitment of 4 to 8 months. We’re rebuilding the chip fabrication process from the ground up, so you’ll be exposed to some really interesting and impactful work. Our engineering projects are highly interdisciplinary and span domains such as structures, optics, robotics, heat transfer, physics, and chemistry. As a startup, we offer interns a ton of ownership and mission-critical work. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience working in at least one of these areas and broad exposure across other domains. Our philosophy is to get things built and tested in days or weeks, not months. Because of this, a portfolio is required to apply: show us the things you’ve actually built! If you’ve shipped a medium-to-high complexity system through a personal project or previous internship, you’d be a good fit here. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Do you want to change how the world creates? Participate in design reviews and help solve design, engineering, and manufacturing problems. Polish your time management and communication skills to increase your effectiveness as an engineer. Build prototype components and assemblies using our in-house facilities. jobs.title: Additive Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: ADDITIVE ENGINEERING INTERN (SUMMER 2027) Freeform builds AI-native manufacturing systems that unify software, hardware, and physics to produce industrial-scale parts at the speed of human ideation.
