jobs.title: GE Vernova Pivot to Value (P2V) Value Engineering Internship 2027
jobs.body: Job Description Summary Job Description University Student Intern – Value Engineering & Steam Turbine Projects Job Description This University Student Co-Op role will be a key contributor within the Product Management function supporting the Pivot to Value (P2V) Value Engineering team. The Co-Op will play an important role in supporting initiatives that advance safety, quality, delivery, cost, and capacity objectives across GE Vernova's Steam Turbine portfolio. Working alongside Product Managers, Value Engineers, Project Leaders, and Senior Engineers, the Co-Op will support projects focused on value optimization, cost reduction, capacity increases, and implementation of standard steam turbine designs, including D600 and D650 product platforms. The successful candidate will gain hands-on experience in engineering project execution, business case development, cost tracking, capacity planning, and cross-functional collaboration across Engineering, Manufacturing, Sourcing, and Supply Chain organizations. Value Engineering is a practice focused on driving continuous value optimization and cost-out across GE Vernova's products and service offerings. Team members identify opportunities to improve processes, increase manufacturing capacity, reduce costs, and enhance product quality while ensuring customer and business requirements are met. The Co-Op will contribute to these efforts through data analysis, project coordination, and engineering support activities. Roles and Responsibilities Support Value Engineering initiatives focused on Steam Turbines, specifically D600 and D650 standard engine design implementation and capacity expansion projects. Assist Senior Engineers with engineering analyses, design reviews, documentation, and implementation activities related to standard steam turbine products. Track project schedules, milestones, risks, action items, and value realization metrics for ongoing Value Engineering projects. Support cost tracking and reporting for engineering and manufacturing improvement initiatives. Collect, organize, and analyze technical, operational, and financial data to support project business cases and decision-making. Collaborate with Engineering, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Supply Chain, and Product Management teams to identify opportunities for cost, quality, and capacity improvements. Assist in the development of presentations, project updates, and executive-level summaries. Participate in value engineering workshops, brainstorming sessions, and continuous improvement activities. Support manufacturing process improvement initiatives aimed at increasing capacity and reducing cycle time. Learn and apply Value Engineering methodologies, project management fundamentals, and cost optimization techniques. Assist with maintaining project documentation, issue tracking, and lessons learned repositories. Support the development and implementation of standardized tools, templates, and reporting methods for Value Engineering projects. Help identify and quantify opportunities for productivity improvements, cost reduction, and value creation across the Steam Turbine product portfolio. Required Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in: Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Engineering Technology, Operations Management, Supply Chain Management, Business Analytics, Or a related technical discipline Minimum sophomore standing with at least one academic term remaining following the Co-Op assignment. Demonstrated academic success with a strong interest in engineering, manufacturing, product management, or project management. Ability to work full-time during the Co-Op assignment period. Desired Characteristics Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Interest in power generation equipment, manufacturing, or heavy industrial products. Excellent organizational skills with attention to detail. Ability to manage multiple assignments and priorities in a collaborative environment. Strong communication and presentation skills. Experience with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and data analysis tools. Familiarity with project management principles and tools. Basic understanding of engineering drawings, manufacturing processes, or product design concepts. Demonstrated ability to work effectively within cross-functional teams. Curiosity, initiative, and a desire to learn from experienced engineers and business leaders. Interest in cost analysis, business case development, continuous improvement, and operational excellence. Knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement methodologies is a plus. What You Will Gain Exposure to GE Vernova's Steam Turbine product portfolio and Value Engineering methodologies. Hands-on experience supporting D600 and D650 steam turbine design implementation projects. Practical project management and cost tracking experience on real business initiatives. Opportunity to collaborate with experienced engineers, product managers, sourcing leaders, and manufacturing experts. Experience developing business cases and supporting strategic capacity increase initiatives. A deeper understanding of engineering, manufacturing, and commercial decision-making within the power generation industry. This position offers a unique opportunity for students to gain meaningful experience at the intersection of engineering, product management, manufacturing, and business operations while contributing to initiatives that improve product value, manufacturing capacity, and customer outcomes. The pay range for this position is $1,000-$2,000 USD weekly. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. jobs.title: GE Vernova Investment Casting Manufacturing Internship – 2027
jobs.body: Job Description Summary Addressing the climate crisis is an urgent global priority, and at GE Vernova, we take our responsibility seriously. We continuously challenge our thinking and are empowered to dream big and take smart risks. Analyze process data, quality results, and production trends to identify variation, recurring defects, and improvement opportunities. Develop and update process-control plans, standard work, visual controls, work instructions, and technical documentation. Apply Built-in Quality principles by helping define defect-prevention methods, in-process checks, reaction plans, and error-proofing solutions. Create or revise CAD models and drawings for tooling, fixtures, gauges, robot end-of-arm tooling, and other manufacturing aids. Assist with robotics and automation projects, including concept development, testing, troubleshooting, documentation, and safe implementation. Plan and execute supervised engineering trials, collect results, and communicate recommendations based on data and shop-floor observations. Participate in root-cause analysis and corrective-action activities using structured problem-solving tools. · Collaborate with operators and cross-functional teams to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and process capability. What you'll bring (Basic Qualifications) Current enrollment in an accredited bachelor’s or master’s degree program in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Robotics, Automation, or a related technical field. Basic proficiency with 2D or 3D CAD software, demonstrated through coursework, projects, or prior experience. jobs.title: Engineering Intern, Wireless Automation and Test (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Who We Are HP IQ is HP’s new AI innovation lab. Combining startup agility with HP’s global scale, we’re building intelligent technologies that redefine how the world works, creates, and collaborates. We’re assembling a diverse, world-class team—engineers, designers, researchers, and product minds—focused on creating an intelligent ecosystem across HP’s portfolio. Together, we’re developing intuitive, adaptive solutions that spark creativity, boost productivity, and make collaboration seamless. We create breakthrough solutions that make complex tasks feel effortless, teamwork more natural, and ideas more impactful—always with a human-centric mindset. By embedding AI advancements into every HP product and service, we’re expanding what’s possible for individuals, organisations, and the future of work. Join us as we reinvent work, so people everywhere can do their best work. About The Role HP IQ's Wireless Automation and Test team is responsible for validating and characterizing wireless subsystems across all HP IQ products and services. This role focuses on ensuring that wireless applications communicate properly with underlying wireless subsystems, conducting quality assurance on wireless software, and establishing testing and characterization platforms for current products and next-generation systems. As a Wireless Automation and Test Engineering Intern, you will work at the intersection of hardware, software, and data analytics, directly contributing to product validation and shipping readiness. What You Might Do Depending on your background and interests, you may pursue work across three technical layers: Data Analytics: You will develop automated processes to compile and clean up test data from multiple test environments, develop a portal where the data can be represented clearly and on-demand, formulate mathematical models that flag performance changes and trends , and support data-driven analysis of wireless performance. Software : You will support software testing by analyzing logs, validating system decisions, identifying timing issues between networking events, validating full-stack protocol behavior, and helping ensure wireless software components communicate correctly. You may also work with networking protocols such as HTTP and TCP/IP, and contribute to log parsing automation. Hardware : You will use lab equipment such as spectrum analyzers, oscilloscopes, power meters, and network analyzers to measure wireless hardware performance, characterize RF behavior, and help automate measurements through scripting. Essential Qualifications Must be a current student pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field. Strong foundational knowledge in at least one of the following: wireless fundamentals and RF concepts, networking protocols (HTTP, TCP/IP), or statistical analysis and data science. Demonstrated ability to debug systems, analyze data, or troubleshoot problems in academic or hobby projects. Comfort working in a fast-paced environment and willingness to learn specialized wireless testing tools and methodologies. Ability to communicate clearly with team members and adjust work priorities when team needs shift. Self-directed learner capable of working independently on defined tasks while seeking help appropriately from team members. Preferred Skills Hands-on experience with laboratory instrumentation such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, or power meters. Experience with low-level scripting or basic automation (Python, Bash, Powershell, or similar languages) for test automation or data processing. Familiarity with network protocol standards and troubleshooting networking issues. Previous experience parsing or analyzing log files from complex systems. Exposure to agentic systems, autonomous agents, or machine learning applications in testing or validation contexts. Experience in product validation, quality assurance, or testing in hardware or embedded systems environments. Hourly Pay Range: $40.00–$50.00 per hour. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as skills, qualifications, and experience. Internship Dates : May/June – August/September (exact start and end dates will depend on candidate availability). Final salary offered is based upon multiple factors including individual job-related qualifications, education, experience, knowledge and skills. At HP IQ, we offer a competitive and comprehensive benefits package, including: Health insurance Dental insurance Vision insurance Long term/short term disability insurance Employee assistance program Flexible spending account Life insurance Generous time off policies, including; 4-12 weeks fully paid parental leave based on tenure 11 paid holidays Additional flexible paid vacation and sick leave ( US benefits overview ) Why HP IQ? HP IQ is HP’s new AI innovation lab, building the intelligence to empower humanity—reimagining how we work, create, and connect to shape the future of work. Innovative Work Help shape the future of intelligent computing and workplace transformation. Autonomy and Agility Work with the speed and focus of a startup, backed by HP’s scale. Meaningful Impact Build AI-powered solutions that help people and organisations thrive. Flexible Work Environment Freedom and flexibility to do your best work. jobs.title: Research Intern - Foundational Models & Agent
jobs.body: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The Microsoft Applied Sciences Group incubates disruptive technologies for Microsoft’s next-generation hardware products. The group is working on projects that will shape how computers and other devices perceive the user and the user's environment. Operating like a startup within Microsoft, the team works closely with research and product teams to bring compelling new experiences to market. Many of these experiences are powered by machine learning, giving you the chance to contribute to nearly every stage of a project, from ideation through shipping, and make an impact at Microsoft scale. As a Research Intern, you will have the opportunity to design and lead the implementation of state-of-the-art language and multimodal models to transform the Windows experience. You will collaborate with experts across the organization and help turn promising ideas into products with real-world impact. This is a hands-on role. Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Doctoral Degree program in Computer Science or a related STEM field. Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. Preferred Qualifications At least 2 years of experience conducting research as part of a research program in academic or industry setting in the area of Large Language Models (LLMs), multimodal models, agents and/or reinforcement learning. Passion for incubating new ideas, solving problems, and building working prototypes. Experience training and/or finetuning large language models, model compression, distillation to small language models. Experience with Python and deep learning libraries. Desire to learn to create reusable software libraries and packages. Experience using dataset curation, data generation using prompting state of art LLMs and/or model alignment. Experience with reinforcement learning libraries or formal methods and verification is a plus. Experience of scientific writing in top-tier conferences or journals (ICLR, ACL, EMLP, ICML, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, TPAMI, etc.). The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: https://careers.microsoft.com/us/en/us-intern-pay Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April). This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. This team owns all hardware between the tanks and engine, and you’ll help design, build, test, analyze, and maybe even fly critical hardware. Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. jobs.title: Summer 2027 Internship - Mechanical Engineering - California
jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will: ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting​ Implement new ideas, be constantly challenged, and develop your skills​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions.​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward.​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts.​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives.​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships.​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​As a Mechanical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams: Research & Development New Product Development R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products. They research new technologies, customer expectations, business requirements and regulations. They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts. These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production. Product Engineering R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies, customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products. Test Lab Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that we get to be the Mythbusters of our division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, we are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you! Majors Targeted: Mechanical Engineering, or related majors $20 min hourly wage – $35 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship.​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above (verified at time of hire) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future.​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment. jobs.title: Vehicle Integration & Test Internship - Summer 2027
jobs.body: About Varda Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses. From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind. Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital. Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL. Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem. About This Role Summer internships will range between the months of May and August. All dates dependent upon the university schedule of the selected students. Internships are full-time and on-site in Los Angeles, CA. To be considered for this internship, candidates must be actively enrolled in an accredited undergraduate or graduate degree program. The Vehicle Integration & Test team at Varda is responsible for the assembly, integration, and verification of our spacecraft and reentry systems. Interns on this team play a critical role in bridging the gap between design and flight, gaining hands-on experience with flight hardware, test operations, and real-time problem solving. Whether you're building test equipment, assembling mechanical systems, or running spacecraft-level checks, you’ll be directly contributing to mission success. Internships at Varda are optimal for students looking to grow technically and professionally while working on impactful projects critical to the company’s success. You will be working on a collaborative team in a startup environment while being able to learn from some of most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the world. We’re dedicated to providing an experience that will let your decisions and contributions help drive Varda’s success. Responsibilities Own or contribute to hardware or software design to support development of Spacecraft or payload Develop and support system test campaigns Perform necessary analysis to support development and verification efforts Basic Qualifications Hands-on experience in any engineering discipline Modeling/Assembly CAD experience Preferred Skills And Experience Previous internship or co-op experience Previous experience on technical project teams (i.e. Rocket club, formula SAE, etc.) Python Candidate Profiles Successful candidates often fall into one of the following technical profiles , though responsibilities may overlap depending on project needs. Avionics / Electrical Systems Develop and interpret wiring schematics and harnessing Support spacecraft electrical integration Assist with avionics hardware testing and troubleshooting Propulsion / Ground Test Engineering Support propulsion system build and operation Design ground support equipment (GSE) and develop propulsion test plans Assist in executing and documenting hardware test campaigns Software / Test Automation Develop Python-based tools and user interfaces for test operations Support test automation and data collection systems Build software utilities to improve hardware testing workflows Projects You May Work On Intern projects will be tailored to company needs and student skillsets closer to the start date. Typical projects include: Procedure generation to build and test spacecraft Ground Support Equipment (GSE) design Test development and execution Flight hardware upgrades and modifications Automating vehicle testing and data review Compensation Hourly Rate : $33.00 Housing stipend for interns relocating to the area Commuter benefit to support local transportation Benefits for Interns Health & Wellness Paid observed holidays 100% company-paid Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance plans for employees and dependents with FSA and employer-matched HSA options $120/month wellness reimbursement for gym and fitness expenses Sponsored One Medical memberships for employees and their dependents Financial $20/pay period cell phone reimbursement Up to $4,000 gross up in relocation support, if eligible Up to $850 commute credit through Lyft or car rental reimbursement, if eligible Workplace Experience & Perks Fully stocked kitchen with lunch provided daily and dinner provided twice weekly Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and mission-success celebrations Complimentary EV charging ITAR Requirements Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license. “US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum). jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer - Summer Internship 2027
jobs.body: Advanced Reentry Technologies Who We Are: Inversion is an aerospace and defense company pioneering advanced reentry technology to enable next-generation capabilities from space. By combining high-performance materials, precision aerodynamics, and mission-driven autonomy, Inversion is transforming reentry into an operational capability for an entirely new class of missions. The company’s highly maneuverable reentry spacecraft, Arc, is designed for rapid global cargo delivery, hypersonic testing, and other national security missions that require precise, controlled flight through the atmosphere. Arc creates an entirely new transportation domain, unlocking unprecedented speed and global reach. Headquartered in Los Angeles, Inversion designs, manufactures, and integrates its spacecraft under one roof, enabling the company to move rapidly from concept to flight. The company is backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, Spark Capital, and Lockheed Martin Ventures, with customers across the U.S. government and commercial space industry. Position Overview: As a Manufacturing Engineer Inten at Inversion, you will report directly to the Manager of Arc Vehicle Integration & Test. In this role, you will build, integrate, and test critical subsystems for our Arc hypersonic reentry vehicle. You will support the transition of designs from the engineering team to the integration floor, develop and improve exsiting build sequences, assembly procedures, and floor tooling. You will work cross-functionally with design engineers and floor technicians to execute physical integration, troubleshoot hardware anomalies in real-time, and ensure flight hardware meets strict quality and schedule milestones. Key Responsibilities Assist in developing, documenting, and improving manufacturing and assembly processes for complex mechanical and electromechanical systems. Create and maintain manufacturing work instructions, process documentation, and assembly procedures. Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing efficiency, quality, safety, and repeatability. Collaborate with Design Engineering to review component and assembly designs for manufacturability, assembly, and serviceability. Participate in design reviews and provide feedback on manufacturing constraints, tooling requirements, and assembly considerations. Support the transition of engineering designs into executable manufacturing processes. Work directly with manufacturing technicians and engineers to support hardware assembly, integration, and troubleshooting. Assist in identifying root causes of manufacturing issues and implementing corrective actions. Collect and analyze manufacturing data to identify process improvements and support engineering decisions. Design, build, and proof-load assembly fixtures, tooling, and ground support equipment (GSE) using CAD. Required Qualifications Rising Senior in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or equivalent technical experience. Experience authoring detailed assembly procedures, managing build configurations, and driving floor execution. Experience designing tooling, fixtures, or GSE in CAD (Siemens NX or equivalent) and applying standard GD&T per ASME Y14.5. Demonstrated excellent verbal and written communication skills. Desired Qualifications Experience with spacecraft, launch vehicle, or high-reliability aerospace hardware assembly. Experience with aerospace cleaning, bonding preparations, and cleanroom operations. Familiarity with high-pressure fluid systems, pyrotechnics installation, or flight avionics harnessing integration. Familiarity with Thermal Protection System (TPS) manufacturing processes. Our office headquarters is located in Playa Vista, CA. This position requires in office presence for the duration of the internship. jobs.title: Research Intern - Next-Generation AI Agents
jobs.body: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. Join M365 Research and contribute to build the next generation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents that take on long-running work, remember what matters, and get better with experience. Our team drives applied research that reimagines how agentic systems are built, evaluated, and deployed at enterprise scale, and we transfer these advances into Microsoft products. We closely collaborate with multiple research teams and product groups across the globe, and we communicate our research through peer-reviewed publications, open-source releases, blog posts, patents, and industry conferences. Our topics of interest include: Agent memory and skills: building and maintaining memory, context, and reusable skills so long-running agents stay current and get better with experience. Reliable, self-improving agents: diagnosing failures in long agent trajectories, improving agents without regressions, and evaluating them in realistic simulated environments. Proactive, long-horizon agents: planning, multi-agent coordination, and self-monitoring for agents that work over extended periods. Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related STEM field. Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. Preferred Qualifications At least 1 year of experience in conducting research and authoring peer-reviewed publications. Experience in machine learning, NLP, or related AI areas such as LLMs and AI agents. Hands-on experience with agent memory, skill or tool learning, RL or post-training, agent evaluation, self-improvement, planning, or multi-agent systems. Demonstrated coding skills, including building agent systems and rapid prototyping with AI coding agents. Proficient written and verbal communication skills. Ability to collaborate across research and product teams and apply research to real-world problems. Publications in top venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, COLM, AAAI, IJCAI, KDD, or SIGIR. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: https://careers.microsoft.com/us/en/us-intern-pay Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April). This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Environmental Test Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About the role Summer internships will range between the months of May and September depending on university schedules. Internship is full-time and on-site in San Jose, California. The Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT) team at Muon is responsible for validating spacecraft hardware through unit acceptance testing as well as spacecraft-level integration and environmental testing. As an Environmental Test Engineering Intern, you will support the planning, setup, execution, and analysis of environmental tests used to validate spacecraft hardware against the extreme conditions of launch and space. You will work alongside experienced environmental test engineers, test engineers, and technicians to prepare hardware and test equipment, develop and execute test procedures, collect and analyze test data, and troubleshoot test issues. This is a hands-on opportunity to gain experience with spacecraft environmental testing and see your work directly contribute to the successful integration and launch of Muon spacecraft. Muon is a small and fast growing startup which offers interns the experience to get direct mentorship and have real impact on our programs. As an intern, you'll collaborate with a dynamic team in a startup environment and have the chance to learn from some of the most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the industry. We're committed to offering an experience where your decisions and contributions play a pivotal role in driving Muon's success. Responsibilities Assist environmental test engineers with the planning, preparation, and execution of spacecraft and subsystem environmental testing, including thermal vacuum, vibration, acoustic, and other qualification or acceptance testing. Support test setup and instrumentation, including thermocouples, accelerometers, pressure sensors, and other test measurement equipment. Assist with preparing spacecraft hardware, fixtures, ground support equipment, and test configurations for environmental test campaigns. Execute functional checkouts and test procedures under engineer supervision before, during, and after environmental testing. Monitor test operations and hardware performance, identify anomalies, and support troubleshooting and root-cause investigations. Collect, process, and perform preliminary analysis of environmental test data to verify hardware performance and test requirements. Support development and improvement of test procedures, test processes, checklists, and laboratory workflows. Assist with configuration and operation of environmental test equipment and data acquisition systems. Support automation and scripting efforts to improve environmental test setup, monitoring, data collection, and analysis. Generate test documentation, data summaries, and reports under the guidance of environmental test engineers. Support integration and handling of spacecraft hardware and ground support equipment in cleanroom, laboratory, and environmental test facilities. Help maintain a safe, organized, and flight-hardware-ready test environment. Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field. Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals, particularly in areas such as mechanics, thermal systems, dynamics, instrumentation, or electrical systems. Demonstrated interest in spacecraft environmental testing, laboratory testing, or hardware development. Experience with a programming or scripting language for data analysis or test automation, such as Python, MATLAB/Simulink, Julia, or C++. Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to approach complex technical challenges from a first-principles perspective. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with an ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment. Ability and willingness to work hands-on with engineering hardware and test equipment. Nice-to-have Skills Previous internship, co-op, research, or laboratory experience involving hardware testing. Experience with thermal vacuum, vibration, acoustic, shock, or other environmental testing. Experience with data acquisition systems, instrumentation, sensors, or test equipment. Experience developing test procedures, test plans, or test reports. Experience with accelerometers, thermocouples, pressure transducers, strain gauges, or similar instrumentation. Experience with Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or other tools used for test automation and data analysis. Previous experience on technical project teams such as a CubeSat, rocketry, Formula SAE, Solar Car, or other hardware-focused engineering project. Familiarity with spacecraft systems or subsystems and environmental test requirements. Experience with hardware integration, troubleshooting, or hardware-in-the-loop testing. Pay range Bachelor's students $40/hour Master's $45/hour PhD $50/hour About Muon Space Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world. Taking Care of Our Team At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave. Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too. Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. We value diversity in the workplace, and that starts with our applicants. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes, and we look forward to reviewing your application! In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know. Muon is currently registered and able to hire in the following states: AL, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, FL, GA, IL, IA, ID, MD, MA, MI, MN, MO, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, TN, TX, VT, VA, WA ITAR/EAR Requirements This position requires access to export controlled information. jobs.title: Autonomy Engineer Intern, Simulation & Robotics, 2027 (HQ)
jobs.body: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions. ABOUT THE ROLE: The core of our system is the computer vision algorithms that allow drones to understand the world around them. You will architect and implement the algorithms that run on every drone powered by Skydio as part of a world class computer vision and deep learning team with researchers who have pushed the state of the art in academia and industry. As a Research Intern, you will be paired up with one or more members of our core software development team, assuming direct ownership of a project that meaningfully advances the capabilities of our team and products. If you have a strong foundation in math, theory, and software development and you are interested in directly contributing to the development of the next generation of autonomy algorithms and pushing them into real products, we would love to hear from you. AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY: - Core Simulator Architecture: Design, implement, and evolve the foundational architecture of the Skydio Simulator, ensuring it scales across vehicle types, environments, and use cases. - Physics and Dynamics: Improve and extend physics models governing vehicle motion, interactions with the environment, and dynamic agents. - Sensor and Hardware Simulation: Build high-fidelity simulations of cameras, IMUs, and other onboard components, including timing, noise characteristics, and hardware behavior. - Autonomy Stack Integration: Run and validate the full Skydio autonomy stack in simulation, ensuring consistency between simulated and real-world behavior. - Feature Development on Top of the Core: Implement simulator capabilities that unlock new workflows for customers and internal autonomy engineers, from training scenarios to advanced testing modes. - Performance and Fidelity: Profile, optimize, and improve simulator performance while continuously pushing realism and accuracy. WHAT YOU’LL DO: - Develop core simulator components in C++ and Python, working close to real-time constraints. - Collaborate with autonomy, perception, and controls engineers to align simulation behavior with real-world systems. - Debug complex interactions between physics, sensors, autonomy logic, and rendering. - Help shape the long-term technical direction of the simulator as both a product and an internal platform. - Contribute to documentation and shared understanding of how the simulator works internally. QUALIFICATIONS: - Strong software engineering experience with C++ and Python. - Experience building complex systems where performance, determinism, or correctness matter. - Comfort reasoning about time-synchronized systems, state machines, or real-time execution. - Ability to work in a large, evolving codebase with multiple stakeholders. - Interest in robotics, simulation, or physical systems (prior robotics experience is a plus, not a requirement). BONUS EXPERIENCE: - Robotics, simulation, game engines, or real-time systems. - Physics engines, sensor modeling, or hardware abstraction layers. - Multithreaded or low-latency system design. - Experience debugging systems that span software and physical behavior. Compensation: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Masters, and $70/hr for PhD students*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. Product Engineering R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies , customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products. Test Lab Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that we get to be the Mythbusters of our division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, we are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you! jobs.title: Test Engineering Intern - Space Technologies
jobs.body: Worker Type Supplemental Job Description Test Engineering Intern - Space Technologies Our paid Summer Internship Program is designed to provide students with an immersive, hands-on experience within the aerospace and defense industry. Interns work alongside AV team members on meaningful projects involving cutting-edge technology while developing professional relationships, strategic problem-solving skills, and practical experience in a full-time work environment. This is a 12-week, onsite program intended for highly motivated and passionate students who are currently enrolled in college or are recent graduates. Applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA, with a preference for students at the junior level or above. Our program has been recognized by Yello and WayUp as one of the Top 100 Internship Programs in the United States for multiple years. Depending on the team and location, students who are willing to relocate for their internship may be eligible for a relocation and housing reimbursement stipend. Job Description AV provides a full suite of space-qualified hardware trusted to operate in the extreme environments of GEO, MEO, LEO, and cislunar orbits. With hundreds of systems currently flying in space, AV delivers reliable solutions for missions where failure is not an option. As a Test Engineer Intern within AV's Space Technologies organization, you will work alongside experienced electrical, systems, mechanical, firmware, software, and test engineers to support the development, integration, and verification of spacecraft hardware. You will gain hands-on experience designing and troubleshooting test setups, developing test automation, operating laboratory instrumentation, executing tests, and analyzing data for space-qualified electronics, sensors, and subsystems. This internship provides an opportunity to apply your academic knowledge to real-world space systems while contributing to innovative capabilities in areas such as laser communications, space electronics, sensors, and advanced spacecraft technologies. You will be part of a dynamic team working to help deliver the next generation of high-reliability space solutions. This is an exciting opportunity to apply your academic training in a high-tech, fast-paced environment while working alongside experienced engineers and mentors. Essential Functions ·Assist in designing, integrating, and troubleshooting automated test equipment for spacecraft electrical systems, CCAs, embedded electronics, and subsystems. ·Develop and maintain test scripts, equipment-control software, data-acquisition tools, using Python, LabVIEW, MATLAB, or comparable software. ·Support the creation and execution of functional, performance, integration, qualification, acceptance, and environmental tests for spacecraft hardware. ·Build, modify, and verify electrical test setups, harnesses, fixtures, simulators, and interface test equipment. ·Use oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, electronic loads, logic analyzers, and data-acquisition equipment to troubleshoot and validate hardware. ·Assist with testing and troubleshooting spacecraft communication interfaces and protocols, including SPI, RS-422, LVDS, SpaceWire, or MIL-STD-1553. ·Support hardware bring-up, subsystem integration, test station calibration, configuration control, and hardware-in-the-loop or software-in-the-loop activities. ·Collaborate with electrical, systems, mechanical, software, manufacturing, quality, and operations teams in laboratory, cleanroom, and other controlled test environments Basic Qualifications ·Entering senior year Fall of 2027 ·Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related field. ·Coursework or project experience in circuits, electronics, embedded systems, controls, or programming. ·Basic programming or scripting experience with Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or a comparable language. ·Familiarity with electrical communication protocols such as SPI, RS-422, LVDS, SpaceWire, or MIL-STD-1553. ·Experience using laboratory test equipment, such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, electronic loads, or logic analyzers. ·Strong analytical, troubleshooting, communication, and teamwork skills Preferred Qualifications and Competencies ·Hands-on experience building, testing, debugging, or modifying electronic hardware, CCAs, harnesses, fixtures, or test assemblies. ·Experience developing test automation scripts, equipment-control software, data-acquisition tools, or data-analysis utilities. ·Familiarity with automated test equipment, system test equipment, hardware-in-the-loop, software-in-the-loop, or spacecraft subsystem integration. ·Experience with SpaceWire or MIL-STD-1553 interfaces, bus analyzers, protocol analyzers, simulators, or traffic-generation tools. ·Familiarity with Git, version control, issue tracking, configuration management, or software development practices. Clearance Level No Clearance The salary range for this role is: AeroVironment considers several factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to, the location, the role and associated responsibilities, a candidate’s work experience, education/training, and key skills. In order to comply with the requirements of the ITAR and/or the EAR, applicants must qualify as a U.S. person under the ITAR and the EAR, or a person to be approved for an export license by the governing agency whose technology comes under its jurisdiction. Benefits : AV offers an excellent benefits package including medical, dental vision, 401K with company matching, a 9/80 work schedule and a paid holiday shutdown. For more information about our company benefit offerings please visit: http://www.avinc.com/myavbenefits . We also encourage you to review our company website at http://www.avinc.com to learn more about us. Principals only need apply. NO agencies please. About AV: AV isn’t for everyone. We hire the curious, the relentless, the mission-obsessed. The best of the best. We don’t just build defense technology—we redefine what’s possible. As the premier autonomous systems company in the U.S., AV delivers breakthrough capabilities across air, land, sea, space, and cyber. From AI-powered drones and loitering munitions to integrated autonomy and space resilience, our technologies shape the future of warfare and protect those who serve. Founded by legendary innovator Dr. Paul MacCready, AV has spent over 50 years pushing the boundaries of what unmanned systems can do. Our heritage includes seven platforms in the Smithsonian—but we’re not building history, we’re building what’s next. If you're ready to build technology that matters—with speed, scale, and purpose—there’s no better place to do it than AV. Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information. To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind: No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links. jobs.title: Manufacturing Test Development Co-op
jobs.body: JOB DESCRIPTION Co-op Cycle: Jan 1st to July 2nd Schedule: Monday- Friday 8: 00 am to 4: 3 0pm Location: Beverly, MA (Onsite ) * To support students commuting to our Beverly, MA facility, we offer a travel stipend . See the Commute section below. Ready to turn what you’re learning in the classroom into real -world impact? Axcelis is a global leader in ion implantation and semiconductor technology. Our co ‑ ops don ’ t just observe — they contribute . For more than four decades, we ’ ve been driving innovation in semiconductor manufacturing technology, working with the world ’ s leading chipmakers to power everything from smartphones to electric vehicles. As a co ‑ op, you ’ ll gain hands ‑ on experience , learn from industry experts, and make a real impact on projects that shape the future of technology . We are searching for o ur next group of engineering co-ops for a 6-month assignment at our Beverly, MA , facility. Our co -op program is designed to develop early career talent and build a strong pipeline of future engineers . Students gain hands-on exposure , work on real projects , and make meaningful contributions . Throughout the program, co -ops build technical skills , strengthen problem- solving abilities , and gain real -world experience that enhances both their academic learning and future career opportunities. About the Role As a Manufacturing Test Development Engineer Co-op , you will gain hands-on experience designing, developing, and supporting test equipment used in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to help ensure products meet quality, performance, and reliability standards. This role provides exposure to real-world engineering challenges, including the design, development, and validation of electrical and mechanical test solutions, fixture design, and hardware-level debugging of test systems. Through this experience, you will develop practical engineering skills, learn how testing integrates into large-scale manufacturing, and contribute directly to improving efficiency and product quality. What You’ll Do Design, develop, build, validate , and maintain electrical and mechanical manufacturing test solutions, including automated test equipment and custom test fixtures Leverage manual, subtractive, and additive manufacturing tools and techniques to meet fixture design and performance requirements C ollaborate with teammates across engineering disciplines, relying on their diverse skill sets to accomplish shared project goals Analyze test data to identify failure modes, root causes, and process variations Perform hardware-level debugging of test systems, including instrumentation and interfaces Collaborate with manufacturing, design, process, and quality engineering teams to meet fixture design requirements of all shareholders Create and maintain detailed test documentation, procedures, and reports Support continuous improvement initiatives to increase test coverage, throughput, and repeatability What We’re Looking For Applicants must be candidates for a Bachelor of Science degree in any of the following fields: Electrical, Computer Engineering, Mechanical, Manufacturing Engineering or similar programs. Familiarity with modeling software such as SolidWorks /Creo or AutoCAD Familiarity with schematic and PCB design tools such as Altium, KiCad , QElectroTech Familiarity with fabrication tools such as calipers, hand tools, 3d printing, etc. Familiarity with measurement tools and equipment such as DMM’s, Oscilloscopes, Data acquisition systems (DAQ), etc. Experience with project management tools such as Gantt charts, Microsoft Project/Planner, etc . Why Choose Axcelis for Your Co - op? Meaningful Work – Work on real projects that make a direct impact on our products, processes, and customers Leadership That Knows Your Name – Senior leaders are invested in our co-ops’ growth and regularly engage with students throughout their assignment. Mentorship – Co-ops are matched with an experienced mentor to help them navigate the company, build connections, and succeed in their role. Engaging Co - op Experience : Enjoy off-site co - op events, weekly c o - op m eetups, and company-hosted luncheons that help you learn, network, and feel part of the Axcelis team. Commute Information: To support students commuting to our facility, Axcelis provides a $1,000 travel stipend , paid as a lump- sum in the first paycheck . Our headquarters in Beverly, MA , is located directly off Route 128 and just 10 minutes from the Beverly Train Station for those using public transportation. How to Apply: Please apply for this position through the Axcelis Careers Page . EQUAL OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT It is the policy of Axcelis to provide equal opportunity in all areas of employment for all persons free from discrimination based on race, sex, religion, age, color, national origin, disability status, medical condition (including pregnancy), veteran status, sexual orientation, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. U.S. BASE SALARY RANGE $20.42 - $35.70 This base salary range reflects the typical compensation for this role across U.S. locations. jobs.title: Electro-Mechanical Instrument Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Overview: Draper is an independent, nonprofit research and development company headquartered in Cambridge, MA. The 2,000+ employees of Draper tackle important national challenges with a promise of delivering successful and usable solutions. From military defense and space exploration to biomedical engineering, lives often depend on the solutions we provide. Our multidisciplinary teams of engineers and scientists work in a collaborative environment that inspires the cross-fertilization of ideas necessary for true innovation. For more information about Draper, visit www.draper.com . Job Description Summary: Electro-Mechanical Instrument Student Co-op or Intern at Draper will primarily support the research and development of precision inertial guidance instruments for existing customers. It is expected that interns will contribute to projects that include electro-mechanical design, thermal model development, magnetics design, materials testing, hardware assembly, test, and debug. Specific projects include but are not limited to: instrument component design using CAD and FEA tools, collaboration with Draper’s prototype machine shop to determine machinability of components, working closely with Draper technicians to build and test hardware, coordinating with Draper’s Center for Additive Manufacturing to produce 3D printed parts. Students will work with 3D modelling software packages such as CREO and SolidWorks and analysis software such as ANSYS or COMSOL, and possibly LabVIEW and MATLAB for various applications. DURATION: This position will the summer of 2027, dates TBD. QUALIFICATIONS: Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering or Applied Physics (or similar) student with a minimum of a 3.0 GPA, and hands-on experience required. Experience with mechanical design using CREO or Solid Works preferred. Intuitive understanding of the physical universe is mandatory. Additional desirable experience: Design, precision mechanics, magnetics, thermal control, electro-mechanical, fluids, circuit theory, machine shop interaction, technical assembly, Excel, LabVIEW, MATLAB, MCAD. * Due to the nature of the work at Draper, US Citizenship status is required. Draper is unable to sponsor or hire individuals holding H1B or Student Visas. Dual-citizens are unable to be accepted for this position. jobs.title: Rotating Equipment Engineer Co-Op / Operations Intern
jobs.body: Flowserve is a global manufacturer of pumps, valves, seals, and aftermarket services, delivering comprehensive flow control solutions that support essential industries such as energy, clean water, and pharmaceuticals. If you're looking for a culture built on ingenuity, innovation, and excellence, Flowserve offers the opportunity to put your experience in motion. Whether you're an individual contributor or a people leader, you'll find meaningful opportunities for professional growth, competitive rewards, and a workplace grounded in our core values: People, Safety, Integrity, Ownership and Ingenuity. At Flowserve, we're inspired by what we can achieve together—creating extraordinary flow control solutions that strengthen today's world while building tomorrow. Flowserve is currently hiring for an Engineering Co-op / Operations Intern for our West Chicago, IL facility. The ideal candidate will be an individual who shows interest in learning and innovation, enjoys being challenged, and who will add value to the Operations team. This person will gain an introduction into the fast-paced rotating equipment repair industry by performing the responibilities listed below. Potential Responsibilities: Assist with order acquisition and fulfillment, especially related to maintaining a positive customer experience. Support manufacturing team on projects related to cost reduction and process improvement. Work with regional operations leadership to develop standardization initiatives. Acquire basic knowledge of pump and mechanical seal fundamentals to support Flowserve activities. Research and collect serial number-specific equipment information per customer requirements. Create technical customer-facing final job reports and as-found condition reports. Document and update records and drawings related to upgrades of customer equipment. Other duties as assigned. Required Qualifications & Skills: Actively pursuing a degree in Engineering, Mechatronics, Manufacturing, Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Engineering Technology, or related curriculum. Must be in good standing. Proficient in basic computer skills, including Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office programs. Willingness to learn and to stay focused on the task at hand. Good communication skills. Ability to work in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment. Strong work ethic with positive attitude. Experience in manufacturing shop environment is a plus. Skilled in SolidWorks is a plus.

jobs.title: Student for Integration MDE engineering
jobs.body: To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology. Group/Division KLA has manufacturing sites worldwide. The Global Operations (GOPS) team, comprised of Manufacturing, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing Engineering, Installation and Quality, builds our leading-edge technology. GOPS partners with KLA's global supply base and design engineering teams to develop new products, working continuously to build better, faster and more cost-efficient solutions. What You'll Do In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise. The NPI Integration Student Engineer supports development, zero-series production, and manufacturing readiness activities by helping integrate mechanical, motion-control, electronics, optics/scanner, and software subsystems into complete working products. The position provides hands-on exposure to system-level integration, validation, troubleshooting, and manufacturing support while working alongside experienced engineers. The role offers a unique opportunity to learn how complex multidisciplinary systems achieve performance targets, stability, quality, and production readiness. The role includes: Supporting integration and validation of multidisciplinary systems including mechanics, motion-control, optics/scanners, electronics, and software. Assisting with system bring-up, integration, testing, and performance validation during prototype, zero-series, and NPI phases. Supporting root-cause investigations of system-level integration, electrical, and motion-control issues observed during development and production. Helping design, build, and maintain validation setups, test benches, jigs, and troubleshooting tools. Collecting, organizing, and analyzing engineering data to support performance improvement and quality initiatives. Supporting preparation of integration documentation, Mfg flows (eQuality system), procedures, engineering files, and manufacturing instructions. Assisting with engineering changes, BOM reviews, cabling documentation, and production readiness activities. Working closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, suppliers, and external partners on technical assignments. Supporting design reviews, validation activities, and product transfer toward high-volume manufacturing. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s or Master’s student in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Automation, Control Engineering, Robotics, Embedded Systems, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field. Electrical qualifications, vocational electrical training, or electrical authorizations (e.g., EuP, EFKffT, EFK, or equivalent) are considered a strong advantage. Interest in system integration, servo/motion systems, electronics, automation, testing, or manufacturing engineering. Basic understanding of electrical circuits, sensors, motors, drives, feedback systems, or control theory. Hands-on mindset with strong curiosity and willingness to learn. Experience gained through university labs, Formula Student, robotics clubs, personal projects, internships, or technical hobbies is highly valued. Basic knowledge of data analysis tools such as Excel, Python, MATLAB/Simulink, LabVIEW, or similar tools is an advantage. Understanding of BOM structures, engineering documentation, or configuration management is an advantage. Exposure to motion-control systems and 3D CAD tools (Creo, SolidWorks, or similar) is an advantage. Strong problem-solving skills, teamwork, and communication abilities. About KLA We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us. Use of AI Statement At KLA, our interviews seek to understand your individual skills, problem-solving approach and authentic thinking. To ensure a fair and consistent evaluation, the use of AI, recording tools or other technologies to generate, suggest or provide responses during interviews—whether virtual or in person—is not permitted unless explicitly approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation or invited by the interviewer. Use of these tools may interfere with our ability to evaluate your individual qualifications and affect your candidacy. KLA is committed to advancing innovation through responsible AI, and we value candidates who share this mindset. We offer a competitive, family friendly total rewards package. We design our programs to reflect our commitment to an inclusive environment, while ensuring we provide benefits that meet the diverse needs of our employees. KLA is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.
