jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Golden, CO | Full-Time | 12-15 Weeks | Summer 2027 Today, everything we send to space is constrained by what fits inside a rocket fairing. That's a fundamental bottleneck to building more capable spacecraft. Rendezvous Robotics is solving this problem with electromagnetic self-assembling tiles: modular spacecraft components that rendezvous, dock, and latch to assemble bigger and more powerful spacecraft than anything that can be folded to fit into a rocket. We're a small team based in Golden, Colorado, executing on a clear path from flight demonstration to our first operational systems. Our work spans hardware, software, and systems engineering. We are looking for the best people in the world who want to build the next generation of advanced spacecraft. Every unit in our system has to dock, undock, and re-dock repeatedly without wearing, fit together in a manner that allows reliable connections, and provide the stiffness needed to build extremely large structures in orbit. That puts a lot of pressure on the mechanical design: docking connector design, mechanical latching, thermal management, structural loads through the docking interface, and packaging everything else around it. You'll be a critical member of the team contributing to the development and hands-on assembly of real flight hardware Responsibilities Design and iterate on structural components and docking interface hardware Work on thermal management for onboard electronics and battery packs Support mechanical integration of electronics, power systems, and sensors within a tight envelope Develop and refine harness and connector layouts between internal subsystems Run structural and thermal analysis to validate designs before build Basic Qualifications Currently pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field Proficiency in CAD (Onshape, NX, SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or similar) Understanding of basic structural and thermal analysis principles Preferred Qualifications Experience designing for space environments (thermal cycling, vacuum, vibration, radiation shielding) Familiarity with ruggedized connectors and cable harness design Hands-on machining, 3D printing, or prototyping experience Experience with FEA tools (NX Simcenter3D, FEMAP, ANSYS, etc.) ITAR Requirements To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Mechanical Engineering Co-op We’re looking for people who put their innovation to work to advance our success – and their own. Join an organization that ensures a more secure world through connecting and protecting our customers with inventive electrical solutions. Early Careers at nVent Innovation, inclusion, and growth. At nVent, we empower you to innovate, welcome you to bring your true self to work, and cultivate bold ideas that fuel both your personal and professional growth. Immerse yourself in a culture of positive energy, unwavering integrity, and respect—a perfect catalyst for launching a purposeful and vibrant career. Mechanical Engineering Co-op Program The Mechanical Engineering Co-op Program with nVent’s Electrical Connections (E C ) Business is a structured experiential learning program that gives students the opportunity to couple their academic knowledge with practical situations in the workplace , and simultaneously allows nVent to evaluate students as potential direct-hire talent. The Program is rotational between various departments, including Product Engineering, Product Development, Manufacturing , Labs and Compliance, and Digital Media Development . It is designed to engage students in the entire engineering process from development, through testing and applications, and to production. Students are assigned rotations and projects based on their academic levels and engineering capabilities and are given opportunities to champion these projects to completion and make significant contributions to existing processes. Our candidates are hands-on problem-solvers who are analytical, creative, and highly professional. We seek confident leaders who take the initiative to drive results. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer (Intern)
jobs.body: Who We Are Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology. What We Offer Location: Fagare,ITA, Treviso,ITA You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more. At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits . General Profile The Mechanical Engineering Intern will support the Manufacturing Engineering Department in the daily production and engineering activities at the European Repair Center (ERC) of Applied Materials based in Fagarè - Bocca di Callalta in the municipality of San Biagio di Callalta (TV). This internship provides an opportunity for students or recent graduates to gain hands-on experience in a high-tech manufacturing environment while developing technical, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Working closely with experienced engineers and technicians, the intern will contribute to process improvement initiatives, production process support, and manufacturing documentation activities, while collaborating with cross-functional teams such as Operations, Quality, and Supply Chain. Technical Skills Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field. Basic understanding of mechanical systems and manufacturing processes. Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings and technical documentation. Familiarity with CAD software (SolidWorks, Creo, AutoCAD, or similar) is a plus. Good analytical and problem-solving skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and PowerPoint. Good communication skills and ability to work in a team environment. Fluent in English and Italian, both written and spoken. Responsibilities Support Manufacturing Engineers improving the daily production processes. Assist in developing and updating manufacturing procedures and work instructions. Participate in process improvement and cost reduction initiatives. Collect and analyze manufacturing data to support operational decisions. Support root cause analysis and corrective actions for manufacturing issues. Assist in new product introduction and process validation activities. Collaborate with Production, Quality, Supply Chain, and Engineering teams. Support the evaluation of tooling, fixtures, and manufacturing equipment. Maintain engineering documentation and manufacturing records. Follow safety procedures and manufacturing best practices. Preferred Qualifications Degree in progress or recently completed in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline. Previous academic project, or laboratory experience is a plus. Interest in manufacturing, operations, and continuous improvement. Proactive attitude, curiosity, and willingness to learn in a fast-paced environment. This internship offers a valuable opportunity to gain practical experience in Manufacturing Engineering within a global technology-driven organization. We offer a six-month training program within a multinational company that is a global leader in the semiconductor industry, including a monthly expense reimbursement and meal vouchers. Additional Information Time Type: Full time Employee Type: Intern / Student Travel: No Relocation Eligible: No The salary offered to a selected candidate will be based on multiple factors including location, hire grade, job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and with consideration of internal equity of our current team members. jobs.title: AI Solutions Engineer Intern
jobs.body: This is a summer internship starting May/June and is fully on-site at the listed office location. Company Overview At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it a reality. For over two decades, we’ve been at the forefront of the global energy transition, pioneering solutions that empower critical industries to thrive in a rapidly digitizing, energy-intensive world. From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm. At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century. Department Overview The Services Business Intelligence team develops analytics, data products, AI solutions, and automation that help Bloom Energy operate and scale its global service organization. The team supports fleet performance, predictive maintenance, product optimization, supply chain and financial forecasting, maintenance planning, and executive reporting. We work across engineering, operations, data engineering, product management, and data science to turn complex operational data into reliable tools and actionable decisions. Intern Project Interns will have a primary project during the summer internship and may work on additional projects. While the project could change by the time of the internship, we anticipate that the main project will involve the following: The intern will help design and develop an enterprise AI solution that enables employees to find information, answer operational questions, and complete workflows using company data and knowledge sources. The project may include agentic AI, retrieval-augmented generation, enterprise search, API integration, prompt and workflow design, and solution evaluation. The intern will collaborate with business and technical teams to develop a secure, source-grounded prototype and measure its accuracy, usability, and business value. Position Responsibilities Develop AI-powered applications using enterprise data and knowledge sources. Build and test agentic AI, retrieval, search, and workflow capabilities. Integrate AI solutions with APIs, databases, and business applications. Evaluate solution accuracy, source grounding, performance, and usability. Document the solution and present results to technical and business stakeholders. Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Information Systems, or a related field. Must be graduating between spring 2027 and summer 2028 Desired Qualifications Proficiency in Python or another modern programming language. Experience developing applications, APIs, or data-driven software. Familiarity with generative AI, large language models, or retrieval-augmented generation. Familiarity with databases, cloud platforms, Git, and REST APIs. Interest in agentic AI, enterprise search, and workflow automation. Strong problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills. Visa Sponsorship Bloom Energy is unable to provide VISA sponsorship to interns or new grad hires on an F-1, J-1 or other visa for this position, regardless of CPT or OPT status. We are committed to compliance with all applicable laws providing equal employment opportunities. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability. Bloom Energy makes reasonable accommodation, consistent with applicable laws, for the known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified applicant or employee with a disability, who can perform the essential job functions, unless undue hardship would result. The total compensation for this position is based on various factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience. The pay range for this position $36 - $50 per hour. jobs.title: GE Aerospace Research - Controls & Optimization Internship, 2027
jobs.body: Job Description Summary Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we believe the world works better when it flies. We are a world-leading provider of jet engines, components, and integrated systems for commercial and military aircraft. We have a relentless dedication to the future of safe and more sustainable flight and believe in our talented people to make it happen. Job Description Our Controls & Optimization team develops advanced control system technology for jet engines and aircraft systems, helping enable more sustainable air travel and the next generation of military propulsion. As an intern on this team, you will work alongside researchers from a range of technical disciplines to develop modeling, controls, optimization, estimation, and detection technologies that are used to design, test, and operate advanced prototypes and products. You will own a focused research project and deliver results you present to the team at the end of the summer. In this role you will: Develop and implement advanced modeling, control, optimization, estimation, or detection algorithms for complex aerospace systems such as jet engines. Build simulation models of dynamic systems and use them to evaluate, tune, and compare your algorithms. Validate the performance of your solution through simulation. Collaborate with researchers across GE Aerospace Research and GE Aerospace, sharing progress in team meetings and technical reviews. Document your methods and results in a technical report and present your work to research leadership at the end of the internship. At GE Aerospace Research, scientists, engineers, and technicians innovate for the future of flight. An internship with us will provide valuable hands-on experience to help you launch your career and you will have the opportunity to work on really cool things with smart and collaborative people. Qualifications/Requirements: Current enrollment in a full-time Master’s or PhD degree program at an accredited university, in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field with a focus on controls. Must be willing to work from the GE Aerospace Research office in Niskayuna, NY. Must be available for a 12 - 14 week internship, May-August, 2027. Minimum GPA 3.0 / 4.0 scale This role requires use of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) or security clearance to access classified information. Therefore, employment is contingent upon your ability to prove that you meet the qualification of being a US Citizen. Desired Qualifications - you will stand out if you have one or more of these attributes: Coursework or research experience in control theory, state estimation, optimization, or fault detection. Proficiency in MATLAB/Simulink and at least one of Python, C, or C++. Experience with dynamic system simulation tools, such as the Numerical Propulsion System Simulation (NPSS) software. Experience implementing algorithms in real time on hardware platforms, such as embedded processors or hardware-in-the-loop test setups. Prior internship or co-op experience in technical research, the aerospace industry or similar. Exceptional academic performance with research orientation. Humble: respectful, inclusive, curious/inquisitive Transparent: clear communicator, collaborator, creative problem solver Focused: sets strategic priorities, uses data to make decisions, critical thinker Eligibility Requirements: Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a background investigation and drug screen. Due to the nature of our projects, US Citizenship is required. The pay range for this position is $1,000-$2,200 USD weekly. The specific weekly rate offered to a candidate may be influenced by a variety of factors including the candidate’s experience, their education, and the work location. GE provides travel reimbursement and housing stipend for qualified interns. GE Aerospace offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE Aerospace is an Equal Opportunity Employer . Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. GE Aerospace will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States for this opening. Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen (as applicable). Employees may also be subject to random and reasonable-suspicion drug and alcohol testing. Relocation Assistance Provided: Yes

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern, Onboard Autonomy, Embodied AI (Masters)
jobs.location: Sunnyvale, California, United States of America
jobs.body: Job Description Work Arrangement: Hybrid: This internship is categorized as on-site. The selected intern is expected to report to the office 3 days a week. Location: Sunnyvale, CA Seattle, WA About the Team The Onboard Autonomy team develops the real-time intelligence that enables autonomous vehicles to perceive their surroundings, plan safe and comfortable behavior, and operate reliably on the vehicle. Our work spans sensor fusion, structured perception, trajectory generation, ML planning, local planning, controls, guardrails, evaluation, and vehicle integration. We combine machine learning, robotics, optimization, and software engineering to build production-oriented autonomy systems that operate in real time and handle challenging driving scenarios. About the Role As an Onboard Autonomy Intern, you will contribute to a focused research or engineering project within the onboard driving stack. You will work with experienced researchers and engineers to prototype, evaluate, and improve algorithms or software using vehicle data, simulation, or production-oriented environments. Potential focus areas include: Sensor Encoders and Fusion: Convert camera, lidar, radar, and other sensor inputs into useful representations for autonomy. Structured Perception: Improve object tracking, online maps, scene understanding, and long-tail scenario handling. ML Planning and Trajectory Generation: Predict behavior, generate trajectories, and select safe driving actions. Local Planning and Controls: Balance collision avoidance, traffic rules, vehicle dynamics, kinematic feasibility, and passenger comfort. Guardrails and Integration: Validate and integrate autonomy components across vehicle platforms to support safe, reliable operation. What You’ll Do Prototype and evaluate algorithms for perception, prediction, planning, trajectory generation, controls, or integration. Work with real-world driving data and simulation to measure performance and investigate failures. Build data-processing, visualization, testing, and evaluation tools. Contribute to production-quality software through design reviews, code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and documentation. Analyze results, improve system performance, collaborate across disciplines, and present technical findings. Required Qualifications Currently pursuing a Master’s in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Controls, Machine Learning, or a related STEM field. Experience through coursework, research, projects, or professional work in machine learning, computer vision, robotics, controls, optimization, or autonomous systems. Strong Python skills and experience with C++ or another systems programming language. Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills. Availability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the internship. Preferred Qualifications Experience with autonomous vehicles, ADAS, robotics, or ROS. Experience with PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, deep learning, transformers, multimodal learning, reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or trajectory prediction. Background in vehicle dynamics, feedback control, trajectory optimization, motion planning, safety-critical software, simulation, closed-loop evaluation, sensor data, large-scale datasets, or distributed computing. Intent to return to a degree program after the internship or co-op. Must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2028 Compensation: The monthly salary range for this role is $11,800 per month GM will provide a one-time lump sum taxable stipend payment to eligible students selected for the 2027 Student Program. Intern events and opportunities to network with company leaders and peers. jobs.title: Intern - Memory Performance and Power Modeling
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. As an AI/ML Workload Analysis Intern , you will work with system architects and performance engineers to analyze emerging AI workloads and evaluate next-generation computing and memory architecture. You will develop methodologies to characterize memory behavior, generate workload traces, and uncover performance bottlenecks across AI training and inference applications. You will develop insights into how large language models (LLMs), recommendation systems, vision models, and multimodal AI applications interact with CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, memory subsystems, and interconnects. You will leverage simulation, profiling, and data analysis tools to study performance bottlenecks, memory behavior, bandwidth requirements, and scalability characteristics of AI workloads. The focus of this role is on memory trace-based workload analysis , helping drive architectural decisions for future memory technologies and AI platforms. You will work with real-world AI workloads, trace collection tools, and analytics frameworks to understand memory access patterns, bandwidth demands, cache efficiency, data movement, and system bottlenecks. Responsibilities Analyze AI/ML workloads including Large Language Models (LLMs), recommendation models, computer vision, multimodal, and generative AI applications. Collect, process, and analyze memory traces from AI training and inference workloads. Characterize memory access patterns, locality, reuse behavior, bandwidth utilization, and latency sensitivity. Characterize compute, memory, storage, and interconnect behavior across AI training and inference workloads. Develop workload traces, performance models, and architecture simulation environments. Investigate system bottlenecks related to memory capacity, bandwidth, latency, cache utilization, and communication overheads. Evaluate architectural tradeoffs across CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, accelerators, and memory technologies. Create automation frameworks for workload execution, data collection, and results analysis. Validate simulation and analytical models using benchmark and hardware measurements. Present findings through technical reports, visualizations, and architecture reviews. Minimum Qualifications Pursuing an MS or PhD in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, or a related field. Coursework or research experience in: Computer Architecture Machine Learning / Deep Learning Parallel Computing Operating Systems Data Structures and Algorithms Performance Analysis Programming experience in: Python C/C++ Strong analytical, problem-solving, and quantitative reasoning skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, or ONNX. Familiarity with LLMs, transformers, diffusion models, recommender systems, or vision models. Experience with workload profiling, tracing, or performance analysis tools. Experience with simulation, modeling, or architecture research is a plus. Experience with AI code assistant is a plus Experience with performance profiling tools such as Nsight, VTune, perf, rocprof, or similar tools. Knowledge of GPU, NPU, TPU, or accelerator architectures. Understanding of memory systems, including cache hierarchies, DRAM. Experience with architecture simulators such as Gem5, Accel-Sim, or similar tools. Familiarity with Linux development environments and data analysis frameworks. jobs.title: Research Intern - Coding Agents & Post-Training Optimization
jobs.body: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. We are hiring a Research Intern to make coding agents better, cheaper and faster through post-training: reinforcement learning, fine-tuning, distillation, compression and inference optimization. Coding agents now plan, edit repositories, run tests and fix failures over long, multi-step trajectories. Making them reliable and affordable is a post-training problem as much as a modeling one. Our team trains, evaluates and ships agentic coding models that power developer tools at scale. As a Research Intern, you will own a research question end to end; form a hypothesis, build the experiment, measure it on realistic agent benchmarks, and push results toward a paper or a product integration. You will work with researchers and engineers across model training, agent infrastructure and hardware acceleration. Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled full time in a Doctoral Degree program in area in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related STEM field. Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. Preferred Qualifications At least one additional quarter/semester of school remaining following the completion of the internship. Research experience in at least one of: LLM post-training (RL, SFT, preference optimization), model compression, or efficient inference. Proficient Python and PyTorch skills, with hands-on experience training or fine-tuning transformer models First-author publications at top venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, MLSys, ICSE, FSE) or equivalent research impact. Experience with RL for LLMs at scale using frameworks such as TRL, verl, OpenRLHF or DeepSpeed-Chat. Experience building or training code-generation models or coding agents, and with benchmarks such as SWE-bench, LiveCodeBench, Terminal-Bench or HumanEval. Hands-on work with quantization, distillation, pruning or speculative decoding; familiarity with serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM or ONNX Runtime. Familiarity with distributed training (FSDP, DeepSpeed, Megatron) and GPU profiling or kernel work (CUDA, Triton). Clear communication, self-direction, curiosity, and a bias toward hands-on experimentation. Experience collaborating across teams, disciplines and cultures. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Maintenance Tool Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Service Tooling & Processes Team Our team’s brief is to make maintenance better across Zipline. From designing smart fixtures that allow us to interact with our aircraft electronically to writing and validating maintenance procedures to kitting mobile maintenance vans that allow technicians to service our system in the summer heat, we aim to improve every aspect of maintenance. Our direct customers are the operational maintenance teams working on our systems in the field, and we’re laser-focused on making their lives better. If a maintenance technician working at 2 in the morning has everything they need to complete their work quickly, efficiently, and reliably, then we’ve done our job well. The Role As Zipline continues to rapidly iterate our hardware, we need to design, validate, and field new tools to allow technicians to do their work safely and efficiently. You’ll work closely with maintenance to understand their needs and pain points, then partner with hardware and tooling engineers to create solutions. Our team is based out of a high-volume test facility, so you’ll see your designs get immediate use, immediate feedback, and plenty of iteration cycles. Once those tools have been perfected at our test facilities they become part of our operational toolkits across all of Zipline and make real, tangible impacts on how we serve our customers. What You'll Do Work closely with Hardware and Operations teams to understand pain points and process requirements. Design and prototype tools for drone and ground system maintenance. Use hand and machine tools to produce the first units. Gather operational feedback on your designs and iterate quickly. Partner with Operations leadership on trade studies to evaluate the optimal, fully-productionized forms of your design. Create usage documentation and lead training sessions as your designs roll out into operation. What You'll Bring A strong grasp of mechanical design fundamentals (statics, dynamics, material properties, fabrication processes, etc). Proficiency with CAD software like NX, Solidworks, Fusion, etc. Hands-on prototyping experience like 3d printing, fabrications, welding, soldering, or assembly. Strong communication skills and an ability to collaborate cross-functionally. Obsessive customer focus and a drive to understand how your designs work in the real world. Ability to work on-site at our test facility in Esparto, CA every day. What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our Esparto, CA Office. jobs.title: Internship- Imaging product engineer
jobs.body: Introduction The Imaging Engineering Intern role supports ASML's mission to advance lithography technology through innovative software and imaging solutions. You will work with experienced engineers to evaluate advanced deep ultraviolet (DUV) and extreme ultraviolet (EUV) imaging concepts, perform feasibility studies, and contribute to software solutions that help customers tackle increasingly complex semiconductor manufacturing challenges. This internship provides valuable exposure to computational lithography, imaging algorithms, simulation technologies, and product development in a collaborative engineering environment. Roles and Responsibilities As a Imaging Engineering Intern, you will support imaging product engineering activities focused on computational lithography and advanced scanner technologies. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to investigate new concepts, develop software capabilities, and generate data-driven insights that support future product innovation. Conduct feasibility studies related to advanced DUV and EUV imaging technologies. Support computational lithography investigations through modeling, simulation, and data analysis. Perform prototype testing and generate technical data to evaluate imaging concepts and software features. Develop and enhance software functionality that meets customer requirements and product specifications. Create and maintain technical documentation, including user guides and engineering reports. Analyze simulation results and communicate findings to engineering teams. Collaborate with software engineers, imaging specialists, and product teams to support ongoing development efforts. Education and Experience Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree or master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Applied Mathematics, Optical Engineering, or a related technical field. Junior, senior, or graduate-level student. Experience through coursework, research, academic projects, or internships related to imaging, lithography, simulation, software development, or data analysis. Familiarity with technical computing tools such as Python, MATLAB, or similar programming environments. Exposure to machine learning, optimization methods, scientific computing, or data analytics is preferred. jobs.title: 2027 Battery Test Lab Undergraduate Intern
jobs.body: The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space. Physical Sciences Laboratories (PSL) supports the effective and timely development and operation of national security systems through scientific research and the application of advanced technologies. PSL has more than 150 specialized laboratories used to test, analyze, and troubleshoot virtually every aspect of rocket and satellite system design, development, construction, deployment, and operation. The expertise of the laboratories’ technical staff allows PSL to stay abreast of new technological developments and program support issues associated with rapidly evolving space systems. The qualified candidate will become part of the Physical Sciences Laboratories, Energy Technology Department, Battery Test Lab, supporting the test and evaluation of spacecraft cells and batteries for flight programs. Work will involve hands-on, battery-related laboratory work to support designing and building custom test stations for space vehicle battery testing. An overall goal in this work is to develop innovative solutions to streamline battery testing, and to improve the battery test life cycle. The selected candidate will be required to work full-time, on-site at our facility in El Segundo, CA. What You’ll Be Doing You will work with an interdisciplinary team of engineers, scientists, and technicians in the Battery Test Lab with a focus on ongoing material, electrochemical, electrical engineering, and data science research areas. You will apply standard techniques and procedures to carry out a series of prescribed scientific and/or engineering tasks, including: Creating new battery cell tests and experiments Fabricating custom test hardware and cabling Assembling/soldering printed circuit boards You will also assist in innovating new testing solutions, including: Developing new diagnostic tools Supporting the team on project designs, test protocols, and experimental validations Performing analysis on battery test data to evaluate performance and identify improvements Developing interface/communication codes for measurement & test equipment Duties, responsibilities and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned as needed Training and mentorship will be provided What Corporate Skills You’ll Bring government. jobs.title: Airframe/Structures Engineering Intern
jobs.body: ABOUT US: Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures. WHO WE ARE: We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy. WHO YOU ARE: Astro Mechanica is seeking an intern to join our Airframe Team for the summer of 2027 (program begins on June 7, 2027 for semester schools and June 27, 2027 for quarter schools). The ideal candidate has a strong foundation in structural design principles and a passion for solving challenging aerospace problems. You’re eager to apply your engineering education to real aircraft hardware while learning from experienced engineers across disciplines. As an intern, you’ll be embedded with the structures team in San Francisco, working on real projects alongside full-time engineers, and you’ll help design, analyze, and test advanced aerospace structures that directly contribute to the performance and safety of our vehicles. WHAT YOU’LL DO: - Contribute to the design, analysis, build, and test of composite and metallic structures for high-performance aircraft - Perform CAD modeling, drawings, and basic structural analysis (hand calcs and FEA) - Assist with trade studies that balance performance, weight, cost, and manufacturability - Work with cross-functional teams (aero, propulsion, manufacturing, test) to understand and support structural requirements - Participate in design reviews, manufacturing support, and testing activities - Document your work clearly and follow configuration control practices for designs and models - Own a scoped project through the summer and present your results to the team at the end of the internship WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR: - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field - Coursework, club, research, or internship experience in structural design and analysis - Familiarity with composite and metallic materials, structural design principles, and manufacturing processes - Hands-on proficiency in CAD (e.g., NX, SolidWorks, or similar) - Exposure to structural analysis methods (hand calculations, FEA tools such as Nastran, Abaqus, or Ansys) - Strong problem-solving skills and willingness to take initiative - Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary environment - Enthusiasm for learning, building, and contributing to innovative aerospace vehicles - Available for a full-time, in-person internship in San Francisco during Summer 2027 (approximately 10-12 weeks) PERKS & BENEFITS: - Competitive hourly pay - Hands-on mentorship from experienced engineers - Company-funded perks, including team lunches, game nights, and other activities ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: At Astro Mechanica, we highly value in-office work to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. We consider working in the office five days a week an essential part of the employee's role. Astro Mechanica is an equal opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Pay range: $40 – $55 per hour.

jobs.title: Product Design Engineering Internship - 6 or 12 months  (2027 start)
jobs.body: Introduction Are you a c urious and creatively minded individual studying product design engineering and looking for exciting and fulfilling experiences ? Do you have creative flare and a passion for design for manufacture and assembly ? Would you like to contribute to a wide selection of products for clients in the Industrial, Consumer, Energy and Defence industries? You may be a graduate, or a candidate with a couple of years of industry experience. You can expect this role to include a mixture of desk-based and practical tasks. Successful candidates can join us on a 6 or 12 month industrial placement. There is no deadline for this role, as we recruit on a rolling basis. Once the position is filled, we will close the advert. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Your role The Real isation group is responsible for dynamic hardware development of products, in both high and low volume markets following the guiding principles of Design for “X” ( DfX ) with particular emphasis on design for manufacture and assembly (DFMA) . The group operates from product conception and design all the way through to manufacture and product launch , often bridging the gap between novel technology and high volume manufacture . Our work spans a range of industry sectors, such as consumer electronic products, energy sensors and metering, sustainability and agricultural systems. The Realisation group is home to some of the most talented and passionate design engineers in the UK , who bring together their collective knowledge and skills to deliver elegant technical solutions. Our projects often involve the development of novel manufacturing techniques and complex supply chain management. jobs.body: Overview: Draper is an independent, nonprofit research and development company headquartered in Cambridge, MA. The 2,000+ employees of Draper tackle important national challenges with a promise of delivering successful and usable solutions. From military defense and space exploration to biomedical engineering, lives often depend on the solutions we provide. Our multidisciplinary teams of engineers and scientists work in a collaborative environment that inspires the cross-fertilization of ideas necessary for true innovation. For more information about Draper, visit www.draper.com . Job Description Summary: Engineering Student internships support the research and development of new or existing microsystems and advanced materials (hardware, software, components, and materials/chemistry research and modeling) or may assist in sustaining and improving the quality processes across the full engineering and manufacturing life cycle. Student interns will contribute to projects in various engineering disciplines such as computer hardware or software design and development, electro-optical design, optical and thermal model development, bioengineering, materials testing, chemistry, electrical system design, hardware assembly, testing, etc. Student interns will test and evaluate products, systems, or components and work with various applications such as LabVIEW, MATLAB, SolidWorks, COMSOL, ANSYS, Mentor Graphics, Python, and GitLab. Student interns collaborate with engineers or technicians to build and test systems, hardware, or components on various projects. They may also be involved in ensuring quality products are produced and quality procedures are upheld. Job Description: Duties/Responsibilities Design, develop, and enhancement engineering solutions for challenging problems. Implement, test, perform analysis, and provide documentation support. Generate and present test reports including plots, tables, evaluation criteria, and conclusions from data collected and analyzed throughout the test process. Complete assignments designed to develop a practical knowledge of processes, procedures, equipment, facilities, and systems as well as their interrelationships within engineering disciplines. Performs other duties as assigned. Program Requirements Enrolled in an accredited full-time undergraduate or graduate degree program required. There is flexibility regarding hours and program duration based on applicant’s school schedule and availability. Skills/Abilities Excellent written and oral communication skills. Excellent work ethic with the ability to work independently or in a team environment. Ability to adapt to ever-changing environments, risks, and vulnerabilities. Strong computer skills including MS Word, PowerPoint and Excel. Additional Job Description: Responsibilities The student will be a part of a team that designs, models, and tests complex multi-physics devices, microsystems, and materials and systems. An example research area would be radiation effects in semiconductor electronics. The multi-disciplinary engineering teams will develop and verify the performance of such systems with a broad understanding of the relevant physics. In addition, the candidate should have an interest in a wide variety of other areas such as MEMS sensors, space systems and electro-optics. Qualifications The ideal candidate will be seeking a degree in electrical engineering, nuclear engineering, physics, materials science, chemistry, or a related field. The desired candidate has many, but not necessarily all, of the skills listed below: Interest in designing, modeling and testing electronic devices Experience using one or more computational tools such as SPICE, Comsol, TCAD, Matlab, MCNP or similar to model complex physical phenomena. Experience with nuclear engineering and related modeling Interest in developing a broad array of novel multi-physics devices and systems This position and/or the facilities in which its duties will be performed are subject to national security programs imposed and administered under U.S. statutes. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Intern
jobs.body: To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology. Group/Division The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The Surfscan® division develops unpatterned wafer inspection systems that detect nanoscale particles and surface defects early in semiconductor manufacturing. Its systems monitor wafer quality across a wide range of applications, enabling faster issue identification and improved process control. What You'll Do In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise. As a Mechanical Engineering Intern, you’ll join our Mechanical Engineering team and work alongside experienced engineers to support the development and testing of next-generation metrology tool. What You’ll Do: Assist in defining requirements and developing specifications for mechanical engineering modules. Support the creation and execution of test plans for new designs and improvements. Participate in troubleshooting and performance analysis of devices and subsystems. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to review designs and test results. Document findings and contribute to reports that support engineering decisions. Use Creo for 3D modeling of the tool design. Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical, Mechatronics Engineering, or related field. Familiarity with CAD modeling tool such as Creo or Solidworks (coursework or projects count). Exposure to precision engineering, robotics or electromechanical systems is a plus. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent communication and teamwork abilities. About KLA We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us. Use of AI Statement At KLA, our interviews seek to understand your individual skills, problem-solving approach and authentic thinking. To ensure a fair and consistent evaluation, the use of AI, recording tools or other technologies to generate, suggest or provide responses during interviews—whether virtual or in person—is not permitted unless explicitly approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation or invited by the interviewer. Use of these tools may interfere with our ability to evaluate your individual qualifications and affect your candidacy. KLA is committed to advancing innovation through responsible AI, and we value candidates who share this mindset. We offer a competitive, family friendly total rewards package. We design our programs to reflect our commitment to an inclusive environment, while ensuring we provide benefits that meet the diverse needs of our employees. KLA is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Research Intern - MSR Systems Research Group - Redmond
jobs.body: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The Systems Research Group in Microsoft Research is devoted to advancing the state of the art in distributed systems and operating systems. Our aim is to make systems scalable, fault-tolerant, manageable, fast, efficient, and verifiably correct. We work on a wide range of infrastructure systems, including data center operating systems, serverless infrastructure, machine learning serving infrastructure, storage systems, etc. Further information on current research projects is listed on the group’s website: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/systems-research-group-redmond/ Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science or a related STEM field. Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. jobs.body: Company: Qualcomm France S.A.R.L. Job Area: Interns Group, Interns Group > Interim Intern General Summary: General Summary: This internship is focused on the hardware design of accelerators for post-Quantum cryptography (PQC), a class of cryptographic algorithms resistant to quantum attacks. As quantum computing advances, traditional encryption methods (like RSA and ECC) become vulnerable, making PQC essential for future-proof security. To meet performance and energy efficiency demands, dedicated hardware accelerators are needed. This project will involve strong collaboration with the architecture team during the specification phase to ensure alignment with system-level constraints and integration goals. Company: A world leader in smart mobile technologies, QUALCOMM (QCT) offers complete solutions that enable continuous innovation for today's smart connected devices. Our vast expertise in wireless technology, combined with our unique systems approach to developing solutions, puts QCT at the forefront of the rapidly expanding mobile industry. QCT offers solutions for CDMA, UMTS, GSM and LTE technologies, providing support for both 3G, 4G and now 5G networks and devices. Qualcomm also offers a broad portfolio of additional wired and wireless technologies for the mobile, networking, computing and consumer electronics product segments. All our solutions and products are elegantly engineered for optimal performance and power consumption. Our system-on-chip solutions like Snapdragon bring together CPU, GPU, connectivity, security, multimedia and GPS technologies in a way that is redefining mobile possibilities for people everywhere. Because of its unsurpassed performance and capabilities, Snapdragon is enhancing the mobile experience and fueling an ever-expanding array of new connected device categories, ranging from smartphones to tablets to e-readers and beyond. The Hardware Security and Cryptography engineering team is seeking an Engineering Internship in our growing SnapDragon team in Sophia-Antipolis - France. The successful candidate will have an exposure to security concepts and implementation techniques. jobs.body: The Bosch Group is a leading global supplier of technology and services. It employs roughly 394,500 associates worldwide (as of December 31, 2020). According to preliminary figures, the company generated sales of 71.6 billion euros in 2020. Its operations are divided into four business sectors: Mobility Solutions, Industrial Technology, Consumer Goods, and Energy and Building Technology. The Bosch Group comprises Robert Bosch GmbH and its roughly 440 subsidiaries and regional companies in some 60 countries. If its sales and service partners are included, then Bosch is represented in roughly 126 locations. This worldwide development, manufacturing, and sales network is the foundation for further growth. BGSV – Bosch Global Software Technologies Company Limited (Previous name: RBVH - Robert Bosch Engineering and Business Solutions Vietnam Company Limited) is 100% owned subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH. BGSV has started its operations from 19th October, 2010 at E-Town2 in HCMC. This engineering development center will be engaged in developing embedded systems and software, mechanical design and simulation, and will provide IT (SAP Consulting, JAVA Development….) and Business Services (Finance and accounting, Economics, Purchasing, Logistics, Translations Japanese-English-Japanese, Information Security ) solutions to the Bosch group of companies globally. Key Contributions Support the creation of 3D models and 2D drawings using CAD tools such as Creo, NX, and Inventor to meet project requirements. Assist in the design and development of machinery parts and machine assemblies under guidance from senior engineers. Contribute to design modifications and Engineering Change Requests (ECRs) to improve functionality, quality. Support project teams by following defined quality processes and maintaining accurate engineering documentation. Learning & Development Opportunities Gain hands-on experience with industrial CAD tools and mechanical design standards. Learn practical aspects of machine design, tolerancing, and design-for-manufacturing. Understand and apply engineering change management and configuration control processes. Develop awareness of project quality systems, documentation practices, and compliance requirements in an engineering environment. Final-year or senior student in Mechanical/ Mechatronics, Computational Engineering or relevant background Available for a 6-month full-time internship (Monday to Friday) Able to provide a university recommendation or introduction letter for the internship Good English communication skills Knowledge of mechanical drawing, Geometric dimension & tolerance, manufacturing process Proficient in CAD design tools, including PTC Creo, NX, AutoCAD, Inventor, and SolidWorks, for mechanical design tasks Monthly Internship Allowance, plus Meal and Parking support. 1 paid leave day + 1 sick leave day for each internship month. 1 birthday leave day if your birthday falls during the internship period. Accident insurance provided throughout the internship. Opportunity to observe and engage in international projects and innovation. Access to our diverse training programs which surely help strengthen both your personal and professionalism. Participation in various company activities such as football, yoga, badminton, and team building.

jobs.title: Paid Mechanical Engineering Intern
jobs.body: Rockwell Automation is a global technology leader focused on helping the world’s manufacturers be more productive, sustainable, and agile. With more than 28,000 employees who make the world better every day, we know we have something special. Behind our customers - amazing companies that help feed the world, provide life-saving medicine on a global scale, and focus on clean water and green mobility - our people are energized problem solvers that take pride in how the work we do changes the world for the better. We welcome all makers, forward thinkers, and problem solvers who are looking for a place to do their best work. And if that’s you we would love to have you join us! Job Description The Performance Engineering team located in Katowice (Francuska Street 46) is looking for a Mechanical Engineer Intern. Our Motion Control team focuses on the development and improvement of products such as servo drives (inverters), motors, and Independent Cart Technology (ICT), including iTRAK and QuickStick. In our daily work, we use engineering tools and systems such as Creo, Windchill, Jira, and SAP. Also, technologies including 3D printing and 3D scanning. This is a paid, part-time internship, typically lasting 6 months, and requiring availability of at least 20 hours per week. It is an opportunity to gain hands-on engineering experience and learn product development processes while working with experienced engineers in an Agile environment. You will report to the Performance Engineering Team Lead and work in a hybrid model in Katowice, Poland. Your Responsibilities: Support local and global engineering teams with 3D modeling and technical documentation Assist the Katowice team in building, modifying, and testing prototypes Support engineering activities in the office and laboratory and remotely Use engineering tools and systems such as Creo, Windchill, Jira, and SAP Support 3D printing and 3D scanning activities Assist the Katowice team with daily engineering tasks and ongoing projects Take ownership of assigned tasks and work independently under the guidance of experienced engineers The Essentials - You Will Have: Availability for at least 20 hours per week Student status in the final years of a Master's or Engineering program (Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Automation and Robotics, or related fields) Basic knowledge of at least one 3D design software (Creo – preferred, SolidWorks, Inventor, Catia, NX or SolidEdge) Good command of English Knowledge of technical drawing and basic engineering documentation The Preferred - You Might Also Have: Knowledge of 3D printing Knowledge of Creo SEP certification Knowledge of Ansys Experience in student research groups What We Offer: Lunch Card – Monthly meal vouchers through the Edenred card. Lunch Card – Monthly meal vouchers through the Edenred card. Paid, part-time internship with flexible working hours. Hybrid working model in Katowice. Hands-on experience with professional engineering tools such as Creo, Windchill, SAP, Jira, and 3D printing. Exposure to an international engineering environment. At Rockwell Automation we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right person for this or other roles. #LI-Hybrid #LI-JS1 Rockwell Automation’s hybrid policy aligns that employees are expected to work at a Rockwell location at least Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays unless they have a business obligation out of the office.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Internship - Mechanical Engineering - Arizona
jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will: ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting​ Implement new ideas, be constantly challenged, and develop your skills​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions.​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward.​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts.​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives.​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships.​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​As a Mechanical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams: Research & Development New Product Development R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products. They research new technologies, customer expectations, business requirements and regulations. They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts. These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production. Product Engineering R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies, customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products. Test Lab Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that we get to be the Mythbusters of our division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, we are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you! Majors Targeted: Mechanical Engineering, or related majors $20 min hourly wage – $35 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship.​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above (verified at time of hire) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future.​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment. Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. Stryker is an EO employer – M/F/Veteran/Disability. Stryker Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor’s legal duty to furnish information.

jobs.location: Simi Valley, CA; Huntsville, AL; Pottstown, PA; Sunrise, FL; Herndon, VA; Moorpark, CA; Germantown, MD; Albuquerque, NM; Minneapolis, MN; Arlington, VA; Petaluma, CA; Melbourne, FL; San Diego, CA
jobs.body: Worker Type Supplemental Job Description Summer Internship Program Our paid Summer Internship Program is designed to provide students with an immersive, hands-on experience within the aerospace and defense industry. Interns work alongside AV team members on meaningful projects involving cutting-edge technology while developing professional relationships, strategic problem-solving skills, and practical experience in a full-time work environment. This is a 12-week, onsite program intended for highly motivated and passionate students who are currently enrolled in college or are recent graduates. Applicants must have a minimum 3.0 GPA, with a preference for students at the junior level or above. Our program has been recognized by Yello and WayUp as one of the Top 100 Internship Programs in the United States for multiple years. Depending on the team and location, students who are willing to relocate for their internship may be eligible for a relocation and housing reimbursement stipend. AV offers internship opportunities across various teams and locations throughout the United States. Specific team, location, and program details will be discussed during the interview process. Summary As an Autonomy & Robotics Engineering Intern, you will work alongside a team of skilled engineers to support the development of autonomous behaviors, machine perception, and robotic control systems for unmanned aerial systems (UAS) and other advanced platforms.
