jobs.title: Validation Intern
jobs.body: Summer 2027 Internship - May 24 - August 13 Must be currently enrolled full time in a university degree program pursing a master degree. 100% onsite We are seeking a proactive Validation Intern to join our team. Key Responsibilities: Assist in the development and execution of Bench Validation plans and conducting validations for new silicon products, including DDR, MCR, Memory Controllers or other integrated circuits. Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Design, Test, and Marketing to understand product requirements and develop comprehensive validation strategies. Utilize lab equipment such as Oscilloscopes, BERT, AWG, and other test instruments to perform electrical characterization and performance benchmarking. Document test procedures, results, and findings in detailed engineering reports and contribute to the continuous improvement of validation methodologies. Assist in debugging and troubleshooting silicon issues, working closely with design and Test Engineers to implement effective solutions. Contributes to the development and enhancement of automated test frameworks and validation scripts to streamline the validation process and improve efficiency. Pursuing a Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field. Graduating December 2027 preferred. Strong understanding of digital and analog circuits, semiconductor devices, and computer architecture principles. Familiarity with lab equipment and measurement techniques for silicon validation, including oscilloscopes, power supplies, BERT, AWGs, etc. Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, C/C++, or scripting languages for test automation and data analysis. Hands-On Experience with Python test automation equipment such programmable power supplies, multimeters, oscilloscopes, etc. Excellent problem-solving skills with the ability to analyze complex technical issues and propose effective solutions. Strong communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams. Eagerness to learn and adapt to new technologies and methodologies in the field of silicon validation. The expected hourly pay range for this position is $41.50/hr. jobs.title: Robotics Research Intern
jobs.body: The Bosch Research and Technology Center North America with offices in Sunnyvale, California, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Cambridge, Massachusetts is a part of the global Bosch Group (www.bosch.com), a company with over 70 billion euro revenue, 400,000 employees worldwide, a very diverse product portfolio, and a history spanning over 125 years. The Research and Technology Center North America (RTC-NA) is dedicated to providing technologies and system solutions for various Bosch business fields, primarily in the field of artificial intelligence, energy technologies, internet technologies, circuit design, semiconductors and wireless, as well as advanced MEMS design. As a part of the global research, our AI research in Silicon Valley focuses on Foundation Models, Big Data Visual Analytics, Explainable AI (XAI), Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision & Mixed Reality, Cloud Robotics, Data Science, AI System Engineering, Time-series Analysis. We develop scalable, intelligent, and trustworthy AIoT solutions for Bosch products and services in application areas such as automated driving, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), robotics, smart manufacturing, enterprise AI, health care, smart home and building solutions. Originating from the AI research in Silicon Valley, our Intelligent Autonomous Systems group is responsible for enabling future autonomous Bosch products by pushing the boundaries of automated driving, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), robotics and automation through key innovations that encompass system architecture and AI components. These include methods for motion planning, high level task planning and decision making as well as systems for making these technologies work on real products by building frameworks that take advantage of technologies in the field of reliable distributed computing. We work with internal partners of different Bosch business units to transfer our solutions into future products. We also actively collaborate with leading groups in academia and industry to promote research ideas and publish research findings in internationally renowned conferences and journals such as CVPR, ICRA, IROS, RSS, NeurIPS and CoRL. As the Robotics Manipulation intern, you will advance Bosch's capabilities in robotic manipulation, specifically in the area of agentic robotics (coding agents for robotics manipulation). A few of your responsibilities will include: * Research the state-of-the-art in agentic robotics. * Evaluate this research on a realistic, industrial Bosch use case. * Develop improvements to make these techniques practical. * Report experimental results and prepare a draft to a high-quality conference. Basic Qualifications: Ph.D. or Masters student in Computer Science, Robotics or related fields. (Must be a current student.) Experience using agents, e.g. Anthropic Claude Code or OpenAI Codex. Experience implementing algorithms on robotic arms, humanoids, or quadrupeds. Proficient in Python and C++, with experience using Ubuntu and ROS2. Minimum GPA of 3.0. Preferred Qualifications: Experience applying large generative multi-modal models, VLAs, VLMs, or LLMs to robotics problems. Familiarity with simulation and motion planning suites (e.g., NVIDIA Isaac Sim, cuRobo). Experience with perception models (e.g., SAM/SAM2, DINOv2) and spatial representation (e.g., Gaussian Splatting, NeRFs). Publication record in top venues, such as ICRA, IROS, CoRL, RSS, etc. Focus on embodiment transfer, learning from demonstration, and/or semantic scene understanding. Able to work independently, has strong research and problem-solving skills. Good communication and teamwork skills. Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability / veterans *Bosch adheres to Federal, State, and Local laws regarding drug-testing. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a drug screen and background check. Candidates who have been offered the position must pass both screenings before their start date. BOSCH is a proud supporter of STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering & Mathematics) FIRST Robotics (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology) AWIM (A World In Motion) The U.S. base salary range for this intern position is $48.00-69.00 hourly. Within the range, individual pay is determined based on several factors, including, but not limited to, type of degree, work experience and job knowledge, complexity of the role, type of position, job location, etc. Your Hiring Manager can share more details about the specific salary range for this position during the interview process. For more information on our culture and benefits, please visit: Culture and Benefits | Bosch in the USA All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships. ​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​ As an Electrical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams: Advanced Quality AQE interns work on engineering projects related to development of new products. Areas of emphasis may include human factors engineering, risk management, application of statistics, reliability engineering, design verification, and design validation including customer interaction. As Homer Stryker pointed out, “If your tools don’t work, make them work. If you can’t make them work, make some that do work.” In this directive, the AQE team works to make sure that the products we develop at Stryker will work consistently for our customers to meet or exceed their expectations. Process Quality PQE interns collaborate with cross-functional teams to support product sustainment. When non-conforming issues arise in production, it is our responsibility to perform robust root cause analysis and implement effective corrective actions. Do you enjoy deep dive investigations and driving collaboration and communication to achieve issue resolution? If so, you may be a great fit for this team! PQE interns are focused on quality, compliance and continuous improvement. They use their education to work with a variety of tools including CAD for fixture design, root cause analysis methods, LabView, and validation activities to optimize production, inspection, and quality system processes. Supplier Quality SQE interns are responsible for all things supplier-related . Stryker uses a number of critical suppliers to manufacture components and finished products, and to provide critical services. This team’s job is to work closely with the suppliers to ensure components and their manufacturing processes meet our required standards. Do you enjoy using your technical background and communication skills to influence suppliers? If so, you might be a great fit for this diverse and talented team! The role requires working closely with internal customers from multiple functions, meeting with suppliers frequently , and the use of both technical and business skills. Quality Quality interns work with our internal cross-functional teams and external sales team and customers to ensure we develop and sustain a product with the highest quality. The team’s job is to ensure we develop the right products up front – evaluate risk, ensure our customer’s user needs are met, and help drive craftsmanship, safety, durability and reliability into the product. On the post-market side, they also work closely with regulatory to handle any complaints and implement design changes, as needed, to address quality issues. The role requires someone who has great communication , problem-solving, and technical skills. Research & Development New Product Development R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products. They research new technologies , customer expectations, business requirements and regulations. They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts. These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production. Product Engineering R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies , customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products. Test Lab Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that they get to be the MythBusters of the division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, they are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you! Manufacturing Manufacturing Engineer interns will collaborate with Design and Operations to deliver best-in-class new products to market. Interns will partner with technicians and engineers to improve Stryker’s manufacturing lines through new fixture development, assembly line process enhancement, implementation of lean manufacturing principles, and improving ergonomics and safety. Majors Targeted: Electrical Engineering, or related majors . What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship . ​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above ( verified at time of hire ) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future . ​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment . $ 20 min hourly wage – $3 5 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Change Management Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the NPI Team The New Product Introduction (NPI) team moves hardware design changes and brand-new products from concept development through large-scale production and commercial use. We coordinate across design, testing, supply chain, quality, manufacturing, and field operations to ensure products are ready to build, launch, and scale in support of Zipline’s mission. About The Role This role on the Change Management/NPI team will help us level up our ability to process and implement changes at high volume and high change velocity. Zipline’s unique ability to quickly improve our hardware and develop new designs allowed us to launch our hardware so successfully, and this role with unlock our ability to expand across the United States and beyond while maintaining the same design improvement velocity. What You'll Do Build a tool that visualizes hardware changes over time, shows how product configurations evolve, and highlights hardware capabilities at specified timestamps. Build a tool that evaluates configuration compatibility across current and previous hardware revisions and summarizes hardware capabilities for specified configurations. Build a user interface for submitting engineering changes that standardizes required information, reduces errors, and generates complete change summaries for technical and non-technical audiences. What You'll Bring Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, computer science, information systems, data science, or a related technical field. Demonstrated experience through coursework, personal projects, research, student organizations, or prior internships building software, data, dashboard, or automation tools. Familiarity with at least one technical tool or language used to build solutions, such as Python, JavaScript, SQL, APIs, spreadsheets, databases, or low-code application platforms. Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills, with the ability to understand relationships, dependencies, and business rules within complex, multi-level assemblies or product data. Ability to gather requirements from users, ask clarifying questions, and turn ambiguous problems into clear workflows, visualizations, or user-friendly interfaces. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document information, explain technical outputs to non-technical audiences, and incorporate feedback from technical and non-technical stakeholders. Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to validate data, manage changing priorities, and work independently and collaboratively on complex projects. What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May/June to August/September. Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position. The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

From systems CONOPs and architecture development to system design and analysis, mission assurance, cost and schedule assessment, and economic market analysis, SED leverages a vast array of engineering and business disciplines across a diverse and dynamic portfolio of space programs and national challenges spanning the total space system lifecycle. jobs.title: Test & Reliability Engineering Intern
jobs.body: WHAT WE DO Gecko Robotics is helping the world’s most important organizations ensure the availability, reliability, and sustainability of critical infrastructure. Gecko's complete and connected solutions combine wall-climbing robots, industry-leading sensors, and an AI-powered data platform to provide customers with a unique window into the current and future health of their physical assets. This enables real-time decision making to increase the efficiency and safety of operations, promote mission readiness, and protect the environment and civilization from the effects of infrastructure failure. ROLE AT A GLANCE Gecko Robotics is seeking a Test & Reliability Engineer Intern to join Field Infra’s Test & Reliability (T&R) team in Pittsburgh for Summer 2027. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday. You will contribute to a defined engineering project focused on making our robotic systems more dependable by building software tools, automating tests, and analyzing system data and logs. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will develop practical tools, execute tests, and generate evidence that improves how Gecko validates and learns from its robotic systems. What you will do - Own a scoped engineering project that improves a test, regression, reliability-analysis, or test-data workflow. - Help plan, execute, and document software and integrated robotic-system tests under the guidance of experienced engineers. - Analyze test results, clearly document findings and open questions, and recommend improvements to test coverage and repeatability. - Develop or improve tooling, automation, scripts, or documentation that makes testing more efficient and reliable. - Collaborate with Test & Reliability engineers and partner teams to understand how field observations and engineering requirements inform validation. - Present your project, results, and recommended next steps at the end of the internship. Technologies We Use Depending on the assigned project, you may work with Python, Linux, Git, hardware and software test equipment, data-analysis tools, and robotic-system logs. The specific tools and technologies will depend on the assigned project. About You You are a curious, hands-on engineering student who enjoys understanding how complex systems behave in the real world. You are comfortable learning across software and hardware boundaries, approaching problems methodically, and communicating what you observed and what you do not yet know. Required Skills - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in engineering, computer science, robotics, or a related technical discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028. - Ability to work onsite in Pittsburgh, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship. - Foundational programming experience in Python or another general-purpose programming language. - Experience writing, testing, or debugging software through coursework, projects, research, competition teams, or a prior internship. - Interest in software testing, reliability, robotics, embedded systems, or complex physical systems. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to structure technical problems, document work clearly, communicate findings, and learn from feedback. Preferred Skills - Previous hands-on experience with robotics, embedded systems, electronics, mechanical systems, or other complex physical systems through an internship, research position, engineering lab, competition team, or substantial project. - Experience using Python to automate test workflows or analyze system data, logs, or failures. - Familiarity with Linux, Git, and structured testing or debugging practices. - Experience designing experiments, debugging system behavior, or building tools for others. - Coursework or projects in software testing, controls, mechatronics, reliability engineering, systems engineering, or a related field. WHO WE ARE At Gecko, our people are our greatest investment. In addition to competitive compensation packages, we offer company equity, 401(k) matching, gender-neutral parental leave, full medical, dental, and vision insurance, mental health, ongoing professional development, family planning assistance, and flexible paid time off. Gecko values collaboration, innovation, and partnership, and we believe we do our best work when we're together in person. We’re an office-first culture but understand that sometimes you may need to work from home. Many people are in the office five days a week, others need a bit more flexibility. Ultimately, we care about the outcomes we achieve - and creating a culture of autonomy and trust that enables that impact. Gecko is committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission to protect today’s infrastructure and give form to tomorrow’s. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. jobs.title: Summer 2027 - Process Simulation Engineering Intern - MS/PhD
jobs.body: The group you’ll be a part of The Office of the CTO is where innovation takes center stage. We inspire our global technical community to take on grand challenges, understand emerging trends, identify the critical inflections, and drive our sustainability, Environment, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices that will define the next generation of semiconductors and continued impact. The impact you’ll make As a Process Simulation Engineer Intern, you’ll help build a virtual twin of plasma etch processes. You’ll develop physics-based models of how plasma etching works and fast machine-learning surrogate versions of those models, together connecting tool settings to predicted feature profiles. Your work will directly support data-driven process development for Lam’s etch products. What you’ll do Build and refine models of how plasma etches a surface: ion and neutral species interactions with the wafer, sticking and reaction probabilities, redeposition, and ion energy and angle effects. Calibrate model parameters against measured profiles (CD vs. depth from SEM/TEM images). Design simulation experiments (parameter sweeps, design of experiments) to generate training data. Build and validate fast surrogate models of the slower physics simulations, including checks on accuracy and uncertainty. Use surrogates to explore which settings matter most and to optimize process conditions. Write Python tools to automate simulation runs, data processing, and plotting. Document the workflow and present results at the end of the internship. Who we’re looking for Currently pursuing an MS or PhD in chemical engineering, physics, materials science, chemistry, or a related field. Strong Python skills, including hands-on experience building and training models in PyTorch (or a similar framework such as JAX or TensorFlow). Background in reaction kinetics, transport phenomena, or surface/plasma science. Hands-on experience building machine-learning or regression models. Strong analytical and communication skills, and the ability to work effectively in a team. Note this is an onsite-flex position (3+ day in the office). Preferred qualifications Coursework or research in plasma physics or plasma-surface interactions. Experience with surrogate modeling methods: Gaussian processes, neural networks, polynomial chaos, or reduced-order models. Experience with GPyTorch/BoTorch, physics-informed neural networks, or uncertainty quantification. Experience with design of experiments, sensitivity analysis, Bayesian calibration, or optimization. Experience with physics-based simulation tools (finite element, Monte Carlo, or feature-scale/profile simulators). Familiarity with semiconductor etch processes or SEM/TEM image analysis. jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. Job Description As a PFA Engineer Intern on the Yield Enhancement (YE) team, you will support physical failure analysis investigations of defect issues found by YE and Fab customers. You will learn to isolate, expose, and image physical defects in advanced memory devices, analyze the results to help find the root cause, and present clear findings to engineering partners. Alongside your daily work in the lab, you will complete a focused improvement project during the 3-month internship and present the results at the end. You will set your priorities following the YE PFA queue, with guidance from a mentor engineer. Responsibilities and Tasks Physical Failure Analysis and Investigation Performs PFA sample preparation and analysis (e.g., deprocessing/delayering, cross-sectioning, FIB, SEM/TEM imaging) according to area skill guidelines. Reviews EFA results, fault isolation data, and probe/yield data to decide where to target the physical analysis. Identifies and categorizes physical defect signatures using defect references, and helps characterize new or unknown defect types. Performs data analysis to back up PFA results in pursuit of root cause. Summarizes findings in clear, concise reports (images, defect location, likely root cause) and communicates them to part owners and YE/Fab engineers. Lab Equipment Operation Learns to operate PFA lab equipment safely and efficiently, following defined safety and contamination-control guidelines. Builds an understanding of how the equipment works and supports basic troubleshooting with equipment owners. Internship Project and Continuous Improvement Owns a focused, short-term project that fits a 3-month timeline and presents the outcome to the team and leadership at the end of the internship. Completes all required safety and equipment training certifications defined by area guidelines. Builds technical knowledge of device structure, process flow, and failure mechanisms for current and future parts. Suggests improvements for the department and participates in team projects that support department and company objectives. AI-Enabled Analysis and Productivity Uses approved AI and digital productivity tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot) to work more efficiently on data analysis, image/report generation, knowledge retrieval, and problem-solving. Uses AI tools to speed up documentation, communication, and investigation workflows while keeping data accurate and applying engineering judgment. Uses AI technologies responsibly, following company policies, data protection requirements, and intellectual property safeguards. Schedule 3-month full-time internship, day shift (Monday–Friday). Education Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering, Physics, Chemical Engineering, or a related field. Qualifications Basic understanding of semiconductor devices and fabrication processes. Hands-on lab experience is a plus (e.g., microscopy, SEM/FIB, sample preparation, cleanroom). Strong attention to detail and good analytical and problem-solving skills. Clear written and verbal communication; able to summarize technical results simply. Familiarity with data tools (Excel, JMP, Python, etc.) is preferred. Experience No prior industry experience required. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Co-Op (Spring Co-Op)
jobs.body: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW REGENT's mechanical team is in the middle of a defining stretch of work: carrying Squire, our production Seaglider, through a full design and release cycle, while simultaneously shaping Viceroy from early concept into preliminary design. As a Mechanical Engineering Co-Op, you'll be dropped right into both efforts — designing parts in CAD, producing drawings, and supporting release on a vehicle headed toward production, while also contributing iterative design work on a program that's still taking shape. This isn't an adjacent, watch-and-learn co-op experience; you'll be trusted with real parts, real drawings, and real ownership from day one. You'll join Hardware Engineering's Mechanical team, helping take Squire from prototype to production. The fast-moving team values sound judgment in early design and disciplined production execution. If you have a foundation in mechanical design and assembly complexity and want ownership of flight hardware bound for the water, this role could shape your education or launch a career building Seagliders that will reinvent coastal transportation. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Design and Release Squire Hardware: You'll design mechanical parts in CAD and carry them through release, stepping into a production cycle where your drawings become real hardware on REGENT's Seaglider platform. It's the kind of direct contribution that goes well beyond a typical co-op assignment. - Help Shape Viceroy From Concept Forward: You'll jump into Viceroy while it's still being defined, doing the iterative CAD work that shapes a vehicle's geometry before anything is locked in. Bring solid engineering instincts and your early ideas will hold up, not get reworked from scratch. - Draft With Precision: A large part of your time will go toward engineering drawings and tolerancing, turning design intent into documentation our team and manufacturing partners can actually build from. If you already have a good eye for drafting, this is where it gets put to work immediately. - Support Manufacturing and Integration: You'll work alongside technicians during build and integration, helping fit checks go smoothly and feeding what you learn on the floor straight back into your CAD models. It's a fast feedback loop that sharpens your design judgment quickly. - Own Systems End to End: You'll take a reasonably scoped project from concept through integration, with support from senior engineers, and build toward real ownership of at least one system on the vehicle. By the end, you'll have a portfolio of work that stands on its own, whether you're headed back to finish school or straight into a full-time role. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Comfort Inside Complex Systems: Whether it came from an internship, a competition team, or a school project that got surprisingly real, you've worked inside assemblies where parts depend on each other. You're used to thinking several components deep instead of in isolation. - CAD as Second Nature: You're comfortable living in CAD day to day, not just opening it when a class requires it. Whatever your tool of choice, you pick up new CAD environments quickly. - An Eye for Drawings: You've spent real time with engineering drawings and tolerancing, enough to know that a good drawing is what keeps a part's design intent alive once it leaves your screen and heads to manufacturing. - Instincts That Hold Up: You have a working sense of load paths, material choices, and how manufacturing methods shape part design. That means your early ideas are something the team can build on, not something they have to rebuild. - Steady Under Ambiguity: You're not thrown off by incomplete information or a plan that's still taking shape. You can make a reasonable call, move forward, and adjust as new information comes in. - A Builder's Instinct: If you've spent time in a machine shop or messing around with rapid prototyping, you know the value of walking over, testing a quick fit, and bringing what you learn straight back into the model. That loop matters a lot while Viceroy is still taking shape. - Real Pull Toward Vehicles: You're genuinely into aerospace, marine, or vehicle programs, not just checking a box for your resume. You'll be helping shape hardware on a Seaglider headed toward production, and that should be exactly the kind of thing that gets you excited to show up. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You're passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineering Intern-3
jobs.body: Be a part of our mission! As a world leader in creating comfortable, sustainable, and efficient climate solutions for buildings, homes and transportation, it's our responsibility to put the planet first. For us at Trane Technologies , and through our businesses including Trane® and Thermo King , sustainability is not just how we do business—it is our business. Do you dare to look at the world's challenges and see impactful possibilities? Do you want to contribute to making a better future? If the answer is yes, we invite you to consider joining us in boldly challenging what's possible for a sustainable world. Learn about our benefits designed for you to Thrive at work and at home. We boldly go. Where is the work: On-Site (5 days) Position Description The Manufacturing Engineering Intern will work directly with manufacturing engineers, production personnel, quality teams, and maintenance technicians to support assembly operations and continuous improvement initiatives. This hands-on position provides practical experience in manufacturing processes, problem-solving, process improvement, and production support within a fast-paced assembly environment. The intern will spend significant time on the manufacturing floor learning production processes, assisting with engineering projects, collecting data, and supporting efforts to improve safety, quality, productivity, and efficiency. Key Responsibilities Production Support - Assist manufacturing engineers in supporting daily assembly operations. - Observe and document manufacturing processes and workflows. - Help troubleshoot production issues and support implementation of corrective actions. - Assist with updating work instructions, process documentation, and assembly procedures. Continuous Improvement - Participate in Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement projects. - Collect and analyze production data to identify opportunities for improvement. - Assist with time studies, workflow analysis, and line balancing activities. - Support implementation of process improvements and error-proofing solutions. jobs.title: Internship- Product Engineer Computational Model

jobs.title: 2027 Industrial Engineer Intern
jobs.location: Ashville, Ohio, United States; Costa Mesa, California, United States
jobs.body: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. Anduril is seeking Industrial Engineering Interns to join our summer internship program. The Manufacturing Engineering organization is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware, including static equipment, moving ground equipment, sensors, undersea, and flight vehicles, and scaling these products in our new 5M sq ft manufacturing facility, Arsenal-1. As an IE intern, you will work alongside a team of Industrial Engineers who will provide guidance and mentorship while you work to optimize Anduril’s manufacturing operations for best-in-class quality, reliability, speed, and asset utilization. The Industrial Engineering Intern will take a data-driven approach to designing production lines and associated manufacturing processes to meet these objectives. In this role, you will work on a summer-long project where you will be required to actively collaborate with and prepare presentations to various Anduril teams including but not limited to Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Analytics, and Quality. WHAT YOU’LL DO Own and lead projects to optimize and improve systems, processes, and manufacturing operations, leveraging a data driven approach. Proactively identify opportunities for improvement including high variation processes, imbalances and bottlenecks caused by line layout, equipment constraints, staffing shortages. Work with the appropriate owners across Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Quality to prioritize and drive to resolution. Translate and drive action from metrics, KPIs, and reporting associated with production line health and efficiency, such as cycle time, throughput rate, capacity, utilization, and first pass yield. Produce and maintain capacity plans, balanced line layouts, staffing allocations, and time standards for manufacturing work content. Work across domains, from execution-based work to the strategic future state of a product or business line. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Industrial Engineering or any related field. Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester. Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. Ability to complete an in-person 12-week internship in one of our offices in summer 2027. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Prior work designing and/or setting up new production lines or factories - from process mapping through to collaborating with infrastructure design partners and detailed workstation design Prior work or project experience with engineering design software, such as AutoCad or LucidChart, to develop factory layouts & support line balancing exercises Prior work or project experience conducting manufacturing time studies Experience with Lean Manufacturing and/or Continuous Improvement and Six Sigma principles either through previous coursework or in practice Experience interacting with data via data visualization applications or SQL queries Ability to completely own a value chain from start to finish, measuring each step of the process, creating actionable tasks that culminated in a significant and sustainable business improvement Prior experience with ERP, WMS and MES systems Prior experience with production process simulation using Discrete Event Simulation software (PlantSim, Simio, FlexSim, or similar) Prior work experience or project experience applying Industrial Engineering / Lean Methodologies Ability to read technical documentation such as facility drawings, assembly drawings, technical specifications and procedures for manufacturing processes for electronics, mechanical and electromechanical assembly, system tests, and/or structures work Ability to work through ambiguity and be a self-starter Motivated to plan aggressively, accept challenges, take responsibility for assignments, and deliver objectives on time Strong skills - especially in areas of teamwork, drive for results, and business acumen US Hourly Range $28 — $40 USD The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. jobs.title: Mission Integration Engineer Internship (Spring or Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Spacecraft represent the most pressing unmet need across the entire aerospace industry. As more launch vehicles come online and the cost to orbit decreases, more companies launching payloads to space continue to emerge. For the first time in history, this influx of payload companies combined with reduced launch costs has resulted in a massive increase in need for commercial spacecraft platforms, known as satellite buses. These buses hold the payloads of our customers and are flown on launch vehicles. Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. Our spacecraft enable the future of society: ranging from earth observation to communications and more. We’d love for you to join us on our mission of providing humankind access to the galaxy beyond our planet. ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking talented engineering students to work closely with Apex’s Mission Integration team for an exciting internship opportunity. This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about space systems, eager to understand how spacecraft, launch vehicles, and ground systems come together, and motivated to learn how real missions are designed, integrated, and flown. As a Mission Integration Engineer Intern, you will support system-level mission planning and integration activities across active programs. You’ll gain exposure to end-to-end mission architecture, customer requirements, and cross-functional engineering collaboration. This role offers a unique opportunity to approach complex mission challenges from a systems perspective, with a focus on reliability, performance, and mission success. INTERNSHIP EXPERIENCE AT APEX During the internship program at Apex, you’ll gain hands-on experience and meaningful professional growth. You’ll be assigned a mission-focused summer project that allows you to contribute directly to real spacecraft programs. Throughout the project, you’ll work closely with a dedicated mentor from the Mission Integration team while participating in technical learning sessions designed to deepen your understanding of satellite systems, launch environments, and mission operations. You’ll also connect with fellow interns and Apex engineers through community events and team activities, making this a well-rounded experience designed to launch your career in aerospace systems engineering. MISSION INTEGRATION ENGINEERING: INTERNSHIP FOCUS Mission Integration Engineer Interns will assist with system-level mission integration activities across spacecraft programs. Responsibilities may include: - Supporting mission architecture definition across spacecraft, launch vehicle, and operations elements - Assisting with mission analysis tasks such as orbital mechanics, deployment concepts, and trajectory trade studies - Helping generate and maintain mission-specific technical budgets (mass, power, data, pointing, etc.) - Supporting requirements analysis, verification, and validation activities - Assisting in the development of technical documentation, interface definitions, and integration procedures - Collaborating with mechanical, electrical, software, and operations teams to ensure system compatibility - Participating in internal design reviews, customer meetings, and technical discussions - Learning how technical risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated at the system level This role emphasizes systems thinking, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and clear technical communication. REQUIREMENTS - Graduating in Fall 2027 or Spring 2028 - Pursuing a BS or MS in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field - Strong interest in spacecraft systems, mission design, and space operations - Coursework or project experience related to orbital mechanics, space systems, or systems engineering preferred - Familiarity with tools such as Python, MATLAB, STK, GMAT, or similar analysis tools is a plus - Strong organizational skills and attention to detail - Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly and work effectively in a team environment - U.S. Person status required due to access to export-controlled data COMMITMENT This internship will begin in March 2027 or June 2027 and offers both full-time (40 hours/week) and part-time (minimum 20 hours/week) options. - Full-time interns should be available to pause or adjust academic commitments (such as taking a semester off or enrolling part-time) for the duration of the 10–12 week program - Part-time interns must maintain consistent availability during standard business hours to collaborate with their teams COMPENSATION $45/hour #LI-RC1 WHY JOIN APEX? Apex believes in creating a work environment that you look forward to embracing every day. Our employees love working at Apex, and we want you to love it too. We're a fast-growing startup that has raised more than $500M in funding, and we invest heavily in our people from day one. WHAT WE OFFER FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES: - Shared upside: Receive equity in Apex, letting you benefit from the work you create - Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision for you and your dependents, plus $100k life insurance at no cost - Comprehensive PTO package: Starting at 15 days vacation, growing to 20+ days annually, plus 10 paid holidays - Competitive 401(k) plan: Generous matching - 100% match on first 3%, 50% on next 2% - 8 weeks paid parental leave: Plus childcare reimbursement up to $350/day for work-related travel - Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks: To keep you fueled throughout the day - Vibrant community: Monthly office socials, pickleball tournaments, run club, and gatherings for you and your family - Your dream desk setup: All the tools you need to be your most productive self - World-class Playa Vista office: With the benefit of in-person collaboration with amazing coworkers and flexibility to integrate work and life - Real impact opportunity: Work alongside experts from aerospace, new space, and other cutting-edge industries to make a lasting difference ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Compensation ranges are set by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. A candidate's specific level and base pay are determined case by case and may vary with job-related skills, education, experience, technical capabilities, and internal equity. Beyond base salary, full-time hires are also eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options, along with medical, dental, and vision coverage and a 401(k) retirement plan. ITAR REQUIREMENTS Apex's work is governed by U.S. export control laws, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). To be eligible for this role, applicants must either (1) qualify as a U.S. Person, meaning a U.S. citizen or national, a lawful permanent resident (green card holder), a refugee admitted under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or an individual granted asylum under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or (2) be able to obtain the required export authorizations from the U.S. Department of State, the U.S. Department of Commerce, or another applicable U.S. government agency. You can learn more about ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineering Intern, CNC Machining (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: MANUFACTURING ENGINEERING INTERN, CNC MACHINING (SUMMER 2027) Freeform builds AI-native manufacturing systems that unify software, hardware, and physics to produce industrial-scale parts at the speed of human ideation. By treating manufacturing as a single integrated system, we unlock a new era of innovation where complex hardware is designed, built, and scaled without limits. As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern (CNC Machining), you will play a critical role in achieving Freeform’s goal of becoming the world leader in the manufacturing of high-value metal 3D printed parts. You will be responsible for developing, implementing, and optimizing CNC programs for precision machining operations as well as working closely with our engineers and machinist to establish machining standards for Freeform’s high-volume, vertically integrated machining workflow. You’ll use top of the line multi-axis machines - including DMG Mori and Haas - to develop complex geometries and refine machining processes for maximum efficiency, quality, and repeatability. The ideal candidate is highly technical, hands-on, and thrives in a fast-paced development environment. If you want to be at the forefront of the next era of manufacturing technology, we’d love to hear from you! 3D printing experience is not required to be successful here—we look for smart, motivated, and collaborative individuals who love tackling complex challenges and building world-class technology! Responsibilities: Assist in developing, implementing, and optimizing CNC programs for complex metal components, including post-processing of 3D printed parts Support programming, setup, and refinement of operations on multi-axis CNC machines (DMG Mori and Haas) Interpret CAD models, technical drawings, and GD&T specifications to help create precise machining programs Help select and evaluate cutting tools, speeds, feeds, and machining strategies for efficiency and repeatability Assist in troubleshooting CNC programming issues, collaborating with machinists and design engineers Help create, maintain, and update CNC program libraries, tool databases, best practices, and process documentation Contribute to process improvement projects that increase productivity, reduce cycle times, and improve machine utilization Collaborate with additive designers on custom workholding and help identify whether design or process changes are the right fix for a given issue Support the design and deployment of automation solutions that enhance quality control and production rates Work on the production floor to gain hands-on experience with machining, setup, and troubleshooting Follow quality control processes, industry standards, and safety regulations Own an intern project from scoping through implementation, and present results to the team at the end of the term Basic Qualifications: Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree in mechanical or aerospace engineering from an ABET accredited university or college Exposure to CNC programming and machining through coursework, labs, makerspace, internships, or collegiate engineering clubs (e.g., Formula SAE, Baja, rocketry, robotics) Familiarity with Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing Nice to Have: Experience with MasterCAM or Hypermill Experience with 5-axis machines Experience with DMG Mori and Siemens controls Experience machining hard metals such as titanium or Inconel Exposure to automation programming for probe alignment, in-situ quality checks, and adaptive process compensation based on measurement feedback Familiarity with metal 3D printed parts and their post-processing requirements Familiarity with machining castings or forgings Strong problem-solving skills and a hands-on approach to debugging machining processes Experience with quality control tools, including CMM, micrometers, and thread gauges Ability to work with power tools, hand tools, and other shop equipment (training provided for cranes, forklifts, and other heavy equipment) Comfortable lifting/moving up to 50 lbs and standing for extended periods Willingness to work extra hours when needed Location: Based in Hawthorne, our vertically integrated facility brings technology development, R&D, and production together under one roof. We operate at the center of LA’s deep tech ecosystem, surrounded by some of the most ambitious hardware innovation happening anywhere in the country. Our fast-paced, cross-functional environment is built on close collaboration, and as such, this role requires full-time onsite presence (five days a week), with very limited exceptions. What We Offer: We have an inclusive and diverse culture that values collaboration, learning, and making deliberate data-driven decisions We offer a unique opportunity to be an early and integral member of a rapidly growing company that is scaling a world-changing technology Compensation and Benefits The compensation for this role: Engineering Intern/Undergraduate: $30/hour Engineering Intern/Masters: $32.50/hour Engineering Intern/PhD: $35/hour Typical working weeks include regular opportunity for overtime Relocation assistance provided Free daily catered lunch and dinner, and fully stocked kitchenette Casual dress, flexible work hours, and regular catered team building events Freeform is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values diversity; employment with Freeform is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern - Research and Development - Energy and Propulsion Systems Architecture
jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.body: Job Description The Role: As a 2027 Summer Intern on the Energy and Propulsion Systems Architecture team, you will work with researchers and engineers to evaluate how energy storage and propulsion systems work together at the vehicle level. You will contribute to architecture studies, simulation and analysis activities, and laboratory testing that help inform the design and development of future electrified propulsion systems. This role offers hands-on exposure to the connection between battery cells, modules and packs, electric propulsion components, power electronics, controls, thermal systems, and vehicle performance. You will apply engineering fundamentals, data analysis, and systems thinking to turn test and simulation results into clear technical insights. The Team: The Research and Development organization explores and evaluates technologies that can improve vehicle energy efficiency, propulsion performance, durability, range, and customer experience. The Energy and Propulsion Systems Architecture team connects research, modeling, simulation, and laboratory experimentation to understand system-level behavior and guide architecture decisions. You will work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment with researchers and engineers across battery, propulsion, controls, thermal management, modeling, and vehicle development. The team values sound engineering judgment, careful experimentation, clear documentation, and the ability to communicate technical findings to both specialists and broader project teams. What You’ll Do: Support energy and propulsion systems architecture studies, including the evaluation of battery, electric machine, drive unit, power electronics, controls, and thermal-system interactions. Develop, run, and interpret vehicle-level propulsion and energy simulations across representative operating conditions and drive cycles. Analyze energy consumption, performance, power capability, operating limits, state-of-charge behavior, and other system-level measures to identify trends and architecture tradeoffs. Assist with cell, module, and battery-pack testing by helping prepare test activities, configure equipment or data acquisition, collect data, and maintain organized test records. Support laboratory work related to battery characterization, pack performance, durability, modeling, and analysis while following applicable laboratory safety and handling practices. Compare experimental results with model predictions, investigate differences, and help improve model assumptions, inputs, or analysis methods. Clean, process, visualize, and interpret test and simulation data; summarize results using clear plots, tables, and written technical explanations. Create or update system block diagrams, interface descriptions, requirements documentation, analysis scripts, test summaries, and technical presentations. Collaborate with researchers and engineers to define questions, document assumptions, review results, and recommend next steps. Present technical findings in team discussions and incorporate feedback into follow-on analyses. Required Qualifications: Pursuit of an advanced degree (MS or Phd) in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, chemical engineering, materials science and engineering, automotive engineering, aerospace engineering, systems engineering, or a related engineering discipline. Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months. Must be willing to work in a laboratory and engineering test environment. Preferred Qualifications: Coursework, research, or project experience in battery systems, electrochemistry, energy storage, electric propulsion, power electronics, controls, thermal systems, vehicle dynamics, or systems engineering. Experience with engineering modeling, simulation, or data analysis using MATLAB/Simulink, Python, Excel, or comparable tools. Experience processing time-series data and communicating technical results through plots, reports, or presentations. Laboratory, test, or instrumentation experience, including an understanding of experimental design, measurement quality, and safe work practices. Ability to organize technical work, manage multiple priorities, and work effectively with cross-functional teams. Strong written and verbal communication skills, curiosity, and a willingness to learn from both successful and unsuccessful experiments. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Michigan office three times per week, at minimum [or other frequency dictated by the business]. jobs.body: > Requirements & Architecture Engineering Co-op Reference #44070 Waterdown, Ontario About L3HARRIS WESCAM As a subsidiary of L3Harris Technologies and within the Integrated Mission Systems Segment, the WESCAM division develops the most advanced optical sensor and targeting systems for global defense and military sectors, National Security, Search & Rescue and Airborne law enforcement agencies. jobs.title: Undergraduate Engineering Intern - Additive Manufacturing
jobs.body: This undergraduate internship is a full-time position Summer-Fall 2027 (May or June through December) on site in Rochester, Minnesota. The primary purpose of the Undergraduate Engineer Internship is to provide an engineering student with relevant engineering experience. One or more mentors will be assigned to the intern to provide instruction, guidance and to assess performance, as well as be a technical resource for questions. The intern is responsible for learning the procedures and processes of the Division of Engineering and the assigned work unit. In addition, the intern will be given selected engineering work assignments to reinforce the learning experience and to provide benefit to the work unit. The engineering assignments may include designing components, developing a project strategy, gathering user needs, requirements and specifications, evaluating commercial components, prototyping, performing design verification and design validation, troubleshooting, and participating in design reviews. All assignments are within the context of the Division of Engineering Quality Management System (including safety risk management) and are performed in a multi-disciplinary development environment. The intern will be responsible for completing all internship-related assignments and reports for both Mayo and the participating educational facility (if applicable). The Additive Manufacturing (AM) intern will be assigned to the Additive Manufacturing Facility (AMF) in the Mechanical Fabrication Unit within the Division of Engineering (DOE). The Mechanical Fabrication Unit leverages mechanical designer, technician, machinist, and engineer expertise as part of DOE’s multidisciplinary approach to developing unique devices and systems for Mayo Clinic providers and researchers. The AMF, a dedicated Mayo Clinic 3D printing space, houses a titanium printer, a variety of polymer printers, and a suite of post-processing equipment. The parts fabricated here support the development of one-of-a-kind medical devices, laboratory instruments, and other products in service to Mayo Clinic patients. DOE designers, technicians, machinists, and engineers iteratively print concept models, functional prototypes, and end-use parts for projects undertaken at the request of Mayo Clinic staff members. The application of AM accelerates the development cycle from initial request through final product by providing parts for faster form, fit, and function evaluation. The candidate will collaborate with designers, technicians, and engineers, and project managers on a variety of project needs. Their project responsibilities will encompass computer-aided design (CAD) using SolidWorks, prototype development with AM, verification testing, and engineering documentation. They will receive guidance and work direction from one or more mentors assigned to them. The candidate will perform hands-on work with both metal and polymer additive manufacturing technologies and will take on tasks from their mentors, including the Additive Manufacturing Facility Coordinator, Metal Lead, and Polymer Lead.​​ The ideal candidate will have experience with 3D printing technologies using one or more feedstock types. Basic understanding of AM processes and material science is preferred. The incumbent must be enrolled in an engineering, management information systems, or other technology-related degree program from an accredited college or university and have completed a minimum of four semesters – or the equivalent – of instruction toward their degree. To be considered for this position please attach the following to your application: 3.3 GPA requirement or higher undergraduate transcript resume Applicants are strongly encouraged to include a cover letter Applicants are strongly encouraged to include a sample of academic work (e.g. screenshots of models or drawings, a lab report)

jobs.title: Research Intern - Extended Perception Interaction Cognition (EPIC)
jobs.body: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. This position is for a research internship with the EPIC (Extended Perception, Interaction & Cognition) research group in Microsoft Research’s Redmond Lab. We have multiple positions available. Research Internships will be focused on creating new interactive experiences that “blend artificial and human intelligence”. Topics range from coupling the power of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques with interaction design to reinvent how we work with content, to building the next generation of multi-modal interfaces adapting in real time to user tasks and contexts. Key skills sought for this internship include: Generative AI: Large Language Models (LLMs), Vision Language Models (VLMs), Stable Diffusion, video/world/action models, real-time models, multi-agent development, and related technologies Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) system building and agentic development: Experience building interactive prototypes with TypeScript, Node.js, and React, using coding agents and agentic workflows to accelerate development. Demonstrated programming and software architecture fundamentals are essential to guide agents, review generated code, and validate system behavior. Additional relevant skills (depending on projects): Interaction design: experience with devising multimodal interactions (touch, pen, speech), context sensing, responsive & adaptive User Interfaces (UIs) Experience design: storyboarding, envisioning video techniques User Experience (UX) research: conducting qualitative and quantitative user studies We value your ideas and unique viewpoints on these topics, as well, and hope that our partnership and collaboration will shape initial directions into exciting, ambitious, and impactful research contributions that only you could have crafted. The EPIC group conducts fundamental research that innovates at the nexus of hardware, software, and human potential. We are an interdisciplinary group of researchers, engineers, scientists, and designers at Microsoft Research who study Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) through prototyping, system-building, design sketching, and observational study of human behavior. You can learn more about the EPIC’s research agenda, publications, videos, and team members at EPIC - Microsoft Research , as well as the broader HCI-AI research area Future Experiences . Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science or related STEM field. Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit contact information of references so we may contact these references if needed Preferred Qualifications 1+ year(s) experience conducting original research in (or closely related to) Human-Computer Interaction, and further be able to document their research contributions with publicly available resources (e.g. by linking to papers, pre-prints, videos, demonstrations, repositories, articles, press coverage, or research proposals in your submitted CV). The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. jobs.title: Industrial Design Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.body: Stanley Black & Decker Intern – Industrial Design Intern Come build your career. It takes great people to achieve greatness. People with a sense of purpose and integrity. People with a relentless pursuit of excellence. People who care about making things better For Those Who Make The World™. Sound like you? Join our top-notch team of more than 50,000 diverse and high-performing professionals globally who are making their mark on some of the world’s most beloved brands, including DEWALT®, BLACK+DECKER®, CRAFTSMAN®, STANLEY®, CUB CADET®, and HUSTLER®. About Our Internship Program: Throughout your internship, you will have regular events, weekly lunch and learn sessions, and receive customized training from our business units. This is a unique opportunity to gain valuable insights into supporting the needs of Stanley Black & Decker both in the US and abroad. The interns will gain first-hand exposure to Stanley Black & Decker and have the opportunity to build a cross-functional professional network. Interns are expected to adapt to change and demonstrate strong interpersonal and communication skills, creativity, and confidence. Interns must be team-oriented and collaborative. The Job: During your internship, you will have the opportunity to support Industrial Design with key activities including: Assist in delivering new concept direction, brand-specific aesthetics, and optimized ergonomic solutions for all new product development across a wide range of global brands. Support other industrial designers by creating photorealistic renderings and animations of new product designs using 3D Cad and Keyshot Rendering software. Work with and support our UX/UI team. Projects will consist of on-product user interface, embedded displays, and digital applications. Help drive breakthrough industrial design advancement through to our customers on various projects, utilizing the best technology available for the process. Work with the Industrial Designers and other disciplines to create original designs that capture the desired intent of the team. You will have exposure to several areas of the Industrial Design at Stanley Black & Decker. You will work on a wide variety of tasks and projects with a cross-functional team of professionals. The Person: The ideal Industrial Design intern candidate will have the following qualifications: Be a rising junior or senior with a target graduation date of 2026 or 2027. A portfolio is required to be submitted to be considered for this role Actively pursuing a degree in Industrial Design, Product Design or related field. Maintains strong academic credentials. Experience in 2D analog /digital sketching and rendering (Cintiq, Photoshop, Sketchbook) Knowledge of parametric 3D modeling is a plus (CATIA, SolidWorks, Alias, Rhino, etc.) Successfully manages strong academics alongside extracurricular activities. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship (H1B, OPT/CPT, TN etc). The Details: This position will provide you with: A utility role interacting with key members of a Fortune 500 company. A flexible schedule featuring a max of 40 hours. Opportunity for career advancement upon graduation. Competitive compensation and career development opportunities. Industrial Design internships are available in the following locations: Towson, MD The Salary range for this position is $38,600.00 - $62,200.00 This is the lowest to highest annual full-time salary range we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. The salary offered within the range may vary depending on multiple factors including job level, geographic location, job-related knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience and in compliance with local wage requirements. Please note that salary is only one component of total rewards at Stanley Black & Decker. ​ The salary range listed in this job posting reflects the range for the primary location specified. The salary range may vary for other locations.​ The successful candidate may be eligible for annual merit increases. ​ Medical, dental, life, vision, disability,401(k), Employee Stock Purchase Plan, paid time off, and tuition reimbursement in addition to programs & benefits in support of your well-being. ​ Discounts on Stanley Black & Decker tool sand other partner programs. We Don’t Just Build The World, We Build Innovative Technology Too. Joining the Stanley Black & Decker team means working in an innovative, tech-driven and highly collaborative team environment supported by over 43,500 professionals in 60 countries across the globe. Here, you’ll get the unique chance to impact some of the world’s most iconic brands including STANLEY TOOLS, DEWALT, CRAFTSMAN, MAC TOOLS and Black + Decker. Your ideas and solutions have the potential to reach millions of customers as we work together to write the next chapter in our history. Come build with us and take your career to new heights. Who We Are We’re the World’s largest tool company. We’re industry visionaries. We’re solving problems and advancing the manufacturing trade through innovative technology and our Industry 4.0 Initiative. We are committed to ensuring our state-of-the-art “smart factory” products and services provide greater quality to our customers & greater environmental and social value to our planet. We are unique in that we have a rich and storied history dating back to 1843, but that hasn't stopped us from evolving into a vibrant, diverse, global growth company. Being part of our global company with 60+ brands gives you the chance to grow and develop your skills along multiple career paths. You’ll find we like to have fun here, too.
