jobs.title: Summer 2027 Internship - Quality Assurance Engineer - Washington -
jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will : ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting ​ Implement new ideas , be constantly challenged, and develop your skills ​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business ​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture ​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions. ​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward. ​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts. ​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives . ​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships. ​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​ As a Quality Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams: Advanced Quality ​ AQE interns work on engineering projects related to development of new products. Areas of emphasis may include human factors engineering, risk management, application of statistics, reliability engineering, design verification, and design validation including customer interaction. As Homer Stryker pointed out, “If your tools don’t work, make them work. If you can’t make them work, make some that do work.” In this directive, the AQE team works to make sure that the products we develop at Stryker will work consistently for our customers to meet or exceed their expectations. ​ ​​ Process Quality ​ PQE interns collaborate with cross-functional teams to support product sustainment. When non-conforming issues arise in production, it is our responsibility to perform robust root cause analysis and implement effective corrective actions. Do you enjoy deep dive investigations and driving collaboration and communication to achieve issue resolution? If so, you may be a great fit for this team! PQE interns are focused on quality, compliance and continuous improvement. They use their education to work with a variety of tools including CAD for fixture design, root cause analysis methods, LabView, and validation activities to optimize production, inspection, and quality system processes. ​ ​ Supplier Quality ​ SQE interns are responsible for all things supplier-related . Stryker uses a number of critical suppliers to manufacture components and finished products, and to provide critical services. This team’s job is to work closely with the suppliers to ensure components and their manufacturing processes meet our required standards. Do you enjoy using your technical background and communication skills to influence suppliers? If so, you might be a great fit for this diverse and talented team! The role requires working closely with internal customers from multiple functions, meeting with suppliers frequently , and the use of both technical and business skills. ​ ​ Quality ​ Quality interns work with our internal cross-functional teams and external sales team and customers to ensure we develop and sustain a product with the highest quality. The team’s job is to ensure we develop the right products up front – evaluate risk, ensure our customer’s user needs are met, and help drive craftsmanship, safety, durability and reliability into the product. On the post-market side, they also work closely with regulatory to handle any complaints and implement design changes, as needed, to address quality issues. The role requires someone who has great communication, problem-solving, and technical skills. Majors Targeted: Quality Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering , Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related majors . What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship . ​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above ( verified at time of hire ) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future . ​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment . $20 min hourly wage – $35 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. Stryker is an EO employer – M/F/Veteran/Disability. Stryker Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor’s legal duty to furnish information.

jobs.title: Internship Mechatronics Engineer
jobs.body: > About VAT Group At VAT, we change the world with vacuum solutions. As the world’s leading supplier of high-performance vacuum valves, we have been driving innovation for more than 60 years. With over 3,200 employees worldwide, we operate from our headquarters in Haag, Switzerland, with manufacturing sites in Switzerland, Malaysia and Romania, as well as sales and service hubs around the world. We are guided by our passions: integrity, teamwork, customer centricity, and innovation – always working together as #oneVAT. Joining us means becoming part of a passionate, international team where your voice is heard, your ideas matter, and your career growth is supported. Purpose of the role As an intern, you will develop an automated controller tuning platform for motion control applications. The objective is to create a complete workflow where a PLC automatically executes experiments on a valve actuator, collects measurement data, and transfers it to a Python-based auto-tuning algorithm. The algorithm will identify the system dynamics, calculate optimized controller parameters, and automatically feed them back to the motion controller. The resulting solution will enable efficient, repeatable, and robust tuning of industrial motion control systems with minimal user intervention. Responsibilities Develop an automated motion control tuning platform for stepper and BLDC motor applications. Develop PLC software to execute measurement campaigns, collect experimental data, and control the testing workflow. Implement Python-based algorithms for system identification and automatic controller tuning. Establish an end-to-end workflow where tuning parameters are automatically generated and fed back to the motion controller. Define and implement standardized validation procedures to evaluate the performance and robustness of the tuning results. Create technical documentation covering system architecture, algorithms, test procedures, and user guidelines. Your competencies acquired at the end of the internship This internship is designed to provide you with practical experience in motion control, automation, and algorithm development within an industrial environment. As part of our R&D team, you will work on a real-world challenge: developing an automated controller tuning platform for valve actuation systems. By the end of the internship, you will have acquired the following competencies: Control Engineering Skills: Gain practical experience in system identification, controller tuning, motion control, and dynamic system analysis for stepper and BLDC motor applications. Software Development Skills: Develop PLC and Python programming skills by creating an end-to-end workflow for automated experimentation, data acquisition, and controller optimization. Automation & Testing Skills: Learn how to design and implement automated test procedures, ensuring repeatable and robust validation of control algorithms in an industrial environment. Data Analysis Skills: Acquire the ability to process measurement data, evaluate system performance, and develop data-driven solutions for real-world engineering problems. Problem-Solving Skills: Apply a structured engineering approach to diagnose system behaviour, identify improvement opportunities, and develop innovative solutions to complex control challenges. Communication Skills: Gain experience in documenting technical work, presenting project results, and discussing technical solutions with experts from different engineering disciplines. Collaboration Skills: Work closely with specialists in software, automation, electronics, and mechatronics, contributing to a multidisciplinary development project. Industry Experience: Gain insight into the development of advanced motion control solutions within the semiconductor industry, from concept development and algorithm design to implementation, testing, and validation in a commercial product environment. Qualifications Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechatronics, Robotics, Automation Engineering, or a related field. Solid understanding of control theory, electrical machines, and mechatronic systems. Strong programming skills in PLCs and Python. Creative and solution-oriented team player with a hands-on, structured, and systematic approach to problem-solving. Good written and spoken English. Our commitment to inclusion, fairness and equal opportunities We believe in meaningful careers, continuous learning, and equal opportunities for everyone to drive our innovation and success. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace. If you have concerns, our compliance channel is available at our website. All reports are handled with strict confidentiality and in accordance with our Code of Conduct . <span

jobs.title: Internship- Co-Op: AI Engineer
jobs.body: Co-Op: AI Engineer Organization: IT & Data, Chief Data Office US Location: United States, hybrid Employment Type: College Co-Op Job Mission As a AI Engineer Co-Op at ASML, you will help develop data pipelines and data products that transform laser-machine and enterprise data into trusted, usable information. Working with experienced data engineers, data architects, IT specialists, and business stakeholders, you will contribute to technical solutions that support product capabilities, analytics, AI, system performance, and ultimately customer satisfaction. This role provides an opportunity to work with complex, high-value data in a collaborative engineering environment while learning how modern data solutions are designed, tested, deployed, documented, and operated at enterprise scale. Job Description As a member of the CDO US team, you will: Develop and enhance data pipeline solutions that contribute to product features, technical roadmaps, analytics, and AI use cases. Build data ingestion, transformation, validation, and integration processes for laser-machine and enterprise data. Contribute to automated continuous data integration pipelines used to build, test, and release data solutions. Develop and optimize SQL transformations, data models, and analytical datasets. Apply systematic problem-solving to identify root causes, resolve technical issues, and standardize reusable solutions. Collaborate with cross-functional engineering and business teams on system design changes and improvements to system performance. Work with business users to understand requirements and translate business goals into feasible technical solutions. Collaborate with data architects, software engineers, AI engineers, and IT team members to achieve shared project goals. Help improve data quality, observability, monitoring, lineage, and governance. Apply industry practices for code quality, automated testing, version control, maintainability, and technical documentation. Refactor and improve existing code so that legacy and modern systems can coexist during technology transitions. Participate in code reviews, technical design discussions, agile delivery activities, and continuous improvement. Document data pipelines, interfaces, data models, decisions, dependencies, and operating procedures. Contribute reusable data components and engineering patterns that can support multiple teams and use cases. Education and Experience Must be pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Engineering, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or a related field. Knowledge of or experience with Python, SQL, Java, or a comparable programming language. Knowledge of relational databases, data modeling, and data integration concepts. Familiarity with Databricks, SQL Server, or other database and data-platform technologies. Familiarity with Microsoft Azure or another cloud environment. Exposure to ETL/ELT development, data pipelines, or analytical data processing. Academic, personal, or professional project experience performing data engineering or similar work. Familiarity with Git, automated testing, CI/CD, or modern software-development practices is preferred. Experience with data quality, pipeline monitoring, or data visualization is a plus. Skills and Competencies Strong customer focus and a commitment to customer satisfaction through quality, prioritization, efficiency, and professionalism. Strong numerical, analytical, and structured problem-solving skills. Ability to decompose complex problems, clarify requirements, and propose feasible solutions. Attention to detail and the ability to complete assignments with a high degree of accuracy. Ownership and accountability for assigned work, including raising risks and following through on commitments. Ability to perform effectively in a demanding environment with changing priorities and workloads. Open, clear, concise, and professional communication. Ability to establish cooperative working relationships with colleagues, technical teams, and business stakeholders. Willingness to seek feedback, learn new technologies, and continuously improve. Understanding of the importance of code health, testing, maintainability, and documentation. Ability to balance immediate delivery needs with the development of scalable and reusable solutions. What Success Looks Like During the co-op, you will have the opportunity to: Deliver working data pipelines, transformations, or data products that contribute to real business or engineering outcomes. Improve the quality, reliability, accessibility, or maintainability of data used by internal teams. Demonstrate disciplined engineering through testing, documentation, code reviews, and version control. Translate a defined business or engineering need into a practical technical solution. Collaborate effectively across data, IT, engineering, analytics, and AI teams. Develop reusable solutions rather than addressing each technical problem in isolation. Build practical experience with enterprise data platforms, cloud technology, and production-oriented engineering. Team Culture The CDO US team works across organizational and technical boundaries to turn data into scalable business and engineering value. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon. jobs.body: The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space. The Aerospace Corporation is hiring a Communication Architectures Modeling and Analysis Engineering Grad Intern for the Communication Architectures Department (CAD) within the Mission Payloads Division (MPD). Position will be full-time and 100% onsite at our office in El Segundo, CA. Job Summary At the Mission Payloads Division (MPD), we are pioneers in remote sensing systems that guide our country’s space enterprise. Our talented and dynamic people create and flourish in electronics, sensors, radar, artificial intelligence (AI), and advanced data network domains. We boldly advance technology through our research and development and then forward to demonstration and integration. With innovative laboratories and prototyping, MPD delivers groundbreaking results. We guide our Department of Defense, intelligence community, and civil clients to enhance national productivity and security and tackle the most critical missions. Bring your intelligence and creative spirit and join us at MPD! CAD also guides the development of spectrum regulations and policies to assure critical wireless systems have access to necessary spectrum resources. Finally, we are actively engaged in the development of RF communications prototypes, especially those involving commercial LEO satellite systems. jobs.title: 2027 Library Science Intern
jobs.body: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. ABOUT THE TEAM Anduril's Maritime Division is transforming American sea power to meet the defining national security challenges of our era and secure our future of maritime dominance. We are scaling at an historic pace, anchored by Arsenal-2, our new software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base. Arsenal-2 is purpose-built to break long-standing industrial bottlenecks and scale production of critical components for the Navy's Virginia-class attack submarines to support fleet requirements. At the same time, it will build the industrial muscle to field our next-generation AUVs at scale. We aren't waiting for the new shipyard to be completed. The work on this transformation starts right now, with development inside our new 160,000 square foot Proto-Factory in Orange County, California, where the team is already laying the foundation. As the prototyping hub for Arsenal-2, this facility gives us a multi-year head start, proving out the advanced manufacturing methods, digital workflows, and quality systems that will scale across our broader shipyard network. In Anduril's Maritime Division, we are actively building America's next decisive advantage at sea, and this is the moment to join us. ABOUT THE JOB Maritime Digital Production builds the digital systems behind Anduril's maritime build chain: data pipelines, contextualization layers, workflow and execution tools, applied intelligence, and the interfaces between OT and IT. Everything we build has to survive production constraints, which means real crews, real equipment, and real disruption. Raw data off the factory floor doesn't mean much on its own. A tag reading PLC4_TT_1142 tells you nothing until someone establishes that it's a temperature sensor, on a specific machine, in a specific cell, measuring a specific process step. Doing that for thousands of signals is a cataloging problem before it's an engineering one. That's the job. You'll build the vocabularies, hierarchies, and metadata standards that give factory data meaning, working alongside data engineers and manufacturing engineers who need the structure and don't have the training to build it. If you like building a taxonomy and want to see one used somewhere other than a library, this is that. WHAT YOU'LL DO Develop and maintain controlled vocabularies for equipment, materials, processes, and locations across the build chain. Build asset hierarchies and naming conventions that structure plant-floor data into a consistent model. Write and apply metadata schemas for industrial data sources, documenting what each field means and how it should be used. Catalog data sources and maintain entries in the team's data catalog, including provenance and ownership. Audit existing tags and data models for inconsistency and gaps and propose corrections. Document standards and authoring guidelines so naming decisions stay consistent after you leave. Work with data and manufacturing engineers to check that the models match how work actually happens on the floor. Present your work to the team at the end of the session. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Library Science, Information Science, Knowledge Management, Archival Studies, Linguistics, or a related field. Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester. Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. Ability to complete a 12 week in-person internship in one of our offices in summer 2027. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Coursework or project experience in metadata, cataloging, taxonomy, controlled vocabularies, or classification systems. Attention to detail, and patience for working through ambiguity toward a consistent structure. Clear writing, particularly for documentation meant to outlast its author. Familiarity with metadata standards and modeling approaches (Dublin Core, SKOS, RDF, OWL, or similar). Exposure to data catalog tooling, knowledge graphs, or ontology editors such as Protégé. Basic scripting in Python or SQL for inspecting and transforming data. Interest in manufacturing and the physical systems behind the data. Coursework in digital curation, data governance, or information architecture. US Hourly Range $24 — $40 USD The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: Benefits At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits . Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information. To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind: No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates. Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links. What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts. Data Privacy To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ . By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.body: Overview Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do. Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers. We are seeking a motivated engineering intern to support the implementation of Smart Visual Inspection within our Austin Order Fulfillment and packaging operations. The intern will work with engineering, operations, quality, and production teams to develop and validate a computer-vision-enabled inspection process for packaging and finished-product verification. The internship will provide hands-on experience with smart manufacturing, computer vision, machine learning, manufacturing process improvement, inspection-system development, and operational deployment. The intern will help convert existing inspection requirements into repeatable digital workflows, develop image datasets, configure inspection recipes, validate model performance, optimize camera and lighting conditions, and document the solution for production use. The Smart Visual Inspection platform enables engineers to create guided inspection procedures, train and deploy AI models, provide immediate pass/fail feedback, and capture inspection results for traceability. The Austin proof of concept will initially focus on pack-out applications such as verifying product accessories, quantities, text, labels, orientation, and packaging contents Responsibilities Assist with the development and implementation of Smart Visual Inspection solutions for Order Fulfillment, packaging, and finished-product inspection. Study current inspection and pack-out processes, identify improvement opportunities, and translate operational requirements into structured inspection workflows. Work with engineers and production personnel to identify representative products and packaging configurations for proof-of-concept testing. Capture, organize, and maintain image datasets under representative operating conditions. Label and annotate images used for computer-vision model training. Safely move, position, and prepare product cartons and packaging materials while capturing images from multiple angles for computer-vision model development and validation. Develop and maintain digital inspection procedures and inspection recipes. Train and test computer-vision models for applications such as: Object presence and absence verification Quantity verification Packaging-content validation Label and text recognition Product-position and orientation checks Region-based classification Evaluate model performance and help adjust confidence thresholds to balance false accepts and false rejects. Conduct controlled tests using representative products, packaging materials, accessories, labels, and configurations. Support the setup and optimization of cameras, fixtures, workstations, backgrounds, and diffuse lighting. Evaluate how camera position, lighting, glare, shadows, object placement, and image quality affect inspection reliability. Record test results, model performance, inspection exceptions, process times, and identified improvement opportunities. Assist with root-cause analysis and troubleshooting when an inspection process produces inconsistent or unexpected results. Develop standard operating procedures, work instructions, training materials, and technical documentation. Support operator training and collect feedback during pilot deployment. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to incorporate operational feedback and improve the inspection process. Help establish a repeatable process for maintaining inspection procedures, trained models, configuration files, and revision history. Present project status, technical findings, validation results, and final recommendations to engineering and operations stakeholders. These responsibilities reflect the project’s documented needs around image capture and annotation, model training, validation thresholds, camera and lighting consistency, inspection-workflow development, traceability, and pack-out verification Qualifications Required: Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in: Industrial Engineering Manufacturing Engineering Mechanical Engineering Robotics, Automation, or a related technical discipline Basic understanding of manufacturing, engineering, quality, automation, computer vision, or data-analysis concepts. Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills. Ability to collect, organize, analyze, and clearly present technical data. Ability to follow defined test methods and accurately document results. Ability to work effectively in a hands-on manufacturing or operations environment. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to collaborate with engineers, operators, quality personnel, and other cross-functional stakeholders. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Willingness to learn new software tools, inspection methods, and manufacturing processes. Ability to manage assigned tasks with appropriate guidance and communicate progress, risks, and technical issues. Ability to occasionally lift and move boxes weighing up to 50 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation, as needed to position products and packaging materials for image capture, model training, and inspection testing. Preferred Qualifications: Coursework or project experience in one or more of the following: Computer vision Machine learning Image processing Industrial automation Robotics Manufacturing systems Quality engineering Operations research Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma Data analytics Experience using Python, MATLAB, OpenCV, or another analytical or image-processing tool. Experience collecting, cleaning, labeling, or analyzing image datasets. Familiarity with object detection, optical character recognition, classification, or anomaly-detection concepts. jobs.title: Intern - Design Engineer, HBM
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. At Micron Technology, our High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Engineering team develops advanced memory solutions that enable next-generation Artificial Intelligence, machine learning, and high-performance computing applications. The team collaborates with global design, verification, validation, and product engineering organizations to deliver innovative semiconductor technologies that power data centers and intelligent systems worldwide. As a member of this team, you will contribute to the development of industry-leading memory solutions that support the evolving needs of AI-enabled computing. As an HBM Design Engineer Intern, you will work alongside experienced engineers to support the design verification and validation of advanced HBM products. This internship provides hands-on experience with industry-standard verification methodologies, simulation environments, debugging techniques, and semiconductor development processes. You will contribute to real product development efforts while building foundational skills in digital design, verification, and AI-supported computing technologies. Responsibilities Support verification of HBM designs by developing and executing simulation test plans to validate functionality, performance, and timing requirements. Analyze design specifications and assist in creating verification strategies using industry-standard design and verification methodologies. Debug design and verification issues in collaboration with design, verification, validation, and product engineering teams. Develop, enhance, and maintain verification environments using hardware description languages and verification tools. Collaborate with global engineering teams developing memory solutions that enable Artificial Intelligence (AI), machine learning, and advanced computing applications, and leverage AI-assisted tools where appropriate to improve engineering productivity and workflow efficiency. Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, and must remain enrolled throughout the internship period. Demonstrated knowledge of transistor-level circuits, CMOS fundamentals, and digital logic design principles through coursework, projects, or research. Experience using Verilog, SystemVerilog, or other hardware description languages through academic projects, research, or industry experience. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills with the ability to learn and apply new technologies quickly. Demonstrated communication, teamwork, and leadership skills through academic, project, research, or extracurricular experiences. Preferred Qualifications Coursework or project experience in semiconductor design verification, digital integrated circuit design, computer architecture, or memory systems. Experience with simulation, debugging, waveform analysis, or industry-standard verification methodologies and tools. Familiarity with scripting languages such as Python, Perl, or Tcl to support automation and verification workflows. Exposure to AI-enabled, AI-assisted, or Artificial Intelligence applications through coursework, research, or technical projects. Experience working in collaborative team environments and delivering technical results through complex engineering projects. jobs.title: Intern - Next-Generation HBM Architecture
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. The Memory Systems Architecture team defines the next generation of High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) solutions that power artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, and data center applications. The team drives architectural innovation across memory systems, controllers, interfaces, and reliability features to deliver industry-leading performance, scalability, and efficiency for future computing platforms. As a Memory Systems Architecture Intern, you will contribute to the architecture and microarchitecture development of future HBM products. You will work alongside experienced architects to evaluate new memory features, analyze architectural trade-offs, develop performance models, and explore solutions that improve memory performance, reliability, and efficiency for AI and high-performance computing workloads. Responsibilities Research and evaluate next-generation HBM architecture and microarchitecture features, including memory scheduling, refresh management, reliability features, thermal behavior, and memory controller interactions. Develop and enhance performance models, simulators, and analytical tools using Python, C++, or similar technologies to assess architectural trade-offs and system performance. Analyze workload behavior, simulation results, and architectural data to provide recommendations for future HBM product development. Utilize AI-assisted engineering tools and workflows to accelerate software development, specification analysis, data exploration, and technical documentation while validating outputs using sound engineering judgment. Collaborate with architecture, design, memory controller, and cross-functional engineering teams to support feature definition, design reviews, specifications, and roadmap development. Minimum Qualifications 0-2 years of relevant experience through internships, research, academic projects, publications, or coursework in computer architecture, memory systems, VLSI, semiconductor design, or related technical fields. Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Coursework or project experience in computer architecture, memory hierarchies, DRAM technologies, interconnects, or hardware system design. Programming experience with Python and at least one of the following: C++, SystemVerilog, or similar engineering languages. Ability to read and interpret technical specifications, standards documentation, datasheets, or hardware interface definitions. Strong analytical, problem-solving, written, and verbal communication skills. Experience utilizing AI coding assistants and large language models (LLMs) such as GitHub Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, or similar technologies as part of engineering workflows. Preferred Qualifications Experience with memory or system simulation environments such as Ramulator, DRAMSim, gem5, or related architectural modeling tools. Knowledge of HBM, DDR, LPDDR, GDDR, memory controller architectures, or memory subsystem design. Familiarity with memory reliability and availability concepts, including ECC, repair mechanisms, refresh algorithms, or RAS features. Experience with SystemVerilog, digital design, RTL development, or verification methodologies. Experience applying AI tools to software development, data analysis, technical research, document analysis, workflow automation, or agentic engineering workflows. Understanding of AI training, inference, accelerator architectures, and the role of HBM in large-scale AI systems. Previous internship, research, publication, or project experience related to memory systems, computer architecture, semiconductor design, or SoC development. jobs.title: Research Intern - Office of Applied Research
jobs.location: Redmond, WA, US; New York, NY, US
jobs.body: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The Office of Applied Research in Microsoft seeks research interns to conduct state-of-the-art applied research. Applied research is impact-driven research. It applies empirical techniques to real world problems in a way that transforms theory into reality, advancing the state-of-the-art in the process. The Office of Applied Research brings together experts in frontier Artificial Intelligence (AI) model development and human-centered AI to tackle real-world challenges at scale in the enterprise AI space. We work closely with research and product partners to ensure Microsoft is advancing cutting-edge research aligned with our core product interests. Ideal candidates have proven experience in various fields such as Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Reinforcement Learning (RL), Learning from human feedback and Human-centered AI. We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in areas such as reinforcement learning and model mid- and post-training, continual learning, differential privacy, human-AI collaboration, or the development and evaluation of enterprise AI agents, including learning from user feedback in real-world deployments. Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, Information Science, Statistics, Information Systems, Economics, Operation Research or a related STEM field. Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. Preferred Qualifications 1+ year(s) of experience in conducting research and writing peer-reviewed publications. Ability to think unconventionally to derive creative and innovative solutions. Actively conducting research in at least one of the following areas: Collaborative or Multi-party AI Agents (e.g. AI teammates) Mid- and post-training for LLMs / Agents Learning from user interaction or feedback Synthetic data generation for LLM evaluation and fine-tuning Understanding, verifying, or evaluating LLMs outputs Differential privacy for LLM and data Continual Learning / Test-time Training Agents (e.g. Memory, Goal management, Inter-Agent conversations) Multi Agent Simulations (e.g. evaluating or training AI agents in collaborative settings) Forward deployment for enterprise AI Ability to collaborate effectively with your mentor and others in Microsoft on research projects. Demonstrated interpersonal and communication skills, cross-group, and cross-culture collaboration skills. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: https://careers.microsoft.com/us/en/us-intern-pay Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April). This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: 2027 Manufacturing Engineering Intern - Elkridge MD
jobs.body: RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: No relocation assistance available CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No CLEARANCE TYPE: None TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. Northrop Grumman Mission Systems is a trusted provider of mission-enabling solutions for global security. We have a wide portfolio of secure, affordable, integrated, and multi-domain systems and technologies. Our differentiated battle management and cyber solutions deliver timely, mission-enabling information and provide superior situational awareness and understanding to protect the U.S. and its global allies. An internship at Northrop Grumman is unique. Sure, you’ll learn new skills, explore our enterprise, network with experts, connect with thought leaders, and finish with a resume that opens doors. But you’ll gain something even more valuable: pride in what you’ve done. Join us and launch your career. We’ll support you with training, professional development and networking opportunities, and our shared vision of global security. jobs.body: Company: Qualcomm France S.A.R.L. Job Area: Interns Group, Interns Group > Interim Intern General Summary: Brief: The goal of the internship is to co-design hardware and firmware for post-quantum cryptography primitives. The process begins with a literature review of the chosen algorithm, followed by the development of efficient hardware and firmware implementations. Background: A world leader in smart mobile technologies, QUALCOMM (QCT) offers complete solutions that enable continuous innovation for today's smart connected devices. Our vast expertise in wireless technology, combined with our unique systems’ approach to developing solutions, puts QCT at the forefront of the rapidly expanding mobile industry. QCT offers solutions for CDMA, UMTS, GSM and LTE technologies, providing support for 3G, 4G and 5G networks and devices. Qualcomm also offers a broad portfolio of additional wired and wireless technologies for the mobile, networking, computing and consumer electronics product segments. All our solutions and products are elegantly engineered for optimal performance and power consumption. Our system-on-chip solutions like Snapdragon bring together CPU, GPU, connectivity, security, multimedia and GPS technologies in a way that is redefining mobile possibilities for people everywhere. Because of its unsurpassed performance and capabilities, Snapdragon is enhancing mobile experience and fueling an ever-expanding array of new connected device categories, ranging from smartphones to tablets to e-readers and beyond. Cryptography is crucial for privacy and security in our digital world, protecting sensitive information and ensuring trust. Crucially, with quantum computing, traditional methods may become obsolete, but PQC ensures security infrastructure remains secure. Implementation security is vital, as even robust algorithms can be compromised if not implemented securely. The aim of this internship is to work on such implementations, on innovative HW/SW platforms, composed of CPU cores and HW accelerators, and to optimize them according to various criteria, but also secure them against diverse attackers. jobs.title: Mass Properties Engineering Intern (Summer)
jobs.body: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW REGENT's Mass Properties discipline sits at the heart of every vehicle program. As the Mass Properties Engineering Intern, you'll work directly on real, high-impact work from day one. This isn't spreadsheet upkeep. You'll do the engineering a full-time hire would do: pulling mass, CG, and inertia data directly from CAD, working with various IPTs to keep the data accurate, and writing scripts that replace manual work. You'll help close out weight and balance control for our prototype vehicle, and help define the management plan, database architecture, and tools that our production craft will rely on through production. You'll join the Aero & Performance team within Hardware Engineering. If you'd rather open a CAD model and find the answer yourself, write a script than repeat a task by hand, and help build a discipline instead of plugging into one that already exists, you'll fit right in! WHAT YOU'LL DO - Support R&D W&B Control: You'll help develop and implement the processes that control our products’ weight and balance properties through the maturation of design, including how mass data is sourced, verified, updated through configuration changes, and reported. - Build Supporting Tools: You'll write scripts to automate reporting of mass properties and mass rollups across programs, establishing the appropriate checks and balances. - Work Laterally Across the Company: You'll gain a system view by interfacing directly with adjacent departments (structures, propulsion, avionics, etc) to collect mass properties, challenge their reports, and keep the database up to date. - Exposure to Design Tools: You'll have visibility into the PLM system and the DMU to gain a deeper understanding of the system layout and reports generated by the responsible engineers. - Identify Risks and Opportunities: You'll assess mass and balance data to flag potential weight or CG issues, identify opportunities to reduce weight, and share your findings with the relevant engineering teams. - Define and Deliver a Real Outcome: You'll scope a clear goal with your manager early in the term and present your results, including your assumptions and data sources, to the team at the end of it. - Set Your Priorities: You'll work independently under the guidance of the Mass Properties Engineer, who will mentor you and help you define your priorities across the different programs to achieve your set objectives. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - CAD Fluency: You can navigate CATIA, SolidWorks, NX or similar tools to independently understand the vehicle layout, pull mass, CG, and inertia data. - Scripting Instincts: You have working proficiency in Python, MATLAB, SQL, VBA, or similar, and you reach for a script when a task is about to become a recurring manual chore. - Weight and Balance Fundamentals: You understand CG calculations, moment of inertia, and how margins and contingencies get carried through a program. - Comfort With Ambiguity: You are able to focus across multiple active programs and changing priorities. - Confidence Reaching Out: You are proactive and comfortable engaging with engineers on other teams directly to track down a number and get it confirmed. - Curiosity About Change Control: Exposure to PLM or PDM systems and interest in how engineering changes are tracked through the lifecycle of a program is an advantage. - A Head Start, If You've Got One: Though we don't expect you to have it, familiarity with aircraft weight management standards, having a private pilot’s license, or prior weight and balance experience from a program, class, or club project, will help you ramp up quickly. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Mechanical Engineering Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to support the team as they develop new concepts and hardware, build and test our designs to ensure they will stand up to the extreme space environments, and ultimately deliver our fully tested hardware to the spacecraft integration team. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts. Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion. Hourly Pay Range (CA Only) $28 — $28 USD WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. jobs.title: Harness Design Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. Harness Design Engineer Intern (Summer 2027) Internships at Astranis typically last for twelve weeks, and are hourly roles designed for students who are currently enrolled at a four-year university. As an Intern, you will have an amazing opportunity to work on hard problems — we pride ourselves on giving everyone at Astranis a chance to do meaningful work on challenging projects, no matter their seniority. Many past interns have designed and tested hardware/software that is heading to space on our first satellite, and many of them are now full-time employees at Astranis. If you have already graduated from a four-year university, please apply to be an Associate Engineer. Role: Work with the harnessing design team on designing flight and test harnessing Create wiring diagrams, block diagrams, schematics, and layout drawings of spacecraft harnessing Work with cross-functional teams to define interfaces between different subsystems Use CAD programs to route harnessing in 3D Utilize EE fundamentals to select appropriate design components based on various requirements like voltage, power, frequency, and data-rate Work with production to fabricate in-house cables Requirements: Currently pursuing a B.S., M.S. or Ph.D. in mechatronics or electrical engineering (or equivalent technical degree) Interest in learning about, designing, and working with various spacecraft systems and subsystems Familiar with power and data transmission concepts Bonus: Experience with Zuken (or other harness design software) Experience with various connectors and wire types including MIL circular and D-Sub/microD Experience with 3D CAD software like Solidworks The base pay for this position is $29.00 per hour. Base Hourly Pay $29 — $29 USD U.S. Citizenship, Lawful Permanent Residency, or Refugee/Asylee Status Required (To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States, or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)) Our mission and products are built for everyone, regardless of gender, race, creed, or background. jobs.title: Service Operations Intern
jobs.body: This is a summer internship starting May/June and is fully on-site at the listed office location. Company Overview At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it a reality. For over two decades, we’ve been at the forefront of the global energy transition, pioneering solutions that empower critical industries to thrive in a rapidly digitizing, energy-intensive world. From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm. At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century. Department Overview Field Service Operations is responsible for admin activities and applications support for the greater Field Service team. We work with cross functional teams to resolve issues seen in the field or to create new processes to relieve the burden of new workflows. Intern Project Interns will have a primary project during the summer internship and may work on additional projects. While the project could change by the time of the internship, we anticipate that the main project will involve the following: Modernize pre-COO PSV incident management by integrating Quickbase “OK to Start” directly into Salesforce Mobile Service Appointments. Use AI-enabled voice capture and criteria-driven forms to reduce manual entry and navigation, while standardizing PSV data for reporting and future system integrations. Position Responsibilities Identify, support, and coordinate process improvements including inventory management, logistics and reverse logistics, software rollout, and vendor management Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify pain points and inefficiencies in current processes to drive process improvement Materials, logistics, and transaction support – responsible for coordination with Supply Chain for parts replenishment, stocking levels and logistics improvement opportunities, ensuring accurate inventory transactions by Field Technicians Administrative support – coordinate administrative support for Field Service operations that includes data entry, organization, analysis, on-boarding and off-boarding technicians, maintaining spare parts list and sites list; creating purchase orders and reconciling invoices, creating and revising procedures Coordinate with other internal partners to maintain Service documentation Provide initial and on-going administrative training to Field Service Technicians Optimization/ Operations Research to scale the organization Complete optimization problem, setup, and execution Develop and maintain applications in QuickBase & Salesforce Create clear and concise data visualization dashboards (Tableau, Quicksight, and Salesforce) Minimum Qualifications Currently a student earning a Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Data Science, Data Analytics, Mathematics, or any relevant discipline to Customer Success / Customer Experience Must be graduating between spring 2027 and summer 2028 Desired Qualifications Experience with machine learning/AI development for predictive models Experience with Salesforce or other CRM’sFamiliarity with no code low code environments like QuickBase Ability to work independently with decisive and thoughtful decisions Strong communication and presentation skills Strong analytical and problem-solving skills1 year of experience in operations and/or analytics Strong ideas in optimization, estimation & data analysis techniquesExperience as a project lead or important technical contributor Visa Sponsorship Bloom Energy is unable to provide VISA sponsorship to interns or new grad hires on an F-1, J-1 or other visa for this position, regardless of CPT or OPT status. Develop improvements to manufacturing methods to improve safety, reduce cost, or increase productivity. Aid operations in ensuring parts are safely fabricated in accordance with product specifications. Analyse processes for safety, quality, and efficiency opportunities. Resolve quality issues, identify trends, determine root causes, and take corrective actions. Improve manufacturing process to reduce process variability and increase yields. Represent engineering as part of a cross-functional team including safety, quality, and operations. Prioritize and execute projects within the agreed upon timeline and provide updates on project status. Take ownership of projects and execute through design, fabrication, implementation, and sustainment. Participate in week-long team-based problem solving / continuous improvement events. Participate in quality improvements as per IATF 16949 2016 ensure to complete toll gates for DFMEA, PFMEA, Control Plan, MSA, Process capability study for in house process Ensure requirements of relevant standards like ISO 9001-2015, PED 2014/68/EU, API Spec. Q1, API 6D, etc. are being consistently met and improved. Essential Qualifications / Experience: In progress of achieving B.S. in Engineering or related degree. Problem solving and root cause analysis skills. Proficient with 2D and 3D CAD software Preferred Qualifications/Experience Exposure to lean manufacturing, six sigma, and 5S practices. jobs.title: Nuclear Engineering Internship/Co-op
jobs.body: FORGE ATOMICS Humanity faces two critical challenges: securing reliable energy and aggressively lowering our environmental impact. At Forge, we believe nuclear fission is the key to solving both at once. Today Forge is developing the technology to rapidly scale the deployment of nuclear fission. NUCLEAR ENGINEERING INTERNSHIP/CO-OP As a nuclear engineering intern at Forge, you'll contribute directly to the nuclear design and safety analysis of our first reactor, Ember — core design and fuel cycle, reactivity control, and radiation release and dose analysis. You'll work inside our simulation and analysis toolchain alongside the engineers carrying the design from today's working models toward licensing and first criticality, and your analyses will feed real design decisions. Internship and co-op positions are available for the Summer 2027 and Fall 2027 terms; you'll indicate which term(s) you're available for when you apply. Responsibilities - Own a well-scoped nuclear analysis end-to-end — criticality, depletion, reactivity coefficients, shielding — with the mentorship of the engineer responsible for that area - Run and extend reactor physics simulations supporting core design, fuel cycle, and reactivity control studies - Support radiation shielding and release analysis against regulatory limits - Build and improve the analysis tools and automation that let a small team move at unprecedented speed - Collaborate daily with fluids, structures, components, and manufacturing engineers to keep the design system-optimized and manufacturable Basic Qualifications - Must be enrolled in a bachelor's degree program in an engineering, physics or math discipline by the start of employment - 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internships and project team experience (i.e. FSAE, Rocketry, Cube Sat, Solar Car) are strongly preferred) - Must be able to comply with U.S. Department of Energy export control regulations governing access to nuclear technology (10 CFR Part 810). U.S. citizenship is not required: Forge can generally host citizens of generally authorized countries (including Canada, the U.K., E.U. member states, Japan, and South Korea), and supports J-1 exchange visitor sponsorship for international students Preferred Skills and Experience - GPA of 3.5 or above - 12+ months experience of application of technical skills outside of the classroom. Prior internships and project team experience are strongly preferred. Exceptional personal projects or laboratory research can serve as substitutes. - Ability to work well in an integrated collaborative team environment, including frequent interactions with technicians, other engineers, and managers - Ability to work effectively in a dynamic professional setting with changing needs and requirements - Coursework or research in reactor physics, radiation transport, thermal hydraulics, or health physics - Experience with reactor physics or radiation transport codes (e.g. OpenMC, MCNP, Serpent) and scientific computing in Python Additional Requirements - Position will be based in the South Bay area of Los Angeles County and will require relocation if not already local. The position will be full-time in the office for the duration of the internship/co-op term. - Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary Compensation and Benefits Pay range: - Engineering Intern/Freshman/Sophomore: $28.00/hour - Engineering Intern/Junior/Senior: $30.00/hour Your actual level and hourly rate will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Interns accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law, and receive access to various other perks. Forge is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Forge is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status. This position involves access to technology that is subject to U.S. export controls. Any job offer made will be contingent upon the applicant's capacity to serve in compliance with U.S. export controls.

jobs.title: Process Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: PROCESS ENGINEERING INTERN (SUMMER 2027) Freeform builds AI-native manufacturing systems that unify software, hardware, and physics to produce industrial-scale parts at the speed of human ideation. By treating manufacturing as a single integrated system, we unlock a new era of innovation where complex hardware is designed, built, and scaled without limits. As a Process Engineering Intern at Freeform, you will help develop and refine novel processes for some of the world’s most advanced metal 3D printing systems. You will work closely with experienced engineers to study complex, multi-physics behavior within the printing process, building a foundational understanding of the system and applying those insights to support the development of next-generation processes. You’ll collaborate with mechanical, software, and simulation engineers to analyze large in-situ data sets and post-print material characteristics, contributing to rapid iteration and continuous improvement of the printing technology using data-driven and machine-learning-enabled approaches. 3D printing experience is not required to be successful here - we look for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving hard problems and creating amazing technology! Responsibilities: Assist the Process Engineering team in developing a deep understanding of the metal additive process and hardware operation by analyzing massive in-situ data sets to gain insight into physical mechanisms of the printing process Execute experiments and analyze data to improve metal additive processes Perform post-build metrology measurements and analysis of material properties such as tensile strength, surface roughness, and alloy microstructure Assist in the development and implementation of tool qualification procedures Basic Qualifications: Currently pursuing Bachelor's degree in material science, physics, or similar engineering discipline Experience with experimental design and statistical data analysis Strong data analysis skills and ability to interpret important information from extremely large data sets Experience with Python and/or MATLAB Nice to Have: Undergraduate research experience in material science, physics, mechanical engineering Process development experience from cutting edge industries such as semiconductor, solar, or displays Experience with statistical data analysis software such as R, JMP, or Minitab Passion for improving the state of metal 3D printing Comfortable working in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and iterating quickly (comfortable building the plane as we fly it) Strong communicator who collaborates across disciplines and proactively seeks support when needed Willing to take ownership of tasks big and small, with a hands-on, problem-solving mindset Strong work ethic with a refuse-to-fail mindset Demonstrated indicators of excellence and/or achieving success against adversity (i.e. top academic performance, leadership in engineering clubs, first-generation college student, or other examples of resilience and achievement) Location: Based in Hawthorne, our vertically integrated facility brings technology development, R&D, and production together under one roof. We operate at the center of LA’s deep tech ecosystem, surrounded by some of the most ambitious hardware innovation happening anywhere in the country. Our fast-paced, cross-functional environment is built on close collaboration, and as such, this role requires full-time onsite presence (five days a week), with very limited exceptions. What We Offer: We have an inclusive and diverse culture that values collaboration, learning, and making deliberate data-driven decisions We offer a unique opportunity to be an early and integral member of a rapidly growing company that is scaling a world-changing technology Compensation and Benefits The compensation for this role: Engineering Intern/Undergraduate: $30/hour Engineering Intern/Masters: $32.50/hour Engineering Intern/PhD: $35/hour Typical working weeks include regular opportunity for overtime Relocation assistance provided Free daily catered lunch and dinner, and fully stocked kitchenette Casual dress, flexible work hours, and regular catered team building events Freeform is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values diversity; employment with Freeform is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.
