jobs.title: CMOS FEOL Reliability Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About GlobalFoundries GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, power-efficient and high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. GF is a trusted and holistic technology partner for customers around the world. GF’s talented, global team remains focused every day on security, longevity and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com. Internship Program Overview: Our Interns & Co-ops are our entry-level talent pipeline for GF across the globe. Our goal is to provide students with a meaningful work experience that will equip them with the skills to embark on a career in the fast-paced and growing semiconductor industry after graduation. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives. Summary of Role: The CMOS FEOL Reliability Engineering Intern will support the Fab 8 Reliability Engineering organization in assessing semiconductor device reliability performance across advanced technology platforms. Working with reliability engineers, device engineers, Process Integration, Product Engineering, Yield Engineering, Reliability Laboratory, and data-analysis teams, the intern will evaluate reliability test data, investigate degradation mechanisms, and improve qualification and monitoring methodologies. Essential Responsibilities include: Learn semiconductor device reliability fundamentals, including Hot Carrier Injection (HCI), Bias Temperature Instability (BTI), Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB), Gate Oxide Integrity (GOI), and Process Reliability Monitoring (PRM). Support reliability qualification and monitoring activities for advanced CMOS technologies manufactured at Fab 8. Analyze wafer-level reliability (WLR) and fast wafer-level reliability (FWLR) test data using statistical and engineering methods. Develop automated data-analysis, reporting, dashboard, and visualization solutions that reduce manual reporting effort and improve visibility of reliability trends across multiple technology platforms. Perform data mining, trend analysis, comparative studies, and historical PRM correlation analysis to identify process and device factors that influence long-term reliability performance. Develop advanced statistical monitoring methods to improve excursion detection and reliability risk assessment. Collaborate with Device Engineering, Process Integration, Product Engineering, Yield Engineering, and Reliability Laboratory teams to support technology qualification and root-cause investigations. Prepare reliability assessment documentation, engineering reports, and technical presentations, and present project findings and recommendations at the conclusion of the internship. Other Responsibilities: Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs. Required Qualifications: Education – At least a sophomore at time of application and actively pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Semiconductor Engineering, or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship. Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and be in good academic standing. Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal) Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Ability to work independently and in a collaborative engineering environment. Preferred Qualifications: Prior related internship or co-op experience Demonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc. Strong interest in leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and support effective decision-making. Project management skills, i.e., the ability to innovate and execute on solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity. Strong written and verbal communication skills Strong planning & organizational skills Knowledge of semiconductor devices and manufacturing processes. Familiarity with statistical data-analysis techniques. Experience with Python, JMP, Minitab, Excel, Power BI, or similar analysis and visualization tools. jobs.title: Intern - Supply Management Analyst
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. Join Micron’s Global Procurement team and start a transformative journey with one of the world’s foremost innovators in memory and storage solutions. Our group contributes to Micron’s success by providing exceptional total cost control and supply chain resilience through forecasting abilities, risk assessment, and a strong dedication to sustainability and inclusion. We consider our team members our most valuable resource and support their growth through a skills-focused learning and development approach that encourages clear career paths. We value diverse viewpoints and nurture camaraderie to build an engaging and welcoming culture. See why Micron’s Global Procurement team is the ideal place to unlock your potential! In your role as an Intern-Supply Management Analyst on the Inbound Supply Management team, you will partner with Supply Managers to keep Micron’s inventory supply steady. Your key task involves ensuring the supply remains available and continuous while developing a detailed inventory management approach. You will work with suppliers and interested parties to solve supply shortages and uncover root causes to prevent recurrence. Be a member of a dedicated team spread across locations, aiming for prompt delivery, waste reduction, and continuous enhancement of parts and materials inventory control. Key Responsibilities: Develop, monitor, and optimize inventory replenishment models and supply execution strategies to effectively support manufacturing and minimize waste. Handle supplier commitments, keep an eye on forecast accuracy, and coordinate with suppliers and business partners to manage concerns regarding demand volume and timing. Supervise inventory scheduling, deliveries, and modify orders with suppliers when required. Speed up and raise delivery problems to guarantee uninterrupted supply. Address inventory shortage issues and determine root causes for resolution. Work with direct and cross-functional teams to implement and complete global strategic direction in supply fulfillment and inventory management. Minimum Qualifications: Currently pursuing a degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, or Industrial Engineering. Must be a current student, cannot graduate before September 2027. Demonstrated proficiency in data analysis methodologies and tools, including advanced use of Microsoft Excel. Strong communication skills with active listening and clear, concise communication to convey complex issues accurately to all levels. Self-motivated, driven individual comfortable operating in a global, fast-paced, and dynamic environment. Excellent interpersonal skills and a strong commitment to integrity. Preferred Qualifications: Ability to manage multiple workstreams with clear prioritization and documentation. Proactive, methodical, and confident working in investigative and developing problem environments. Strong time management, organization, and prioritization skills. jobs.title: Research Intern - MSR AI Interaction and Learning

jobs.body: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The AI Interaction and Learning team in Microsoft Research studies and builds next-generation Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems that help people accomplish more valuable work. Our research spans understanding how people use AI in real-world settings, evaluating agents in realistic workflows, and developing methods that make AI systems more capable, adaptive, and effective collaborators. Current research directions include agent evaluation and environments, reinforcement learning and post-training, user modeling and simulation, agent and group memory, personalization and continual learning, analysis of large-scale interaction logs, and human-AI collaboration. We are particularly interested in candidates with research experience in one or more of the following areas: Foundation Models, Reinforcement Learning and Post-Training, Agents, Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning, Interactive or Continual Learning, User Modeling and Simulation, Evaluation, Computational Social Science, Human-AI Interaction and Collaboration, or related areas of Artificial Intelligence. Candidates are encouraged to browse some of our recent publications for examples of active research in the group. Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a related STEM field. Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. Preferred Qualifications 2+ years of experience conducting research, developing research software, and/or writing peer-reviewed publications. Ability to identify important research problems and develop creative, rigorous approaches to addressing them. Active research experience in one or more of the following areas: Foundation Models, Reinforcement Learning and Post-Training, Agents, Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning, Interactive or Continual Learning, User Modeling and Simulation, Evaluation, Computational Social Science, Human-AI Interaction and Collaboration, or related areas of Artificial Intelligence. Ability to collaborate effectively with a research mentor and with researchers, engineers, and product partners across Microsoft. Proficient interpersonal, cross-group, and cross-cultural collaboration skills. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. jobs.title: Differentiable Simulation Research Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.body: Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in an inclusive, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world. Research in this internship will focus on scalable differentiable algorithms, including adjoint and automatic differentiation methods. The work will connect simulations with experimental data for calibration and data assimilation using AI/ML methods. These approaches will be evaluated on simulation workloads and assessed for integration into NVIDIA software used by researchers, engineers, and partner developers. If you enjoy working across mathematics, code, hardware, and engineering applications, we would love to meet! What you'll be doing: Prototype GPU-native solvers with adjoint and automatic differentiation techniques for engineering simulations. Integrate AI-based methods with simulation algorithms for parameter calibration, inverse problems, and data assimilation using experimental or simulation data. Co-design numerical algorithms and differentiation strategies for GPU parallelism, memory hierarchy, mixed precision, reduced synchronization, and distributed multi-GPU execution. Evaluate numerical accuracy, convergence, gradient quality, performance, and scalability on workloads in CFD, mechanics, thermal systems, and multiphysics. Identify promising methods and help move them toward reusable capabilities in CUDA-X libraries. What we need to see: Pursuing a PhD in applied mathematics, scientific computing, computational engineering, computer science, mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or equivalent program area. Strong foundations in algorithms related to PDEs, numerical linear algebra, iterative solvers, optimization, or scientific computing. Research experience with adjoint methods, automatic differentiation, inverse problems, data assimilation, gradient-aware simulation approaches, or a related area. Experience writing numerical software in Python and C++, with familiarity with parallel or GPU computing. Ability to design computational experiments, evaluate numerical and performance tradeoffs, and communicate technical results clearly. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Experience developing, scaling, or analyzing GPU solvers, including multi-GPU or distributed execution. Hands-on CUDA experience and use of profiling, benchmarking, or performance analysis to improve numerical algorithms. Experience calibrating computational models or assimilating experimental data in scientific or industrial applications. Experience with NVIDIA Warp, CUDA-X libraries, PyTorch, JAX, PETSc, Trilinos, MFEM, libCEED, OpenFOAM, or related computational science frameworks. Publications, open-source contributions, or deployed research software in numerical methods, scientific computing, differentiable simulation, or computational engineering. NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you! Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay based on the position, your location, year in school, degree, and experience. The expected hourly rate for this position is 38 USD – 94 USD. You will also be eligible for Intern benefits . ​ Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 3, 2026. This posting is for an existing vacancy. NVIDIA uses AI tools in its recruiting processes. NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Modular Engineering Internship – Summer 2027
jobs.body: Company: Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. Job Area: Interns Group, Interns Group > Interim Engineering Intern - SW General Summary: About Qualcomm Qualcomm relentlessly innovates transforming businesses, enriching lives and fortifying societies. Our solutions are pivotal in crafting a smarter, interconnected world. Building on our nearly 40-year history of era-defining technology breakthroughs, we deliver leading-edge AI, high performance, lower-power computing, and unrivaled connectivity. We’re proud to be the partner of choice to many of the world’s largest enterprises. Together with our ecosystem partners, we enable next-generation digital transformation. At Qualcomm, we are engineering human progress. Join Us in Shaping the Future At Qualcomm, we're committed to engineering human progress by delivering intelligent computing everywhere. We're passionate about harnessing the power of technology to transform industries and improve lives. Our early career programs offer limitless opportunities for growth, mentorship, and meaningful work. By joining our team, you'll be part of a community that's pushing the boundaries of what's possible in AI, computing, and connectivity. With a global footprint spanning over 30 countries, you'll have the chance to collaborate with diverse talent and contribute to projects that are shaping the future of technology. Our early career programs are designed to attract inventive minds, offering a platform to contribute to our long-term innovation pipeline. You'll be part of a community that values collaboration, creativity, and continuous learning. Our programs provide real-world experience, technical skills, and professional development opportunities, empowering you to make a meaningful impact and achieve your career goals. Join us for our U.S. 2027 summer intern class ! About Modular At Modular, a Qualcomm company, we’re on a mission to revolutionize AI infrastructure by systematically rebuilding the AI software stack from the ground up. Our team, made up of industry leaders and experts, is building cutting-edge, modular infrastructure that simplifies AI development and deployment. By rethinking the complexities of AI systems, we’re empowering everyone to unlock AI’s full potential and tackle some of the world’s most pressing challenges. If you’re passionate about shaping the future of AI and creating tools that make a real difference in people’s lives, we want you on our team. Maximize Your Opportunities: Our internship hiring model routes candidates from this application into multiple project-specific roles. Your "Profile Visibility" choice will guide how we manage your data across our systems. To be considered for the full breadth of internship opportunities, select the option to use your profile data for "Any Roles Globally". If you choose to limit your data to "Only The Role I'm Applying For", it will restrict the opportunity for you to be considered across matching internship opportunities. You can update your profile visibility preferences at any time through the Candidate Home Portal. Steps: Log Into Your Eightfold Candidate Home Account Hover Over The "Profile" Dropdown Open Settings Edit "Profile Visibility" Role Overview As a Modular Engineering Intern , you will contribute to next-generation AI infrastructure and software technologies spanning the AI Inference stack. Depending on your background, interests, and project needs, you may work on AI/ML model bring up, AI Inference performance and optimization, compiler development, the Mojo programming language, GPU kernels and accelerator optimization, cloud and distributed systems, security, quality engineering, or software development tooling. You may help optimize AI models for inference workloads, develop high-performance software for GPUs and emerging accelerators, improve compiler and runtime technologies for MAX or Mojo, scale distributed AI systems, develop AI infrastructure and model-serving platforms, build automated performance and quality frameworks, or improve developer tooling and CI/CD systems. This internship supports the Modular Engineering track . Based on your resume, skills, and experience, you will be aligned to projects within this track. Projects may include: AI Inference & Model Serving AI Systems & Infrastructure GPU & Kernel Engineering Compilers, Runtimes & Programming Languages Distributed & Cloud Systems AI Performance & Optimization AI Quality, Evaluation & Reliability Platform & Developer Engineering Security Engineering Software Development & Full-Stack Engineering Developer Tools & Open-Source Technologies Minimum Qualifications Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s, master’s, or Ph.D. degree program in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, software engineering, mathematics, artificial intelligence, or a related technical field. Must be available for 11–14 weeks during Summer 2027 (May–September) . Expected graduation date of November 2027 or later . 1+ years of academic or project experience with programming languages such as Python, C, C++, Rust, Go, or related languages. Preferred Qualifications Candidates actively pursuing a degree with an anticipated graduation between November 2027 and June 2028 . Experience with machine learning, deep learning, generative AI, LLMs, transformer architectures, AI inference, or ML frameworks and ecosystems such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Hugging Face. Knowledge or experience with compiler design, compiler/runtime implementation, programming languages, library development, APIs, or frameworks such as MLIR, LLVM, GCC, TVM, or XLA. Experience with parallel computing, GPU programming, high-performance computing, CUDA, ROCm, or other accelerator programming models, including kernel optimization, computer architecture, memory systems, memory layouts, or data movement. Experience developing or optimizing AI/ML models and workloads, including model acceleration, quantization, profiling, benchmarking, inference optimization, performance analysis, or translating AI research and existing model implementations into production-ready code. Knowledge or experience with distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, large-scale AI infrastructure, model serving, Kubernetes, cloud-native technologies, multi-node or multi-cluster deployments, or scalable inference systems. Experience with systems programming or software development using Python, C/C++, Rust, Go, object-oriented languages, Python multiprocessing/asyncio, or related technologies. Experience with software engineering, application development, operating systems, APIs, software libraries, developer tooling, build systems, release automation, testing, CI/CD, or developer productivity tools. Familiarity with AI/ML evaluation, software quality, unit/integration testing, regression detection, performance testing, benchmarking, observability, reliability engineering, reproducibility, or failure analysis. Experience with profiling and performance-analysis tools such as NVIDIA Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute, PyTorch Profiler, Linux perf, Intel VTune, or similar technologies. Knowledge or interest in software security, AI security, secure development, data protection, access controls, developer security tooling, AI-assisted coding tools, or secure AI systems and workflows. Experience building web, full-stack, AI/ML, or systems applications, developer integrations, technical examples, or other developer-facing solutions. Experience contributing to open-source projects, GitHub communities, technical documentation/blogs, developer education, or developer-focused technical content. Familiarity with AI developer and agentic coding tools or related developer workflows. Strong debugging, analytical, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills, with demonstrated curiosity and the ability to learn and operate effectively in a fast-paced engineering environment. Research experience or publications in relevant AI/ML, systems, compiler, or engineering areas is a plus. Qualcomm’s Internship Program Our interns join world-class teams to help define and build what is next for mobility and the world. jobs.title: Internship: Forward Deployed Engineer, Test
jobs.body: ABOUT REVEL At Revel, we are revolutionizing the way the world’s most critical hardware is controlled—across aerospace, automotive, energy, and manufacturing sectors. Our next-generation software stack combines an intuitive command/control interface, a specialized programming language tailored for hardware control, and a high-performance runtime environment. We empower engineers to build, test, and deploy critical systems rapidly, reliably, and safely. THE INTERNSHIP As a Forward Deployed Test Engineering Intern at Revel, you’ll work at the intersection of software, hardware, and testing to help our customers build and operate better test systems. You’ll work alongside our Forward Deployed Engineering and Software teams to integrate Revel with customer test stands, build test infrastructure, troubleshoot hardware and software issues, develop dashboards and workflows, and help engineering teams get more out of their test operations. You’ll get hands-on exposure to the systems behind aerospace, defense, automotive, energy, and advanced manufacturing. You’ll learn how software, hardware, sensors, data acquisition systems, and test infrastructure come together in real-world environments—and how to diagnose problems when things don't work as expected. This is a highly technical, hands-on internship. You’ll work closely with experienced engineers, take ownership of meaningful projects, and have the opportunity to see your work used with real hardware. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Help deploy and integrate Revel with customer test stands, sensors, actuators, and existing infrastructure - Work alongside customer engineering teams to understand their test processes and identify opportunities to improve them - Build and maintain test infrastructure, dashboards, and software workflows - Write RevelCode and other software to automate and streamline testing - Support data acquisition, telemetry, and hardware validation efforts - Troubleshoot issues across software, networking, firmware, hardware, and physical test systems - Help run and support test campaigns in real-world hardware environments - Deliver training and documentation to help new users get up and running with Revel - Collaborate with internal software and product teams to turn field learnings into product improvements - Occasionally travel to customer sites with the team WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, or a related technical field - Rising Junior or Senior graduating in 2027 or 2028 - Hands-on experience with engineering projects involving hardware, software, testing, or instrumentation - Strong problem-solving and debugging skills - Basic programming experience in Python, C, C++, or another programming language - Basic understanding of how software, hardware, sensors, and networks interact - Interest in test engineering, embedded systems, robotics, aerospace, automotive, or other hardware-focused environments - Comfortable getting hands-on with physical hardware and troubleshooting problems in real-world environments - Strong written and verbal communication skills - Curious, self-directed, and excited to learn from experienced engineers - Comfortable working in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment - US citizen, lawful permanent resident, refugee, or asylee (ITAR requirement) BONUS POINTS - Experience with data acquisition systems, test stands, instrumentation, or test automation - Experience with sensors, actuators, oscilloscopes, multimeters, or other test equipment - Experience with PLCs, control systems, NI software suite, TwinCAT, or CodeSys - Experience building or maintaining test infrastructure through academic, personal, or previous internship projects - Experience with embedded systems, robotics, aerospace, automotive, or other hardware-focused projects - Proficiency in C, C++, Python, Rust, or other systems programming languages - Familiarity with networking and debugging communication between hardware and software - Startup experience and passion for aerospace, defense, advanced manufacturing, or robotics WHY REVEL - Work on hardware that matters — our customers are building aerospace systems, advanced manufacturing lines, and critical infrastructure - Build and test real things — work directly with the hardware and systems used in real-world engineering environments - Learn from exceptional engineers — work closely with experienced Forward Deployed, Test, and Software Engineers - Get customer exposure — see firsthand how engineering teams design, test, and operate complex hardware - Own meaningful projects — take responsibility for projects that directly impact our customers and product - Grow quickly — work in a small, ambitious team where your contributions are visible INTERNSHIP DETAILS - Program: Summer 2027 Internship - Duration: June - August 2027 - Type: Summer, paid internship - Location: Los Angeles or San Francisco - Work environment: On-site - Travel: Occasional travel to customer sites may be required Join us to redefine what’s possible in software for hardware. ITAR Requirements To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/ddtc_public?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987.

jobs.title: Advanced Operations Summer Intern
jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Intern s hip ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will : ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting ​ Implement new ideas , be constantly challenged, and develop your skills ​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business ​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture ​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions. ​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward. ​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts. ​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives . ​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships. ​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​As an Electrical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams: Work on specific purchase product which will involve working on ongoing project deliverables, Robotic projects, Advanced Quality AQE interns work on engineering projects related to development of new products. Areas of emphasis may include human factors engineering, risk management, application of statistics, reliability engineering, design verification, and design validation including customer interaction. As Homer Stryker pointed out, “If your tools don’t work, make them work. If you can’t make them work, make some that do work.” In this directive, the AQE team works to make sure that the products we develop at Stryker will work consistently for our customers to meet or exceed their expectations. Process Quality PQE interns collaborate with cross-functional teams to support product sustainment. When non-conforming issues arise in production, it is our responsibility to perform robust root cause analysis and implement effective corrective actions. Do you enjoy deep dive investigations and driving collaboration and communication to achieve issue resolution? If so, you may be a great fit for this team! PQE interns are focused on quality, compliance and continuous improvement. They use their education to work with a variety of tools including CAD for fixture design, root cause analysis methods, LabView, and validation activities to optimize production, inspection, and quality system processes. Supplier Quality SQE interns are responsible for all things supplier-related . Stryker uses a number of critical suppliers to manufacture components and finished products, and to provide critical services. This team’s job is to work closely with the suppliers to ensure components and their manufacturing processes meet our required standards. Do you enjoy using your technical background and communication skills to influence suppliers? If so, you might be a great fit for this diverse and talented team! The role requires working closely with internal customers from multiple functions, meeting with suppliers frequently , and the use of both technical and business skills. Quality Quality interns work with our internal cross-functional teams and external sales team and customers to ensure we develop and sustain a product with the highest quality. The team’s job is to ensure we develop the right products up front – evaluate risk, ensure our customer’s user needs are met, and help drive craftsmanship, safety, durability and reliability into the product. On the post-market side, they also work closely with regulatory to handle any complaints and implement design changes, as needed, to address quality issues. The role requires someone who has great communication , problem-solving, and technical skills. Research & Development New Product Development R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products. They research new technologies , customer expectations, business requirements and regulations. They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts. These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production. Product Engineering R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies , customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products. Test Lab Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that they get to be the MythBusters of the division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, they are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you! Manufacturing Manufacturing Engineer interns will collaborate with Design and Operations to deliver best-in-class new products to market. Interns will partner with technicians and engineers to improve Stryker’s manufacturing lines through new fixture development, assembly line process enhancement, implementation of lean manufacturing principles, and improving ergonomics and safety. Majors Targeted: Electrical Engineering, or related majors . What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship . ​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above ( verified at time of hire ) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future . ​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment . Majors Targeted: Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering , or related majors What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship . ​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above ( verified at time of hire ) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future . ​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment . $ 20 min hourly wage – $3 5 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. Stryker is an EO employer – M/F/Veteran/Disability. Stryker Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor’s legal duty to furnish information.

jobs.title: Intern- PhD Applied Scientist, Robotics Planning
jobs.body: Who we are With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility. Timeframe: Summer (May-Aug 2027) At Symbotic, Early Career talent plays a meaningful role in helping us reimagine the future of supply chain automation. Through our Internship and Co-op programs, students have the opportunity to contribute to real projects, collaborate with experienced engineers and business leaders, and gain hands-on exposure to the technologies powering our end-to-end robotics and automation solutions. We are looking for curious, motivated students who are excited to solve complex problems, bring new perspectives to cross-functional teams, and see their work make an impact in a fast-moving, innovative environment. Along the way, Interns and Co-ops are supported through mentorship, professional development, networking opportunities, and a robust calendar of events designed to help them build community and grow their careers. Symbotic offers transportation and housing benefits for students who meet our relocation requirements. Continue reading below to learn more about this exciting opportunity! What we need Symbotic is looking for an applied scientist intern with a passion for multi-agent motion planning, tasking and motion planning, and inventory optimization to improve the performance and reliability of our systems as we rapidly scale our product and organization. The right candidate is excited about concepts like deadlock resolution and time-space reservations. This is a hybrid position based at our headquarters in Wilmington, MA. What you’ll do Identify high-impact scenarios where AI Planning and machine learning can be applied to optimize the Symbotic robotics software Adapt state-of-the-art approaches or develop high-performance algorithms to solve real-world multi-robot problems. Conduct simulations and experiments to validate the performance of the multi-robot algorithms Present results in verbal and written communications internally, and in top-tier academic venues What you’ll need Pursuing PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field. Proficiency in one or more general-purpose programming languages: C++, Python, Java, or C#. Strong research background in combinatorial optimization, robotics planning, multi-robot systems, or Agentic AI for optimization. Publications at high-impact conferences/journals (e.g., CoRL, ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, RSS, ICRA, IROS, RAL, AAAI, ICAPS, IJCAI, JAIR, etc.) on some of the aforementioned topics. #LI-JH1 #LI-Onsite About Symbotic Symbotic is an automation technology leader reimagining the supply chain with its end-to-end, AI-powered robotic and software platform. Symbotic reinvents the warehouse as a strategic asset for the world’s largest retail, wholesale, and food & beverage companies. Applying next-gen technology, high-density storage and machine learning to solve today's complex distribution challenges, Symbotic enables companies to move goods with unmatched speed, agility, accuracy and efficiency. As the backbone of commerce the Symbotic platform transforms the flow of goods and the economics of supply chain for its customers. For more information, visit www.symbotic.com . We are a community of innovators, collaborators and pioneers who embrace our differences, because we know unique perspectives make us stronger and smarter. Every perspective matters. We depend on the collective voices of our employees, customers and community to help guide us as we build a better place to work – for you and the world. That’s why we’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, or genetic information. The base range for this position in the posted location is $52.00 - $54.00 however, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The compensation package includes medical, dental, vision, disability, 401K, PTO and/or other benefits.

jobs.body: The 2027 Summer Internship Program will run from May 17, 2027, through August 6, 2027. Candidates must be available to start on May 17 and participate through the duration of the program. jobs.title: Development Engineering Co-Op
jobs.body: Work Schedule Standard (Mon-Fri) Environmental Conditions Office Job Description Why Join Us? At Thermo Fisher Scientific, our co-op program is designed to be a strategic pipeline for future leadership talent. Students who demonstrate exceptional performance, leadership potential, and alignment with our values will be considered for full-time opportunities during their co-op with us to begin post-graduation. As a global company with opportunities spanning multiple businesses, functions, and locations, applicants are required to be geographically flexible and mobile for both their co-op assignment and potential future employment opportunities. Onsite and in-office work is an essential function of this role and a requirement of the position. Strategic Business Impact For this role, projects may include the following responsibilities: ​ • Partner with Great Coworkers: Participate on cross functional project teams to develop new products and manufacturing processes. Present development results at technical reviews. Work with your mentor on specific engineering assignments. • Concept Design and Development: Contribute to product and packaging design through design reviews and design analysis. Participate in Design for Manufacturing (DFM) reviews of new product and package designs. Review process specifications and development plans with team members and external suppliers such as mold makers, prototyping services and equipment suppliers. • Equipment Selection: Assist with the selection of primary and secondary plastic processing equipment. jobs.title: Test Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Position Summary Vertiv is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Test Engineering Intern to join the Product Integrity organization within the Power Management business unit at our Delaware, Ohio facility. This internship provides hands-on exposure to electrical equipment testing, test instrumentation, data collection, documentation, troubleshooting support, safety practices, and continuous improvement in a high-power engineering lab environment. The Product Integrity team supports validation activities that include planning, test case development, test execution, compliance, and data collection, with outputs such as test cases, schedules, results, conformance evidence, and compliance documentation. This internship is designed as a learning role: the intern will support engineers and technicians with supervised lab activities, documentation, data organization, and an assigned summer project, while developing practical skills in product validation and engineering test operations. Responsibilities The Test Engineering Intern will work under the direction of Test Engineers, Test Technicians, and lab leadership. Responsibilities may include: Support test setup activities by helping prepare units under test, test fixtures, cables, labels, sensors, wiring 480V setups before energization, and documentation under supervision. Assist with instrumentation setup using tools such as oscilloscopes, power meters, current transformers, voltage probes, temperature loggers, data acquisition equipment, and other lab equipment, as training and authorization allow. The Delaware Product Integrity operating system lists equipment such as Yokogawa oscilloscopes, differential probes, power meters, AC/DC current transformers, temperature loggers, data loggers, and related test equipment as part of the test environment. Support execution of documented test cases by observing test steps, collecting measurements, recording results, organizing files, and escalating issues to the responsible engineer or technician. Document test results and engineering observations Assist with data quality and analysis, including organizing raw data, checking completeness, preparing plots/tables, and helping translate lab data into clear engineering summaries. Help troubleshoot test setups and units under test by supporting engineers and technicians with data review, wiring checks, instrumentation checks, and repeatability checks. Support continuous improvement projects such as improving test documentation, creating templates, developing simple dashboards, organizing lab data, improving fixture usability, or applying approved automation/data-analysis tools. Participate in 5S and safety practices and complete required safety/lab access training before entering or working in Delaware test bays and labs. Delaware lab access guidance states that access requires a need to enter the area and completion of training based on access level. Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, Mechanical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering Technology, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Physics, or a related technical field. Interest in electrical equipment testing, power systems, product validation, instrumentation, data analysis, or engineering lab operations. Ability and willingness to learn in a hands-on, fast-paced engineering lab environment and produce high-quality work. This wording aligns with Vertiv internship postings that commonly call for willingness to learn in a fast-paced environment, strong work ethic, attention to detail, analytical thinking, communication, collaboration, and teamwork. Basic proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Word; ability to document work clearly and professionally. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Demonstrated attention to detail, curiosity, and commitment to safe work practices. Ability to work onsite at the Delaware, Ohio facility for the Summer 2027 internship period. Ability to complete required Vertiv onboarding, safety, and lab access training before performing lab activities. Delaware badge guidance identifies training requirements by access level, including Safety Orientation for Test Bays and Labs and additional electrical safety courses for higher access levels. Ability to stand and/or walk while supporting lab activities and to safely handle test equipment, tools, or cables as required, with appropriate training and assistance. Learning Opportunities During the internship, the Test Engineering Intern can expect exposure to: Product Integrity and design validation testing: understanding how requirements, test cases, test sets, and test results connect in the validation process. High-power lab operations: gaining supervised exposure to the Delaware lab environment, test bays, instrumentation, safety expectations, and 5S practices. Instrumentation and measurement discipline: learning how test equipment is selected, configured, checked, and documented to support engineering conclusions. Engineering documentation: preparing clear technical summaries, data packages, charts, and presentations for engineers and stakeholders. Cross-functional teamwork: working with Test Engineering, Test Technicians, Product Engineering, Compliance, Lab Operations, and other functions as appropriate. Professional development: participating in Vertiv internship programming, which includes professional development, exposure to the business, and social interaction. Vertiv Principals and Priorities The successful candidate will embrace Vertiv’s Core Principals & Behaviors to help execute our Strategic Priorities. Vertiv internship postings commonly include this style of closing section, including Core Principals, Strategic Priorities, and Behaviors. OUR CORE PRINCIPALS: Safety. Integrity. Respect. Teamwork. Diversity & Inclusion. OUR STRATEGIC PRIORITIES: Customer Focus. Operational Excellence. High-Performance Culture. Innovation. Financial Strength. OUR BEHAVIORS: Own It. Act With Urgency. Foster a Customer-First Mindset. Think Big and Execute. Lead by Example. Drive Continuous Improvement. Learn and Seek Out Development. Work Authorization No calls or agencies please. Vertiv will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States. This position is not expected to be eligible for sponsorship; TA/HR should confirm final work authorization language before posting. jobs.body: What we’re building The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. jobs.title: 2027 Internship Sensor Systems Engineer
jobs.body: JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs. In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks. This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us. ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM Every new machine type we bring into the fleet raises the same question from scratch: which sensors, where do they go and what are they used for? The Systems / Sensors team answers it with analysis rather than guesswork, trading off coverage, cost, durability, and what will actually survive on a jobsite. As our Sensor Systems intern, you'll own sensor selection and placement analysis for a new machine platform, from first trade study to validation on real steel. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Work at the intersection between sensor physics, autonomy systems architecture, mechanical integration and design. - Analyze sensor coverage, occlusion, and blind spots for candidate sensor suites on new machine types - Build or extend tooling that models field of view, range, and coverage geometry - Run trade studies weighing performance against cost, durability, and mounting constraints - Prototype mounting concepts and validate coverage assumptions on actual machines - Turn your analysis into sensor requirements and specs the hardware team can build to - Work across perception, hardware, and safety to make sure the suite serves everyone downstream WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR REQUIRED - Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in an engineering or engineering-adjacent discipline such as mechanical, electrical, physics, mechatronics, robotics, or computer science (or bringing equivalent hands-on experience) - Solid grasp of 3D geometry, coordinate frames, and transforms - Python for analysis and tooling - CAD fluency - enough to reason about where hardware physically goes - Willingness to go to mock construction sites and test sensor configurations PREFERRED - Experience with device physics, ray tracing, rendering or coverage simulation - Familiarity with autonomous vehicle sensor suites - Exposure to heavy equipment or off-road machinery About This Internship This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited." jobs.title: Deployment Engineering Intern
jobs.body: Figure is an AI robotics company developing autonomous general-purpose humanoid robots. The goal of the company is to ship humanoid robots with human level intelligence. Its robots are engineered to perform a variety of tasks in the home and commercial markets. Figure is headquartered in San Jose, CA. We are looking for a Deployment Engineering Intern to join our Commercial Operations team for Winter 2027. This role works directly with deployment engineers and the pilot team to make our humanoid robots easier to operate and troubleshoot in real-world settings. You will help triage and organize issues from the field: reproducing problems, spotting patterns and preparing clear, well-documented reports for the deployment engineering team. You'll also turn what you learn into documentation and training that helps pilots troubleshoot on their own. Responsibilities: Triage incoming field issues alongside deployment engineers. Reproduce problems, gather logs and context, and build a playbook for pilots to reference for common issues. Test software and hardware changes and gather feedback from pilot team to create robust SOP and technical systems. Build and maintain a system that keeps technical documentation and training up to date as software and hardware change. Develop curriculum that strengthens pilots' troubleshooting skills, and help coaches teach it efficiently. Shadow deployment engineers on bug triage, issue tracking, and testing, and turn what you learn into better documentation. Collect feedback from pilots and coaches and communicate gaps clearly to engineering. Requirements: Currently pursuing a Bachelor's in Electrical, Computer, or Robotics Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Minimum 10 weeks internship, starting January 2027. Excellent problem solving and debugging skills. Strong technical writing skills and the ability to explain complex concepts simply. Comfortable learning new systems quickly and working hands-on with hardware. Organized and self-directed, with good judgment in a fast-paced environment. Clear communicator who works well with pilots, coaches, and engineers. Bonus Qualifications: Experience creating tutorials, training materials, or teaching (TA, tutoring, mentoring). Familiarity with Linux, Python, or debugging robotic or automated systems. Experience with project management or documentation tools (Confluence, Jira, Notion). The US base pay range for this full-time position is $35.00 to $40.00 per hour. The pay offered for this position may vary based on several individual factors, including job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package may also include additional components/benefits depending on the specific role. This information will be shared if an employment offer is extended.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: MANUFACTURING ENGINEERING INTERN (SUMMER 2027) Freeform builds AI-native manufacturing systems that unify software, hardware, and physics to produce industrial-scale parts at the speed of human ideation. By treating manufacturing as a single integrated system, we unlock a new era of innovation where complex hardware is designed, built, and scaled without limits. As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern at Freeform, you’ll be at the forefront of scaling production for high-performance metal 3D printed parts. You’ll work with a talented engineering team from some of the world’s most innovative companies across a range of projects to develop and refine the processes, tooling, and CNC machining workflows that enable precision manufacturing at speed and scale. This role is hands-on and fast-paced, ideal for someone eager to learn and contribute to the development of our autonomous metal 3D printing factories. You’ll focus on optimizing post-processing and machining operations, helping to bridge the gap between R&D and production. 3D printing experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, collaborative individuals who love solving hard problems and creating amazing technology! Responsibilities: Support the design and implementation of scalable manufacturing processes for new hardware and printed parts Assist with fixturing, test procedures, and post-processing steps to improve part flow through the factory Help develop documentation and process standards to support production scaling Build and iterate on tooling, jigs, and test setups for reliable, high-throughput production Identify bottlenecks and inefficiencies in part, material, and data flow- and work with cross-functional teams to improve them Support early production efforts and help transition R&D into high-rate manufa cturing Contribute to CNC machining workflows, including programming, setup, and optimization of multi-axis operations for post-processing of printed parts Basic Qualifications: Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, or manufacturing engineering from an ABET accredited university or college Hands on manufacturing or build experience from internships or engineering clubs such as FSAE, Baja SAE, solar car, rocket club, robotics club, or similar Experience working with hand tools, machinery, or complex hardware assembly Nice to Have: Advanced degree (Master's, PhD) in mechanical, aerospace, or manufacturing engineering Experience with CNC machining, including 3 or 5-axis programming and/or setup Experience with metal additive manufacturing or precision post-processing Exposure to fixturing, DFM, or process validation Experience scaling early-stage R&D into production Familiarity with MRP/ERP tools and lightweight production tracking systems Familiarity with manufacturing process development in a fast-paced hardware environment Ability to translate high-level engineering goals into practical factory processes Comfortable working in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and iterating quickly (comfortable building the plane as we fly it) Strong communicator who collaborates across disciplines and proactively seeks support when needed Willing to take ownership of tasks big and small, with a hands-on, problem-solving mindset Strong work ethic with a refuse-to-fail mindset Demonstrated indicators of excellence and/or achieving success against adversity (i.e. top academic performance, leadership in engineering clubs, first-generation college student, or other examples of resilience and achievement) Location: We are located in Hawthorne, CA in a 35,000 square foot, state-of-the-art facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access to the 405, 105, and 110 freeways. Our facility is in the heart of Los Angeles' vibrant emerging tech ecosystem alongside many other high growth startups and enterprises. What We Offer: We have an inclusive and diverse culture that values collaboration, learning, and making deliberate data-driven decisions We offer a unique opportunity to be an early and integral member of a rapidly growing company that is scaling a world-changing technology Compensation and Benefits The compensation for this role: Engineering Intern/Undergraduate: $30/hour Engineering Intern/Masters: $32.50/hour Engineering Intern/PhD: $35/hour Typical working weeks include regular opportunity for overtime Relocation assistance provided Free daily catered lunch and dinner, and fully stocked kitchenette Casual dress, flexible work hours, and regular catered team building events Freeform is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values diversity; employment with Freeform is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: New Product Development Test Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About GlobalFoundries GlobalFoundries is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing a unique combination of design, development, and fabrication services to some of the world’s most inspired technology companies. With a global manufacturing footprint spanning three continents, GlobalFoundries makes possible the technologies and systems that transform industries and give customers the power to shape their markets. For more information, visit www.gf.com. Internship Program Overview: Our Interns & Co-ops are our entry-level talent pipeline for GF across the globe. Our goal is to provide students with a meaningful work experience that will equip them with the skills to embark on a career in the fast-paced and growing semiconductor industry after graduation. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives. Summary of Role: Join the New Product Development team for a hands-on engineering internship focused on automated test solutions for complex digital, analog, and mixed-signal integrated circuits used in automotive and industrial applications. You will work alongside Product and Test Engineers on defined assignments spanning test planning, ATE development, silicon bring-up, validation, data analysis, and manufacturing-readiness activities using Advantest and Teradyne platforms. Essential Responsibilities include: Support pre-silicon planning by translating product requirements and datasheets into technical specifications, specification-compliance matrices, design-for-test requirements, and ATE test plans. Assist with the design of cost-effective ATE hardware and resource allocation that improve multisite efficiency and pin multiplexing for silicon bring-up, validation, and production release. Develop, bring up, validate, and debug automated test programs for digital, analog, and mixed-signal integrated circuits on Advantest and Teradyne ATE platforms. Analyze test and characterization data to investigate design margins, wafer-fabrication process variation, parametric performance, yield, and test-time opportunities. Support process-window experiments, silicon and package qualification activities, and product specification compliance across automotive, industrial, or commercial requirements. Collaborate with Design, DFT, Design Validation, Program Management, Quality and Reliability Engineering, Customer Quality Engineering, Bench Characterization, Applications, Fab, Assembly, and factory Test teams. Contribute to ATE test hardware, socket design, board schematics, layout, diagnostic code, and test automation specifications under the guidance of experienced engineers. Document gaps, lessons learned, and best practices, and contribute reusable methods to the Standard Test Methods Library (STML) across ATE platforms. Other Responsibilities: Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs. Required Qualifications: Education – At least a sophomore at time of application and actively pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship. Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and be in good academic standing. Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal) Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship. Preferred Qualifications: Prior related internship or co-op experience Demonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc. Strong interest in leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and support effective decision-making. Project management skills, i.e., the ability to innovate and execute on solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity. Strong written and verbal communication skills Strong planning & organizational skills Coursework or project experience in semiconductor test, design-for-test, integrated-circuit design, electronics, or semiconductor physics. Programming experience in one or more languages, including C, C++, Python, or Perl. Familiarity with digital, analog, or mixed-signal circuits, test automation, or laboratory measurement equipment. #InternshipProgramUS Expected Salary Range $20.00 - $40.00 Expected Salary Range $0.00 - $0.00 The exact Salary will be determined based on qualifications, experience and location. jobs.body: Overview Keysight is a mission-critical design enablement partner for organizations solving the world’s most complex engineering challenges. With deep engineering expertise and leading design, emulation, and test solutions, our ~16,800 employees help customers in over 100 countries accelerate innovation across communications, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace and defense, semiconductor, and artificial intelligence markets. Learn more about what we do. At Keysight, people come together to explore new ideas, challenge what's possible, and advance the technologies defining the future. Here, you'll find opportunities to do your best work, take your career further, and thrive in an award-winning culture. Learn more about our benefits. Responsibilities About the Job: You will join our team for a 3-month project in RF signal conditioning circuit design aimed at future products. Keysight fosters a collaborative engineering environment which emphasizes teamwork, mentoring, enthusiasm, and excellence in design About the Team: Our Keysight Labs team develops (and often publishes) world’s-fastest amplifiers and other mixed-signal integrated circuits. Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate, and advance faster than ever. Department Process and Equipment Engineering (Diffusion) Project Title F10 CMOS Matching and RegE Wafer Edge Exclusion Programme Project Description The Process and Equipment Engineering Intern will participate in an engineering project focused on CMOS matching analysis and wafer edge yield enhancement within advanced semiconductor manufacturing processes. Working alongside Process and Equipment Engineers, the intern will gain hands-on exposure to yield learning methodologies, inline process monitoring, defect characterization, and data-driven manufacturing optimization. The project provides opportunities to investigate process variations, evaluate wafer edge performance, and develop analytical solutions that enhance manufacturing quality and yield performance. The project combines semiconductor process engineering fundamentals with advanced data analytics, automation, and AI-enabled engineering tools to accelerate learning, improve engineering efficiency, and drive fact-based decision making. The internship provides exposure to: Semiconductor manufacturing processes and process integration. Yield analysis, defect characterization, and process monitoring methodologies. Statistical analysis and data-driven engineering problem solving. Automation, visualization, and AI-enabled engineering workflows. Cross-functional collaboration across manufacturing, process, and yield engineering teams. Objective of the Project The intern will: Develop an understanding of CMOS matching methodologies and wafer edge performance analysis. Analyze manufacturing, metrology, inspection, and defect data to identify yield improvement opportunities. Evaluate factors contributing to process variation and yield mismatches across manufacturing populations. Apply data analytics, automation, and AI-enabled solutions to improve engineering investigations and productivity. Generate engineering recommendations that improve manufacturing performance and process learning. Opportunities for Full Time Employment High-performing interns may be considered for future full-time opportunities within Process and Equipment Engineering, subject to business needs, individual performance, and graduation requirements. Project Scope The intern will participate in activities such as: Studying CMOS matching behavior and wafer edge performance characteristics within semiconductor manufacturing processes. Integrating process, inspection, defect, and metrology datasets to perform comprehensive engineering analysis. Developing analytical methodologies to identify yield loss mechanisms and process improvement opportunities. Creating automation, visualization, or AI-enabled tools that enhance engineering productivity and data interpretation. Collaborating with cross-functional engineering teams to evaluate and validate improvement opportunities. Learning Opportunities Interns will gain valuable exposure to: Advanced semiconductor manufacturing and process engineering. Yield enhancement methodologies and defectivity analysis techniques. Statistical analysis, data visualization, and engineering problem-solving approaches. Python programming, automation, and AI-enabled engineering applications. Cross-functional collaboration within high-volume semiconductor manufacturing environments. Deliverables By the end of the internship, the intern will deliver: A technical assessment of CMOS matching performance, yield variation drivers, and improvement opportunities. Data analysis and visualization solutions that improve engineering insight into wafer edge and yield behavior. An analytical, automation, or AI-enabled solution that enhances engineering workflow efficiency or decision-making effectiveness. Engineering recommendations that improve wafer edge performance, yield learning, and process optimization. A final presentation and technical report summarizing methodology, findings, limitations, and future recommendations. Impact of the Project The project is expected to: Improve understanding of yield variation and wafer edge-related performance characteristics. Demonstrate the value of analytics, automation, and AI-enabled tools within semiconductor manufacturing engineering workflows. Contribute reusable methodologies that accelerate future yield improvement and manufacturing optimization initiatives. jobs.title: PhD Research Intern, Hardware and Systems Architecture - 2027
jobs.body: NVIDIA’s development of the GPU in 1999 revolutionized the PC gaming industry, reshaped contemporary computer graphics, and transformed parallel computing. In recent years, GPU deep learning has propelled modern AI, ushering in a new era of computing where GPU systems serve as the core intelligence for computers, robots, and autonomous vehicles, enabling them to perceive and interpret the world around them. NVIDIA Research is at the forefront of developing cutting edge hardware, software, and algorithmic technologies for next generation GPU systems. We are eager to expand our teams with the most brilliant minds globally. What you'll be doing: Conduct cutting edge research on algorithms, hardware, and system software extending the state of the art in deep learning, humanoid robotics, database analystics, general computing, and other technology areas surrounding NVIDIA's business. Invent new techniques, technologies, methodologies, processes, and devices that can enable new products or types of products. Deliverable results include prototypes, patents, leading to products and publications. Develop new methods and processes for research and scientific evaluation of research techniques and artifacts including agentic driven techniques, simulation, modeling, and benchmarking. Produce technology vision and the basis for products 5-10 years out. Focus should not be on products currently shipping or in development, except as to how they can be extended and improved. What we need to see: Pursuing PhD Degree in relevant discipline(s) (CS, CE, EE, Physics, Math) At least one year of university or industrial research experience in computer architecture or computer systems, including operating systems, distributed systems, compilers, or AI/ML systems. Strong programming ability: C, C++ and Python preferred. Eagerness to learn and use AI tools for software development and system design. Experience designing and evaluating research ideas through prototyping, simulation, modeling, or experimentation. Strong programming skills and the ability to communicate research ideas, methods, and results clearly. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Chip/system level arch: agentic techniques for computer architecture; specialized accelerators for deep-learning and humanoid robotics Systems for AI/ML: systems infrastructure for LLM training, inference, and agents/tools; state management in agentic systems; systems for humanoid robotics AI/systems co-design Experience contributing to research targeting leading architecture and systems conferences, such as ISCA, ASPLOS, MICRO, HPCA, SOSP, MLSys, NSDI, or OSDI. Publications are a plus but are not required. We welcome candidates with research in progress, including manuscripts in preparation or submissions under review. NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-looking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you! Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay based on the position, your location, year in school, degree, and experience. The expected hourly rates for this position are: US, CA, Santa Clara: 38 USD – 94 USD. US, MA, Westford: 30 USD – 94 USD. You will also be eligible for Intern benefits . ​ Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 3, 2026. This posting is for an existing vacancy.
