jobs.title: System Level Test Engineer (RDSS Intern)
jobs.body: By submitting your resume, you’re expressing interest in our 2027 RDSS (Research and Development Substitute Services) program. Please confirm your eligibility with the local district office before applying the role. We are looking to hire a System Level Test Engineer (Cultivating talent via RDSS program) who will work in the Test Solutions Group at NVIDIA developing manufacturing GPU/CPU test solutions. Our team is responsible for creating and delivering the diagnostic test programs which serve as a final test for millions of chips before they are sent to our customers. We bring together different pieces of software, firmware, and settings, working through issues with several teams to deliver these programs to our manufacturing partners. We monitor the performance of these programs, working to improve their efficiency and effectiveness. NVIDIA is the leader in groundbreaking developments in Artificial Intelligence, High-Performance Computing and Visualization. The GPU, our invention, serves as the visual cortex of modern computers and is at the heart of our products and services. Our work opens new universes to explore, enables amazing creativity and discovery, and powers what were once science fiction inventions from artificial intelligence to autonomous cars. NVIDIA is looking for extraordinary people like you to help us accelerate the next wave of artificial intelligence. Make the choice to join our growing team today! What you will be doing: Responsible to develop and improve the test programs for NVIDIA's state of the art GPU products. Your duties include test program creation, validation and support. Expect to interface with other engineering groups including ASIC, ATE, systems/silicon validation, software, VBIOS, and product engineering teams to coordinate efforts to resolve test program issues. Initiate and drive process improvements and preventative actions, possibly through root cause analysis. Continuously improve work, products, functions, and methodologies through ongoing analysis, while actively communicating and sharing new information and approaches with cross-functional teams to support company goals. What we need to see: Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or similar hardware systems background. Strong written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to collaborate effectively with diverse teams across different locations. Demonstrated ability to quickly narrow down and solve issues in complex stacks of hardware and software. Good organization skills, with a logical approach to problem solving, good time management and task prioritization. Be proactive and drive projects with minimum supervision and be able to work effectively across multiple teams. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Familiar with Linux OS and background with Python programming and bash scripting. jobs.body: Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms. jobs.title: Autonomy Engineer Intern, Simulation & Robotics, 2027 (Zurich)
jobs.body: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions. ABOUT THE ROLE: The core of our system is the computer vision algorithms that allow drones to understand the world around them. You will architect and implement the algorithms that run on every drone powered by Skydio as part of a world class computer vision and deep learning team with researchers who have pushed the state of the art in academia and industry. As a Research Intern, you will be paired up with one or more members of our core software development team, assuming direct ownership of a project that meaningfully advances the capabilities of our team and products. If you have a strong foundation in math, theory, and software development and you are interested in directly contributing to the development of the next generation of autonomy algorithms and pushing them into real products, we would love to hear from you. AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY: - Core Simulator Architecture: Design, implement, and evolve the foundational architecture of the Skydio Simulator, ensuring it scales across vehicle types, environments, and use cases. - Physics and Dynamics: Improve and extend physics models governing vehicle motion, interactions with the environment, and dynamic agents. - Sensor and Hardware Simulation: Build high-fidelity simulations of cameras, IMUs, and other onboard components, including timing, noise characteristics, and hardware behavior. - Autonomy Stack Integration: Run and validate the full Skydio autonomy stack in simulation, ensuring consistency between simulated and real-world behavior. - Feature Development on Top of the Core: Implement simulator capabilities that unlock new workflows for customers and internal autonomy engineers, from training scenarios to advanced testing modes. - Performance and Fidelity: Profile, optimize, and improve simulator performance while continuously pushing realism and accuracy. WHAT YOU’LL DO: - Develop core simulator components in C++ and Python, working close to real-time constraints. - Collaborate with autonomy, perception, and controls engineers to align simulation behavior with real-world systems. - Debug complex interactions between physics, sensors, autonomy logic, and rendering. - Help shape the long-term technical direction of the simulator as both a product and an internal platform. - Contribute to documentation and shared understanding of how the simulator works internally. QUALIFICATIONS: - Strong software engineering experience with C++ and Python. - Experience building complex systems where performance, determinism, or correctness matter. - Comfort reasoning about time-synchronized systems, state machines, or real-time execution. - Ability to work in a large, evolving codebase with multiple stakeholders. - Interest in robotics, simulation, or physical systems (prior robotics experience is a plus, not a requirement). BONUS EXPERIENCE: - Robotics, simulation, game engines, or real-time systems. - Physics engines, sensor modeling, or hardware abstraction layers. - Multithreaded or low-latency system design. - Experience debugging systems that span software and physical behavior. Compensation: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Masters, and $70/hr for PhD students*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends. *Compensation for certain positions may vary based on the position's location. #LI-DK1 At Skydio we believe that diversity drives innovation. We have created a multidisciplinary environment that embraces the power of diverse perspectives to create elegant solutions for complex problems. We are committed to growing our network of people, programs, and resources to nurture an inclusive culture. jobs.title: Packaging Engineering Intern
jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will : ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting ​ Implement new ideas , be constantly challenged, and develop your skills ​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business ​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture ​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions. ​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward. ​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts. ​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives . ​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships. ​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​ As a Mechanical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams: Research & Development New Product Development R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products. They research new technologies , customer expectations, business requirements and regulations. They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts. These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production. Product Engineering R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies , customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products. Test Lab Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that we get to be the Mythbusters of our division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, we are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you! Majors Targeted: Biomedical Engineering , Mechanical engineering or related majors What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship . ​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above ( verified at time of hire ) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future . ​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment . $ 20 min hourly wage – $3 5 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Facilities Mechanical & Process Water Intern
jobs.body: About TI Texas Instruments Incorporated (TI) is a global semiconductor design and manufacturing company that develops analog ICs and embedded processors. By employing the world’s brightest minds, TI creates innovations that shape the future of technology. TI is helping about 100,000 customers transform the future, today. We’re committed to building a better future – from the responsible manufacturing of our semiconductors, to caring for our employees, to giving back inside our communities and developing great minds. Put your talent to work with us – change the world, love your job! About the Internship As an Intern at TI, you will be assigned meaningful projects related to your educational background that are challenging, rewarding, and beneficial to the Facilities organization. Your projects will focus on cost and energy reduction, plant and process safety improvements, reliability enhancement, and complex problem-solving. You will be fully integrated into the Facilities team and supported by a network of engineers, technicians, operators, and leadership as you work through real-world industrial challenges. Beyond your technical work, you will have unique opportunities to network with other interns through social events, volunteering, and professional development sessions. Put your talent to work with us as a Manufacturing Facilities Mechanical Engineering Intern – change the world, love your job! About the Job Facilities Mechanical Engineering interns will have the opportunity to work on the critical infrastructure and mechanical systems that support our semiconductor manufacturing operations. You will gain hands-on experience with large-scale mechanical systems, including HVAC (air systems, Fan Filter Units, and exhaust systems), chilled and condenser water systems, cooling towers, and fire protection systems. Working in a cross-disciplinary setting, you will collaborate alongside electrical, chemical, and controls engineers to improve the reliability and efficiency of our facility's mechanical infrastructure. Key Learning & Support Opportunities: 1. Sustaining & Systems Engineering: Mechanical Systems Exposure: Gain practical knowledge of Non-Process Systems such as HVAC, DX systems, and plant/house vacuum systems. Operational Excellence: Support the team in maximizing operational and maintenance efficiency for mechanical systems. Reliability & Risk Analysis: Learn to apply reliability-focused methodologies, including FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) and Root Cause Analysis (RCA). Technical Modeling: Assist in learning hydraulic system calculations, flow modeling, and psychrometric heat transfer calculations. Compliance: Understand how mechanical systems integrate with building codes (IFC, IBC, NFPA) and semiconductor high-purity requirements. 2. Project Management Support: Project Lifecycle: Participate in the engineering analysis, design, and installation oversight for mechanical distribution systems. Construction Management: Support the review of construction documentation, such as submittals and Requests for Information (RFIs). Financial Literacy: Learn how to manage project-related financial information, including change notices, purchase orders, and capital forecasting. Commissioning: Assist in the execution of project commissioning to ensure all mechanical equipment and infrastructure perform as designed. Design Documentation: Assist in creating and managing project documentation, including construction drawings, Piping & Instrumentation Diagrams (P&ID), and Process Flow Diagrams (PFD). jobs.body: About Varda Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses. From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind. Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital. Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL. Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem. Internships are full-time and on-site in Los Angeles, CA. To be considered for this internship, candidates must be actively enrolled in an accredited undergraduate or graduate degree program. jobs.title: Government Affairs Intern
jobs.body: About Us At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space. The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy. ABOUT THE SUMMER INTERNSHIP PROGRAM Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater. Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else. We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer. We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules: Cohort #1 Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13 Cohort #2 Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10 All internship roles are based at one of our offices (Torrance/Idaho Falls/Washington D.C.) and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package if eligible. ABOUT THE ROLE Antares Nuclear is seeking a highly motivated and resourceful Government Affairs Intern to support the company's government affairs, communications, international business development, and commercial business development efforts from our Washington, D.C. office. This position offers a unique opportunity to work on emerging national security and energy policy issues while helping advance the commercialization and international deployment of next-generation nuclear technology. The intern will support research, stakeholder engagement, strategic planning, and business development initiatives, working closely with Antares leadership and cross-functional teams. The ideal candidate is an excellent writer and researcher, has a strong interest in national security, energy, public policy, or emerging technologies, and thrives in a fast-paced environment where initiative and attention to detail are essential. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: - Monitor congressional activity, federal legislation, appropriations, defense authorization, and executive branch initiatives relevant to advanced nuclear energy and microreactor deployment. - Research and analyze policy developments across the Pentagon, Department of Energy, Department of State, Department of Commerce, NASA, and other relevant federal agencies. - Assist in preparing briefing materials, talking points, policy memoranda, presentations, and other materials for meetings with government officials and congressional offices. - Track engagement with congressional offices, federal agencies, military services, and other key stakeholders. - Identify opportunities to advance policies, programs, and funding initiatives that support microreactor deployment for national security and commercial applications. - Support the development of strategic communications materials that articulate Antares’ mission, technology, and value proposition to government, commercial, and international audiences. - Draft and edit executive talking points, briefing materials, presentation content, website copy, and other communications products. - Monitor media coverage, industry developments, and public discourse related to advanced nuclear energy, national security, and microreactor deployment. - Help translate complex technical and policy issues into clear, accessible messages tailored to different audiences, including policymakers, prospective customers, strategic partners, and the general public. - Assist in developing communications strategies for key company milestones, government announcements, industry events, and strategic partnerships. - Identify opportunities to raise awareness of Antares’ work through relevant publications, industry forums, conferences, and other external channels. - Research international markets and identify countries, government agencies, utilities, defense organizations, and other prospective customers for Antares microreactors. - Assess country-level opportunities based on energy demand, national security priorities, regulatory frameworks, financing mechanisms, and government support for nuclear energy. - Support engagement with U.S. embassies, the State Department, the Foreign Commercial Service, international partners, and prospective overseas customers. - Research foreign government procurement processes, export requirements, financing options, and other factors affecting international reactor deployment. - Prepare country profiles, market assessments, customer briefings, and presentations to support Antares' international growth strategy. - Identify prospective commercial customers and strategic partners across sectors such as data centers, critical infrastructure, industrial facilities, remote power systems, and other energy-intensive applications. - Research customer power requirements, market dynamics, competing energy technologies, and potential use cases for microreactors. - Assist with developing customer presentations, market analyses, business cases, and strategic partnership proposals. - Maintain and update business development pipelines, stakeholder databases, and opportunity trackers. - Support preparation for customer meetings, industry conferences, and strategic partner engagements. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: - Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in public policy, international relations, political science, economics, business, engineering, energy policy, or a related field. - Strong research, analytical, and written communication skills. - Demonstrated interest in national security, energy, emerging technologies, international affairs, or commercial strategy. - Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, concise briefings and recommendations. - Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously. - Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly PowerPoint, Word, and Excel. - A proactive, intellectually curious approach and willingness to take ownership of assignments. PREFERRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE: - Sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to manage sensitive matters and competing priorities in a fast-moving environment. - Experience with congressional offices, federal agencies, think tanks, political campaigns, consulting, or business development. - Familiarity with U.S. national security policy, federal appropriations, international trade, or the energy sector. - Experience conducting market research, developing presentations, or preparing policy and business memoranda. - Foreign language proficiency or international experience. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: - Ability to travel as needed for government, regulator, supplier, customer, and international partner engagements. - Ability to support time-sensitive milestones or incidents outside standard business hours when necessary. LOCATION - We are located in downtown Washington, DC in a space designed for team collaboration and easy access to Capitol Hill, federal government offices, foreign embassies, and DC-based think tanks. Culture At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful: - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done” - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption Equal Opportunity Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status. ITAR REQUIREMENTS To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987. Pay range: $34 per hour.

jobs.title: 2027 Internship Product Intern
jobs.body: JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs. In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks. This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us. ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM Bedrock's Product team decides what our autonomous machines should learn to do next. We also make sure the people who work alongside them get real value from them: operators, site managers and the construction companies we partner with. Our problems rarely arrive as specs. Which task or machine type is worth taking on next? How do you turn "digs like an expert" into a number you can measure? What does a partner need to see before trusting a 40-ton machine on their site? As our Product intern, you'll get a problem like that, not a task list, and own it for the summer. You'll frame it, work out the answer, build what's needed, and bring the team a recommendation they can act on. You'll work the way our team does: with AI tools in hand, going from question to working prototype in days, not weeks. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own an open product problem end to end: frame it, find the data and the people who know, decide what to build, and ship it before the summer ends - Turn fleet data from real jobsites into decisions: how well our machines perform, where they struggle, and what that means for what we build next - Prototype with AI coding tools and agents: internal tools, data pipelines, automated workflows, and working demos that make an idea concrete instead of slides about it - Spend time at our field sites with operators and site teams, and turn what you see into requirements engineers can build against - Work across autonomy, evaluation, operations and commercial teams to pressure-test ideas and unblock yourself - Write up your findings and present a clear recommendation to leadership: what you found, what you built, and what we should do next WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR REQUIRED - Currently pursuing a BS or MS in computer science, engineering, math, economics or another technical or quantitative field, or bringing equivalent experience building things - A track record of agency: you've taken on a problem nobody assigned you (a project, a tool, a company, a research question) and carried it to a real result - AI-native: you use tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex every day to build, analyze and write, and you know how to check their output and when not to trust it - Hands-on with data: Python or SQL, plus comfort reading code and following a technical discussion with engineers - Clear, concise writing: you can turn a messy problem into a one-page recommendation someone can act on - Willingness to spend time at our field sites, in PPE, around heavy equipment PREFERRED - Something you built that real people use: an app, an internal tool, an open-source project, a startup - Prior product, engineering or founding-team experience at a startup - Experience with robotics, autonomy, ML or data-heavy products - Interest in construction or other physical-world industries; no prior experience needed About This Internship This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited." Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic. Reasonable Accommodations We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please let your recruiter know so we can support you.

jobs.body: > Requisition Number: 79307 The company built on breakthroughs. ​ Join us.​ Corning is one of the world’s leading innovators in glass, ceramic, and materials science. Projects span machine-learned force field (MLFF) development for mixed-oxide thin films, mesoscale modeling of glass-ceramic etching, and coupled multiphysics modeling of laser damage in optical coating systems — each tied to an active experimental or engineering program. You'll select a project aligned with your background, develop and validate models, and deliver findings at the close of the summer. quantify uncertainty and sensitivity to key parameters Deliver a documented model or workflow, a concise technical summary, and a final presentation with results and recommendations for follow-on work Experiences/Education - Required Currently enrolled in an accredited Master's or doctoral degree program in Materials Science, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Computational Science, or a related discipline Completed foundational coursework in materials science and at least one relevant area (e.g., numerical methods, thermodynamics, kinetics/transport, heat transfer, quantum mechanics, solid-state physics, or machine learning) Required Skills Working proficiency in Python or another scientific programming language, including data analysis and visualization Familiarity with generative AI tools and agentic workflow frameworks Experience working in a Linux and/or high-performance computing (HPC) environment Prior research or project experience using computational methods Desired Skills Experience with atomistic simulation packages (e.g., LAMMPS, VASP, or ASE -- Atomic Simulation Environment) Experience training, fine-tuning, or validating machine-learning models for materials or molecular systems Experience with COMSOL Multiphysics, finite-element methods, or coupled multiphysics simulation Familiarity with thin films, optical coatings, glass or glass-ceramics, etching, defects, or laser-material interactions Experience with version control, workflow automation, statistical analysis, or uncertainty quantification Soft Skills Scientific curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar modeling methods and materials systems. jobs.body: Job Description The Role: Improved cellular communication standards, e.g., 5G, and infrastructure supports make rich infotainment applications in vehicles more feasible. Yet the highly dynamic cellular connectivity makes it very challenging to provide consistent Quality of Experience (QoE) to GM customers. To this end, there is an immediate demand to improved system architecture and optimization mechanisms to maintaining service quality, especially under the highly dynamic cellular networks. Data-intensive applications under cellular networks are most easily affected by network performance fluctuations due to their exclusive demands for network resources. As a result, Cloud and vehicle system co-design will offer unique opportunities in guaranteeing user QoE. What You’ll Do: · Understand the current status of cellar network, including deployment and communication performance. · Algorithm design to address QoE degradation as hinted by cellular communication performance issues, including latency reduction, service continuity, service smoothness and if necessary minimum QoE sacrifice. ·Vehicle and Cloud/Edge end-to-end system design in support of the design algorithms to ensure QoE. · Implement and test an end-to-end system in GM test vehicles, demonstrating efficacy of the system design and algorithmic contribution. Actively document and potentially further improve ideas generated while working on the system. · Extensively evaluate system performance using a data-driven approach with good test scenario coverage. · Practice forward-thinking, be comprehensive in system and algorithmic design, foresee research challenges and proactively identify solutions. Required Qualifications: Pursuit of a Master or PhD degree Must be a current student Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months Background in mobile networks and wireless communications, particularly on Cloud/Edge computing and 4G/5G/6G standards. Knowledge in end-to-end system design and optimization, and protocols on handling heavy data delivery. Experience in working with data-intensive applications, e.g., video streaming. Experience in commonly used tools in handling video data, e.g., Gstreamer, ffmpeg, etc. Software engineering skills such as C++, C#, Java/Kotlin and/or Python as well as understanding of multithreading programming and real time system development. Strong in data-driven analytics Highly motivated to conduct quality work, independent in thinking and able to actively communicate with team members. Excellent communication skills in writing and verbal communication. Preferred Qualifications: PhD GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need GM immigration sponsorship now or in the future. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc). jobs.title: Product Development Engineer Intern
jobs.body: To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology. Group/Division The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The Film and Scatterometry Technology (FaST) division delivers industry-leading metrology solutions essential to advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Its portfolio includes systems for measuring film thickness, critical dimensions, composition, and resistivity—key to developing and scaling next-gen IC processes. FaST partners closely with customers from early R&D through high-volume production, ensuring performance and process alignment. What You'll Do In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise. Responsibilities: In this role you will be responsible for: Assisting in the development, release and support of KLA Film metrology products. Integral to this role is using one’s technical knowledge and skill for the development of a deep understanding on the customer applications and develop the technologies and products to resolve the challenging problems. The successful candidate will develop the ability to collect and appropriately filter observations to generate problem statements, produce data collection plans, analyze data and prescribe corrective actions. Greatcommunication is required, including oral, writing, and publishing after action reports, meeting minutes and project summaries. Qualifications: PhD candidate with a background in Experimental Physics or Engineering (electrical, mechanical, optical, etc.) Understanding of optical, electrical, mechanical and software systems and their interactions in the context of complex industrial equipment is a plus. Enthusiastic communicator to provide detailed guidance to colleagues to solve problems, and technical summaries for internal functional teams and management. Minimum Qualifications PhD candidate with a background in Experimental Physics or Engineering (electrical, mechanical, optical, etc.) About KLA We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us. jobs.title: Integration & Missile Validation Engineer - Undergraduate Placement 2027
jobs.body: Integration & Missile Validation Engineer - Undergraduate Programme 2027 MBDA develop some of the world’s highest performing weapon systems; but how do we demonstrate and prove this? Integration and Missile Validation (IMV) is an integral part to ensuring our weapon systems meet customer requirements and increasing the sovereign capability. Within this role, you will experience the many aspects of proving to become a well-rounded IMV Engineer. Salary : £25,420 Dynamic working: 4-5 days per week on site due to workload classification Security clearance : British Citizen or a Dual UK national with British citizenship. Restrictions and/or limitations relating to nationality and/or rights to work may apply. As a minimum and after offer stage, all successful candidates will need to undergo HMG Basic Personnel Security Standard checks (BPSS), which are managed by the MBDA Personnel Security Team. This role is scheduled to close for applications at midnight on Monday 4th January 2027 but may close earlier depending on application volumes. What we can offer you: 1 year placement: Starting September 2027, that allows you to apply your university learning to real-world projects and technologies Perform well on your placement and you could secure a graduate role before your final year Company bonus : Based on company performance and will vary year to year Pension : Maximum total (employer and employee) contribution of up to 14% Overtime: Opportunity for paid overtime Annual Leave: 25 days plus option to purchase extra holiday Flexi Leave: Up to 15 additional days Facilities : Fantastic site facilities including subsidised meals, free car parking and much more… Healthcare Cash Plan: The Healthcare Cash Plan benefit provides the option to claim cash back on everyday healthcare expenses such as optical, dental, health and wellbeing and more. The opportunity: Examples of IMV activities you could be involved with include: Ground Trials: Testing the robustness of our products through various environments to ensure it can survive and operate within the real world. This can involve vibration, shock and climatic testing. Flight Trials: Integrating subsystems onto aircraft to simulate the behaviour of the missile during flight. Functional Integration: Demonstrating hardware and software of systems work together and respond as expected. Firing Trials: Final evaluation testing to ensure the full weapon system works and demonstrating the capability of the product to the customer. In-Service Support: Testing and monitoring in-service products with the customer. Support Trials and Test Equipment: Designing support test equipment and software to support proving activities. As part of completing these activities, you will have the opportunity to learn: How to plan and design test strategies to support proving the capability of various missile systems. How to integrate various missile equipment to test rigs. To develop your problem-solving skills through debugging test systems. Strengthen software skills through generating test scripts. To develop confidence with handling various hand and power tools. How to design, develop and use test equipment to support overall proving activities. To increase confidence in the processing, analysing and forming conclusions from data, as well as writing technical documentation. Whether your background is in engineering, sciences, maths or any STEM related subject, you will enjoy this role if you: Enjoy team collaboration and the opportunity to communicate technical information with a variety of teams. Like to find solutions to problems using creativity and new ways of thinking. Find exploring new experiences and developing new skills exciting. Are logical in the methods you use to prove. Are eager to get hands-on supporting work within a lab environment or offsite on a trial. What we’re looking for from you: Current undergraduate working towards a degree in an Engineering, Physics, Mathematical Sciences, Technology, Computing or a General Science discipline. Our company: Peace is not a given, Freedom is not a given, Sovereignty is not a given MBDA is a leading defence organisation. We are proud of the role we play in supporting the Armed Forces who protect our nations. We partner with governments to work together towards a common goal, defending our freedom. We are proud of our employee-led networks, examples include: Gender Equality, Pride, Menopause Matters, Parents and Carers, Armed Forces, Ethnic Diversity, Neurodiversity, Disability and more… We recognise that everyone is unique, and we encourage you to speak to us should you require any advice, support or adjustments throughout our recruitment process. Follow us on LinkedIn (MBDA), X (@MBDA_UK), Instagram (MBDA_UK) and Glassdoor or visit our MBDA Careers website for more information.

jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. Join Micron’s Advanced Packaging Technology Development (TD) team, where innovation and precision come together to develop next-generation interconnect technologies. The team develops solutions designed to improve semiconductor performance, reliability, and advanced packaging capabilities. As an Advanced Package TD Process Intern, you will collaborate with experienced engineers to support development of technologies including hybrid bonding, micro bump technology, Through-Silicon Vias (TSV), and thermal management. You will gain hands-on experience in structured problem-solving, line monitoring, data analysis, experimental design, and project management while contributing to process optimization and yield improvement. Define, complete, and analyze Design of Experiments (DoE) for advanced packaging and interconnect process development. Analyze process, line-monitoring, and yield data; develop new monitoring methods and critical metrics to support process optimization. Present technical findings and collaborate with engineering teams across sites and functional areas. Demonstrated ability to collaborate and communicate technical findings across multi-functional teams. Ability to prioritize multiple technical projects, adapt to changing responsibilities, and deliver results within project timelines and resource constraints. Experience Using AI, Code Assist, or Agent-based solutions for technical analysis, engineering workflows, or related applications. Preferred Qualifications Experience with semiconductor process technologies, including advanced packaging, back-end-of-line (BEOL), advanced interconnect, hybrid bonding, micro bump technology, or TSV. Experience with structured problem-solving or decision-making methodologies such as Kepner-Tregoe (KT). Academic or research experience related to advanced packaging, interconnect technologies, or package thermal performance and thermal management. jobs.body: About Oshkosh Delivery, an Oshkosh company Oshkosh Delivery is dedicated to redefining the future of last-mile and commercial delivery. Built on Oshkosh Corporation’s legacy of engineering excellence and innovation, we design and manufacture advanced delivery vehicles that are durable, efficient, and sustainable. With a focus on reliability, driver experience, and cutting-edge technology, Oshkosh Delivery empowers fleets and businesses to move goods smarter, safer, and with confidence, today and for the road ahead. Position Overview: The Mechanical Engineer Intern will support the Design Engineering organization and manufacturing operations by assisting with production readiness activities, engineering investigations, and corrective actions under the guidance of senior engineers. YOUR IMPACT: Assist with design support activities in production operations, learning vehicle systems and manufacturing processes. Support communication and liaison activities between the Product Design Team and the Operations Team. Assist with torque studies and related testing activities. Support root cause analysis of production issues by collecting data, documenting observations, and assisting with failure analysis under engineer supervision. Help develop and document corrective actions in collaboration with Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, and Operations teams. Participate in production trials of new product designs and design changes, including data collection, observation, and results documentation. Perform engineering calculations, analysis, and research tasks as assigned under supervision, following Oshkosh and industry engineering standards. Assist in communicating technical findings and issue status to team members and supervision. Support project activities of limited scope, working as part of a cross-functional engineering team. Help create and maintain project documentation, technical reports, and analysis records. Collaborate with engineers, technicians, and other interns on assigned tasks and projects. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related engineering field from an accredited institution. Completed at least sophomore year coursework (or equivalent). Strong academic performance (minimum 3.0 GPA preferred). Basic understanding of engineering principles and problem-solving methodologies. jobs.body: The Bosch Group is a leading global supplier of technology and services. OfficeHaus Building – 32 Tan Thang Street, Son Ky Ward, Tan Phu District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam 3. jobs.title: Driving Foundations Research Intern
jobs.body: The Bosch Research and Technology Center North America with offices in Sunnyvale, California, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Cambridge, Massachusetts is a part of the global Bosch Group (www.bosch.com), a company with over 70 billion euro revenue, 400,000 employees worldwide, a very diverse product portfolio, and a history spanning over 125 years. The Research and Technology Center North America (RTC-NA) is dedicated to providing technologies and system solutions for various Bosch business fields, primarily in the field of artificial intelligence, energy technologies, internet technologies, circuit design, semiconductors and wireless, as well as advanced MEMS design. As a part of the global research, our AI research in Silicon Valley focuses on Foundation Models, Big Data Visual Analytics, Explainable AI (XAI), Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision & Mixed Reality, Cloud Robotics, Data Science, AI System Engineering, Time-series Analysis. We develop scalable, intelligent, and trustworthy AIoT solutions for Bosch products and services in application areas such as automated driving, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), robotics, smart manufacturing, enterprise AI, health care, smart home and building solutions. Originating from the AI research in Silicon Valley, our Intelligent Autonomous Systems group is responsible for enabling future autonomous Bosch products by pushing the boundaries of automated driving, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), robotics and automation through key innovations that encompass system architecture and AI components. These include methods for motion planning, high level task planning and decision making as well as systems for making these technologies work on real products by building frameworks that take advantage of technologies in the field of reliable distributed computing. We work with internal partners of different Bosch business units to transfer our solutions into future products. We also actively collaborate with leading groups in academia and industry to promote research ideas and publish research findings in internationally renowned conferences and journals such as CVPR, ICRA, IROS, RSS, NeurIPS and CoRL. At Bosch Research, you will work on the latest challenges drawn from Mobility, including autonomous parking and driving. You will work closely with experienced Bosch researchers in Silicon Valley and across our global research network, receive mentorship from leading AI experts, and contribute to publications in top-tier AI conferences and journals. This internship offers a unique opportunity to combine scientific innovation with real-world deployment and technology transfer. Depending on your expertise and interests, you will contribute to one or more cutting-edge research topics, including: Autonomous E2E/ World Action Models (WAM) models Planning and decision making under uncertainty and noise Road user behavior modeling in dynamic scenarios Post-training, Reinforcement Learning, and Self-Play Foundation model distillation (i.e. student/teacher) Multi-modal trajectory modeling using vision and priors Key responsibilities include: Conduct novel research in E2E, Distillation, and RL methods. Develop research prototypes that demonstrate innovative ideas and solutions. Collaborate closely with Bosch researchers and subject-matter experts. Analyze experimental results and identify opportunities for scientific innovation. Publish research outcomes in top-tier AI and robotics conferences and journals, such as CoRL, ICRA, CVPR, NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR. Present research findings internally and externally through technical reports, publications, and presentations. Basic Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Ph.D. or Master's program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, or a related field. Minimum GPA of 3.0 Strong research background in autonomous driving, robotics, computer vision, machine learning, or related areas Research experience in post-training, reinforcement learning, self-play, and end-to-end systems. Experience developing AI and robotics systems using modern frameworks and ecosystems Strong programming skills in Python and experience with modern AI/ML framework Experience conducting independent research, designing experiments, and analyzing results. Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to work effectively in a collaborative research environment. Preferred Qualifications Publication record in top-tier AI, CV, or robotics venues (e.g., CoRL, ICRA, CVPR, NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR). Research experience in autonomous driving and robotics architectures, task planning, reasoning, and autonomous decision making. Experience with behavior modeling, scene understanding, and prediction Experience with multi-modal foundation models involving language, vision, and structured data. Experience in reinforcement learning, online learning, or adaptive decision-making systems. Experience with autonomous driving benchmarking, evaluation methodologies, reliability, and safety. Experience working with real-time systems and full driving/parking/robotics stack(s) Open-source contributions or demonstrated leadership in AI research communities. Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability / veterans *Bosch adheres to Federal, State, and Local laws regarding drug-testing. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a drug screen and background check. Candidates who have been offered the position must pass both screenings before their start date. BOSCH is a proud supporter of STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering & Mathematics) FIRST Robotics (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology) AWIM (A World In Motion) The U.S. base salary range for this intern position is $46.00-69.00 hourly. Within the range, individual pay is determined based on several factors, including, but not limited to, type of degree, work experience and job knowledge, complexity of the role, type of position, job location, etc. Your Hiring Manager can share more details about the specific salary range for this position during the interview process. jobs.title: Test Engineering Intern Summer 2027
jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Test Engineering Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Stennis, Mississippi, you will have the opportunity to learn about the Archimedes Engine test operations on-site as well as actively participate as an operator by supporting engine rebuilds, test readiness, and hardware swaps. The Test Operations team manages the activation and operation of test facilities for the Archimedes rocket engine, collaborating with propulsion teams to develop test procedures and sequencing and ultimately enabling the path to launch our Neutron vehicle. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an engineering discipline such as Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Experience with Soildworks, MATLAB, and SiemensNX Python and Java experience Proficient in Computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/ CAM) Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing experience Experience working with pressurized systems ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Rate: $25.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. jobs.title: Autonomy Engineer Intern, Computer Vision / Deep Learning, 2027
jobs.body: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions. About the role: The core of our system is the computer vision algorithms that allow drones to understand the world around them. You will architect and implement the algorithms that run on every drone powered by Skydio as part of a world class computer vision and deep learning team with researchers who have pushed the state of the art in academia and industry. As a Research Intern, you will be paired up with one or more members of our core software development team, assuming direct ownership of a project that meaningfully advances the capabilities of our team and products. If you have a strong foundation in math, theory, and software development and you are interested in directly contributing to the development of the next generation of autonomy algorithms and pushing them into real products, we would love to hear from you. How you'll make an impact: - Enable rapid research and development of intelligent systems with advanced autonomous capabilities beyond anything that exists in the world today - Research, prototype, and generally assess the feasibility of new approaches - Imagine and then implement new features that unlock magic for our users - Characterize and quantify the performance of core components of the software and hardware stack What makes you a good fit: - High proficiency in C++ and/or Python and PyTorch - Demonstrated enthusiasm for one or more of the following: computer vision, deep learning, motion planning, dynamics and controls, 3D graphics, distributed systems, and tools/infrastructure - Solid software engineering foundation and a commitment to writing clean, well-architected code - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative, small team environment - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions. jobs.title: Advanced Manufacturing Engineering Intern - The Toro Company
jobs.body: The 2027 Summer Internship Program will run from May 17, 2027, through August 6, 2027. Candidates must be available to start on May 17 and participate through the duration of the program. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future. Who Are We? The Toro Company (TTC) has delivered market-leading, innovative products and outstanding customer care for more than 100 years. With over 11,000 employees worldwide, TTC is headquartered in Bloomington, Minnesota, USA. Our company designs and manufactures turf maintenance equipment; turf irrigation systems; landscape and lighting products; snow and ice management solutions; agricultural irrigation systems; rental, specialty and underground construction equipment; and residential turf and snow equipment. We market and sell TTC products worldwide through a network of distributors, dealers, mass retailers, hardware retailers, equipment rental center and home centers—as well as online direct to end users. Join The Toro Company’s Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) Team, where innovation meets hands-on experience. As an intern, you’ll work alongside industry experts to help bring new products from concept to production. You’ll gain exposure to design for manufacturability (DFMA), process development, cost optimization, and advanced tooling technologies—all while contributing to real-world projects that make an impact. What Will You Do? In order to grow and build a successful career with The Toro Company, you will be responsible for: Work under the guidance of an Advanced Manufacturing Engineer on active projects. Participate in the New Product Development (NPD) process from prototype to production. Support local plant builds (prototype, pilot, and production). Assist in assembly process development and improvement. Perform DFMA reviews and contribute to cost justification/ROI analyses. Evaluate vertical integration and outsourcing opportunities. Contribute to the creation of data-driven analytics tools. Deliver a final presentation to Toro leaders on your project work and outcomes. What Do You Need? To be considered for this role, an individual should meet the following minimal requirements: Currently enrolled in a 4-year accredited program in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Industrial, Electrical or Agricultural Engineering. Junior standing or higher (graduation no sooner than Dec 2026). Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work independently or in a team. Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite. Experience with Microsoft Power BI and Power Apps. Experience with CAD/CREO/CreoView (preferred). Interest in manufacturing technologies and continuous improvement. What Can We Give You? At The Toro Company, we are always working to make sure our interns know just how valued they are. In addition to a competitive pay- The Toro Company offers interns a variety of perks, including: Dress for your day – We know you're more productive when you're comfortable, which is why TTC employees are encouraged to take advantage of our casual, corporate environment. Volunteerism – The Toro Company is proud to provide interns 8 hours of paid time to volunteer in the community. Summer Hours *Based on Location* – Enjoy a flexible schedule during the summer! By working a little more during the first few days of the week, TTC employees at certain locations are able to start their weekends early and leave by noon on Friday. Competitive Pay – Competitive compensation with an anticipated hourly rate of $22–$28. Actual rates may vary based on factors such as academic standing, business function, and other relevant considerations. The Toro Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants based on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military service, or other non-merit factors. jobs.title: R&D Internship - Corrosion Protection
jobs.body: > About VAT Group At VAT, we change the world with vacuum solutions. As the world’s leading supplier of high-performance vacuum valves, we have been driving innovation for more than 60 years. With over 3,200 employees worldwide, we operate from our headquarters in Haag, Switzerland, with manufacturing sites in Switzerland, Malaysia and Romania, as well as sales and service hubs around the world. We are guided by our passions integrity, teamwork, customer centricity, and innovation – always working together as #oneVAT. Joining us means becoming part of a passionate, international team where your voice is heard, your ideas matter, and your career growth is supported. R&D Internship - Corrosion Protection Purpose of the role We at VAT Group AG invite a talented and passionate Internship candidate to join our Corporate R&D. Fueled by the ever-growing demand for computational power, the leading-edge technology nodes (≤7nm) require process control at the atomic scale. At VAT, we are developing the next generation of advanced sensing and vacuum solutions for the semiconductor industry. Semiconductor manufacturing processes often utilize corrosive gases and plasma environments that pose a risk for VAT’s products. We are seeking an intern to join our team and focus on advancing the corrosion protection strategies for our sensors and products. This internship will be located in Zürich, Switzerland and will require occasional travel to Haag, Switzerland. What we offer Join a global leader at the forefront of semiconductor innovation, we are a globally leading company in the semiconductor industry. A technologically advanced and innovative working environment with Modern Laboratory and testing facilities. Thrive in a collaborative, innovative environment that celebrates bold ideas and outstanding execution — where your potential knows no bounds. Enjoy an exceptional working environment with great amenities at our VAT Group offices in Zurich and Haag. Receive competitive compensation and benefits aligned with your expertise and contributions. Responsibilities Support the development of protective measures to enhance material and sensor durability under extreme conditions. Assist in the design, implementation, and testing of corrosion protection strategies. Conduct failure analysis and material testing to identify failure mechanisms. Design experiments for testing the durability of VAT’s products in plasma etching systems. Your competencies acquired at the end of the internship This internship aims to provide you with practical skills and knowledge in testing and experimental procedures in the semiconductor industry, preparing you for a future technical career. As a research & development intern in our dynamic environment, you will get the opportunity to work on real-life industrial challenges. By the end of the internship, you will have acquired the following competencies: Technical Skills: Gain hands-on experience in a cross-disciplinary project, where you will expand your knowledge in physics, chemistry, materials science, and both mechanical and electrical engineering. Analytical Skills : Ability to plan, execute, and evaluate experiments, and to analyze and interpret experimental data. Communication Skills: Experience in presenting technical information and progress reports, as well as participating in technical discussions. Problem-Solving Skills : Practical experience in diagnosing and solving real-world problems in the semiconductor industry. Collaboration Skills: Work within a dynamic team, including engineers, materials scientists, and designers, to address complex challenges. Industry Experience: Insight into the practical aspects of product design, testing, and refinement within a commercial product development cycle. Qualifications Current master’s student or recently completed master’s degree in materials science, chemistry, physics, or engineering. Excellent communication skills, able to work independently, and passionate about learning. Experience with or knowledge of material characterization and semiconductor fabrication. (optional) Understanding of dry etching processes and thin-film deposition processes. (optional) Practical experience working in a laboratory or clean environment. Our commitment to inclusion, fairness and equal opportunities We believe in meaningful careers, continuous learning, and equal opportunities for everyone to drive our innovation and success. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace. If you have concerns, our compliance channel is available at our website. jobs.title: Aerodynamics & Analysis Engineering Internship - Summer 2027
jobs.body: About Varda Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses. From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind. Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital. Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL. Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
