jobs.title: Launch & Scale Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Launch & Scale Team The Launch & Scale team builds the operating system that brings new sites, metros, and partners online and helps the network scale reliably. We turn complex dependencies into clear launch plans, readiness mechanisms, tools, and operating rhythms. We partner across infrastructure, permitting, flight operations, maintenance, commercial, partner readiness, and field operations. Our work stays close to real launches so that field lessons become repeatable systems rather than one-off fixes. As an intern, you will report to the Director, Launch & Site Operations and work closely with Launch Managers and cross-functional teams that bring the network online. The Role As the Launch & Scale Intern, you will contribute to a high-impact project that improves how Zipline plans, executes, and learns from launches. You will support Launch Managers by bringing structure to dependencies, analyzing readiness and performance, and helping teams turn field lessons into repeatable tools. You may spend time close to active launches, but you will work with experienced teammates rather than serve as the accountable launch owner. You will also own a clearly scoped project—such as a dashboard, process improvement, playbook, or lightweight automation—from problem definition through pilot and handoff. Along the way, you will receive coaching from the Director, Launch & Site Operations and collaborate with operators, engineers, commercial teammates, and field teams. What You'll Do Support integrated launch plans for assigned workstreams by organizing milestones, dependencies, owners, risks, and open decisions. Analyze launch and site-operations data to identify bottlenecks, inconsistencies, and opportunities to improve speed, quality, or repeatability. Prepare materials for readiness reviews and operating forums, including concise status summaries, action logs, and decision briefs. Work with Launch Managers and functional teams to follow up on commitments, reconcile conflicting information, and surface blockers early. Build or improve practical tools such as dashboards, playbooks, templates, checklists, or lightweight automations. Participate in selected onsite launch activities, capture field observations, and translate lessons into process improvements. Own a scoped internship project from problem definition through pilot, measurement, and an accepted handoff to the team. What You'll Bring Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in operations, engineering, business, supply chain, data and analytics, or a related field. Structured problem-solving skills and curiosity about how complex physical or technical systems work. Comfort with quantitative analysis, including spreadsheets and at least one data or automation tool such as SQL, Python, or a business-intelligence platform. Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to make complex information easy to understand. Evidence of following through on a project involving multiple contributors through coursework, work, research, or extracurricular experience. Comfort operating in ambiguity, asking good questions, incorporating feedback, and staying reliable on details. Ability to work onsite in South San Francisco and willingness to travel occasionally within the United States to support launches. What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September). Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position. The hourly rate for this internship is $34 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

jobs.title: Chemical | Mechanical Engineering | Resilience Engineering internship: critical gas infrastructure
jobs.body: Introduction Every advanced chip in the world depends on lithography systems that only ASML can build. In Veldhoven, these systems are developed, built and tested with the support of a continuous supply of ultra-pure process gases. ASML invests extensively in robust gas infrastructure, redundancy and strong partnerships with leading industrial gas suppliers. The Process Technology team for critical assets owns these process-critical utilities end to end. In this internship, you will explore how this infrastructure performs under exceptional circumstances, and how engineering, operations and suppliers coordinate an effective response. You will strengthen resilience through scenario-based engineering, at the heart of the world's most advanced semiconductor equipment manufacturing. Your assignment What happens when the unexpected hits the infrastructure behind the world's most advanced lithography systems? At ASML, bulk gases play a critical role in our manufacturing and testing operations. Ensuring their continuous availability requires sophisticated engineering, robust infrastructure, redundancy and close collaboration with leading industrial gas suppliers. In this internship, you will take that resilience one step further. Working within the Process Technology team, you will explore challenging what-if scenarios. What happens if a major installation becomes unavailable? How do storage capacities, backup systems and alternative supply arrangements respond? Which engineering and operational decisions matter most, and how can different stakeholders coordinate effectively? You will combine engineering analysis with real-world operational challenges, working closely with experts across ASML and its supplier network. Your main responsibilities will be: Understand the infrastructure, technologies and redundancy concepts supporting ASML's bulk gas systems Develop and evaluate credible disruption scenarios using chemical and mechanical engineering principles Model gas consumption, storage capacities, system behavior and available response options under different operating conditions Assess process safety and operational risks during abnormal operating conditions. Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, operations, safety teams, and external suppliers. Create practical mitigation plans, recovery strategies, and decision-making frameworks. Present findings and recommendations to technical experts and department stakeholders. This is a master's internship for minimum 5 months. The start date of this internship is as of February 2027. Your profile To be suitable for the internship, you: Are pursuing a master's degree in chemical engineering or mechanical engineering Can quantify a complex, real-world problem and make sound engineering judgments when data is incomplete Are curious about how technical systems behave beyond normal operating conditions, and what that means for the business Can explain a technical risk clearly to engineers, operators, safety specialists and senior managers, each in their own language Take ownership and drive your work forward without waiting to be told the next step This internship is for students who want to understand systems, not just components. You will see how critical industrial infrastructure behaves, from the physics of the installation to the business consequences of exceptional events. You will build hands-on experience in scenario modelling, process safety and decision-making under pressure, skills most engineers only develop after years in industry. You will be mentored and coached by technical experts. Your recommendations will directly contribute to the resilience of advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Other requirements you need to meet: You are enrolled at an educational institute for the entire duration of the internship, and you are at least 18 years old at the start of the internship; If you are a non-EU citizen, studying in the Netherlands, your university is willing to sign the documents relevant for doing an internship (i.e., Nuffic agreement); You attach your cover letter with a clear motivation on why you are interested in this internship assignment in particular; You need to be located in the Netherlands to be perform your internship. In case you are currently living/studying outside of the Netherlands, your application shows the willingness to relocate. Inclusion and diversity ASML is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values and respects the importance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. It is the policy of the company to recruit, hire, train and promote persons in all job titles without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. We recognize that inclusion and diversity is a driving force in the success of our company. jobs.title: Industrial Engineering internship: logistics process improvement
jobs.body: Introduction The EUV Factory in Veldhoven is responsible for producing and installing some of the world's most advanced lithography systems. Within the factory, the Logistics & Operational Planning department helps ensure materials, tools, and resources are available at the right place and time to support growing production demand. As production capacity continues to expand, efficient logistics processes become increasingly important. This Industrial Engineering internship: logistics process improvement, offers you the opportunity to improve material flows, identify operational bottlenecks, and contribute directly to factory performance. During this internship, you will work on real challenges and help create measurable improvements in a high-tech manufacturing environment. Your assignment During this Industrial Engineering internship: logistics process improvement, you will independently analyze logistics processes and identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency. You will use data analysis, process mapping, and continuous improvement methods to uncover bottlenecks and develop practical recommendations. Working closely with logistics, manufacturing, and planning teams, you will translate insights into actionable improvement proposals. Your main responsibilities will be: Analyze existing logistics and operational planning processes Identify bottlenecks using data analysis and process mapping techniques Evaluate material flow performance and operational efficiency Apply Lean and continuous improvement principles to identify opportunities Collaborate with logistics, manufacturing, and planning stakeholders Develop practical recommendations to optimize processes and material availability Present findings, insights, and improvement proposals to stakeholders This is a bachelor/master non-thesis internship for minimum 5 months, minimum 4 days per week (4 days on-site). The start date of this internship is as of February 2027. Your profile To be suitable for the internship, you: Are pursuing a bachelor's or master’s degree in industrial engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Business Engineering, Technology Management, or a related field. Have knowledge of data analysis, process mapping, Lean methodologies, or continuous improvement principles Are analytical and able to approach problems in a structured manner Are proactive, curious, and comfortable asking questions to understand root causes Can collaborate effectively with different stakeholders and communicate insights clearly Have a hands-on mindset and enjoy improving processes in a manufacturing environment This Industrial Engineering internship: logistics process improvement provides hands-on exposure to complex manufacturing operations and the opportunity to deliver measurable business impact through process optimization and data-driven decision-making. Experience in logistics or manufacturing is beneficial but not required. We value learning agility, curiosity, and a strong interest in process improvement. This internship is well suited for students who enjoy combining analysis with practical implementation. Other requirements you need to meet: You are enrolled at an educational institute for the entire duration of the internship, and you are at least 18 years old at the start of the internship; If you are a non-EU citizen, studying in the Netherlands, your university is willing to sign the documents relevant for doing an internship (i.e., Nuffic agreement); You attach your cover letter with a clear motivation on why you are interested in this internship assignment in particular; You need to be located in the Netherlands to be perform your internship. In case you are currently living/studying outside of the Netherlands, your application shows the willingness to relocate. Inclusion and diversity ASML is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values and respects the importance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. It is the policy of the company to recruit, hire, train and promote persons in all job titles without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. We recognize that inclusion and diversity is a driving force in the success of our company. jobs.title: Coop - Mechatronics Engineer (Internship)
jobs.body: Introduction to the job The DUV Reticle Stage IBS MDU team is responsible for engineering activities supporting the reticle stage, a precision mechatronic subsystem within ASML’s DUV lithography systems. Our mechatronics engineers use MATLAB-based analysis tools to evaluate system dynamics and performance using large sets of measurement data. As our analysis needs evolve, these engineering tools need to evolve with them. Many have been developed and extended over time by different engineers, which means that understanding the existing methods often requires combining code investigation, technical documentation, and knowledge from experienced engineers. We are looking for a co-op student who is excited to work at the intersection of mechatronics, data analysis, signal processing, and software development . Role and responsibilities Your primary assignment will be to develop and improve MATLAB-based analysis tools for DUV Reticle Stage dynamic performance , with a particular focus on power spectral density (PSD) analysis and visualization . You will work closely with experienced ASML mechatronics engineers to understand existing analysis methods, identify requirements, implement improvements, and validate the results against existing engineering analyses. Your responsibilities will include: Develop and update MATLAB tools for analysis and visualization of Reticle Stage dynamic performance data, particularly PSD and frequency-domain analysis. Learn how existing analysis tools and methods work by reviewing MATLAB code, available documentation, and example datasets. Interview and collaborate with mechatronics engineers to gather requirements and uncover engineering knowledge that may not yet be fully documented. Translate engineering requirements into maintainable MATLAB functions, analysis workflows, and visualizations. Validate new or modified analysis methods against known datasets and existing engineering results. Investigate discrepancies and work with subject-matter experts to determine whether they originate from data processing, algorithms, assumptions, or implementation. Improve usability and documentation so future engineers can understand and confidently use the analysis tools. Participate in code reviews and incorporate feedback from the mechatronics engineering team. This assignment offers the opportunity to work on a real precision-mechatronics system while gaining hands-on experience with engineering data analysis, signal processing, MATLAB development, and collaborative problem solving. This position is located on-site in Wilton, CT. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation. Must be available for 6 to 9 months Education and experience We are looking for a college junior or senior pursuing a bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Robotics, or a related engineering field , who is available for a 6-month co-op assignment . To be successful in this role, you should have: Technical skills Experience programming in MATLAB through coursework, projects, research, or previous internships/co-ops. Understanding of fundamental mechanical dynamics and vibrations . Familiarity with signal processing and frequency-domain analysis , such as Fourier transforms, frequency response, or power spectral density. Ability to work with experimental or measurement datasets and create clear engineering plots and visualizations. A structured approach to testing and validating computational results. Familiarity with Git, SVN, or another version-control system is beneficial but not required. Personal skills Strong curiosity and willingness to dig into an unfamiliar technical problem. Comfortable approaching engineers, asking questions, and gathering information from multiple subject-matter experts. Able to take loosely documented requirements and turn them into a structured engineering solution. Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail, particularly when validating numerical results. Able to work independently while actively seeking feedback and collaborating with an engineering team. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work for future users. The current base hourly range for this role is currently: $18.00 to $48.00 per hour Pay scales are determined by role, level, location and alignment with market data. Individual pay is determined through interviews and an assessment of several factors that that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and pay relative to other team members This position may require access to controlled technology, as defined in the Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. § 730, et seq.). Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. Business demands may require the Company to proceed with candidates who are immediately eligible to access controlled technology. jobs.title: 2027 Communication Architectures Modeling and Analysis Engineering Undergraduate Intern
jobs.body: The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space. The Aerospace Corporation is hiring a Communication Architectures Modeling and Analysis Engineering Undergraduate Intern for the Communication Architectures Department (CAD) within the Mission Payloads Division (MPD). Position will be full-time and 100% onsite at our office in El Segundo, CA. Job Summary At the Mission Payloads Division (MPD), we are pioneers in remote sensing systems that guide our country’s space enterprise. Our talented and dynamic people create and flourish in electronics, sensors, radar, artificial intelligence (AI), and advanced data network domains. We boldly advance technology through our research and development and then forward to demonstration and integration. With innovative laboratories and prototyping, MPD delivers groundbreaking results. We guide our Department of Defense, intelligence community, and civil clients to enhance national productivity and security and tackle the most critical missions. Bring your intelligence and creative spirit and join us at MPD! The Communication Architectures Department (CAD) has three main lines of work: the department performs trade studies, analyses, and simulations to optimize the overall communications performance of terrestrial, satellite, launch vehicle, and ground-based systems. CAD also guides the development of spectrum regulations and policies to assure critical wireless systems have access to necessary spectrum resources. Finally, we are actively engaged in the development of RF communications prototypes, especially those involving commercial LEO satellite systems. What You’ll Be Doing Perform analysis of communication systems to ensure architectures support mission objectives Develop tools to provide analysis and evaluations of communication architectures Assess the performance of satellite and ground systems, communication links, and wireless network protocols Gain hands-on expertise by designing, constructing, and evaluating prototype RF systems that interface with and assess satellite communications performance. Document work products in briefings and/or technical reports to customers and colleagues Tasking will vary during the internship and may include simultaneous projects Training and mentorship will be provided in this position What Corporate Skills You’ll Bring Strong written and oral communication skills Must work well in a team environment. Possess organizational, time management and project management skills. Demonstrate flexibility and ability to adapt to changing organizational need. Interpersonal skills to coordinate efforts and work with other internal and external organizations. What You Need to be Successful Minimum Requirements: Currently enrolled full-time in an accredited college/university program pursuing a Bachelors degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Aerospace Engineering, or another STEM-related discipline Minimum GPA 3.0, transcripts required. Availability to work full-time for a minimum of 10 weeks outside of university term and ability to return to a degree program full-time after completion of the internship. Experience programming in Python, C/C++, or Matlab. Exposure to modern development practices, including the use of Git for version control. Familiarity and/or coursework/project experience in communications theory, digital signal processing, electromagnetics, or satellite communications Strong written and oral communication skills This position requires ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance, which is issued by the US government. U.S citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance. How You Can Stand Out It would be impressive if you have one or more of these: GPA 3.5 or higher. Hands-on experience with RF measurement equipment (e.g., oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, signal generators) and proficiency in programmatically interfacing with these instruments is highly desirable. Experience implementing AI/ML techniques—particularly as applied to diverse data types in communications or signal processing. Project experience involving analysis of wireless communication systems. Demonstrated use of Git for version control along with experience in writing tests, and managing code through CI/CD pipelines. Demonstrated interest in space and communication systems. Active security clearance. Temporary housing assistance is not available. We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. The grade-based pay range for this job is listed below. Individual salaries within that range are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge and skills. At Aerospace, our commitment is our people. To cultivate our talent and ensure that we have a strong pipeline of future leaders, we want individuals who: Operate Strategically Lead Change Engage with Impact Foster Innovation Deliver Results Ways We Reward Our Employees During your interview process, our team will provide details of our industry-leading benefits. Benefits vary and are applicable based on Job Type. jobs.title: #Discover I 2027-2028 Maintenance Programs (Powerplant) Internship
jobs.body: Job Description: Ready to join one of our Graduate Programs in Spain? AIRBUS offer more than 70 vacancies for our full time graduate program in Spain - #Discover I 2027/2028 - Starting date March 2027 until February 2028. We are looking for recent graduates from different disciplines interested in developing their professional career in the aeronautical sector. The current context demands different ways of looking, thinking and relating. The selection process will be during October 2026 until January 2027. What does this internship consists in? Together with Camilo José Cela University, Airbus has developed an exclusive program (Discover) designed for those interested in the best training in new areas of knowledge essential to be able to develop as professionals of the future. You will have the opportunity to study a Master, organized in three training blocks, that will allow you to Discover the skills most in demand today. It will be combined with an 11 month internship at Airbus in an area related to your degree, where you can learn and complete your academic background. The start of the internship will be in early March 2027, and will last 11 months (August disabled for all purposes). It is a full-time experience (40h/week), in which you will receive an attractive study grant. Internship Job Description Airbus DS Maintenance Programs Department main mission is to ensure the Airworthiness Authorities approval of the different aircraft/products Scheduled Maintenance Requirements. Related aircraft/products are: - A400M aircraft, - C-295 aircraft (transport, humanitarian and maritime patrol versions). One of the activities related to the above is the direct and permanent contact with Operators and Airworthiness Authorities responsibles through Maintenance Working Groups and Industry Steering Comitees where the team is responsible for the presentation of the different analyses , and any related or necessary documentation, that supports the Scheduled Maintenance Requirements development/revision approval. The MSG-3 logic is the means for developing the scheduled maintenance tasks and intervals which will be acceptable to the regulatory authorities, the operators, and the manufacturers. TASSE4 also develops optimized maintenance programs to customers and maintenance programs for prototypes. In the Systems area of Maintenance Programs Department , the different Aircraft systems are analyzed using the MSG-3 methodology in order to identify the scheduled maintenance requirements. The starting point is the design office documentation related with systems/structure/wiring descriptions, drawings (catia) and digital mock-ups, safety analyses, certification plans, etc). These analyses contain a high level of systems description and a thorough analysis of its functions, functional failures, failure effects and failure causes. Examples of the analyzed systems are: Engines, Propeller and Auxiliary Power Unit. Main tasks: - Analyze the aircraft systems using the MSG3 logic in order to identify/optimize Scheduled Maintenance Requirements. - Check in-service documentation to perform its analysis and optimize maintenance based on A/C experience. - Collect the major suppliers inputs for scheduled maintenance for Engines, Propellers and APU. - Collaborate and support to other department areas (Systems, Zonal, Structure and Program management) Required skills #AirbusDiversity As a successful candidate, you will be able to demonstrate the following skills and experience: - Degree in Aeronautical Engineering. Specialization in engines will be an asset. - Knowledge on Excel/Data Bases Tools or similar. - English: Advance level. - Spanish: Advance level. - Analytical and problem-solving skills. - Team spirit and great collaboration skills. - Ability to work in complex and international environments. Why should you apply? - Foster your professional development with a strong academic background and an in depth collaboration in AIRBUS projects. - Expand your network within the aeronautical industry. - Meet our people working with passion and determination to make the world a more connected, safer and smarter place. - Be part of our diversity and teamwork culture that propel us to accomplish the extraordinary on the ground, in the sky and in space. Are you interested? Apply and make it fly! #Graduates_Spain #DISCOVER This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growth. CTC is Germany's leading centre for research and development in the field of design and production of large and complex CFRP components; with an international reputation as an expert for process development, series readiness and production optimisation. The focus of the CTC's work is the development of series technologies for the production and assembly of CFRP components in aircraft construction. jobs.title: Automation & Controls Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. Automation & Controls Engineering Intern (Summer 2027) As an Automation & Controls Engineering Intern, you’ll help build the automated test infrastructure used to shake, heat, cool, evacuate, and otherwise stress satellite hardware during environmental testing. From electrical control systems and safety interlocks to test automation software and telemetry pipelines, your work will help enable safe, reliable, and repeatable spacecraft testing. You’ll work at the intersection of hardware and software, collaborating with experienced engineers and technicians from early design and prototyping through commissioning, validation, and operational support. jobs.title: Materials Engineering Summer 2027 Intern
jobs.body: About Helion We are a fusion power company based in Everett, WA, with the mission to build the world's first fusion power plant, enabling a future with unlimited clean electricity. Our vision is a world with clean, reliable, and affordable energy for everyone. Since Helion's founding in 2013, we have raised $1.5 billion from long-time investors such as Sam Altman, Mithril, and Capricorn Investment Group as well as new investors including Thrive Capital, LightSpeed Venture Capital, SoftBank, and others to propel us forward. Our current prototype, Polaris, has reached record-breaking plasma temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius (13 keV). Helion is continuing to iterate and on the path to the world's first fusion power plant, Orion. This is a pivotal time to join Helion. You will tackle real-world challenges with a team that prizes urgency, rigor, ownership, and a commitment to delivering hard truths – values essential to achieving what no one has before. Together, we will change the future of energy, because the world can't wait. What You Will Be Doing: The materials engineering team at Helion is responsible for developing novel metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites necessary to successfully operate current and next generation nuclear fusion systems. As a Materials Engineering Intern, you'll assist in literature reviews to guide laboratory experiments and perform material characterization tests, including sample preparation, instrument operation, and data acquisition. Your work will support ongoing research and includes presenting results during weekly team meetings and at the year-end intern showcase. This role offers a unique opportunity to develop technical skills, collaborate with industry experts, and play an active part in shaping the future of clean energy. This is a 12-week onsite internship at our Everett, WA office. You Will: - Assist in the research and development of new materials, including polymers, metals, ceramics, and composites - Conduct experiments to test the properties and performance of materials under various conditions - Analyze data from material tests and experiments to identify trends and optimize material properties - Support the characterization of materials using techniques such as microscopy, spectroscopy, and mechanical testing - Contribute to the documentation and reporting of research findings, including technical reports and presentations - Participate in cross-functional team meetings to discuss project progress and challenges Required Skills: - Ability to work full time, onsite for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks during summer 2027 in Everett, WA - Currently enrolled in Graduate (Master’s or PhD) degree in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemistry or a related field - GPA of 3.0 or above - Fundamental background in materials science principles, including material properties, thermodynamics (incl. phase diagrams), and mechanics - Experience with laboratory techniques and material characterization tools and a willingness to learn - Proficiency in data analysis and familiarity with software tools (e.g., MATLAB, Python, or Origin) #LI-Onsite #LI-TM1 Benefits Our total compensation package includes benefits, including but not limited to: - Medical, Dental, and Vision plans for employees and their families - 31 Days of PTO (21 vacation days and 10 sick days) - 10 Paid holidays, plus company-wide winter break - Up to 5% employer 401(k) match - Short term disability, long term disability, and life insurance - Paid parental leave and support (up to 16 weeks) - Annual wellness stipend Helion is an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. If you need assistance or an accommodation during the interview process, please let us know. Pay range: $59 per hour.

jobs.title: Quantum R&D Engineer Intern
jobs.body: Overview Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do. Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers. The Quantum Engineering Solution (QES) team at Keysight designs and develops measurement solutions that enable the future of quantum technologies. QES’s world-class solutions address the challenging and exciting market of quantum technologies, including quantum computing, quantum communications, and quantum sensing. Responsibilities We are seeking a curious, creative individual to develop and evaluate techniques for characterizing the electrical properties of quantum devices used in quantum computing. As the industry drives toward utility-scale quantum computing, it is critical to optimize the processes for manufacturing quantum devices repeatably and reliably. Keysight’s expertise in test and measurement in both labs and foundries uniquely positions us to help customers meet these challenges. In this role, you’ll have access to high-performance instrumentation to develop measurement strategies for testing and characterizing quantum devices. In addition, you’ll develop Python workflows to demonstrate how these measurements can be automated through software programming interfaces. Your work will help shape QES’s approach to delivering world-class quantum test and measurement solutions. The ideal candidate has an interest in quantum engineering, particularly quantum computing, and strong Python programming skills. Prior experience with measurement equipment is not required; you will work alongside a team of experts who will provide guidance and support. Success in this role requires initiative, the ability to work independently, and a willingness to ask questions and seek help when needed. Responsibilities Develop measurement techniques on quantum devices using a parametric analyzer Create Python scripts to automate the measurements and demonstrate repeatability Collaborate with QES physicists to identify measurement challenges and develop practical solutions. Present findings and alternative approaches to the team, incorporate feedback to refine measurement techniques and automation workflows. Qualifications Required Skills Currently pursuing a BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field. Experience programming in Python, including writing scripts for data collection, analysis, and automation. Strong written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with ability to explain technical concepts clearly. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment. Willingness to quickly learn new technologies and communicate technical concepts clearly. Desired Skills Familiarity with quantum computing or other quantum technologies. Experience programming test instrumentation using PyVisa or similar API. Portfolio or examples of relevant work or academic projects preferred. jobs.title: Intern - Next Gen HBM Platform Arch
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. The HBM Platform Architecture team defines the electrical, thermal, and power-delivery architectures that enable Micron's next-generation High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) solutions. Working closely with architecture, design, packaging, and technology teams, the organization drives innovation in signaling, power integrity, thermal management, and system optimization to support AI, high-performance computing, and data center applications. As an HBM Platform Architecture Intern, you will contribute to the development of future HBM platforms by evaluating electrical, thermal, and power delivery architectures for advanced memory systems. You will work alongside experienced architects to analyze design trade-offs, develop modeling tools, and investigate solutions that improve performance, power efficiency, reliability, and scalability for next-generation memory products. Responsibilities Perform signaling and timing analysis for on-die and off-die interfaces across multiple system and packaging topologies. Develop and evaluate thermal models to analyze heat transfer, thermal performance, and design trade-offs in advanced memory systems. Analyze power delivery networks (PDNs), including IR-drop, electromigration (EM), power integrity, and power grid optimization for advanced HBM architectures. Develop modeling, simulation, and automation tools to support power delivery, thermal analysis, and architecture evaluation activities. Collaborate with architecture, design, packaging, and technology teams to evaluate system-level trade-offs and support future HBM technology development. Minimum Qualifications 0-2 years of relevant experience through internships, research projects, coursework, or academic projects in electrical engineering, VLSI design, signal integrity, power integrity, thermal analysis, semiconductor design, or related technical fields. Coursework or project experience in analog design, I/O design, signaling, DRAM technologies, high-speed interfaces, packaging, or 2.5D/3D integration technologies. Experience developing engineering automation tools, simulation environments, data analysis workflows, or modeling frameworks using Python or similar programming languages. jobs.title: Construction Project Management INTERN
jobs.body: Overview Come build community, explore your passions and do your best work at Microsoft. This opportunity will allow you to bring your aspirations, talent, potential and excitement for the journey ahead. The AMERS EPC construction team delivers the critical infrastructure that powers our cloud services, including new data center campuses, expansions, and upgrades across the Americas. As a Construction Project Management Intern in Querétaro, you will support the project team through planning and field execution of new data center construction, helping coordinate stakeholders and track schedule, cost, safety, and quality to contribute to the successful delivery of safe, reliable data center capacity. You will contribute to all construction priorities, including safety (e.g., leading and driving a safety culture), compliance (e.g., MS Policy/SOX, OLC/Anti-Bribery Anti-Corruption), quality, schedule and cost (e.g., financial accountability), and help create detailed scope of work documentation and troubleshoot issues to avoid delays or escalations. Working alongside the project team in a role similar to an entry-level project engineer, you may review drawings and submittals, track requests for information (RFIs) and action items, document field progress, and coordinate with contractors, designers, and internal stakeholders. You may also help maintain schedules, cost and change logs, safety and quality documentation, meeting minutes, and project status reports, gaining exposure to preconstruction, active construction, commissioning, and the transition to operation. At Microsoft, Interns work on real-world projects in collaboration with teams across the world, while having fun along the way. You’ll be empowered to build community, explore your passions and achieve your goals. This is your chance to bring your solutions and ideas to life while working on cutting-edge technology. This role is located in Querétaro, Mexico and is fully on-site at the data center construction site. It is expected to start in May 2027 Responsibilities Project Management: Contributes to datacenter construction/integration activities on local/campus projects (e.g., new or retrofit data center facilities) and provides findings and learns to provide recommendations on all datacenter fit-out related activities and ensures sound and data-driven decisions, as well as prioritization of security in documentation, design, and/or execution, with guidance from a manager and/or experienced peers. Technical Acumen: Provides feedback to engineering documentation/designs, site, and building plans by examining and analyzing technical information. Analyzes and reviews potential risks/gaps and provides recommendations to teammates, with guidance from a manager and/or experienced peers to ensure solutions adhere to security core priorities and guidelines. Coordination: Coordinates meetings and activities of vendors and cost managers, and attends project meetings, advocating for a safe and secure, security-first mindset during project planning, as needed and with guidance from a manager and/or project team. Project Tracking: Assists with the organization of specific project data supporting cost and key performance indicator (KPI) metrics, invoices, processes, and policies in order to communicate the status to the project team. Assists with the reporting on project progress regarding scope, schedule, standards, and budget with guidance from a manager and/or project team. Drives Results: Follows guidance from others to complete local projects (e.g., new construction, infrastructure improvements) by organizing information to help others make timely data-based decisions in partnership with the local project team and stakeholders, supporting milestone delivery and core priorities (Safety, Security, Quality, Schedule, Cost). Safety and Regulation: Follows guidelines to ensure adherence to Microsoft safety standards and regulatory requirements to ensure compliance. Conducts routine safety program, security, project, and contractor audits with direction from a manager or senior colleagues. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program in Construction Project Management, Architecture, Engineering, or a related field (e.g., Civil, Production, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering; Architecture and Urbanism). Must remain enrolled for the entire internship period, with an expected graduation date after the internship end date. Preferred Qualifications Familiarity with tools such as, AutoCAD, Autodesk BIM, Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC), Revit, and Microsoft 365. Ability to communicate effectively in English (verbally and in writing) at an intermediate or Higher level. This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. jobs.body: Position: Service Router Test Student Number of Position(s): 4 Duration : 4+ Months Date: January 4th - April 30th, 2027 Location : Hybrid (3 Office days) in Ottawa, ON, CANADA Education Recommendations: Currently a candidate for a Master’s or Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with an accredited school in Canada. As a part of our team, you will: Contribute as an integral member to one of the following IP Routing Platform Test sub-teams: Ethernet, Optics, Fabric, Sync/Timing, Firmware, Operating System, Secure Trust, Cflowd, SAS/IXR Satellites, System Test, Operations Administration Maintenance (OAM), MACsec, ANYsec, IPsec or Application Assurance. Develop automated test cases to validate new hardware and software features for innovative network infrastructure technology using a Linux-based regression environment. Receive quality one-on-one engineering mentorship while learning and using network protocols to configure high-capacity routers within the 7750 Service Router and 7250 Interconnect Router product families. Experience using Wireshark or some other type of network protocol analyzer.

jobs.body: Onto Innovation is a leader in process control, combining global scale with an expanded portfolio of leading-edge technologies that include: 3D metrology spanning the chip from nanometer-scale transistors to micron-level die-interconnects; macro defect inspection of wafers and packages; metal interconnect composition; factory analytics; and lithography for advanced semiconductor packaging. We are a group who always look for opportunities - whether that's in researching and testing a new technology; improving a piece of equipment's efficiency; or even making a process more sustainable to help reach the company's 2030 and 2040 Sustainability Goals. We believe that there is always an opportunity to grow and develop. If you were to join our team, you would be given responsibility from Day 1 to collaborate with vendors to design, develop and deliver equipment to our global partners, and be part of design reviews to expand initial concepts into our world-renowned products and packs. About our Reading Innovation Centre This role is available in our Reading Innovation Centre which is home to over 200+ scientists and engineers responsible for innovating consumer products in several business areas including Personal Health Care (Vicks) Oral Care (Oral-B), Grooming (Gillette and Venus) and Beauty Care (Olay). The site is a specialist Healthcare & Grooming Research & Development Hub in Europe and supports our European Beauty Franchise business. The site is friendly, diverse and has a rich history in innovation in multiple business areas. Our site is located close to the town centre and is served by motorway networks of M4 and M25 as well as the A33. We’re within 20 mins of Reading Central and Green Park railway stations and are served by buses that run every 10 minutes. What To Expect: We offer 3 or 6 month internship placements in either our Packing or Assembly groups. During your internship, you will get a first-hand experience of what a career in P&E with P&G involves, and if it is right for you. You will be working on live business projects and expected to dive straight in and take the lead. Previous Mechanical Engineering internship projects have covered topics such as creating a 'Gold Standard' process in sustainability for our worldwide Moulding equipment, improving the design of razor assembly machines, and evaluating automation in packing tool lines. Sounds challenging? Don’t worry – we don’t expect you to know how to do this, we can teach you. Each intern receives a customized learning plan to ensure they get the right levels of coaching, mentoring and training as they deliver their work. If you are looking for an exciting and challenging experience, have a passion for winning, strong leadership credentials and an interest in pursuing a career at P&G – this internship is for you! What You Will Gain: Responsibilities and Real Work from Day 1: You will be given specific projects and responsibilities working on real and live business challenges, just like a true P&Ger. Continuous training & coaching: You will work with passionate people and receive both formal training as well as day-to-day mentoring from your manager. Competitive Compensation & Benefits: The monthly salary for this summer internship is £2,625. On top of this you’ll enjoy lots of benefits like the option to enrol in our pension, flexible working arrangements, and your very own ‘Flex4Me’ Fund which enables you to allocate a portion of your benefits package to the areas that matter most to you. Full Time Role: Successful interns have the potential to secure a full-time position with P&G after graduation if available. As a 'build from within' company, our people start at entry level and progress through the organization. When we make a job offer, it’s with the expectation that you will grow into one of our future leaders, and to help you get there, you will work closely with skilled P&G veterans for mentoring and coaching at every step. Job Qualifications What We Look For: University students graduating in 2028 and pursuing a degree in one of the following fields: Mechanical Engineering, Process Engineering, Material Science/Engineering, or a related field such as Production, Product Design Engineering, Mechatronics, or Robotic Engineering. Evidence of passion and achievements in academic and/or non-academic activities. Tell us what you’re proud of – be it playing a musical instrument or holding down a job alongside your studies. We want to get to know you during your application! Demonstrated leadership skills with a desire to challenge the established way of doing things through continual improvement and innovation, delighting our consumers. Be a strong self-starter, able to drive real-world projects with your own initiative through to completion. Strong interest in investigating and implementing new technologies and processes to step change our products and equipment. Strong verbal and written English language skills. Right to Work: For our internship roles, you will need to provide your own right to work in the UK for the full duration of your internship without requiring sponsorship from P&G. Note, this will require your right to work permission to be valid between 5th July 2027 to 24th September 2027 for a minimum of 37.5 hours per week. P&G is legally required to ensure all candidates have the right to work in the UK from Day 1 of their employment. All applicants will therefore be asked to provide evidence of their right to work at the conclusion of the recruitment process as a condition of employment. Start date: The internship's duration is flexible as either 3 months or 6 months, with a start date of April or July 2027. Application Deadline: 1pm (GMT) November 13th, 2026. You must apply by the deadline. We encourage you to apply and complete our online assessments as soon as possible , as we may close early if positions are filled. Application Process: Complete your Application (Deadline 1pm GMT 13th November 2026) Complete our Online Assessments (Deadline 1pm GMT 20th November 2026) Virtual Interviews (These will run from October until our roles are filled) At P&G #weseeequal We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. At P&G we strive to build a culture where everyone feels welcome, included, and able to bring their full selves to work. We champion social mobility and believe socio-economic status should not be a barrier to accessing job opportunities. That’s why in addition to this internship being paid, we offer provision of all the necessary technology and electronic equipment, access to a range of benefits, and financial support if you need to relocate for your internship - such as covering the cost of travel to your internship location. We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process. Please click here if you require an accommodation during the application process. Please make sure to wait to hear back from us regarding your accommodation before proceeding with the online assessment, we thank you in advance for your patience. jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Combustion Devices Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to support the team in designing, analyzing and testing combustion devices, as well as gain experience with GD&T drafting and data processing and testing. From designing and testing structures and components, to firing up new engines, to setting up launch pads and test sites across the United States, joining the Combustion Devices team is your opportunity to help launch a new large rocket for the very first time. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an engineering, physics or math discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Experience with CAD/CAM Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) drafting experience Finite Element Analysis (FEA) experience Experience with 3D printing Experience with programs such as: ANSYS, MATLAB, Siemens NX Propulsion experience ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Range CA: $28.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match. Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts. Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion. Hourly Pay Range (CA Only) $28 — $28 USD WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. jobs.title: Intern- Robot Perception
jobs.body: Who we are With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility. Timeframe : Summer (May-Aug 2027) At Symbotic , Early Career talent plays a meaningful role in helping us reimagine the future of supply chain automation. Through our Internship and Co-op programs, students have the opportunity to contribute to real projects, collaborate with experienced engineers and business leaders, and gain hands-on exposure to the technologies powering our end-to-end robotics and automation solutions. We are looking for curious, motivated students who are excited to solve complex problems, bring new perspectives to cross-functional teams, and see their work make an impact in a fast-moving, innovative environment . Along the way, Interns and Co-ops are supported through mentorship, professional development, networking opportunities, and a robust calendar of events designed to help them build community and grow their careers. Symbotic offers transportation and housing benefits for students who meet our relocation requirements. Continue reading below to learn more about this exciting opportunity! About t he Opportunities Symbotic’s Robot Perception team is an accomplished group of engineers who are working on sophisticated algorithms in areas such as perception and computer vision . Perception and Computer Vision interns will evaluate and propose new projects for replacing legacy tools with vision-based algorithms. These interns will scope projects from literature review, to dataset design and aggregation, training pipeline development, all the way through production deployment. Practical projects include vision-based collision avoidance . SLAM interns will develop and test algorithms for robust robot localization in complex, real-world environments, applying sensor fusion, state estimation, and probabilistic methods to solve SLAM challenges at scale. What you’ll do Research and experiment with traditional computer vision methods and deep learning methods for object detection, classification, segmentation, pose estimation, anomaly detection on images or videos. Evaluate and benchmark computer vision methods on production data. Deploy software to production on robot hardware. Design data pre and post processing methods. Document designs, code, experiments, evaluations. Identify high-impact scenarios where AI Planning and machine learning can be applied to optimize the Symbotic robotics software. Adapt state-of-the-art approaches or develop high-performance algorithms to solve real-world multi-robot problems. Conduct simulations and experiments to validate the performance of the multi-robot algorithms. Present results in verbal and written communications internally, and in top-tier academic venues. W hat you’ll need Pursuing a Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related technical field. Proficiency in Python and/or C++, including experience writing code and working in Jupyter notebooks. Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow. Familiarity with computer vision and perception tools such as OpenCV, including image classification, object detection, segmentation, and camera calibration. Exposure to robotics perception concepts such as sensor fusion, SLAM, 3D pose representations, coordinate transforms, probabilistic graphical models, and Bayesian inference. Working knowledge of sensors, including RGB cameras, 3D sensors, and point cloud processing tools such as PCL. Experience working in Linux environments and using command-line tools. Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure, REST APIs, and/or SQL-based data tools such as Snowflake. Exposure to deployment or optimization tools such as Docker, ROS/ROS 2, Jetson, ONNX, VLMs, or Vision-Language-Action models is a plus. What’s good to have Publications at high-impact conferences/journals (e.g., CoRL , ICLR, NeurIPS , ICML, ICLR, RSS, ICRA, IROS, RAL, AAAI, ICAPS, IJCAI, JAIR, etc.) Our Environment Up to 10% of travel may be required . Employees must have a valid driver’s license and the ability to drive and/or fly to client and other customer locations. The employee is responsible for owning a credit card and managing expenses personally to be reimbursed on a bi-weekly basis. #LI-JH1 #LI-Onsite About Symbotic Symbotic is an automation technology leader reimagining the supply chain with its end-to-end, AI-powered robotic and software platform. Symbotic reinvents the warehouse as a strategic asset for the world’s largest retail, wholesale, and food & beverage companies. Applying next-gen technology, high-density storage and machine learning to solve today's complex distribution challenges, Symbotic enables companies to move goods with unmatched speed, agility, accuracy and efficiency. As the backbone of commerce the Symbotic platform transforms the flow of goods and the economics of supply chain for its customers. For more information, visit www.symbotic.com . We are a community of innovators, collaborators and pioneers who embrace our differences, because we know unique perspectives make us stronger and smarter. Every perspective matters. We depend on the collective voices of our employees, customers and community to help guide us as we build a better place to work – for you and the world. That’s why we’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, or genetic information. The base range for this position in the posted location is $32.00 - $44.00 however, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The compensation package includes medical, dental, vision, disability, 401K, PTO and/or other benefits.

Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Cleanliness and Contamination Control department as an intern (d/f/m)! Location: Immenstad am Bodensee Start: April 2027 Duration: 6 months Your location At the Airbus site in Immenstaad on Lake Constance, you’ll work where the future of Connected Intelligence, Space, and Air Power takes shape. In an environment that offers vision, you will shape technological innovations across domains. Our location thrives on dialogue: on campus, you’ll connect with a unique network of experts in satellite technology, military aviation, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, as well as tomorrow's Combat Cloud and Ground Support. Our collaboration is equally dynamic—in agile teams, we tackle the most complex challenges, from AI-powered Earth observation to secure cloud architectures. Anyone seeking technological excellence and interdisciplinary collaboration will find the ideal environment here. International environment with the opportunity to network globally. Work with modern/diversified technologies. Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network. Your tasks and responsibilities Tool Improvement & Monitoring: Apply and optimize innovative C&CC monitoring tools and procedures for tracking particle and molecular contamination across active space programs. Digitalization of Lab Notes: Follow up on and expand the automation of laboratory notes, reporting templates, and data aggregation routines (using Python, MATLAB, or Excel VBA). Analytical Support: Assist in sample verification and contamination qualification using FTIR spectroscopy, optical microscopy, and SEM/EDX. Methodology Development: Support the evaluation of new contamination measurement methods to improve cleanliness verification workflows. Desired skills and qualifications Currently enrolled in a university program (Bachelor's or Master's) majoring in Chemistry, Physics, Materials Science, or a related engineering field. jobs.title: Quality Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.body: About Us At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space. The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy. About the Summer Internship Program Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater. Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else. We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer. We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules: Cohort #1 Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13 Cohort #2 Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10 All internship roles are based at our Torrance headquarters and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package. About the Team Interns on the Quality Engineering team develop inspection methods and qualify inspection equipment for a variety of mechanical and electrical systems. They work cross-functionally with design, manufacturing, test, supply chain, and materials teams to validate hardware, characterize the uncertainty of inspection techniques, and ensure rigor in the build of nuclear systems, structures, and components. Interns begin with small starter projects and quickly progress to a long-duration project that culminates in a technical deliverable and presentation. You will be integrated and evaluated as a first-year junior engineer, not simply as an intern. The bar for success is high: you are expected to use your mentor and available resources thoughtfully, execute on your project, and proactively identify additional issues and opportunities for improvement. Roles and Responsibilities: - Develop inspection methods for mechanical and electrical systems. - Support the qualification and implementation of inspection equipment and techniques. - Collaborate with design, manufacturing, test, supply chain, and materials teams to validate hardware. - Characterize measurement and inspection uncertainty and document technical conclusions. - Help ensure rigor and traceability in the build of nuclear systems, structures, and components. - Research new tools and technologies that could close gaps in the Quality Engineering team's capabilities. - Develop automation and implement process improvements that increase inspection effectiveness and repeatability. - Own a long-duration project through a final technical deliverable and presentation while communicating progress, risks, and opportunities. Basic Qualifications: - Currently enrolled in at least a bachelor's degree program in an engineering discipline relevant to the work and entering the junior or senior year of study. - Prior internship experience or more than one year of significant project-team, laboratory, or research experience. Preferred Skills & Experience: - GPA of 3.5 or above. - Experience in a university club or organization; leadership experience is preferred. - Strong interpersonal and technical communication skills, such as leading a student project team or presenting research at a conference. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with close attention to detail. - Ability to work cross-departmentally with different groups and teams. - Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements. - Ability to work independently and as part of a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively. Location - We are located in Torrance, CA in a 322,000 square foot, brand new facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access to the 405, 105, and 110 freeways. Our facility is in the heart of Los Angeles' vibrant emerging tech ecosystem alongside many other high growth startups and enterprises. Culture At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful: - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done” - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth.
