Throughout the program, Interns will have exposure to mentorship, networking, and professional development opportunities. The Systems Engineer intern will support Voyager Technologies at one of the following locations: San Diego, CA Long Beach, CA Pittsburgh, PA The Systems Engineering Intern will support the Systems Engineering team with a variety of activities related to requirements, system architecture, integration, testing, analysis, and technical documentation. This internship provides an opportunity to apply engineering principles to real-world projects while gaining exposure to how complex systems are defined, developed, integrated, and verified. The intern may contribute to projects across different engineering disciplines and product areas based on current business and engineering priorities. The specific project assignment will provide opportunities to work collaboratively with experienced engineers and cross-functional teams. Responsibilities Assist with defining, reviewing, decomposing, and tracking system-level requirements. Support the development and documentation of system architectures, interfaces, and technical specifications. Assist with identifying and evaluating technical risks, dependencies, and potential system-level issues. Collaborate with engineering teams and cross-functional partners to support system development and integration activities. Support the definition of verification and validation methods for system requirements. Assist with developing, reviewing, and executing test plans, procedures, and other verification activities. Participate in system integration, troubleshooting, and technical problem-solving activities. Support the collection, analysis, and documentation of engineering data and test results. Assist with maintaining technical documentation and engineering artifacts throughout the development process. Participate in engineering reviews, team meetings, technical discussions, training sessions, and other learning opportunities. Collaborate with other internal teams, such as project management, operations, and business development, as needed. Contribute ideas for process improvement, engineering efficiency, and operational effectiveness. Complete assigned projects and deliverables accurately and within established timelines. Requirements Currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at an accredited university, preferably pursuing a degree in Systems Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Physics, or a related technical field. Broad understanding of fundamental engineering principles and systems engineering concepts. Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a cross-functional team environment. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Strong organizational and time-management skills with attention to detail. Ability to learn and apply new engineering tools, processes, and methodologies. Familiarity with engineering software, modeling tools, requirements management systems, programming languages, or other technical tools is preferred. Ability to travel for in-person orientation and program kickoff, as well as for the final presentation at program completion. Preferred Qualifications Previous internship, coursework, academic project, laboratory experience, or other relevant engineering experience. Experience with requirements development, systems engineering, system integration, testing, or technical documentation. Familiarity with engineering design or analysis software, such as CAD, electrical design, modeling/simulation, or requirements management tools. Experience with programming or data analysis tools such as Python, MATLAB, C/C++, or similar languages. Hands-on experience with laboratory equipment, engineering test equipment, prototyping, or experimental testing. Exposure to multidisciplinary engineering projects or cross-functional development environments. jobs.title: Systems Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Axiom Space is a human space exploration company, building era-defining space infrastructure and delivering technology-driven solutions that will empower civilization to transcend Earth. Beginning with Axiom Station, successor to the International Space Station, the company is pioneering a next-generation orbital settlement that will foster groundbreaking innovation and research in microgravity and drive the global space economy of tomorrow. Today, guided by the vision of leading humanity's expansion off planet, Axiom Space is the principal provider of commercial human spaceflight services and developer of advanced spacesuits for the Moon and beyond. This role supports systems engineering activities — including requirements definition, interface management, system architecture, and verification and validation planning — across Axiom's spaceflight hardware and ground systems programs. The role requires strong organizational, time management, and communication skills, along with a genuine curiosity for how complex systems fit together. jobs.title: Drone Operations, Intern - Labs (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About the Team DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. The Drone Operations team keeps DoorDash's drones airworthy and operates them safely. Our missions range from experimental test flights to commercial delivery. We're hiring Drone Operations interns to work at the intersection of operations and robotics to solve key business problems with elegant technical solutions. If you have a passion for applying robotics solutions to a service loved by millions of people, then we want to talk to you! About the Role As a Drone Operations Intern, you will support daily flight operations for DoorDash’s drone delivery program, from our test flight program to our commercial operation. You will get exposure to all elements of our operation, including Pilots, Maintenance Technicians, Quality/Safety, and Engineering. You will rotate around our facilities and get an end-to-end view of our program. In your first 30 days, you will learn our flight procedures and safety practices. By 90 days, you will own a project that improves flight safety, reliability, or efficiency. Success means the team adopts your work and our operations measurably improve. It is an exciting time to join as we scale from test flights to commercial delivery.You will report into the Head of Drone Operations on our Drone Operations team in our Labs organization. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Work with pilots, technicians, and engineers to troubleshoot issues and improve procedures. Review flight logs and mission data to find trends in safety, reliability, and delivery performance. Help run field operations at flight sites, including aircraft setup, loading, and recovery. Own an intern project and present your results to the team at the end of summer. We’re excited about you because… You are pursuing a B.S. or M.S. Degree in Aviation Studies or equivalent, have no more than 2 years of full-time work experience, and are graduating between Fall 2027 to Summer 2028.You are available for a May or June 2027 start date (Internships are only hosted during the Summer) You hold, or are willing to obtain, a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate. You have hands-on experience building, flying, or maintaining drones or radio-controlled (RC) aircraft. You can operate in field environments with extended periods of standing, repetitive drone handling, and outdoor exposure to varying weather (heat, dust, cold, wind, etc.). You communicate clearly and follow safety procedures carefully. Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis Compensation The internship is 12 weeks long. The intern’s starting pay will fall within the weekly pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including education, work location, and market conditions. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base pay, interns are eligible for both a housing stipend and relocation stipend. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer our interns a wellness reimbursement benefit, access to an employee assistance program, in-office lunch credits and more! Base Pay (Weekly) $1,200 — $1,200 USD About DoorDash At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods. DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more. jobs.title: GE Vernova- Grid Engineering Internship - Summer 2027
jobs.body: Job Description Summary Addressing the climate crisis is an urgent global priority, and at GE Vernova, we take our responsibility seriously. That is the singular mission of GE Vernova: to continue electrifying the world while simultaneously working to help decarbonize it. Vernova Purpose Come and join our powerful, unified force with the energy to change the world. Our mission is BIG. Our TRANSFORMATION is key – bringing the right businesses together to LEAD the ENERGY TRANSITION. Our TEAM is ready. What impact you’ll make: As an Intern of the Grid Engineering Team, you will be an active contributor to the enhancement of grid reliability and efficiency and supporting initiatives that facilitate the integration of renewable energy sources into the grid. Job Description What you’ll do (Job Responsibilities) Collaborate on Grid Reliability Projects: Work with the engineering team to analyze current grid systems and identify areas for improvement. Contribute to projects aimed at enhancing grid performance, reducing downtime, and improving overall reliability. Support Renewable Energy Integration: Assist in evaluating and implementing strategies for integrating renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind, into the grid. Conduct research and analysis to assess the impact of these sources on grid stability and capacity. Data Collection and Analysis: Gather and analyze data related to grid operations and renewable energy integration. Use this data to support model development and testing of new technologies or methodologies that could enhance grid performance. Participate in Cross-Functional Teams: Engage with various departments and teams to support GE Vernova's mission of electrification and decarbonization. Collaborate on initiatives that drive the energy transition and contribute to a sustainable energy future. Innovative Problem Solving: Utilize analytical skills to troubleshoot and propose innovative solutions to engineering challenges in grid operations and renewable energy integration. Report and Present Findings: Prepare reports and presentations summarizing project outcomes, research findings, and recommendations. Communicate these insights effectively to team members and stakeholders. What you’ll bring (Basic Qualifications) Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree program at an accredited university or credentialed software accelerator program. Degree focused in Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, Software Engineering Power Systems, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Computer Information Systems, Informatics, Information Science/Technology, Management Information Systems, Security and Risk Analysis, or other relevant STEM majors Must commit to working full time (40 hrs/wk) during the internship. Graduating between December 2027 or May 2028 . What will make you stand out (Desired Qualifications) You have a passion for grid engineering and renewable energy integration, demonstrating a keen interest in enhancing the reliability and efficiency of electrical systems. You are someone who brings strong analytical skills and a collaborative mindset, effectively working with cross-functional teams to drive innovation and support GE Vernova's mission of electrification and decarbonization. You have experience with data collection and analysis in engineering contexts, and have been involved in projects addressing grid reliability or renewable energy integration. Prior intern, co-op, or research experience in software, electrical engineering, power systems or relevant area. Leadership experience inside and/or outside the classroom. A strong commitment to a career in technology and passion/aptitude for both software and electrical engineering. Excellent written and verbal communication skills and ability to articulate clearly. Demonstrated creative problem solving and proactive learning. Minimum cumulative or in-major 3.0/4.0 GPA. Additional Notes: Must be willing to work out of an office located in Bellevue, Washington Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required. In order to meet this mission, we provide varied, competitive benefits to help support our workforce. jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern - Research and Development - Aftertreatment Catalysis
jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.body: Job Description The Role General Motors is seeking a motivated student to join the Energy and Propulsion Systems Research team as a Summer Intern in aftertreatment catalysis. The intern will contribute to research supporting next-generation automotive emissions-control technologies, including catalyst performance, durability, materials development, reaction kinetics, system modeling, and data-driven materials discovery. This opportunity is intentionally broad and may be well suited for students with experimental, computational, modeling, data science, or artificial intelligence and machine learning backgrounds. The specific project will be aligned with the candidate’s skills and the team’s research priorities. The Team The team is re-establishing and advancing GM’s aftertreatment catalysis research capabilities. Current research areas include three-way catalysts, platinum-group-metal reduction, catalyst aging and durability, alternative catalyst and substrate materials, hydrocarbon and nitrogen-oxide traps, reaction kinetics, predictive modeling, and AI/ML-enabled materials discovery. What You’ll Do Depending on your background, you may: Design, conduct, and analyze laboratory experiments for catalyst, washcoat, powder, or aftertreatment core evaluation. Prepare samples and support testing using laboratory reactor systems and analytical tools. Investigate catalyst activity, selectivity, conversion efficiency, thermal durability, aging, sintering, and degradation mechanisms. Apply characterization methods such as Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, diffuse-reflectance infrared Fourier-transform spectroscopy, surface-area analysis, chemisorption, microscopy, spectroscopy, or related techniques. Develop reaction-kinetic, catalyst-performance, degradation, or system-level models. Process and interpret experimental data using Python, MATLAB, or similar tools. Apply statistical learning, machine learning, optimization, or uncertainty quantification to catalyst and materials datasets. Build data-driven tools to accelerate catalyst screening and reduce reliance on hardware testing. Explore AI/ML approaches for materials discovery, composition optimization, performance prediction, or experiment planning. Correlate material properties, operating conditions, and catalyst performance to identify design principles. Document methods, analyze results, prepare technical summaries, and present findings to research and engineering teams. Collaborate with researchers, engineers, universities, national laboratories, suppliers, and other GM organizations. Follow all laboratory safety procedures, data-quality practices, and applicable documentation requirements. Required Qualifications Currently pursuing a master’s, or doctoral degree in chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, materials engineering, mechanical engineering, computer science, data science, physics, or a related STEM field. Available to work full-time, 40 hours per week during the summer internship. Demonstrated interest in at least one of the following: Heterogeneous catalysis, reaction engineering, emissions control, or materials science. Laboratory experimentation and analytical characterization. Mathematical modeling, simulation, scientific computing, or numerical methods. Data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, or optimization. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary research environment. Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and technical documentation skills. GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. jobs.body: Job Description Work Arrangement: Hybrid: This internship is categorized as on-site. The selected intern is expected to report to the office 3 days a week. Location: Sunnyvale, CA About the Team The Data Scaling team builds the data, machine learning, and infrastructure foundations that enable Embodied AI models to improve with scale. We work across data collection, curation, mining, labeling, dataset quality, model inputs, distributed training, experiment workflows, and the systems that help researchers and engineers develop, evaluate, and deploy models more efficiently. Our work supports large-scale autonomous driving models and the broader Embodied AI flywheel. We combine machine learning, data engineering, distributed systems, and software engineering to make high-quality, product-aligned driving data available for perception, planning, trajectory generation, and other autonomy capabilities. About the Role As an Embodied AI Data Scaling Intern, you will work on a well-scoped project that improves the scale, quality, efficiency, or reliability of data and model development for autonomous driving. You will collaborate with researchers and engineers to build data pipelines, analyze large datasets, improve training workflows, or develop infrastructure that increases the number and quality of experiments the team can run. Potential focus areas include: Data Curation and Quality: Build methods to select, filter, balance, and validate large driving datasets aligned with product and modeling needs. Data Mining and Scenario Discovery: Identify valuable, rare, or challenging driving situations and develop tools to improve coverage of long-tail scenarios. Dataset and Labeling Pipelines: Improve automated labeling, data transformation, feature generation, and dataset release workflows. Distributed Training and Model Scaling: Optimize the systems, input pipelines, and compute workflows used to train large models on large datasets. ML Experimentation and Flywheel Infrastructure: Build tools that help teams develop, train, evaluate, debug, and deploy models more quickly and reliably. Present technical findings and document experiments, results, and recommendations. jobs.location: Sant Cugat del Valles, Barcelona, Spain
jobs.body: AI & Computer Vision Engineering Intern Description - Before applying please note that, to be eligible for this position, you must be currently enrolled at a university in Spain , remain enrolled until the end of the internship, and be eligible to sign an internship agreement with your university. You must also be available to start the internship in February 2027 and continue participating in the program until June–July 2027 . About the role Join HP Additive Manufacturing (HPAM), one of HP's most innovative and fast-growing businesses, where breakthrough technologies are transforming the future of digital manufacturing. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to next-generation industrial 3D printing solutions while working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, computer vision, and additive manufacturing. As part of a highly collaborative organization, you will work with experts across R&D, Quality, Manufacturing, and Data Science to develop an AI-powered visual inspection solution for 3D printed parts. The goal is to automate the evaluation of print quality and detect manufacturing defects through images, helping improve consistency, efficiency, and scalability of quality assessment processes. This internship offers hands-on experience with real-world industrial challenges, including building image acquisition strategies, creating and annotating datasets, defining defect taxonomies, and developing machine learning models capable of identifying defects such as porosity, bubbles, alignment issues, elephant skin, and other surface anomalies. You will have the opportunity to work on a project that could evolve from an internal efficiency tool into a customer-facing capability integrated into future HP 3D printing workflows. Key responsibilities: Design and implement image acquisition strategies for capturing 3D printed parts under controlled and repeatable conditions. Build a high-quality computer vision dataset, including image collection, organization, and annotation. Develop computer vision and deep learning models to automatically identify and classify print quality defects. Evaluate and compare classification, object detection, and segmentation approaches. Develop image preprocessing, augmentation, and data preparation pipelines to improve model performance and robustness. Analyze model performance and define validation methodologies and success metrics. Collaborate with quality and manufacturing experts to understand defect characteristics and improve model accuracy. Explore automated inspection workflows, including multi-view image acquisition and solutions that can evolve from an internal evaluation tool into a customer-facing quality assessment capability. Document experiments, datasets, models, and development processes, and present findings to engineering and business stakeholders. Requirements: Currently enrolled in a Master's degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Computer Vision, Robotics, or a related field, with at least 12 months of university enrollment remaining. Strong Python programming skills and solid understanding of machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision fundamentals. Experience with PyTorch and/or TensorFlow for model development and Tensorboard and/or MLFlow for experiment tracking. Familiarity with image classification, object detection, segmentation, and model evaluation methodologies. Experience with Git and collaborative software development practices. Preferred: Experience working with image datasets, data annotation, and dataset preparation. Preferred: Experience designing and building machine learning datasets from raw data, including image acquisition, data collection strategies, annotation guidelines, and quality control processes. Preferred: Experience with OpenCV, image processing, and image analysis techniques. Preferred: Experience with object detection and segmentation models such as YOLO, Faster R-CNN, DETR, U-Net, Mask R-CNN, or similar architectures. Preferred: Familiarity with Databricks, cloud-based ML workflows, MLOps concepts, and model deployment. Strong analytical thinking, problem-solving skills, attention to detail, curiosity, and ability to work independently in an exploratory research environment. Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams and domain experts. Fluent in English, both spoken and written Experience our benefits : Paid internship within a global, technology driven company. Join an international work environment, with opportunities for learning, professional development, and networking across teams. Flexible working schedule, with options for part-time agreements (4 hours/day) or full-time (8 hours/day). The length of the internship ranges from 4 to 12 months. Access to our intern community, including career development workshops, learning sessions, and social activities that help you grow professionally and connect with other interns. Mentor assigned. Opportunity to join the HP Graduate Program following the placement. Lunch at reduced prices at our canteen. Access to our on‑site sports center, including: Gym facilities Squash, tennis, and basketball courts 25+ organized sports and wellness activities, such as HIIT training, squash, basketball, and yoga Participation in the NextGen Employee Network, offering regular events and opportunities to connect with other early‑career professionals. jobs.body: Job descriptions may display in multiple languages based on your language selection. What we offer: At Magna, you can expect an engaging and dynamic environment where you can help to develop industry-leading automotive technologies. We invest in our employees, providing them with the support and resources they need to succeed. As a member of our global team, you can expect exciting, varied responsibilities as well as a wide range of development prospects. Because we believe that your career path should be as unique as you are. Group Summary: Transforming mobility. Making automotive technology that is smarter, cleaner, safer and lighter. That’s what we’re passionate about at Magna Electronics, and we do it by creating world-class Electronic systems. We are a premier supplier for the global automotive industry with full capabilities in design, development, testing and manufacturing of complex Electronic systems. Our name stands for quality, environmental consciousness, and safety. Innovation is what drives us and we drive innovation. Dream big and create the future of mobility at Magna Electronics. Job Responsibilities: Position Overview Magna’s ADAS technologies are shaping an autonomous future and improving lives. The ADAS Intern/Co-op (onsite) primarily supports ADAS vehicle integration by coordinating prototype vehicle activities (build readiness, installations, scheduling support, and issue tracking) across cross-functional teams. The role also supports deployment and use of ROS-based tools as needed. A strong drive to learn, clear communication, and teamwork are essential. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Coordinate ADAS prototype vehicle activities across cross‑functional teams (build readiness, scheduling support, parts/tools readiness, stakeholder communication, and issue tracking/closure). Support prototype vehicle-build activities with the Engineering Services team, including RRS PC installation and related vehicle integration tasks. Support End-of-Line (EOL) and USS sensor calibration activities as scheduled, and document calibration outcomes and follow-up actions. Create utilities/tools to support the team (e.g., build/test checklists, data/log organization, basic geometry/FOV calculations, or converting a manual workflow into a repeatable script). Support engineers in vehicle testing activities as a second person (as required), following safety procedures and test plans, and capturing results, issues, and logs. Support deployment and use of ROS‑based tools (training will be provided as needed) to assist with sensor feasibility studies and integration workflows. Qualifications: Valid driver’s license Comfortable working hands-on in a garage/vehicle environment (installations, instrumentation, calibration support) and able to follow all safety procedures and PPE requirements. Education / Experience Enrolled in an engineering degree program (Electrical, Automotive, Mechanical, Robotics/Mechatronics, or Computer Science or equivalent) Special Knowledge / Skills: Mandatory: Basic Python programming skills (scripts for automation, data handling, and repeatable workflows). Experience with C++ is a plus. Coursework, projects, or work experience related to ADAS/autonomous systems, sensor integration, or automotive software development. Basic familiarity with a Linux/Ubuntu development environment and version control (Git) is preferred; willingness to learn is required. Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively in a cross-functional team setting (tracking actions, following up, and clearly documenting status). Demonstrates drive to learn and take ownership. Familiarity with ADAS/autonomous driving concepts and common sensors (LiDAR, camera, radar, ultrasonic). Comfortable learning and using new tools and processes to support vehicle integration and coordination (training and mentoring provided as needed). Troubleshooting and debugging skills (software and basic hardware integration issues). Good documentation and reporting habits (test logs, build notes, calibration records). Problem-solving and critical-thinking mindset Must follow safety procedures for vehicle testing, shop/garage environments, and bench testing environments. Attention to detail Preferred: Experience with vehicle testing and data collection using tools such as Vector CANoe/CANalyzer, dSPACE, ETAS, or similar toolchains. Experience with vehicle instrumentation and prototype sensor/ECU integration (mounting, harnessing, power/network bring-up) and/or supporting sensor calibration activities. Exposure to ROS/ROS2 tools (e.g., running existing nodes, basic package structure, RViz/rosbag) and ability to deploy/use ROS-based workflows. Working knowledge of creating maintainable, reusable scripts/tools (clear inputs/outputs, basic testing, readable documentation) in a team environment. Physical Demands / Work Environment: Combination of office and garage/vehicle environments. Includes sitting/standing; working at a computer; frequent walking around vehicles; bending/kneeling; and occasional lifting/moving of equipment (e.g., test hardware, tools, sensors) consistent with safe work practices. Work may occur outdoors or in varying temperatures during vehicle build, testing, and calibration activities. jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all. Join an inclusive team passionate about one thing: using their expertise in the relentless pursuit of innovation for customers and partners. The solutions we build help make everything from virtual reality experiences to breakthroughs in neural networks possible. We do it all while committing to integrity, sustainability, and giving back to our communities. Because doing so can fuel the very innovation we are pursuing. Location Singapore Department Heterogeneous Integration Group, High Bandwidth Memory Product System Engineering Project Title Artificial Intelligence-Enabled High Bandwidth Memory Defect Library and Analytics Dashboard Development Project Description High Bandwidth Memory products generate significant volumes of engineering, electrical test, and failure analysis data throughout the manufacturing and test lifecycle. Consistent documentation and structured management of defect signatures are important for strengthening engineering knowledge retention, improving information accessibility, and enabling data-driven technical analysis. This internship project focuses on developing a structured High Bandwidth Memory Defect Library that captures the electrical and physical signatures of selected defect modes across multiple test flows. The intern will apply engineering, data analytics, Python programming, and dashboard-development concepts to organize defect information and present it through an interactive visualization platform. Under the guidance of experienced engineers, the intern will also evaluate appropriate Artificial Intelligence-enabled approaches, including Generative Artificial Intelligence, Artificial Intelligence Assistants, Agentic Artificial Intelligence solutions, and Large Language Model-based tools. These approaches may be used to improve defect categorization, information retrieval, engineering knowledge management, and insight generation. The assignment is a supervised, educational, and project-based internship. It is intended to develop the intern’s technical and professional capabilities and does not replace the responsibilities of regular employees. Objective of the Project Establish a standardized High Bandwidth Memory Defect Library that documents the electrical and physical signatures of selected defect modes. Develop an interactive dashboard for visualizing, tracking, and analyzing defect information across multiple test flows. Create a consistent data structure and categorization framework that strengthens engineering knowledge retention and information retrieval. Evaluate feasible Artificial Intelligence-enabled methods for improving defect classification, searchability, and technical insight generation. Opportunities for Full Time Employment Strong internship performance may provide opportunities for consideration for future full-time employment. Any employment consideration will be subject to business requirements, position availability, candidate suitability, and the applicable recruitment process. Project Scope The intern will undertake the following project-based activities under appropriate technical guidance: Study the electrical and physical signatures associated with selected semiconductor defect modes and examine how these signatures appear across different process stages and test flows. Organize engineering and failure analysis information into a structured, searchable, and reusable defect knowledge repository. Develop an interactive dashboard for standardized defect categorization, visualization, trend analysis, and technical reporting. Apply Python, statistical methods, and data analytics techniques to examine relationships between physical defect characteristics and electrical test results. Evaluate Artificial Intelligence-enabled methods, including Generative Artificial Intelligence, Artificial Intelligence Assistants, Agentic Solutions, and Large Language Models, for defect categorization, information retrieval, and engineering knowledge management. Learning Opportunities Through this internship project, the successful candidate will have opportunities to: Develop knowledge of High Bandwidth Memory technology, semiconductor product engineering, manufacturing processes, and defect mechanisms. Learn electrical testing methodologies, failure signature interpretation, defect characterization, and failure analysis concepts. Apply Python programming, statistical analysis, data management, dashboard development, and data visualization to an engineering project. Explore responsible applications of Artificial Intelligence, Generative Artificial Intelligence, Artificial Intelligence Assistants, Agentic Artificial Intelligence, and Large Language Models in engineering workflows. Strengthen technical documentation, engineering communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Deliverables At the completion of the internship, the expected project deliverables include: A structured and searchable High Bandwidth Memory Defect Library containing documented electrical and physical signatures for selected defect modes. An interactive and user-friendly dashboard that enables standardized visualization, tracking, filtering, and analysis of defect information across multiple test flows. A documented defect categorization framework, data structure, and methodology that enable consistent future knowledge capture. A technical report describing the project methodology, analytical observations, dashboard functionality, limitations, and recommended future enhancements. A final presentation and demonstration communicating the project outcomes, engineering insights, and potential Artificial Intelligence-enabled applications. Impact of the Project The project is expected to: Improve the accessibility, consistency, and usability of defect-related engineering information. Strengthen visibility and understanding of defect signatures across selected test flows and process stages. Enable more efficient technical investigation, information retrieval, and knowledge transfer. Establish a scalable foundation for future data analytics and Artificial Intelligence-enabled engineering knowledge-management initiatives. Skillsets Required The ideal candidate should possess: A degree-level foundation in electrical engineering, materials science and engineering, semiconductor technology, physics, data science, or a related engineering or science discipline. Proficiency in Python programming and an understanding of data processing, statistical analysis, or engineering data applications. Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to organize and interpret complex technical information. Familiarity with data analytics, data visualization, dashboard development, database concepts, or knowledge-management methods. Interest in and familiarity with Artificial Intelligence tools or AI-enabled workflows, such as Generative Artificial Intelligence, Artificial Intelligence Assistants, Agentic Artificial Intelligence solutions, and Large Language Models. Course of Interest The ideal candidate should be pursuing a master’s degree in electrical engineering, Materials Science and Engineering, Semiconductor Technology and Operations, Physics, Data Science with Semiconductor Applications, or a related engineering or science discipline. Duration of Period The ideal candidate should be able to commit to a full-time internship period of at least 6 months. About Micron Technology, Inc. jobs.title: Research Intern - Quantum Algorithms
jobs.body: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The Research Intern will perform research on quantum algorithms and/or quantum information protocols for fault-tolerant quantum computers. A focus of the work will be on designing efficient quantum circuits for algorithmic primitives and to understand the complexity for concrete instances as well as the asymptotic behavior. Applications in areas such as simulation and communication may also be considered. Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. jobs.title: AI Developer Intern — Interconnect Hardware Frontend, 2027
jobs.body: NVIDIA's MSS-Interconnect frontend team is looking for an intern to help explore where modern AI can create real value for RTL, verification, debug, and design-review workflows. During your internship, you will take a focused AI-for-hardware use case from idea to working prototype, evaluate current AI tools and agents on real engineering problems, and help the team learn which capabilities are worth adopting. You will work alongside RTL, verification, CAD, and methodology engineers on a global, cross-site team. What you'll be doing: Prototype AI-assisted workflows for a focused hardware frontend problem — RTL, verification, debug, code understanding, or design review — and iterate with the engineers who use it. Evaluate new AI tools, models, and agent capabilities on real engineering tasks, and help assess which are worth adopting. Build small, reusable tools or automation that make a concrete workflow faster or more reliable. Partner with hardware engineers to turn a real pain point into a practical AI use case, and refine it based on usage and feedback. Share what works and what doesn't so the team can decide where to experiment and invest further. What we need to see: Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Solid Python and software engineering fundamentals, with some experience building automation, scripts, or tools. Exposure to hardware frontend workflows — RTL design, verification, debug, or design methodology — through coursework, projects, research, or prior internships. Enough hardware understanding to judge whether an AI-assisted solution is actually useful and technically sound. Strong problem-solving, communication, and a collaborative, self-driven attitude. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Hands-on experience building or using LLM-based tools, agents, or AI-assisted workflows — in coursework, research, or personal projects. Strong familiarity with modern AI tooling and good judgment on which new tools are worth trying. Coursework, research, or projects in frontend hardware development or debug-intensive workflows. Familiarity with Interconnect, NoC, Memory System, bus-fabric, or related silicon domains.

jobs.body: Job Location MASON BUS AND INNOVATION CTR Job Description Research and Development (R&D) at Procter & Gamble, the largest consumer packaged goods company in the world, includes a diverse group of roles that contribute to the innovation and development of our products. It encompasses roles in product research, formulation, testing, and scientific analysis. You will find variety and excitement starting Day 1. This internship is specifically designed for individuals working towards a PhD who are developing proficiency in their field. As an intern or co-op in management, you will have the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals in a supportive environment. This is a 12-week paid internship, designed to provide you with a solid foundation for future career growth. The internship will take place from May (potentially early June) to August of 2027. Join us at P&G, where your contributions will play a vital role in shaping the future of consumer products! The Opportunity: Research & Development at Procter & Gamble brings together science, innovation, and technology to create safe, high-quality products for consumers worldwide. Within Beauty Care, Global Product Stewardship applies exposure science, toxicology, and regulatory science to support product safety and responsible innovation. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to join our Beauty Human Safety organization, located in Mason, OH, as a PhD Summer Intern. The intern will collaborate with scientists and modelers on a quantitative research project supporting the evaluation of consumer product exposure to beauty spray products. The role will involve generating and analyzing scientific data, applying computational methods, evaluating model performance, and communicating findings and recommendations to a cross-functional team. This opportunity offers hands-on experience applying advanced technical skills to real-world product safety questions in a multidisciplinary research environment. Key Responsibilities: Use existing internal experimental design & protocols to generate experimental data for various product types. Use experimental data to create an exposure model. Compare model predictions, evaluate performance, document assumptions and limitations, and recommend refinements. Deliver a prototype model interface or workflow, a technical report, and a final internal presentation. jobs.body: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW We're looking for a Composite Structures Engineering Intern to join our Structures team as REGENT scales up design work across multiple Seaglider programs. In this role, you'll work in NX with Fibersim to model composite parts and develop laminate schedules, with the chance to follow those parts through build, analysis, manufacturing, and final assembly into the vehicle. You'll also pick up cross-functional sustaining work that supports our build and maintenance teams, giving you exposure well beyond a single corner of the design process. This is a chance to get hands-on with the kind of detailed composite design work that keeps a novel vehicle program moving — incorporating structural refinements, closing out important sustaining tasks, and helping unlock faster design iterations for the team. As part of Hardware Engineering, you'll work alongside engineers who care deeply about rigor and craftsmanship, and who are excited to introduce you to the advanced composite design and manufacturing technology REGENT uses to bring Seagliders to life. If you're curious about composite structures, energized by variety across the product lifecycle, and eager to learn by doing, we'd love to have you on the team. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Model Composite Parts: You'll work in NX with Fibersim to model composite parts and develop the laminate schedules behind them. - Follow Parts End to End: You'll have the opportunity to take parts through full design cycles, from build and analysis through manufacturing and final assembly into the vehicle. - Support Multiple Programs: You'll contribute to part modeling and drafting work as REGENT scales up design across several active programs at once. - Incorporate Structural Refinements: You'll help translate updates coming out of structural analysis into accurate, build-ready part models. - Pick Up Sustaining Work: You'll take on cross-functional tasks that support our build and maintenance teams, keeping important work from falling through the cracks. - Collaborate Across Teams: You'll partner with manufacturing, build, and analysis engineers, gaining visibility into how composite parts move from concept to finished vehicle. - Learn Cutting-Edge Tools: You'll be introduced to the advanced composite design and manufacturing technology REGENT uses to build Seagliders. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - CAD Fluency: You're comfortable navigating CAD software and thinking like a designer, with an eye for precision and detail. - Mechanical or Aerospace Foundation: You bring a solid grasp of fundamental mechanical or aerospace concepts that helps you integrate smoothly into cross-functional work. - Composite Materials Know-How: You've studied composites and understand Classical Laminate Theory well enough to apply it to real part design. - Creative Problem-Solving: You enjoy adaptive, critical thinking and aren't afraid to find non-traditional solutions for a genuinely novel vehicle. - Clear Communication: You can translate technical concepts for teammates outside your immediate discipline, which helps when working across build and manufacturing teams. - Hands-On Manufacturing Exposure: Any experience working directly with composite manufacturing is a plus and helps you speak the same language as the build team. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You're passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.title: Intern - Field Application and Services Eng (Teradyne, Mexico)
jobs.body: > Teradyne Robotics — Redefining Automation Together At Teradyne Robotics, we’re shaping the future of automation. As part of Teradyne Inc., we unite market-leading automation brands Universal Robots and MiR to create next-generation robotics for markets across the world. With over 110,000 industrial collaborative robots and autonomous mobile robots sold globally, we’re transforming industries and empowering businesses of all sizes. We’re proud to say that our customers count on us. Our Purpose At Teradyne Robotics, our mission is simple: Automation for Anyone. Anywhere. Our vision is to create a world where people work with robots, not like robots. With more than 100,000 collaborative robots deployed worldwide, Universal Robots leads the global market in collaborative automation while MiR provides cutting-edge autonomous mobile robots that transform internal logistics. Together, we enable manufacturers of all sizes to automate, improve productivity, and empower people through robotics. Opportunity Overview The Field Applications and Service Engineer Intern is an early-career technical role designed to support the Teradyne Robotics Service Center in Mexico. Working side by side with experienced service and application engineers, the intern helps deliver day-to-day service operations for the Universal Robots collaborative robots and Mobile Industrial Robots autonomous mobile robots portfolio, including unit intake and diagnostics, repairs and testing, case documentation, and warranty support. Beyond the service bench, this role acts as a flexible support resource for the team: extending its capacity, helping standardize processes, building documentation and tools, and supporting field visits, demonstrations, and application validations when needed. This is a hands-on learning opportunity, with mentorship and real responsibility, for students who want to build a career in robotics and industrial automation. Key Responsibilities Play an active role in daily Service Center operations for UR and MiR products, gaining hands-on experience with unit intake, inventory, logistics, equipment readiness, and essential safety and quality practices. Learn alongside experienced engineers as you help diagnose, troubleshoot, repair, test, and validate robotic systems, and participate in field service, installations, inspections, application trials, demonstrations, and hands-on training. Help deliver a great customer experience by providing first-level technical support to customers and partners, maintaining accurate service and warranty records, and supporting administrative and invoicing documentation. Make a meaningful impact on team performance by analyzing service trends, creating reports and technical resources, improving processes and tools, and supporting events, pre-sales activities, and other team priorities. All About You We seek individuals who share our passion and determination. Our commitment to customer success drives us to go the extra mile. If you’re ready to join us in this mission, take a closer look at the minimum criteria for the position. Minimum Job Requirements Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program in Mechatronics, Electrical, Electronics, Mechanical, Robotics, Industrial, or a related field. At least two (2) years remaining to complete university studies. Availability to work 20 hours per week, with a schedule agreed upon with the manager and compatible with class schedules. Ability to provide proof of active student status and to formalize the internship through the university’s agreement process, in accordance with applicable regulations in Mexico. Working knowledge of English, with the ability to read technical documentation and communicate in writing. Solid fundamentals in electrical and electronic circuits, mechanical systems, and basic programming or industrial automation concepts. Hands-on aptitude and willingness to work in a service center and workshop environment, including handling equipment and tools. Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools, especially Excel and Word, and ability to learn new software and case management systems quickly. Availability for occasional local travel within Mexico to support customer visits, events, or partner activities. Preferred Job Requirements Exposure to collaborative or industrial robotics through coursework, projects, competitions, or internships, with hands-on experience in technical support, laboratory, or workshop settings preferred. Knowledge of PLCs, industrial communication protocols, sensors, vision systems, electrical schematics, mechanical drawings, or CAD tools. Programming experience in Python or C++, familiarity with ROS, PolyScope, or URScript, and exposure to ticketing, CRM, or case management systems. Curious, proactive, and safety-minded team player with strong analytical, organizational, communication, and customer-service skills; able to work independently, collaborate across teams, take ownership, and seek feedback. *This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship or relocation assistance. #LI-PS1 <span

jobs.title: Controls Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Flight Controls Team Our Flight Controls team is at the heart of Zipline’s product success - we are responsible for developing, testing and maintaining some of the critical flight software systems that enable our aircraft to complete missions autonomously, from takeoff through to predicting and executing a successful delivery, through to landing safely and accurately. We develop novel solutions to give us the responsiveness, robustness and quality we need to ensure our delivery platforms can function in a wide range of increasingly challenging conditions and truly serve everyone in the world equally. The Role Zipline’s people thrive on finding elegant solutions to complex problems, given what exists today and what we can develop to maturity quickly and confidently. We stay close to our customers, learn what really works, and find where we can put the leverage to make a big difference for them now. As an intern on the Flight Controls team, you will learn how we fly autonomous aircraft in a range of challenging flight conditions. Using data from flight testing and simulation as well as our global fleet of customer aircraft, you will be looking for insights that can help improve our design. Through this you’ll have the opportunity to make changes to our systems that will measurably improve our product - your work will not just be theoretical; you will have the opportunity to see your contributions fly! What You'll Do Contribute to the design, implementation, testing and release of innovative flight algorithms that improve the operational performance of our vehicle controllers Create tools and tests to demonstrate your design performance and protect against software regressions, using both theoretical guarantees and simulations Develop and improve simulation and other controls analysis tools so we can predict vehicle performance ahead of time and prove safety and reliability Analyze flight data to assess recent changes and upgrades, looking for regressions and potential areas for future improvement Design onboard integrity tests to communicate when the system performance is degraded Present key results and changes to the broader engineering team What You'll Bring Your applied math skills stand out even among aerospace engineers. You think simulations and working with hardware are both fun. You have owned and developed controls solutions for a team project, thesis, or competition Exposure in one or more of the following areas: precision integrated inertial navigation, dynamic modeling of complex systems, linear control analysis, or optimal control with uncertainty. Software engineering skills, preferably with both embedded software (C, C++, Rust) and technical computing (MATLAB, python, Julia, etc.). Experience with Github and working in a multi-developer environment is an advantage. What Else You Should Know Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco or Dallas office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May/June to August/September. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply! Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Voluntary Self-Identification For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

jobs.title: Thermal Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. As an Intern, you will have an amazing opportunity to work on hard problems — we pride ourselves on giving everyone at Astranis a chance to do meaningful work on complex projects, no matter their seniority. Many past interns have designed and tested hardware/software that is heading to space on our first satellite, and many of them are now full-time employees at Astranis. Design, evaluate, procure and test thermal solutions such as heaters, heat pipes, thermal interface materials, and surface coatings. jobs.title: Technical Communications & Project Management  Intern
jobs.body: Additional Location(s): N/A Diversity - Innovation - Caring - Global Collaboration - Winning Spirit - High Performance At Boston Scientific, we’ll give you the opportunity to harness all that’s within you by working in teams of diverse and high-performing employees, tackling some of the most important health industry challenges. With access to the latest tools, information and training, we’ll help you in advancing your skills and career. Here, you’ll be supported in progressing – whatever your ambitions. At Boston Scientific, we value collaboration and synergy. This role follows an onsite work model, requiring employees to be in our local office at least five days per week. Relocation and housing assistance may be available to those who meet the eligibility criteria. Boston Scientific will not offer sponsorship or take over sponsorship of an employment VISA for this position at this time We will consider qualified applicants of all ages who are starting (or restarting) their careers As a Technical Communications & Project Management Intern , you will gain hands-on experience supporting project management activities and cross-functional teams within the Active Implantable Systems division. You will work alongside experienced project managers and technical professionals, gaining exposure to medical device product development while developing skills in project planning, communication, coordination, and technical documentation. This internship is ideal for a student pursuing a degree in Technical Communications, Communications, or a related field who is personable, organized, collaborative, and interested in learning how complex projects move from planning through execution. Through job shadowing, mentorship, and participation on core project teams, you will see firsthand how project managers bring together diverse functions to achieve shared goals in a regulated, purpose-driven environment. Your responsibilities will include: Shadow and support project managers to gain practical exposure to project planning, execution, and cross-functional coordination within medical device product development. Collaborate with cross-functional core teams, including R&D, Quality, Regulatory, Clinical, and other business partners, to support project activities and team objectives. Assist in developing and maintaining project schedules, timelines, milestones, and action items to help teams stay aligned and on track. Serve as a communication liaison between project teams and functional groups, helping facilitate information sharing, follow-up, and alignment across stakeholders. Support project meetings by assisting with agendas, meeting materials, notes, action items, and follow-up communications. Help organize and maintain project documentation and technical communications , ensuring information is clear, accurate, accessible, and appropriately documented. Apply strong written and verbal communication skills to translate technical and project information into clear communications for a variety of audiences. Assist project managers with project planning, tracking, status reporting, and coordination of deliverables associated with key product development milestones. Work with engineers, technical experts, and other cross-functional partners to understand project needs, dependencies, risks, and priorities. Gain familiarity with project management tools, processes, and best practices used to support medical device development in a regulated environment. Contribute to continuous improvement opportunities related to project communication, documentation, planning, and team collaboration. Throughout the internship, you will have opportunities to shadow the Project Management team, participate in core team activities, build relationships across functions, and develop practical project management and technical communication skills that can serve as a foundation for your future career. Required qualifications: Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s or master's degree program, with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 and Spring 2028. Pursuing a degree in Technical Writing/ Technical Communications or a writing-related major, with relevant technical writing work/academic experience. Academic project or work experience involving technical writing. Able to start the internship on May 17 or May 24, 2027, and work for 12 weeks. Must have reliable transportation to and from work. Preferred qualifications: Experience with single-source authoring tools. Experience with content management systems (CMS). Experience with XML-based authoring. Experience with AI-assisted writing tools. Coursework in medical terminology or medical-industry writing experience. Ability to understand and convey complex technical information clearly and concisely. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to communicate effectively with diverse, cross-functional teams. Attention to detail and ability to work independently Requisition ID: 634772 Minimum Salary: $ 43368 Maximum Salary: $ 73736 The anticipated compensation listed above and the value of core and optional employee benefits offered by Boston Scientific (BSC) – see www.bscbenefitsconnect.com— will vary based on actual location of the position and other pertinent factors considered in determining actual compensation for the role. Compensation will be commensurate with demonstrable level of experience and training, pertinent education including licensure and certifications, among other relevant business or organizational needs. At BSC, it is not typical for an individual to be hired near the bottom or top of the anticipated salary range listed above. Compensation for non-exempt (hourly), non-sales roles may also include variable compensation from time to time (e.g., any overtime and shift differential) and annual bonus target (subject to plan eligibility and other requirements). Compensation for exempt, non-sales roles may also include variable compensation, i.e., annual bonus target and long-term incentives (subject to plan eligibility and other requirements). For MA positions : It is unlawful to require or administer a lie detector test for employment. Violators are subject to criminal penalties and civil liability. Boston Scientific transforms lives through innovative medical technologies that improve the health of patients around the world. As a global medical technology leader for more than 45 years, we advance science for life by providing a broad range of high-performance solutions that address unmet patient needs and reduce the cost of healthcare. Our portfolio of devices and therapies helps physicians diagnose and treat complex cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, oncological, neurological and urological diseases and conditions. Learn more at www.bostonscientific.com and follow us on LinkedIn . Boston Scientific Corporation has been and will continue to be an equal opportunity employer. To ensure full implementation of its equal employment policy, the Company will continue to take steps to assure that recruitment, hiring, assignment, promotion, compensation, and all other personnel decisions are made and administered without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, citizenship, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, age, mental or physical disability, genetic information or any other protected class. Candidates will be notified during the interview and selection process if the role(s) for which they have applied require proof of vaccination as a condition of employment. Boston Scientific continues to evaluate its policies and protocols regarding the COVID-19 vaccine and will comply with all applicable state and federal law and healthcare credentialing requirements. As employees of the Company, you will be expected to meet the ongoing requirements for your roles, including any new requirements, should the Company’s policies or protocols change with regard to COVID-19 vaccination. jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern – Research and Development – Vehicle Health Management
jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.body: Job Description The Role We are seeking highly motivated, technically exceptional interns to join our team in the rapidly growing field of Vehicle Health Management (VHM). This is an exciting opportunity to work at the intersection of connected vehicles, data science, physics-based modeling, and advanced AI to develop technologies that make vehicle ownership more convenient and seamless for millions of customers. You will also help advance vehicle and propulsion systems in support of enterprise cost reduction through improved warranty performance and greater engineering development efficiency. In this role, you will transform vehicle engineering data into actionable insights that can predict system issues and identify root causes before they affect vehicle performance or disrupt customers’ daily lives. Our VHM research combines fundamental physics-based understanding with modern machine learning approaches, including but not limited to large language models, causal AI, and reinforcement learning, to deliver scalable solutions for diagnostics, prognostics, and system performance management. GM is a leader in this field. One example is the industry-first OnStar Proactive Alert for Starting System, which warns customers of potential component failures before they become emergencies, turning unplanned repairs into scheduled maintenance. Now available on more than 15 million GM vehicles, this service demonstrates the real-world impact of our work at scale. By joining this team, you will help advance technologies that improve the ownership experience for millions of customers. What You’ll Do: Generate innovative ideas in VHM related areas, utilizing physics-based, data-driven, as well as latest AI-based modeling methodologies Develop next-generation technologies for vehicle system diagnosis, prognosis, and fault-tolerant controls as well as integration Develop and execute specific research plans, including concept generation, prototype development, system implementation, and performance evaluation Document and present results Required Qualifications: Pursuit of an advanced degree (Master or PhD) in one of the following areas: Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, or related field of study Must be a current student Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months Background in fault detection and isolation, diagnostics and prognostics, root cause analysis Understanding of AI/ML development workflows, including data preparation, model training and deployment, performance evaluation and monitoring Experience in Python (including familiarity with ML frameworks such as PyTorch or Tensorflow), PySpark, MATLAB/Simulink Effective verbal and written communication skills Ability to work both independently and in teams Preferred Qualifications: Prior internship experience in automotive, technology, or manufacturing Strong critical thinking and analytical skills, especially the ability to synthesize large amounts of data involving multiple variables into comprehensive, impactful insights Strong theoretical and experimental skills, especially in controls, optimization, signal processing Background in latest AI technologies such as deep learning, LLMs, causal AI, reinforcement learning, foundation models, physics-informed machine learning GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need GM immigration sponsorship now or in the future. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.) The position is subject to export control restrictions and requires the successful candidate to be a U.S. Person (U.S. citizen, U.S. permanent resident, asylee or refugee). Work Arrangement: Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Warren, MI three times per week, at minimum. Start dates for this internship role are in May 24th & June 14th of 2027.
