Location Singapore Department Process and Equipment Engineering, Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) Project Title Workstation Performance Acceleration Through an Artificial Intelligence-Driven Root Cause Analysis Tool Project Description The intern will explore the application of Artificial Intelligence and machine learning to incident analysis within the Chemical Vapor Deposition process area. The project aims to transform equipment, process, and human-written incident data into structured, actionable insights that enable engineering teams to investigate recurring workstation failures more effectively. Through this project, the intern will gain exposure to semiconductor process and equipment engineering while developing and validating an AI-Enabled root cause analysis solution. The experience will involve technical learning, data analysis, model experimentation, and cross-functional engagement with production, equipment, process, hardware, and planning subject-matter experts. Objective of the Project Develop an AI-Enabled approach for interpreting human-written incident records from the Equipment Tracking Interface (ETI). Organize incident data into meaningful Pareto categories to provide clearer investigation direction. Explore correlations across equipment alarms, Fault Detection and Classification data, Statistical Process Control data, and historical incident records. Strengthen incident validation through appropriate integration with Microsoft Teams. Identify recurring failure patterns and opportunities to accelerate engineering learning cycles. Opportunities for Full-Time Employment High-performing interns may be considered for suitable full-time or future internship opportunities, subject to business needs, position availability, and the applicable selection process. Project Scope Prepare, classify, and analyze incident inputs from equipment alarms, Fault Detection and Classification systems, Statistical Process Control records, and the Equipment Tracking Interface. Explore and train Artificial Intelligence or machine learning models to interpret technical context and human-written terminology in incident logs. Develop methods for grouping incidents into Pareto categories and identifying chronic or recurring failure signatures. Evaluate an integration concept between the Equipment Tracking Interface and Microsoft Teams for incident validation. Conduct correlation studies and model validation using historical manufacturing data under the guidance of engineering subject-matter experts. Learning Opportunities Gain practical exposure to Chemical Vapor Deposition processes, semiconductor equipment engineering, process control, and workstation performance. Learn how Artificial Intelligence, machine learning, and Large Language Model techniques can be applied to unstructured engineering records. Apply root cause analysis methods such as Failure Mode and Effects Analysis, Eight Disciplines problem-solving, Pareto analysis, and Statistical Process Control. Build experience in data preparation, model simulation, validation, visualization, and the communication of technical findings. Engage with cross-functional experts from process, equipment, production, hardware, and planning functions. Deliverables A validated AI model or prototype capable of interpreting human-written Equipment Tracking Interface incident logs. A methodology for categorizing incidents into Pareto groups and identifying recurring failure patterns. A proof of concept for linking relevant incident records with Microsoft Teams validation inputs. Data visualizations, correlation-study results, and documented recommendations for further solution development. Impact of the Project Target a productivity improvement of approximately 12 engineering hours per week. Reduce information gaps in incident validation by connecting relevant data and engineering inputs. Accelerate learning cycles for chronic issues by an estimated two to three weeks. Improve the consistency and clarity of root cause investigation directions for engineering teams. Skillsets Required Strong analytical, logical, and critical-thinking skills with an interest in semiconductor manufacturing and engineering problem-solving. Knowledge of statistical data analysis, Design of Experiments, Statistical Process Control, or root cause analysis methods is advantageous. Familiarity with Python, structured data analysis, machine learning, Generative AI, Large Language Models, or other AI-Enabled workflows is preferred. Ability to apply digital fluency and role-appropriate AI literacy responsibly while exercising sound judgment and complying with organizational, confidentiality, and legal requirements. Effective communication and collaboration skills for engagement with cross-functional engineering teams. jobs.body: Job Title Internship: EMC/EMI Test Setup for IVUS Image Interference (Master) Job Description Start Date: February 2027 Duration: minimum 6 months Type: Internship Weekly Presence: 40h (minimum 32h) Location: Best ( 4x/week for 2 months, then depending on the project timeline can be 3x/week) Internship: EMC/EMI Test Setup for IVUS Image Interference (Master) As an R&D Engineering Intern, you will investigate the “spoke-wheel” interference pattern that can appear as an artefact in phased-array and rotational IVUS imaging during EMC/EMI verification testing. Your role: Develop a test setup that mimics the relevant IVUS system behavior and enables investigation of EMI susceptibility. Investigate potential sources of the interference pattern and assess how conducted EMI and other disturbances affect image quality. Plan and execute EMC/EMI lab measurements, including controlled noise injection and capture of relevant data sets. Analyse the impact of interference on medical-device performance and functionality. Explore practical options to prevent, attenuate, or remove the interference pattern. Document the approach, results, conclusions, and recommendations in a final report or research paper. Main Deliverables: Test setup for EMI susceptibility investigation EMC/EMI lab data sets, including disturbances superimposed on clinical data Final presentation of key findings Final report or research paper You're the right fit if: Strong command of English (spoken & written) Currently a Master’s degree in Telecommunications, Electrical Engineering, or related field Ability to read, synthesize, and critically analyze scientific and technical literature Excellent communication skills, both oral and written Solid critical thinking and problem‑solving abilities Ability and interest to work hands-on in a laboratory environment and operate relevant measurement/test equipment (such as a spectrum analyzer, antennas, signal generators, oscilloscopes, RF amplifiers, Power meters, etc.) Knowledge of RF communication, interference mechanisms, and electromagnetic principles How we work together We believe that we are better together than apart. For our office-based teams, this means working in-person at least 3 days per week. Onsite roles require full-time presence in the company’s facilities. Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations. Monthly full-time allowance between €500 - €700 gross, depending on your education level. If you need to relocate to The Netherlands specifically for the internship there will be a different allowance. Part-time internships receive the allowance pro-rata. Housing compensation, in case of relocating to the vicinity of the office, €300,- net if location is in the vicinity of Amsterdam, €255,- net for all other Philips locations. To be eligible, your usual home-work travel distance needs to be more than 50 km or 1.5 hours of travel time (one way). Afterwards, you need to provide the rental contract from your (new) landlord. Discover opportunities to make a difference at RTX. We bring the strength of more than 100 years of experience and renowned engineering expertise to meet the needs of today’s mission and stay ahead of tomorrow’s threat. Our team solves tough, meaningful problems that create a safer, more secure world. Raytheon’s Air & Space Defense Systems (ASDS) strategic business unit (SBU) specializes in multi-domain integrated air and missile defense, advanced sensors, space-based systems, hypersonics, effectors and cyber solutions. Focused on program execution, business growth and the highest level of customer satisfaction, the ASDS team provides customers with unmatched capabilities of detection and sensing, command and control, and air-to-air, air-to-surface, and surface-to-air munitions to accomplish air, space and missile defense missions. Within ASDS, Space Intelligence, Surveillance & Reconnaissance is our Sub-SBU that delivers information superiority from space, multi-mission automation and orchestration, multiple intelligence (Multi-INT) and resilient operations, secure processing, and data management. Raytheon is hiring electrical engineers with an emphasis in RF communications and antenna system design and is part of the Raytheon Cooperative Education Program (Co‑op). Upon selection, Co‑op participants will be submitted for a U.S. Government security clearance. jobs.body: We’re the nation’s favourite heating brand, here to warm up people’s homes, lives, and futures. From boilers, hybrids and heat pumps to solar thermal and smart controls, we’re giving our customers plenty of choice. With cutting-edge tech and research, we’re right in the thick of the drive for a better future of home heating. It’s not all tools and tech. People are the real heart of our company. If that sounds like something you’d like to be a part of, we’d love to meet you. Come and work #LikeABosch at Worcester Bosch. Join us for your placement year in summer 2027/28! In this role, you will be responsible for: Based in Worcester, you will have the chance to work for a dynamic company to enrich your knowledge and experience. jobs.body: Launch Your Engineering Career: Automated Test Engineering Intern (16-Month Co-op) Are you ready to own a codebase end-to-end and see your technical contributions directly protect the user experience? Join Trimble as an Automated Test Engineering Intern, where you will build advanced web UI testing frameworks, integrate with real-time navigation simulation platforms, and gain high-value software engineering experience across our product ecosystem. What Makes This Role Great: In this role, you will bridge the gap between frontend UI testing and hardware simulation tools, driving software quality and system reliability while owning a scalable web automation framework from concept to deployment. Key Exciting Responsibilities: Spearhead the design, construction, and deployment of scalable automated web UI testing frameworks integrated with real-time navigation systems. Integrate automated UI test suites directly into continuous integration pipelines to prevent software regressions before production releases. Partner with test engineers and software developers to maintain, update, and optimize real-time navigation simulation scenarios and automated test workflows. Execute end-to-end test suites across web interfaces and simulation layers to analyze performance and report detailed technical feedback. Essential Skills & Experience: Active enrollment in an undergraduate or graduate program in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field. Availability for a full-time, 16-month placement starting in May 2027 located in Richmond Hill, Ontario. Submission of a link to a personal or public code repository (such as GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket) displaying original code samples. Demonstrated programming capability in Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, or Java alongside solid Git version control skills. Hands-on experience or coursework with web UI automation tools like Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, or Puppeteer. Bonus Points For: Familiarity with hardware-in-the-loop testing, Spirent automation tools, or location simulation software. Exposure to spatial data, mapping interfaces, or real-time communication protocols like WebSockets and REST APIs. Practical experience configuring CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Jenkins. Logistics: Location: Richmond Hill, Ontario (In-Office) Travel Requirement: 0% Start Date: May 2027 Why You'll Love Working With Us At Trimble, we're not just a company that "does good"—we are a team dedicated to making a tangible, positive Real-World Impact. We build innovative solutions designed to solve the world's most critical challenges. From construction sites to transportation hubs, our work tangibly improves how people live, build, move, and grow. You'll work on projects that truly matter: Our purpose-driven culture means you'll be helping to build and deliver solutions that make work faster, safer, and more sustainable for millions of people worldwide. Our impact is tangible, from connected machines that save fuel to data-driven insights that reduce waste. Collaborate with like-minded people: Our strong internal culture is a "hidden gem." You will work with a collaborative, supportive team that shares your purpose and fosters a genuine sense of belonging. We're a company of "visionary pragmatists" who think boldly and build things that work. Be an owner: Trimble thrives on individuals who take initiative and embrace ownership. You'll find an entrepreneurial spirit where success is often "self-authored," empowering proactive "doers." Automated Test Engineering, QA Automation, Python, Selenium, Playwright, Continuous Integration, Spirent Simulation, Software Quality Assurance, Test Automation Framework, Web UI Testing How to Apply: Please submit an online application for this position by clicking on one of the Apply buttons located in this posting. Join a Values-Driven Team: Belong, Grow, Innovate. At Trimble, our core values of Belong, Grow, and Innovate aren't just words—they're the foundation of our culture. jobs.body: An internship at onsemi offers a dynamic opportunity to gain hands-on experience through real-world projects that drive innovation in the semiconductor industry. Interns are entrusted with meaningful responsibilities and exposed to cutting-edge technologies, fostering both technical skill development and professional growth. onsemi views internships as a strategic pipeline for entry-level career positions, providing a collaborative and inclusive environment where interns work alongside diverse teams and contribute to high-impact initiatives. The company’s commitment to sustainability, including its goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2040, enables interns to engage in projects that align with global environmental priorities. Key benefits include: Competitive compensation and medical benefits Flexible work hours aligned with academic schedules Access to Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) which foster a sense of belonging and provide opportunities for mentorship and community engagement Networking events, professional development workshops, and project showcases that build career readiness and visibility across the organization Internship roles span multiple disciplines including engineering, business operations, data analytics, and finance, and are designed to align with onsemi’s strategic goals of innovation and workforce development. Structured programs such as rotational field sales and finance analyst tracks offer additional career pathways for interns transitioning into full-time roles. onsemi is seeking a graduate-level Device Characterization Intern in San Jose to support next-generation semiconductor technology development. In this role, the intern will perform hands-on wafer-level measurements, automate test and reporting workflows, analyze characterization data, and work with devices across image sensor, ASIC, high-voltage, analog mixed-signal, and low-voltage integrated circuit technologies. This internship is intended for a graduate student who wants to combine hands-on wafer-level characterization, test automation, and data-driven analysis. The intern will work with engineering teams in San Jose to characterize devices, automate measurement and reporting workflows, and contribute to AI-enabled approaches for improving characterization efficiency. · Carry out wafer-level measurements on test structures using semiconductor parameter analyzers, capacitance meters, and source measurement units · Perform flicker noise measurements using noise characterization instruments · Testing ESD (electrostatic discharge) devices using TLP (transmission line pulse) testers · Generating test reports and summaries · Automate test report generation, summary creation, and recurring characterization data workflows. · Participate in AI-related initiatives that improve device characterization workflows, data analysis, or test automation. Qualifications – External Requirements: · Understand semiconductor device physics and circuit operation. · Have experience doing measurements with lab equipment like IV meters, power supplies, and oscilloscopes. · Experience with Python, Visual Basic, C or LabVIEW. · Be a quick learner who can work efficiently both independently and as part of a team. · Excellent verbal and written communication skills. · Nice-to-have qualifications include: o Have experience with semiconductor characterization equipment like semiconductor parametric analyzers, capacitance meters, and source measurement units. o Be familiar with programming test instruments with GPIB. o Have experience with machine learning, AI, and developer-assistance tools such as GitHub Copilot. o Have experience using AI frameworks or similar tools to develop practical engineering solutions. To be considered for an internship, you must be currently enrolled in a degree seeking program. This position is specifically looking for someone who will be enrolled in a Bachelors degree program in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Applied Physics, or Systems Engineering in the US. Here at onsemi we take great pride in our internship program and the efforts we take to provide students with hands-on industry experience. We provide competitive pay medical benefits, various networking event opportunities, and flexible hours based on school schedule. onsemi is excited to share the base salary range for this position is $33.35/hr. The final pay rate for the successful candidate will depend on geographic location, skills, education, experience, and/or consideration of internal equity of our current team members. We also offer a competitive benefits package. https://www.onsemi.com/site/pdf/Benefits-Summary-USA.pdf

jobs.body: The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. The Structural Mechanics Subdivision provides expertise in the areas of static and dynamic structures, mechanisms, environments, and materials for government and commercial space applications. jobs.title: AI Research Intern (PhD)
jobs.body: Who we are Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress. Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that. Atoms builds Physical AI real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive. This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale. We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life. If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us. About the Role We are seeking an AI Research Intern to join our founding team and bridge the gap between high-level AI research and real-world physical actuation for our next-generation autonomous transport platforms. In this role, you will contribute to core research initiatives on Perception, World Models and Action models. You will help translate cutting-edge theoretical breakthroughs into scalable, real-world deployment on physical autonomous systems, driving how our platforms perceive, simulate, and navigate complex environments. What you'll do Integrate emerging research from the broader AI community, identifying and prototyping the most promising solutions. Design and build end-to-end multimodal models that translate real-time visual perception and high-level behavioral goals into physical vehicle actuation. Research and develop cutting-edge RL and distillation techniques for trajectory planning. Develop interactive world models from raw multi-sensor logs, allowing the team to re-simulate events and query what a vehicle would see if it altered its trajectory. Ensure core autonomous driving models can seamlessly adapt to novel urban environments and edge cases. Partner with validation and research teams to run model experiments through rigorous simulated scenarios, detecting regressions and identifying systemic performance bottlenecks. What we're looking for Education: Currently enrolled in a PhD degree program in Computer Science, EECS, Robotics, AI, or a closely related field. Research Track Record: Publications or active submissions in top-tier AI or robotics venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, RSS, ICRA, CoRL). Core Expertise: PhD level research background focused on at least one of the following domains: Generative World Models / Video Generation / Diffusion Models Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models or embodied AI Reinforcement Learning (RL), trajectory optimization, or decision-making systems Large-scale multimodal Transformer architectures applied to robotics or spatio-temporal data Framework Fluency: Advanced hands-on proficiency with PyTorch or JAX for training and fine-tuning large-scale neural networks. Programming: Proficiency in Python and working knowledge of C++. Preferred qualifications Prior research or internship experience in autonomous driving, mobile robotics, or spatial AI. Hands-on experience with Sensor Fusion integrating inputs across multi-camera setups, LiDAR, and Radar. Familiarity with Bird’s-Eye-View (BEV) visual representations, 3D occupancy forecasting, multi-task learning, or specialized data tokenization for spatial data. Prior experience with large-scale distributed training on GPU/TPU clusters (e.g., DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM, Ray, or PyTorch FSDP). Why join us At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow. What else you need to know This role is based in our Mountain View or San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change, we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week. The hourly pay range for this internship role is $70/hr per hour. Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications. Atoms accepts applications on an ongoing basis. Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others? #LI-Onsite

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Engineering and Tech Internship
jobs.body: Most engineering internships teach you how products are built. At Boom, you help build them. Boom Supersonic is building Overture, the world's fastest airliner, and Superpower, an industrial gas turbine built on the same core technology that advances our supersonic engine program. We believe the best engineering internships don't happen on the sidelines. They happen where real engineering is getting done. This is not a traditional internship. You won't sit quietly in meetings, take notes, or shadow from the sidelines. As a Boom intern, you will be embedded directly within core teams, tackling real, high-stakes engineering problems. Working alongside best-in-class engineers, you'll take on more responsibility and ownership than anywhere else in the industry. You’ll leave knowing your work actively pushed history forward. Who you are This program isn't for everyone. You are built for Boom if: You have a track record of building: You've built real hardware independently, led a competitive design team, or executed high-impact work during past roles that most engineers don't touch for years. You crave ownership, not hand-holding: You get uncomfortable waiting for answers and prefer diving headfirst into complex, ambiguous problems. You thrive under high stakes: When a problem gets harder, your drive goes up, not down. You're drawn to execution: The shop floor, lab, or test stand sounds significantly more exciting to you than a conference room. Select your discipline When applying, select the discipline below that best matches your background and passion: Materials & Manufacturing Processes: You'll work on the materials and processes that go into Superpower, Boom's gas turbine engine. That means hands-on involvement in material selection, process development, lab categorization and coupon-to-part testing for the high-performance alloys that make an engine possible. Own the whole process from ingot to forged disks and single crystal castings. Ideal Candidate: Solid fundamentals in material science of metallics and ceramics, with knowledge of the strengthening mechanisms of nickel superalloys and the thermal processing of ceramics both as coatings and molds. Hands-on experience in an M&P lab to test, categorize and evaluate high performance materials including creep and LCF testing and metallography of superalloys. Exposure to and experience running the machines for advanced processes including printing nickel superalloys and fabricating ceramics to support investment casting. Manufacturing: You'll support the production processes turning Superpower's designs into real hardware. That means hands-on work across engine assembly, machining, tooling, and process development as the program builds toward production. You won't observe – you'll own a piece of it. Ideal Candidate: Hands-on manufacturing experience – time in a machine shop, on an assembly line, or building real hardware. This is required, not a nice-to-have. Familiarity with machining processes, tooling, work instructions, or quality control in a production or R&D environment. Genuine curiosity about how complex hardware comes together – and how to make it come together better, faster, and more reliably. Electrical or Embedded Controls: You'll help design, build, and validate the electrical or control systems that bring Superpower to life. That includes instrumentation, controls, wiring architecture, and test systems that generate the data needed to develop Superpower. Your work will connect hardware, software, and test, turning ideas into reliable systems. Ideal Candidate: Experience designing, integrating, or testing electrical systems, whether through internships, research, Formula SAE, personal projects, or industry experience. Familiarity with electrical design, controls, instrumentation, embedded systems, or hardware integration. Someone who enjoys debugging complex systems and is energized by seeing hardware come to life. Mechanical: You'll help define how Superpower comes together. This team is responsible for translating requirements into an integrated system, balancing performance, reliability, manufacturability, and testability while partnering closely with propulsion, electrical, and manufacturing engineers throughout the development process. You'll work across design, analysis, manufacturing, and test to solve real engineering problems as the engine evolves from concept to hardware. Ideal Candidate: Experience designing, analyzing, or building mechanical hardware through industry, research, internships, Formula SAE, or personal projects. Familiarity with CAD, mechanical design principles, manufacturing processes, or structural analysis. Genuine curiosity about how complex hardware works and the drive to iterate until it works better. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to break down complex technical challenges and make thoughtful engineering tradeoffs. Excited by working across disciplines to solve first-of-their-kind engineering challenges with a highly collaborative team. Turbomachinery: You'll help design the actual core engine within both Superpower, Boom's gas turbine for AI power generation and Symphony, our Mach 1.7 medium bypass turbofan. This team is responsible for the design, performance modeling, and detailed analysis of the engine, with work spanning thermodynamic cycle analysis, aerodynamics & aeromechanics, internal cooling flow, mechanical & structural component design, combustion, and testing. Ideal Candidate: Experience with propulsion, turbomachinery, thermodynamics, fluids, combustion, or heat transfer through coursework, research, internships, or industry. Strong analytical skills with the ability to connect theory to real hardware and experimental data. Excited by not just using state-of-the-art analysis tools, but by creating their own; scripting together multi-disciplinary workflows that bring capabilities once only available to large teams to a single user’s fingertips. Software: You'll build the software that makes Boom's engineers faster. That means embedding directly with the teams designing, building, and testing Superpower - on the shop floor watching a part get made, at the test stand when data comes in - and shipping tools that remove whatever is slowing them down. Your code goes into daily use the same week you write it, and the people using it sit next to you. Ideal Candidate: Experience building real software people actually used - personal projects with users, open source contributions, hackathon wins, or production code from prior internships or research. Strong fundamentals in at least one serious language, and fluency with modern AI development tools. More excited to write code standing next to the machine it controls than alone in a cubicle - you want to see the part come off the line faster because of what you shipped. Special Projects: You'll join Boom's team of universal problem-solvers — the group we point at whatever is most broken, most urgent, or most important, anywhere in the company. Instead of going deep in one business function, you'll own a real piece of a high-stakes, cross-functional problem: driving a critical project that's slipping back on track, building the analysis behind a major decision, standing up a business process that outlasts your summer, or getting to ground truth on an operation that isn't working. You won't build the engine — you'll help make sure the company building it runs. You'll own the fix, not a recommendation. Ideal Candidate: Strong analytical horsepower — fast in a spreadsheet, and able to turn messy data into a clear answer. A track record of solving or leading something real — a competition team you drove, research or a role that stretched you well past your experience level. Equally comfortable in a spreadsheet and on a shop floor — you'd rather get to ground truth in person than wait for a report. Energized by ambiguity and ownership: when a problem gets harder and no one is handing you the answer, your drive goes up, not down. Work Location Internships require 100% onsite at Boom's headquarters located at 6803 S Tucson Way, Centennial, CO 80112. Internship Duration Internships will run for 12 weeks with flexibility to accommodate for the academic semester. What is it REALLY like to work at Boom? Find out here . Compensation The hourly pay rate for this position is $35 per hour for Hardware, $40 per hour for Software. Boom will also provide a housing allowance of $2,000. Additional perks include on-site meals and gym access. Due to the nature of this position, candidates must be eligible to access export-controlled information and technology as required by applicable U.S. export control laws. Learn more about ITAR here. jobs.title: R&D Intern (Suzhou)
jobs.body: At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com . As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit. Job Function: Career Programs Job Sub Function: Non-LDP Intern/Co-Op Job Category: Career Program All Job Posting Locations: Suzhou, Jiangsu, China Job Description: Department: R&D Work Address: J&J Suzhou Campus (299 Changyang Street, Suzhou) Internship Term : Full time, 5 days/week, 4-6 months Hire Manager : R&D Manager Johnson & Johnson MedTech China R&D Suzhou team is seeking two motivated R&D interns to support test development, laboratory operations and equipment qualification for medical device projects. This is a hands ‑ on role for students who want practical exposure to test system setup, data acquisition and analysis, and laboratory quality practices in a regulated environment. Key Responsibilities Support test execution and data activities: acquire, organize and analyze test data; prepare clear summaries and test reports. Assist in building and validating test systems: support equipment installation, verification, commissioning activities and the associated documentation. Support laboratory operations and equipment management: routine maintenance, calibration scheduling and record keeping to meet internal and external audit requirements. Contribute to test method documentation and continuous improvement initiatives. Maintain a safe and compliant lab environment, following established procedures and quality standards. Requirements Majoring in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, sophomore year or above. Commit to a full ‑ time (5 days/week) internship for at least 4 consecutive months. Basic data analysis skills and familiarity with test data handling; ability to produce clear tables, charts and technical summaries. Experience with statistical tools (Minitab) is a plus. Hands ‑ on experience with mechanical/test lab equipment (e.g., universal testers, load frames, data acquisition systems) and familiarity with calibration practices. Experience writing or executing test procedures and producing test reports. Good self ‑ management and learning ability; proactive, detail ‑ oriented and reliable. What You Will Gain Domain learning: deepen your understanding of medical device product lifecycle, verification data, and regulatory considerations in China. Hands‑on project experience: participate in real test and validation work, prototype activities and equipment setup/verification. Transferable skills: improve technical analysis, test planning, reporting, presentation & storytelling, project collaboration and English business communication. Mentorship & professional growth: receive regular coaching and feedback from experienced engineers and R&D leads. Cross‑functional collaboration & global exposure: work with R&D, Manufacturing, Quality, global stakeholders and external suppliers. Factory & operational exposure: opportunities to visit manufacturing or assembly areas and learn about prototyping and production processes. Required Skills: Preferred Skills:

jobs.body: > Production Planning Co-op Reference #43257 Waterdown, Ontario About L3HARRIS WESCAM As a subsidiary of L3Harris Technologies and within the Integrated Mission Systems Segment, the WESCAM division develops the most advanced optical sensor and targeting systems for global defense and military sectors, National Security, Search & Rescue and Airborne law enforcement agencies. About the Role This is a 16 month role to start in September 2027. They collaborate with Inventory Control and Purchasing to address material requirements and component shortages, negotiate recovery dates with Production Supervisors, and provide critical information to the Master Scheduler. This role demands strong communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills, as well as the ability to create and maintain reports for Key Performance Indicators in Production Planning and Scheduling. The Co-op actively supports Continuous Improvement initiatives and is proficient in data analysis within a team-oriented environment. reports and take action to ensure WOs start on time Open, release and close manufacturing Work Orders while ensuring data accuracy Review and execute planning responsibilities for Kanban processes Inventory & Material Coordination Collaborate with the Inventory Control Group (stockroom) on material requirements kitting, POU replenishment and material movement Communicate with Purchasing to provide visibility on component shortages for upcoming WOs Monitor Point-of-Use inventory accuracy, proactively investigating and resolving discrepancies Support and complete monthly cycle counts and annual WIP counts Cross-Functional Communication & Reporting Coordinate and negotiate schedule recovery dates with Production Supervisors to maintain on-time Work Order completion Provide critical updates to the Master Scheduler on delays impacting customer order completion Generate weekly reports on WO completion rates for assigned work centers Monitor workflow between production cells and other departments, ensuring seamless operations Contribute scheduling insights to daily Operations Status meetings Continuous Improvement & Process Optimization Support Continuous Improvement (CI) and Kaizen initiatives to enhance operations efficiency Provide weekly metrics related to on-time WO completions along with root cause Analyze production data and Team Key Results (TKRs) to improve planning accuracy Assist the work center supervisor with capacity planning for assigned work orders and feedback information to the Master Schedulers for consistent improvement in factory scheduling Required Qualifications & Skills Technical Skills Data analysis skills with experience in Microsoft Excel and PowerBI Soft Skills Intense ownership – takes full responsibility for planning outcomes and drives solutions proactively Meticulous attention to detail – ensures accuracy in schedules, inventory and work orders Strong accountability – follows through on commitments, owns results and holds others accountable Problem solving and analytical skills – quickly identifies issues and implements effective solutions Excellent communication and interpersonal skills – collaborates effectively across teams and leadership levels Highly organized with efficient time management – prioritizes tasks efficiently in a fast-paced environment Resilient, action-oriented and results-driven jobs.body: Electro-Optic Seekers & Systems Engineer - Undergraduate Placement 2027 Would you like to utilise your degree to push the cutting edge of sensing and imaging technology? This opportunity within the Electro-Optics Seekers and Sensors will allow you to innovate within a supportive team, at a company that invests in its people and supports our Armed Forces. The opportunity: Our Electro-Optic (EO) Seekers & Sensors department provides expertise and support into all projects within MBDA involving EO technologies, as well as investing in research and development of innovative technologies which will shape the future of our products. We work on projects that cover the whole product lifecycle from concept and assessment through to full product design, testing and production. This role presents an exciting opportunity to experience all of these areas through a range of systems design, computational modelling, lab testing and field trials within a diverse team of engineers. Some of the EO technologies we specialise in include: Infra-Red (IR) Seekers & Sensors Optics Computational Imaging Lasers & Directed Energy Weapons Across the department we have a variety of different teams to get involved in, who work together to deliver our overall functional capability. What we’re looking for from you: Current undergraduate studying for a degree in a Physics, Engineering, Electronics, Computing or any Applied Science discipline. We are looking for candidates with an interest in electro-optic systems and technologies, who are keen to apply their knowledge and skills to challenge themselves, the team and our technical capability. You will produce visual designs from concept through delivery and sustainment, support interaction designs for hardware and/or software-based experiences, and partner with internal and external development teams, marketing and design groups to research and analyze customer feedback for incorporation into product enhancements, new product designs and overall design language and strategy. jobs.body: NVIDIA is looking for research interns with a strong background relevant to applying modern AI methods to re-imagine technology across the Earth System Simulation and Analytics stack. Skills should be relevant to research on applied topics such as generative data assimilation, hybrid climate simulation, full model emulation of climate model components, regional-to-global high-resolution AI autoregressive weather prediction, and dynamical downscaling. We are hunting for highly creative, independent and self-starting research interns to help us invent that future. jobs.title: Autonomy Engineer Intern, Autonomy Infrastructure, Systems and Tools, 2027 (Zurich)
jobs.body: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions. ABOUT THE ROLE: The core of our system is the computer vision algorithms that allow drones to understand the world around them. You will architect and implement the algorithms that run on every drone powered by Skydio as part of a world class computer vision and deep learning team with researchers who have pushed the state of the art in academia and industry. As a Research Intern, you will be paired up with one or more members of our core software development team, assuming direct ownership of a project that meaningfully advances the capabilities of our team and products. If you have a strong foundation in math, theory, and software development and you are interested in directly contributing to the development of the next generation of autonomy algorithms and pushing them into real products, we would love to hear from you. AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY: - Design and build robust replay and analysis systems that enable engineers to inspect and reproduce recorded autonomy behavior, with fine-grained control over system state, perception outputs, and decision-making at every stage of the stack. - Develop scalable infrastructure for automated testing and failure triage, expanding our simulation and log-driven test coverage while accelerating root-cause analysis through automated log processing and diagnostics. - Operate at the interface between autonomy software and core robotics middleware, defining clear APIs, data contracts, and performance requirements for messaging, state propagation, and coordination across subsystems, while partnering closely with downstream teams to support their implementation and integration. - Design and implement high-quality developer infrastructure and tools that prioritize reliability, performance, and usability, enabling rapid iteration, safe experimentation, and sustained velocity across the autonomy organization. WHAT YOU’LL DO: - Lead the design and implementation of scalable tools used across autonomy development and testing workflows. - Collaborate with autonomy, QA, and infrastructure teams to gather requirements, align on priorities, and deliver impactful tooling. - Build tools that streamline stages of the robotics development process. - Take ownership of internal services from concept through deployment and monitoring. - Contribute to the long-term vision and roadmap for developer tools that improve debugging efficiency, test coverage, and system understanding. QUALIFICATIONS: - Proficiency in C++ and Python, with a strong grasp of performance-sensitive and multi-threaded systems. - Experience with simulation frameworks, time-synchronized data systems, or state-machine-driven applications. - Familiarity with structured data visualization, log processing, or developer tooling design. - Strong communication skills and the ability to partner effectively with cross-functional teams. - Comfort operating in a fast-paced environment where requirements evolve and priorities shift. BONUS EXPERIENCE: - Experience building performance-sensitive systems (profiling, multithreading, real-time constraints) in robotics, aerospace, automotive, or similar domains. - Exposure to robotics / simulation / physics engines. - Background in telemetry systems, log ingestion pipelines, or automated test environments. - Front-end development skills in modern web frameworks (e.g., React, TypeScript, Three.js, Plotly) with a focus on data interaction and visualization. - Familiarity with distributed systems or cloud-hosted services used to support internal tools and customer applications. Compensation: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Masters, and $70/hr for PhD students*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends. *Compensation for certain positions may vary based on the position's location. #LI-DK1 At Skydio we believe that diversity drives innovation. We have created a multidisciplinary environment that embraces the power of diverse perspectives to create elegant solutions for complex problems. We are committed to growing our network of people, programs, and resources to nurture an inclusive culture. jobs.title: Sustaining Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Position Summary The Sustaining Engineering Intern will support the Busbar Sustaining Engineering team in maintaining and improving released products throughout their lifecycle. Unlike new product development roles, this position focuses on solving real-world manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and product support challenges affecting existing products. The intern will work closely with sustaining engineers, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and product engineering teams to investigate production issues, support engineering changes, improve product documentation, analyze recurring problems, and assist with continuous improvement initiatives. This role provides hands-on exposure to engineering problem solving in an engineered-to-order (ETO) manufacturing environment and offers opportunities to contribute to product reliability, quality, manufacturability, and operational excellence. Key Responsibilities Production & Manufacturing Support Assist sustaining engineers in investigating manufacturing and production-related issues. Support resolution of drawing discrepancies, BOM errors, and configuration issues. Participate in shop floor observations and data collection activities. Work with manufacturing teams to understand fabrication, assembly, and quality challenges. Help document and track recurring issues that impact production efficiency. Engineering Change Management Support Engineering Change Orders (ECOs) and Engineering Change Requests (ECRs). Assist with updating drawings, specifications, and Bills of Materials (BOMs). Verify engineering documentation for accuracy and completeness. Help maintain engineering records within PLM and ERP systems. Root Cause Analysis & Quality Improvement Participate in structured problem-solving activities related to product and manufacturing issues. Assist in collecting and analyzing data to identify root causes. Support corrective and preventive action initiatives. Help track implementation and effectiveness of improvement actions. Continuous Improvement & Cost Reduction Support Value Analysis / Value Engineering (VAVE) initiatives. Research opportunities to improve product quality, reduce cost, or simplify manufacturing processes. Assist with standardization and process improvement projects. Analyze engineering and operational data to identify trends and improvement opportunities. Cross-Functional Collaboration Work with manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and engineering teams to support business objectives. Participate in engineering reviews and project meetings. Assist with technical documentation and engineering reports. Communicate findings and recommendations to team members and stakeholders. Internship Project Complete a structured internship project focused on product improvement, manufacturing support, quality enhancement, or process optimization. Present project results, recommendations, and lessons learned to engineering leadership at the conclusion of the internship. Qualifications Required Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in: Mechanical Engineering Mechanical Engineering Technology Manufacturing Engineering Industrial Engineering Related Engineering Discipline Completed sophomore year or higher. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment. Preferred Exposure to manufacturing processes and engineering drawings. Familiarity with SolidWorks or similar CAD software. Coursework in: Manufacturing Processes Quality Engineering Materials Mechanical Design Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing or Continuous Improvement concepts. Previous engineering project, internship, robotics, Formula SAE, or manufacturing experience. Learning Opportunities Interns will gain exposure to: Engineering Change Management Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) ERP and BOM Management Root Cause Analysis Quality Systems and Corrective Actions Manufacturing Operations Product Reliability Improvement VAVE and Cost Reduction Cross-Functional Engineering Support Busbar Product Manufacturing and Design Processes Success Measures Successful interns will: Contribute to the resolution of active sustaining engineering issues. Demonstrate effective analytical and problem-solving skills. Support implementation of engineering changes and documentation updates. Deliver measurable improvements in quality, manufacturability, cost, or process efficiency. Successfully complete and present a sustaining engineering project with clear business impact. #LI-RB

jobs.title: Design and Verification Engineer Intern
jobs.body: Design and Verification Engineer Intern The Opportunity: As an electrical engineer, you understand the workings behind complex systems. That knowledge is key when it comes to designing, simulating, and verifying digital circuits for advanced microelectronic systems. We’re looking for an electrical engineer who can use their skills to help government clients develop reliable, mission-ready semiconductor technologies. At Booz Allen, you’ll use your engineering skills to transform the defense and national security microelectronics industry. Our team develops and evaluates secure, reliable digital hardware solutions for mission-critical applications. That’s why we need you, an electrical engineer with foundational knowledge of digital design and hardware verification, to help us design and develop digital logic, verification environments, testbenches, and reusable verification components for microelectronic systems. On our team, you’ll learn how to translate system requirements into hardware specifications, develop RTL using a hardware description language, create simulation-based testbenches, execute verification plans, analyze coverage, and troubleshoot any bugs. You’ll impact national security and defense missions by helping deliver trusted and assured microelectronics that operate as intended. This is a chance to grow your digital design and verification skills while gaining experience in RTL development, functional verification, semiconductor design workflows, and electronic design automation tools. Take on exciting challenges in national security microelectronics with us as we improve the reliability and availability of trusted microelectronics technologies for critical government missions. Join us. The world can’t wait. You Have: Knowledge of digital logic design concepts, including Boolean logic, finite-state machines, combinational logic, and sequential logic Knowledge of at least one hardware description or hardware verification language, such as Verilog or SystemVerilog Ability to develop, simulate, debug, or verify digital hardware through academic coursework, laboratory assignments, internships, or technical projects Ability to use scripting or programming languages, such as Python, C, C++, Tcl, or Bash, for engineering or test automation Ability to communicate technical information and collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams Ability to obtain a Secret clearance Scheduled to obtain a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering by Spring 2030 Nice If You Have: Experience developing RTL, testbenches, assertions, verification plans, or functional coverage Knowledge of verification methodologies, including Universal Verification Methodology Ability to use electronic design automation or simulation tools from vendors such as Cadence, Siemens, or Synopsys Clearance: Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. Compensation At Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page. Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $55,200.00 to $126,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud. Candidate AI Usage Policy AI is a part of our daily work at Booz Allen, and we are committed to the responsible and ethical use of AI tools. However, we want to ensure a fair candidate process based on your own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other tools to assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is prohibited unless permission is explicitly provided . Work Model Our people-first culture prioritizes the benefits of collaboration. To support engagement and effective communication, employees working virtually are generally expected to have their cameras on during meetings. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer Intern
jobs.body: Position Summary: Manufacturing Engineer Intern is responsible for supporting production through daily trouble shooting and root cause analysis to ensure processes are safe, meet quality and throughput requirements and making the work easier for the operators. This requires hands on involvement and working on the shop floor. In addition to this support, they will be responsible for design and implementation of tooling and/or process changes to improve manufacturing processes. They will also own larger cost reduction projects from ideation, feasibility and design, Capital Expenditure approval, and implementation. Principle Duties (includes, but is not limited to): Provides support to obtain safe, efficient, productive and economical manufacturing operations. Develops and maintains routings, tool lists, fixtures, process instructions and process requirements, for manufacturing equipment and operations. Develops Work instructions and standard work to document processes and flow. Drives out waste from manufacturing operations through the deployment of lean and CBS methodology. Addresses production Andon stoppages and develops counter measures using 5 why methodology. Trains operators on proper, efficient manufacturing methods and procedures, to maximize machine and process productivity. Coordinates the purchase of necessary production materials and tooling. Implements changes to tools and fixtures. Supports new process and product development implementation. Assists with developing and implementing current and future state value stream maps and continuous Improvement plans. Audits and improves existing manufacturing processes. Solves daily manufacturing process problems. Tries out experimental commercial tooling. Simplifies the methods/tooling and therefore reduces cycle times and W.I.P. Improves area equipment layouts and material flow. Assists operators with daily assembly problems with equipment, methods and tooling. Assists in justifying and coordinating the installation of capital equipment. Participates actively in the Continuous Improvement and Quality processes including project team involvement and problem solving. Essential Qualifications / Experience: In process of obtaining B.S. in Engineering or related degree. Problem solving and root cause analysis skills. Proficient with 2D and 3D CAD software Preferred Qualifications/Experience Exposure to lean manufacturing, six sigma, and 5S practices. Proficient with data analysis, statistics, and applied mathematics. Demonstrated ability to understand process & product specifications. Basic understanding of industrial assembly, fabrication, and machining processes. Working experience with Autodesk Inventor Professional EOE/Women/Minorities/Veterans/Disabled Salary range: $25.00 hourly. This is a hands-on opportunity to apply coding and AI skills to real laboratory challenges — helping automate manual workflows, streamline data handling, and prototype AI-assisted tools that improve lab efficiency and data quality. You will work alongside lab managers, scientists, and analysts to understand real lab processes and build practical, reliable tools that make everyday lab work faster and more consistent. This is a great fit for a student who enjoys working at the intersection of science, data, and automation. jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern - Research and Development - Magnetic Materials
jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.body: Job Description The Role: As a valued Intern in the Mechanics, Materials and Process Research Lab at General Motors Research and Development, you will innovate in magnetic materials for next-generation vehicle and manufacturing applications. You will propose new research directions, establish technical research plans, and lead collaborative studies spanning magnetic materials discovery, computational modeling, processing, characterization, and validation. You will generate new insights into the relationships among composition, crystal structure, microstructure, magnetic behavior, thermal stability, manufacturability, and system performance. Your work will guide experimental efforts, accelerate materials down-selection, and help translate research results into practical solutions for motors, sensors, actuators, power systems, and other GM applications. You will document and communicate results through high-quality technical reports, external publications, presentations, and records of invention. What You’ll Do: • Plan and execute collaborative research in magnetic materials, generating new knowledge and enabling innovative materials solutions. • Apply physics-based modeling, simulation, and data-driven approaches to magnetic-materials discovery, design, and performance prediction. • Investigate structure–property relationships involving magnetization, coercivity, remanence, permeability, loss, temperature dependence, phase stability, and degradation. • Partner closely with experimental researchers to guide synthesis and processing, interpret characterization data, and accelerate materials down-selection. • Evaluate magnetic materials and material systems for applications including electric machines, sensors, actuators, power electronics, and manufacturing processes. • Connect computational predictions with experimental validation using appropriate magnetic, structural, thermal, electrical, and mechanical measurements. • Drive internal and external collaborations with GM engineering teams, universities, national laboratories, suppliers, and research partners. • Maintain awareness of the state of the art in magnetic materials, computational materials science, materials characterization, and related disciplines. • Prepare timely, high-quality technical reports, presentations, publications, and invention disclosures to communicate research outcomes. • Generate intellectual property to protect new inventions and research results. • Assist and mentor other employees in accomplishing project and research goals. jobs.body: Job Description 2027 Summer Intern – Computational Design The Role: General Motors Design is seeking a Computational Design Intern to support the development of innovative digital tools, workflows, and automotive design studies within a creative studio environment. This internship offers qualified candidates the opportunity to explore careers at GM while gaining practical experience at the intersection of computational design, digital sculpting, automotive form development, and advanced 3D modeling. The intern will collaborate with Design, Sculpting, and Engineering teams to investigate new ways of generating, evaluating, and refining digital models of future automotive themes. The role provides exposure to aesthetic decision-making, design technology, production methods, program timing, and the materials and processes used in automotive digital development. The Team: The intern will collaborate with GM Design, Sculpting, and Engineering teams in an automotive design studio environment. What You’ll Do: · Collaborate with Design, Sculpting, and Engineering teams to interpret sketches, design intent, and technical requirements. · Develop digital studies, tools, and model variations for future automotive themes using computational design and digital-sculpting techniques. · Explore parametric, procedural, generative, and automation-based approaches to support automotive form development and design iteration. · Build and refine 3D models while maintaining an understanding of proportion, line, surface quality, and visual harmony. · Translate creative concepts into clear digital workflows, prototypes, visualizations, or production-ready modeling studies. · Support the development of reusable scripts, definitions, templates, or processes that improve design exploration and studio efficiency. · Work within established digital modeling standards while helping evaluate emerging technologies and best practices. · Present project progress, design studies, and finished work for Design leadership during midterm and final reviews. · Support general computational design and sculpting assignments within the studio environment. · Document methods, iterations, and results so that workflows can be communicated and reused by the broader team. Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications): · Pursuit of a bachelor’s or advanced degree in Computational Design, Industrial Design, Product Design, Transportation Design, Architecture, Animation, Game Design, Computer Science, Fine Arts, Sculpture, Ceramics, or a related field. · Must be graduating between December 2027 and May 2029. · Able to work full-time, 40 hours per week during the summer months. · Strong interest in the relationship between design, technology, geometry, and 3D form development. · Ability to work collaboratively in a creative, iterative, and feedback-driven studio environment. · Portfolio demonstrating 3D design, computational design, digital modeling, visual development, or related creative work. What will give you a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications): · Experience with computational, parametric, procedural, or generative design workflows. · Experience with software such as Rhino/Grasshopper, Alias, Unigraphics/NX, or comparable 3D platforms. · Programming or scripting experience in Python, C#, or a similar language. · Basic understanding of automotive design and sculpting principles, including proportion, line, surface, volume, and reflection quality. · Experience developing tools, scripts, plug-ins, procedural definitions, or automated modeling workflows. · Understanding of digital sculpting, polygonal modeling, NURBS modeling, subdivision surfaces, or related 3D techniques. · Ability to communicate design intent and technical concepts through sketches, diagrams, models, renderings, or presentations. · Curiosity, initiative, and the ability to learn new software and workflows quickly. jobs.body: About GlobalFoundries GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, power-efficient and high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. GF is a trusted and holistic technology partner for customers around the world. GF’s talented, global team remains focused every day on security, longevity and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com . Internship Program Overview: Our Interns & Co-ops are our entry-level talent pipeline for GF across the globe. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives. Summary of Role: This internship is in the Failure Analysis Laboratory at GlobalFoundries’ 300mm fabrication facility in Malta, New York. The intern will gain hands-on experience with semiconductor failure analysis through sample preparation, imaging, and analytical techniques while developing an understanding of semiconductor technology and manufacturing. Essential Responsibilities include: Support advanced analyses that meet turnaround-time requirements without compromising quality. Collaborate with laboratory shift teams, engineers, and managers to define analytical methods, align on analysis expectations, and interpret results. Work closely with Process Integration, Process Module, Product Engineering, and Customer Engineering organizations to meet technology requirements and deadlines. Assist in identifying opportunities to improve workflow optimization, cycle time, equipment utilization, and cost. Participate in continuous-improvement activities and laboratory process enhancements. Communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with peers and cross-functional teams. Other Responsibilities: Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs. Required Qualifications: Education – At least a sophomore at time of application and actively pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Physics, Materials Science, Optical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship. Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and be in good academic standing. Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal) Travel - Up to 10% Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship. Preferred Qualifications: Prior related internship or co-op experience Demonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc. Strong interest in leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and support effective decision-making. Project management skills, i.e., the ability to innovate and execute on solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity. Strong written and verbal communication skills Strong planning & organizational skills Relevant coursework, research, or laboratory experience in failure analysis, wafer processing, or semiconductor materials and device characterization. Hands-on experience with sample preparation, cross-sectioning, microscopy, or analytical characterization techniques. Familiarity with one or more failure-localization or analytical methods, such as OBIRCH, emission microscopy, thermal microscopy, SEM, FIB, X-ray analysis, C-SAM, AFM, SIMS, or TEM imaging. Self-driven approach, strong analytical skills, structured work style, and ability to understand complex technical matters quickly. jobs.title: Supplier Quality Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.body: HydraForce, a Bosch Rexroth company, offers one of the most comprehensive lines of high-quality hydraulic cartridge valves for the mobile and industrial equipment markets. We design and manufacture high performance valves that meet virtually any need encountered in machine design. HydraForce cartridge valves are designed to fit a wide range of industry-common valve cavities. Our employees enjoy a fast-paced and challenging work environment that provides them with daily opportunities to Power Forward their careers. Through interaction with our global network of employees and customers, our employees provide products and solutions that have a global impact. For almost 35 years, HydraForce has been producing the most innovative electro-hydraulic control solutions for the mobile machinery and industrial equipment markets. Throughout the world, you can find our products in a broad range of applications: Agricultural and Turf Care Machinery Construction and Road-Building Equipment Material Handling and Personnel-Lift Equipment Transmission, Engine and Powertrain Controls Forestry and Resource Management Equipment Refuse and Waste Handling Equipment Injection Molding and Press Machinery Other Specialized Mobile and Industrial Applications The goal of HydraForce’s internship program is to develop future engineering resources for our organization while providing support to our Supplier Quality Engineering team. We structure the engineering internship to allow candidates the opportunity to develop knowledge and skill-sets unique to our industry. Project tasks reflect an increasing level of technical complexity based on demonstrated proficiency and success on prior assignments. Although there is no guarantee of employment, it is our goal to have our interns fully capable of stepping into an entry-level engineering position upon graduation. Supporting Job Elements: Create Value Stream Maps and then create projects to lean out process Clean, merge and analyze data from multiple data sources Create databases to house past and future data Use tools and techniques from Six Sigma, Lean, to analyze and solve problems Assist in continuous improvement projects Day to day support activities but not limited to inspection, sorting, problem investigations, and PPAP approvals Assist in non-conforming material reports and analysis Create and modify existing systems that track our metrics Create, improve on documentation such as control plans, FMEAs, WI, and process flows Qualifications: Advanced Excel skills; Power Bi, Minitab Committed to an engineering college undergraduate program Completed a minimum of 24 hours at the university level Coursework and/or experience in setting up databases, SPC, data collection Coursework and/or experience in statistical analysis, lean tools Coursework and/or experience in measurement systems Basic experience in 3D modeling; Understanding of GD&T Working knowledge of problem solving techniques and FMEAs Great written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills Majors Desired: Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering Internship Dates: June 2, 2027-August 6, 2027 The US base hourly range for this position will be in between $20- $27 depending on the credits accumulated for the undergraduate students. Your Recruiter can share more details about the specific hourly range during the interview process. Indefinite U.S. work authorized individuals only. Future sponsorship for work authorization unavailable. By choice, we are committed to a diverse workforce and are an equal opportunity employer. Bosch Rexroth welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in the selection process. BOSCH is a proud supporter of STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering & Mathematics) Initiatives FIRST Robotics (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology) AWIM (A World In Motion)

jobs.title: Extracurricular Internship: R&D Engineer for Domestic Hot Water Tanks (f/m/div.)
jobs.body: The Bosch Group has more than 400 000 employees around the world, present in 60 countries, and we are proud to impact people’s lives and to work towards a more sustainable future. In the city of Aveiro, Bosch has one of its biggest production sites for Bosch Home Comfort division, as well as a Research and Development Center for new and improved heating solutions for the residential segment. With more than 1400 employees, focused on innovation, sustainability and collaboration, Bosch Aveiro joins together experts in diverse areas, from mechanical engineering to connectivity and software solutions, as well as industrialization and quality. At Bosch, we shape the future by inventing high-quality technologies and services that spark enthusiasm and enrich people’s lives. Our promise to our associates is rock-solid: we grow together, we enjoy our work, and we inspire each other. Join in and feel the difference in mindsets, cultures, generations, identities and perspectives. Everyone should bring their authenticity and work together respectfully. Bosch is an employer that values diversity and equal opportunities. We welcome applications from people with disabilities and we can provide reasonable accommodations during the recruitment process and in the performance of professional activity. By including everyone and ensuring equal opportunities we unleash our full potential. We are looking for a motivated engineer to join our R&D team and support the development, validation and launch of next-generation heat pump water heaters. This role offers the opportunity to work close to product innovation, laboratory testing and engineering decision-making, contributing directly to new product introduction and continuous improvement. Your contribution to something big: Support the development and industrialization of new domestic hot water tanks; Analyze current and upcoming legislation, standards and technical requirements applicable to products; Define validation strategies, test plans and engineering test methods; Execute laboratory testing, measurements and performance evaluations; Prepare clear technical reports and communicate results to stakeholders; Participate in troubleshooting, brainstorming and root cause analysis activities; Support engineering change management processes during product development; Collaborate with cross-functional teams including R&D, Quality, Product Management and Manufacturing. What distinguishes you: Academic Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering or similar technical field; Knowledge in turbomachinery and aerodynamics and strong interest in thermal systems, refrigeration or sustainable technologies; Good communication skills in Portuguese and English; Ability to manage multiple priorities and technical topics simultaneously; Innovative mindset with willingness to challenge and improve existing solutions. Duration: 12 months Work #LikeABosch includes: ⚖️ Flexible work conditions 🔀 Hybrid work system 💲 Access to great discounts in partnerships and Bosch products 🏋️ Sports and health related activities 🅿️ Free parking lot 🍽️ Canteen Success stories don´t just happen. They are made... Make it happen! We are looking forward to your application!
