With more than 1400 employees, focused on innovation, sustainability and collaboration, Bosch Aveiro joins together experts in diverse areas, from mechanical engineering to connectivity and software solutions, as well as industrialization and quality. At Bosch, we shape the future by inventing high-quality technologies and services that spark enthusiasm and enrich people’s lives. Our promise to our associates is rock-solid: we grow together, we enjoy our work, and we inspire each other. Join in and feel the difference in mindsets, cultures, generations, identities and perspectives. Everyone should bring their authenticity and work together respectfully. Bosch is an employer that values diversity and equal opportunities. We welcome applications from people with disabilities and we can provide reasonable accommodations during the recruitment process and in the performance of professional activity. By including everyone and ensuring equal opportunities we unleash our full potential. We are looking for a motivated engineer to join our R&D team and support the development, validation and launch of next-generation heat pump water heaters. This role offers the opportunity to work close to product innovation, laboratory testing and engineering decision-making, contributing directly to new product introduction and continuous improvement. Your contribution to something big: Support the development and industrialization of new heat pump water heater products; Analyze current and upcoming legislation, standards and technical requirements applicable to products; Define validation strategies, test plans and engineering test methods; Execute laboratory testing, measurements and performance evaluations; Prepare clear technical reports and communicate results to stakeholders; Participate in troubleshooting, brainstorming and root cause analysis activities; Support engineering change management processes during product development; Collaborate with cross-functional teams including R&D, Quality, Product Management and Manufacturing. What distinguishes you: Academic Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering or similar technical field; Knowledge in turbomachinery and aerodynamics and strong interest in thermal systems, refrigeration or sustainable technologies; Good communication skills in Portuguese and English; Ability to manage multiple priorities and technical topics simultaneously; Innovative mindset with willingness to challenge and improve existing solutions. Duration: 12 months Work #LikeABosch includes: ⚖️ Flexible work conditions 🔀 Hybrid work system 💲 Access to great discounts in partnerships and Bosch products 🏋️ Sports and health related activities 🅿️ Free parking lot 🍽️ Canteen Success stories don´t just happen. They are made... Make it happen! We are looking forward to your application!

jobs.title: [EMN] Internship – Automotive Hardware Penetration Testing
jobs.body: The Bosch Group is a leading global supplier of technology and services. It employs roughly 394,500 associates worldwide (as of December 31, 2020). According to preliminary figures, the company generated sales of 71.6 billion euros in 2020. Its operations are divided into four business sectors: Mobility Solutions, Industrial Technology, Consumer Goods, and Energy and Building Technology. The Bosch Group comprises Robert Bosch GmbH and its roughly 440 subsidiaries and regional companies in some 60 countries. If its sales and service partners are included, then Bosch is represented in roughly 126 locations. This worldwide development, manufacturing, and sales network is the foundation for further growth. BGSV – Bosch Global Software Technologies Company Limited (Previous name: RBVH - Robert Bosch Engineering and Business Solutions Vietnam Company Limited) is 100% owned subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH. BGSV has started its operations from 19th October, 2010 at E-Town2 in HCMC. This engineering development center will be engaged in developing embedded systems and software, mechanical design and simulation, and will provide IT (SAP Consulting, JAVA Development….) and Business Services (Finance and accounting, Economics, Purchasing, Logistics, Translations Japanese-English-Japanese, Information Security ) solutions to the Bosch group of companies globally. Technical Skills Embedded Systems Knowledge: Familiarity with microcontrollers (preferably RH850 or similar), memory maps, and boot processes. Programming: Proficiency in C/C++, basic Python; experience with embedded firmware development is a plus. Hardware Debugging: Exposure to tools like oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG/SWD debuggers. Security Concepts: Basic understanding of cybersecurity principles, threat modeling, or cryptography. Hands-On Experience (Preferred but not mandatory) Projects involving embedded systems, IoT devices, or automotive ECUs. Participation in hackathons, security competitions (e.g., CTFs). Experience with reverse engineering or hardware hacking tools (e.g., Ghidra, ChipWhisperer) 3rd or 4th student in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Mechatronics, or related fields. Available to commit to a full-time internship for 6 months, working Monday to Friday. Able to communicate effectively in English, both written and verbal. Curiosity & Problem-Solving: Strong interest in automotive security and willingness to explore new attack vectors. Teamwork: Ability to collaborate in a team setting, especially during the innovation project phase. Communication: Capable of documenting findings and presenting technical results clearly. Why BOSCH? Because we do not just follow trends, we create them. Together we turn ideas into reality, working every day to make the world of tomorrow a better place. Do you have high standards when it comes to your job? So do we. At Bosch, you will discover more than just work. Benefits and Career Opportunities Monthly Internship allowance + Meal & Parking allowance 1 day of paid leave per month Good benefits of Trade Union activities, team building and company trip. Opportunity to work in global projects of fast developing company and being a part of innovation team contributing initiative ideas to the hi-tech world. Engage in our diverse training programs which surely help strengthen both your personal and professional skills

jobs.title: Systems Engineering Intern Summer 2027
jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Systems Engineering Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Chantilly, Virginia, you will have the opportunity to support subsystem/system development testing and verification. This Systems Engineering team helps develop and execute to the technical baseline across all programs. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an engineering, physics or math discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Familiarity with optics Solidworks experience Cameo experience JAMA experience Proficient with Microsoft Office (Excel) ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Rate: $25.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. Important information: FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY: To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here . Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com. This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days. FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY: For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant. These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations. Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality. For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Internship - RA/QA - Quality Assurance - California
jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will: ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting​ Implement new ideas, be constantly challenged, and develop your skills​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions.​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward.​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts.​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives.​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships.​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ As an RA/QA Quality Assurance intern at Stryker, you will gain hands-on experience supporting quality processes that help ensure our products meet internal standards, regulatory requirements, and customer expectations. You will collaborate with cross-functional partners to support Quality Management System activities, contribute to continuous improvement efforts, and help drive compliance across product and process quality initiatives. You will contribute to projects that strengthen quality systems, improve documentation, and support safe, effective products for patients and customers: Support Quality Management System activities to help maintain compliance with applicable regulations, standards, and internal procedures Assist with Nonconformance reporting by helping investigate quality issues, document findings, and support timely resolution Contribute to Corrective and Preventive Action activities by supporting root cause analysis, action planning, and effectiveness checks Partner with cross-functional teams such as Manufacturing, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, Supplier Quality, and Operations to support quality initiatives Review and organize quality documentation, records, and process information to ensure accuracy, completeness, and alignment with procedural requirements Support continuous improvement projects focused on strengthening quality processes, reducing risk, and improving efficiency Gain exposure to audits, quality metrics, and compliance activities that help ensure products and processes meet Stryker’s high standards Majors Targeted: Scientific or technical disciplines preferred (e.g., Biomedical Engineering, Biological Sciences, Chemistry, or related fields) $20 min hourly wage – $35 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship.​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above (verified at time of hire) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require sponsorship now or in the future.​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment. Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. Stryker is an EO employer – M/F/Veteran/Disability. Stryker Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor’s legal duty to furnish information.

jobs.title: Intern - Industrial Controls
jobs.body: Who we are With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility. Timeframe: Summer (May-Aug 2027) At Symbotic, Early Career talent plays a meaningful role in helping us reimagine the future of supply chain automation. Through our Internship and Co-op programs, students have the opportunity to contribute to real projects, collaborate with experienced engineers and business leaders, and gain hands-on exposure to the technologies powering our end-to-end robotics and automation solutions. We are looking for curious, motivated students who are excited to solve complex problems, bring new perspectives to cross-functional teams, and see their work make an impact in a fast-moving, innovative environment. Along the way, Interns and Co-ops are supported through mentorship, professional development, networking opportunities, and a robust calendar of events designed to help them build community and grow their careers. Symbotic offers transportation and housing benefits for students who meet our relocation requirements. Continue reading below to learn more about this exciting opportunity! About the Opportunities Symbotic’s Industrial Controls team designs, implements, tests, and supports the control systems that power our automated warehouse equipment. Intern opportunities in our Industrial Controls function include: PLC interns contribute to the design and implementation of PLC hardware and software systems, troubleshoot system issues with site operators, develop and execute testing plans, participate in code reviews, and support commissioning and site installation. Electrical Engineering interns support electrical design for fixed automation equipment, including adapter cells, lift cells, motors, wiring, power, and variable frequency drives (VFDs). Software Tools interns support software tools used for data generation, structure validation, bot playback simulation, and data rendering for commissioning, testing, and system integration engineers. What You’ll Do: Assist one of our Industrial Controls teams with the design, implementation, testing, and support of controls technologies for automated warehouse systems. Contribute to the design and implementation of PLC hardware and software systems. Work with site operators and engineering teams to understand and diagnose PLC system issues. Develop and execute testing plans to validate PLC system performance. Participate in code reviews and adhere to PLC programming best practices. Support electrical design and troubleshooting involving circuits, motors, wiring, power distribution, and variable frequency drives (VFDs). Assist with site installation, commissioning, implementation, and support activities for automated equipment. Collaborate with commissioning, testing, system integration, software, and electrical engineering teams. Depending on team placement, contribute to software tools for data generation, structure validation, bot playback simulation, and data rendering. What you’ll need Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in engineering required (Electrical, Controls, Automation, Mechatronics, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related engineering/technical field). Familiarity with programmable logic controllers (PLCs), controls, industrial automation, or electro-mechanical systems. Ability to read or trace electrical circuits and an interest in motors, wiring, power systems, and VFDs. Familiarity with object-oriented programming and a programming language such as C# a plus. Exposure to AutoCAD, source control such as Git, software testing frameworks, or CI/CD pipelines a plus. Experience with technologies such as Jenkins, Redis, Docker, or Kubernetes a plus for software tools opportunities. Strong analytical, creative problem solving, critical thinking, and organizational skills. Outstanding communication skills with demonstrated ability to organize and present data. Our Environment Up to 10% of travel may be required. Employees must have a valid driver’s license and the ability to drive and/or fly to client and other customer locations. The employee is responsible for owning a credit card and managing expenses personally to be reimbursed on a bi-weekly basis. #LI-JK2 #LI-Onsite About Symbotic Symbotic is an automation technology leader reimagining the supply chain with its end-to-end, AI-powered robotic and software platform. Symbotic reinvents the warehouse as a strategic asset for the world’s largest retail, wholesale, and food & beverage companies. Applying next-gen technology, high-density storage and machine learning to solve today's complex distribution challenges, Symbotic enables companies to move goods with unmatched speed, agility, accuracy and efficiency. As the backbone of commerce the Symbotic platform transforms the flow of goods and the economics of supply chain for its customers. For more information, visit www.symbotic.com . We are a community of innovators, collaborators and pioneers who embrace our differences, because we know unique perspectives make us stronger and smarter. Every perspective matters. We depend on the collective voices of our employees, customers and community to help guide us as we build a better place to work – for you and the world. That’s why we’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, or genetic information. The base range for this position in the posted location is $32.00 - $44.00 however, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The compensation package includes medical, dental, vision, disability, 401K, PTO and/or other benefits.

jobs.title: Validation / Characterization Engineering Intern m/f/d
jobs.body: Change the world. Love your job. The Validation / Characterization Engineering Intern at Texas Instruments is powered by a passion for continual improvement. Our solutions make a real difference and yours will, too. We make the semiconductor product design process easier and faster, which helps our customers succeed in today's fast-paced marketplace. In this role you are going to join the validation team of the Isolated Analog-Digital-Converters group in Freising, Germany. Validation engineers cover electrical, parametric characterization of the integrated circuits, silicon debug support and data analysis. This includes printed circuit board design, test software development and error analysis. You are going to be an integral part of the new product development team, where you will be interfacing across multiple functions in an international team with focus on the following points: Characterization of key product parameters using laboratory instruments (oscilloscope, spectrum analyzer, pattern generator...) Verification, optimization and automation of existing measurement and test concepts Processing, statistical analysis and presentation of measurement data Assignment to one or more owned development projects: measurement automation, optimization of measurement throughput or development of concept boards. Minimum requirements: Pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in Electrical Engineering or related degree Good programming skills, preferable LabVIEW, Python and C/C++ Good understanding of analog digital converters and analog front-ends Basic awareness for parasitics in analog measurements & derive associated errors Minimum 20 weeks Preferred qualifications: Demonstrated proficiency with bench test equipment Experience with analog-mixed-signal parts and signal processing Experience in metrology Ability to take the initiative and drive for results Strong time management skills that enable on-time project delivery Strong verbal and written communication skills Ability to work in teams and collaborate effectively with people in different functions Ability to quickly ramp on new systems and processes Ability to establish strong relationships with key stakeholders critical to success, both internally and externally Demonstrated strong interpersonal, analytical and problem-solving skills Our offer for you: Benefit from attractive compensation Join an international work environment where your ideas count and where you can thrive in a diverse culture Explore a world of opportunities for your personal and professional development

jobs.title: Test Engineer Intern - Exmark
jobs.body: The 2027 Summer Internship Program will run from May 17, 2027, through August 6, 2027. Candidates must be available to start on May 17 and participate through the duration of the program. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future. Who Are We? The Toro Company (TTC) has delivered market-leading, innovative products and outstanding customer care for more than 100 years. With over 11,000 employees worldwide, TTC is headquartered in Bloomington, Minnesota, USA. Our company designs and manufactures turf maintenance equipment; turf irrigation systems; landscape and lighting products; snow and ice management solutions; agricultural irrigation systems; rental, specialty and underground construction equipment; and residential turf and snow equipment. We market and sell TTC products worldwide through a network of distributors, dealers, mass retailers, hardware retailers, equipment rental center and home centers—as well as online direct to end users. Exmark, located in Beatrice, Nebraska is a division of The Toro Company. Exmark is the leading manufacturer of commercial mowers and equipment for the landscape professional. Exmark mowers are trusted 2-to-1 over the next best-selling brand of zero-turn mowers by landscape professionals. All Exmark products are designed to help customers increase productivity, while delivering unmatched quality. What Will You Do? In order to grow and build a successful career with The Toro Company, you will be responsible for: Work within multi-discipline team to qualify prototype machines in advance of production (mechanical, electrical, electromechanical, software systems). Develop test plan then perform test setup, including Instrumentation and fixturing. Analyze and document test results. Opportunities to gain deeper understanding and learning of: instrumentation and data acquisition, LabVIEW, Thermal imaging, modal analysis, accelerometers, thermal and sound measuring equipment, Mat Lab, Creo. Collaborate across all functions of the business and learn what it takes to be part of a great team. What Do You Need? To be considered for this role, an individual should meet the following minimal requirements: Demonstrated mechanical aptitude with an ability to learn and apply new things Strong analytical and organizational skills Problem solving acumen Preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher Experience with MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook), CAD software, Test Instrumentation Ability to manage multiple projects at once and prioritize based on due dates or importance What Can We Give You? At The Toro Company, we are always working to make sure our interns know just how valued they are. In addition to a competitive pay- The Toro Company offers interns a variety of perks , including: Dress for your day – We know you're more productive when you're comfortable, which is why TTC employees are encouraged to take advantage of our casual, corporate environment. Volunteerism – The Toro Company is proud to provide interns 8 hours of paid time to volunteer in the community. Competitive Pay – Competitive compensation with an anticipated hourly rate of $22–$28. Actual rates may vary based on factors such as academic standing, business function, and other relevant considerations . The Toro Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants based on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military service, or other non-merit factors. We are committed to creating a welcoming environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Emerging Talent - Mechanical/Aerospace Engineering Internship
jobs.body: Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and capital-efficient approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to support a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and supporting a growing space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to design, build, and operate its own spacecraft in orbit. Next, Haven-1 is targeted to become the world’s first commercial space station, with launch anticipated in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced two new offerings leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo: Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line; and Vast Lunar Systems, power, communications, and habitats for the Moon. Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities capable of manufacturing America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for Mars, dedicated modules for government partners, and other crewed systems designed to unlock the expanding long-term space economy. Vast offers an advanced engineering internship program with hands-on opportunities to design and build space hardware and software. You will play a crucial role in the development of the systems that will be required for the operation of human-rated space stations and space infrastructure. We have five engineering internship postings for different areas of focus. Please only apply to the most relevant posting for your background. Our interns are mentored by industry experts to solve challenging real-world engineering problems across our hiring teams. This is a 12 week internship at our offices in Long Beach, CA or Hawthorne, CA or Mojave, CA. Responsibilities will vary depending on each intern’s area of expertise. We are currently looking for candidates with experience in the the following engineering disciplines: ECLSS (Environmental Control & Life Support Systems) ECLSS Test Mission Operations GNC (Guidance, Navigation, & Controls) E-2 Propulsion Propulsion Test Solar Structures Design Structures Test Thermal Analysis Thermal Hardware Thermal Test Minimum Qualifications: Qualified candidates must be enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master’s degree program from an accredited college or university in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or other related engineering discipline. Ability to work full-time onsite in Long Beach, Hawthorne, and Mojave, CA. Preferred Qualifications: Application of technical skills outside of the classroom (examples include: extracurricular projects, volunteering, personal projects, laboratory research, or prior internship/work experience) Proficiency in CAD software (e.g., NX, CATIA) for 3D modeling and simulation Attention to detail Strong engineering problem solving capabilities Basic knowledge of engineering and equipment Prior knowledge of analysis tools Ability to collaborate across different teams Self-directed with a positive attitude and team spirit Pay Range: California $35 — $42 USD We calibrate level and compensation to the selected candidate's experience and demonstrated capability. We welcome applicants across a range of experience levels to apply. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS Base salary will vary depending on job-related knowledge, education, skills, experience, business needs, and market demand. jobs.title: Industrial Engineering | Systems Engineering internship: cost driver modeling
jobs.body: Introduction Within ASML’s Manufacturing and Supply Chain environment in Veldhoven, you will contribute to improving transparency in Make & Install costs across a highly complex operational landscape. This Industrial Engineering | Systems Engineering internship: make & install cost modeling sits at the intersection of engineering, operations, finance, and program management. You will help develop a high-level cost model that explains how operational cost drivers influence overall Make & Install costs and supports fact-based decision-making. The outcome of this internship will help teams understand where improvement efforts create the greatest impact. If you enjoy connecting data, systems thinking, and stakeholder perspectives, this internship offers an opportunity to make a visible contribution. Your assignment During this internship, you will develop and validate a high-level model that creates transparency between cost drivers, cost categories, and total Make & Install costs. You will work with stakeholders from multiple departments and translate complex information into actionable insights and visualizations. The goal is to enable both forward-looking cost impact assessments and backward target-setting from overall cost objectives. Your main responsibilities will be: Develop a high-level cost model linking key cost drivers, cost categories, and total Make & Install costs. Analyze available data to determine model inputs, parameters, and assumptions. Quantify how changes in operational drivers influence overall costs. Translate overall cost targets into practical driver-level targets for stakeholders. Create intuitive visualizations and reporting concepts that explain model logic. Validate the model through data analysis, stakeholder feedback, and logical testing. Present recommendations for future use, governance, and further development of the model. This is a bachelor/master non-thesis internship for minimum 6 months, for minimum 4 days per week (hybrid). The start date of this internship is as of February 2027. Your profile To be suitable for the internship, you: Are pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in industrial engineering, systems engineering, operations management, mechanical engineering, data analytics, business economics, econometrics, or a related field. Have strong analytical skills and a genuine interest in cost modeling, operational performance, and complex systems. Have working knowledge of Microsoft Excel; experience with Power BI is considered an advantage. Are proactive and take ownership when working in an environment with multiple stakeholders. Collaborate and communicate effectively with different disciplines and confidently engage stakeholders at various organizational levels. This internship offers broad exposure across engineering, operations, finance, and program management functions. Throughout the internship, you will build a diverse network, gain insight into how strategic cost decisions are made, and contribute to improvements that support ASML’s business objectives. By the end of this internship, you will have delivered a validated model concept, a prototype solution, stakeholder-oriented reporting, and recommendations that support future cost management practices. Other requirements you need to meet: You are enrolled at an educational institute for the entire duration of the internship, and you are at least 18 years old at the start of the internship; If you are a non-EU citizen, studying in the Netherlands, your university is willing to sign the documents relevant for doing an internship (i.e., Nuffic agreement); You attach your cover letter with a clear motivation on why you are interested in this internship assignment in particular; You need to be located in the Netherlands to be perform your internship. In case you are currently living/studying outside of the Netherlands, your application shows the willingness to relocate. Inclusion and diversity ASML is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values and respects the importance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. It is the policy of the company to recruit, hire, train and promote persons in all job titles without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. We recognize that inclusion and diversity is a driving force in the success of our company. jobs.title: Medical Education & Communication Intern
jobs.body: It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide. We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world. The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life. If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here. Primary Function of Position The Medical Education & Communications Intern will support Medical Affairs activities through scientific communications, publication support, literature review, and content development related to novel fluorescence imaging agents, which are designed to help visualize specific tissues during surgery. The intern will help review and synthesize scientific information, support development of scientific communication resources, and contribute to initiatives that enhance evidence communication and education for internal and external stakeholders. This position reports to the Medical Education Communications Manager and works cross-functionally within the Future Forward Fluorescence Imaging team. Essential Job Duties Conduct targeted literature reviews and summarize scientific and clinical evidence relevant to fluorescence imaging, surgery, oncology, and related fields. Support development of scientific communication resources that translate complex evidence into clear and scientifically accurate content for internal and external audiences. Assist with scientific content management. Support publication activities. Prepare presentations, reports, and scientific summaries. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure scientific communications are accurate, consistent, and aligned with available evidence. Contribute to special projects supporting clinical and scientific evidence communication for novel fluorescence imaging agents. Required Skills and Experience Strong scientific and clinical research and literature evaluation Ability to analyze, interpret, and synthesize scientific and clinical information from multiple sources Strong written and verbal communication skills Proficiency with Microsoft Office (PowerPoint, Excel, Word) Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements: University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship. Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process. Required Education and Training Current enrollment in a PharmD, Master’s or PhD, biomedical sciences, life sciences, or related graduate degree-seeking program. Bachelor’s level students with significant relevant experience may also be considered. Working Conditions None Preferred Skills and Experience Interest in Medical Affairs, scientific communications, publications, evidence generation, or medical education Experience conducting literature reviews using PubMed, Embase, or similar databases Experience summarizing scientific publications or clinical research findings Familiarity with scientific publications, congress abstracts, clinical trials, and evidence generation Experience developing presentations, reports, educational materials, or scientific communications Knowledge of oncology, surgery, medical devices, imaging technologies, or related areas Experience working in a healthcare, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or medical device environment Due to the nature of our business and the role, please note that Intuitive and/or your customer(s) may require that you show current proof of vaccination against certain diseases including COVID-19. jobs.title: Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) Intern
jobs.body: It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide. We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world. The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life. If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here. Primary Function of Position The HEOR Intern will join Intuitive’s Future Forward Medical Affairs team for a 10–12 week summer internship, reporting to the Staff Epidemiologist, Future Forward Medical Affairs. The intern will own a defined, scoped real-world evidence project, using administrative claims data and reimbursement coding (CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, MS-DRG) to characterize patient populations, procedure volumes, healthcare resource utilization, and costs for a technology in development. Working alongside senior epidemiology, data science, and market access colleagues, the intern will contribute analyses that inform value propositions and may help translate findings into inputs for budget impact or other economic models. The internship culminates in a final presentation to Future Forward leadership and cross-functional partners. Essential Job Duties Real-World Data Analysis: With guidance from senior team members, conduct a retrospective claims-based analysis to characterize patient populations, estimate procedure volumes, and describe utilization, outcomes, and costs relevant to a Future Forward pipeline technology. Coding & Cohort Definition: Identify and validate CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, and MS-DRG code sets to define target populations, procedures, comorbidities, and outcomes; document code lists and assumptions so they can be reused by the team. Study Planning & Programming: Contribute to a brief study protocol and statistical analysis plan; write, document, and quality-check analytic code, partnering with the team’s data scientist on shared data pipelines. Evidence Review: Conduct a targeted literature review to inform study design, benchmark findings against published evidence, and surface evidence gaps for the technology under study. Economic Modeling Support: Where relevant, translate claims-based estimates (e.g., procedure volumes, event rates, costs) into inputs for budget impact or other economic models, and support model development or validation. Communication: Summarize findings in clear visualizations and slides; deliver a final presentation to Future Forward leadership; contribute to a draft abstract where findings warrant. Required Skills and Experience Hands-on experience with reimbursement coding systems (CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, and MS-DRG), gained through dissertation research, research-assistant work, or prior employment, including using codes to define cohorts, procedures, and outcomes. Demonstrated experience analyzing at least one large administrative claims or hospital database (e.g., Medicare MedPAR/SAF, MarketScan, Optum Clinformatics, Premier, PearlDiver, Komodo Health, or similar), from data extraction and cleaning through analysis. Proficiency in SAS and/or R and working knowledge of SQL Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to translate technical analysis for non-specialist audiences. Comfortable working on a defined deliverable under the guidance of senior team members, with the independence to drive it to completion within the internship period. Intellectual curiosity and comfort with ambiguity; this team works on problems that are not yet fully defined. University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements: University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship. Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process. Required Education and Training Current enrollment in a Health Economics, Health Outcomes/Services Research, Health Policy, Pharmaceutical Outcomes Research, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, or related degree-seeking program at the Doctorate (PhD) level. Working Conditions None Preferred Skills and Experience Experience developing or adapting budget impact models or other health economic models (e.g., cost-effectiveness, cost-consequence) in Excel, consistent with ISPOR good-practice guidelines. Familiarity with Medicare payment methodologies (IPPS/MS-DRG, OPPS/APC, MPFS/RVU) and how coding drives payment across sites of service. Research experience in medical devices, surgery, or procedural care. Peer-reviewed publications or congress abstracts (e.g., ISPOR, AcademyHealth). Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI). jobs.title: Reinforcement Learning Intern
jobs.body: It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide. We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world. The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life. If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here. Primary Function of Position The Reinforcement Learning Intern will report to future forward research lead and contribute to the development and evaluation of reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms in support of supervised autonomy initiatives. The intern will identify, train, and test several RL algorithms using data collected from the Intuitive surgical robot systems. While the bulk of this work will take place on offline -collected data (i.e., not in real-time on the robot), a stretch goal would be to deploy an RL algorithm to control the robot in real-time . Essential Job Duties Collect tele-operated simulation and/or real data from the surgical robot while performing a realistic exercise (e.g., Fundamentals of Laparoscopic Surgery pick-and-place). This is referred to as trajectory data and is critical for RL training. Train off-the-shelf reinforcement learning algorithms (e.g., policy gradient methods, actor-critic methods, etc.) on the trajectory data and benchmark their performance using established metrics. Adapt reinforcement learning algorithms to the surgical domain and exercise of interest and identify techniques for improving performance relative to off-the-shelf RL models. Recommend a suggested algorithm / experimental setup moving forward (beyond the internship) based on experimental results, and present findings to the broader team. Deploy chosen RL algorithm either in simulation or on the dV5 to validate its performance in real-time (vs. purely offline evaluation). Required Skills and Experience University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements: University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship. Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process. Required Education and Training Current enrollment in an Engineering (e.g., Biomedical, Electrical), Robotics, Computer Science, or related degree-seeking program at the Doctorate level. Working Conditions None. Preferred Skills and Experience Competitive applicants have one or more of these skills and a willingness to learn others. Deep experience with a deep learning framework (e.g., PyTorch or JAX). Strong familiarity with reinforcement learning algorithms (e.g., policy gradient methods, actor-critic methods). Willingness to learn about robotics and the application of RL to surgical robotics. Excel in communicating, both in written and verbal form, about motivation for running experiments, experimental findings, and the implications of the work. Experience with video-based and multimodal data analysis and processing. jobs.body: > Specialty Engineering Co-op Reference #42985 Waterdown, Ontario About L3HARRIS WESCAM As a subsidiary of L3Harris Technologies and within the Integrated Mission Systems Segment, the WESCAM division develops the most advanced optical sensor and targeting systems for global defense and military sectors, National Security, Search & Rescue and Airborne law enforcement agencies. From long-range covert surveillance missions to search and rescue operations, our MX-series systems, and the mission systems solutions they are a part of, produce stabilized high-magnification electro1-optical and infrared images from airborne, marine and ground based platforms, enabling our customers to see first and act first. About the Role This is a 16 month co-op term to start May 2027. Our products are only valuable to our customers if they are reliable and safe. That’s where you come in. You will be working closest with the Reliability and Safety Engineering team on a variety of tasks and initiatives. You will also have the opportunity to support the Integrated Logistics Support team. This role requires someone with a can-do attitude, strong technical background, and eagerness to learn new things. Primary Responsibilities Perform data analysis to quantify the reliability of our fielded products and lower level parts. Improve and automate this process as much as possible. Assist in developing predictive maintenance policies using telemetry data. Learn about and assist with activities to influence the reliability of products in the design phase (ex: DFMEA). Communicate results of analyses, findings, and studies in thorough written reports and presentations. Assist with product safety analyses, such as fault tree analysis. Required Capabilities Motivated self-starter who seeks out opportunities to collaborate with others. Confidence to ask questions and probe. Analytical thinker with the ability to extract meaningful data from various sources. Meticulous attention to detail. Written and verbal communication that is concise and factual. A curiosity in how things work and break. Background in programming, and probability and statistics is an asset. Desired Education and Experiences Enrollment in a Bachelors or Advanced degree in Engineering or Science program Must be able to complete a 16 month Co-Op term starting May 2027 Currently enrolled and in good standing with co-op program through accredited university Able to obtain Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) clearance Diversity & Inclusion We believe that diversity among our employees makes us a stronger organization. jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all. Location F10NX Department Probe Project Title Move Table Optimizer: Applied Artificial Intelligence for Wafer Test Optimization Project Description Develop an applied Artificial Intelligence solution that automatically generates optimized wafer test movement configurations. During wafer testing, a probe card moves across the wafer to contact and test each die. The movement sequence must cover all required dies using as few contacts as possible. This represents a constrained coverage and sequencing problem that is currently optimized manually on a case-by-case basis. The intern will apply optimization, machine learning, and software engineering techniques to develop an optimization engine and a web application for engineers to visualize, compare, and evaluate recommended configurations. The project provides practical exposure to Artificial Intelligence-enabled optimization, web application development, and semiconductor wafer probe testing. Objective of the Project Develop an optimization engine that generates and ranks wafer test movement configurations. Reduce the manual effort required to evaluate individual wafer test cases. Enable engineers to visualize and compare recommended configurations through a web application. Quantify potential improvements in test time and tester utilization using representative production cases. Opportunities for Full Time Employment High-performing interns may be considered for future internship or full-time employment opportunities, subject to business needs, role availability, and the applicable selection process. Project Scope Apply optimization and machine learning techniques to generate and rank wafer test movement configurations. Analyze historical configuration data and benchmark model results against manually optimized configurations. Develop a web application for engineers to visualize, compare, and select recommended configurations. Validate the recommendations using representative production cases and quantify the improvements achieved. Learning Opportunities Develop an applied Artificial Intelligence solution from problem formulation through model development, application integration, and validation. Gain experience working with real semiconductor manufacturing data and practical engineering constraints. Build hands-on knowledge of semiconductor wafer probe testing in a high-volume manufacturing environment. Collaborate with cross-functional Automation, Equipment, and Engineering teams. Deliverables An optimization engine that generates and ranks wafer test movement configurations. A web application featuring wafer visualization and side-by-side comparison of recommended configurations and potential savings. A validation report documenting the methodology, results, limitations, and quantified improvements. Impact of the Project A previous manual optimization study for one product reduced the number of contacts per wafer by two, resulting in a 7.14% reduction in test time for that product. As manual optimization limits the number of cases that can be evaluated, automating the process could make similar optimization methods repeatable across a broader product mix. The solution has the potential to shorten test time, improve tester utilization, and provide engineers with a consistent method for evaluating wafer test movement configurations. Skillsets Required Strong analytical, problem-solving, and software engineering skills. Experience with Python, Linux, Angular, and Structured Query Language. Familiarity with machine learning, optimization libraries, or Artificial Intelligence-enabled workflows. Exposure to combinatorial optimization, coverage optimization, sequencing, or path-planning problems is an advantage. Course of Interest The ideal candidate should be pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, or a related field. jobs.title: Deep Learning Model and System Optimization Engineering Intern – 2027
jobs.body: We are now looking for a Deep Learning Performance Engineer Intern to join our team. Large language models are transforming how people interact with computing, while placing unprecedented demands on inference performance, memory efficiency, scalability, and deployment cost. Our team develops GPU-accelerated software for deep learning inference. We work across model architectures, algorithms, numerical representations, inference systems, and GPU architectures to continuously improve the performance and deployment capabilities of large language models on NVIDIA GPUs. Our work contributes to inference frameworks such as TensorRT-LLM and helps bring state-of-the-art models to production efficiently. We are looking for outstanding interns who are passionate about large language model inference, low-precision computing, GPU performance optimization, and hardware-software co-design. What you’ll be doing: Analyze and optimize inference performance across model architecture, numerical precision, GPU kernels, memory systems, and end-to-end serving frameworks. Develop low-bit quantization techniques for model weights, activations, attention operands, and KV caches. Explore numerical formats and mixed-precision strategies involving FP8, NVFP4, MXFP4, and other emerging low-precision formats while preserving model accuracy and capabilities. Design and evaluate techniques for KV cache compression, sparsification, hierarchical storage, and reuse across inference requests. Optimize the inference of model architectures including MHA, GQA, MQA, MLA, sliding-window attention, sparse attention, linear attention, and state space models. Investigate model-system co-optimization techniques such as speculative decoding, state reuse, and computation reuse. Build performance models and optimization strategies for long-context inference and agentic workloads, with a focus on throughput, time to first token, inter-token latency, memory efficiency, and deployment cost. Collaborate closely with model, framework, kernel, library, system software, and GPU architecture teams to influence the design of future models, software platforms, and hardware architectures. What we need to see: Pursuing an MS or PhD from a leading university in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field, with an expected graduation date in 2028. Available to work as an intern for at least three months and at least four days per week. Strong understanding of Transformer architectures and large language model inference, including core components such as attention, MoE, and KV cache management. Experience with at least one large language model inference framework, such as TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, SGLang, or a comparable framework. Proficiency in Python and PyTorch, with strong experimental design, data analysis, debugging, and problem-solving skills. Experience with at least one GPU programming technology, such as CUDA C/C++, Triton, or a comparable parallel programming framework. Understanding of GPU architecture, memory hierarchy, Tensor Cores, parallel computing, and performance analysis. Familiarity with low-precision computing concepts, including quantization error, scaling, rounding, clipping, group or block quantization, and mixed-precision computation. Ability to evaluate an optimization technique across model accuracy, kernel performance, and end-to-end inference performance. Good communication, technical writing, organization, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Hands-on experience optimizing kernels or end-to-end workloads on NVIDIA GPUs. Research or engineering experience in model quantization, KV cache optimization, efficient attention, speculative decoding, or long-context inference. Contributions to inference frameworks, GPU libraries, compilers, or other relevant open-source projects. Experience profiling and optimizing production-scale LLM inference workloads. jobs.title: Internship in Health, Safety & Environment Department
jobs.body: Welcome to a world, where your ideas lead to something big. Welcome to Bosch! Bosch Thermoteknik AB in Tranås develops, manufactures, and sells heat pumps for the European market. We are approximately 650 employees and form part of the large Bosch Group, which consists of approximately 417,000 employees worldwide. We work with sustainable simplification of everyday life where the focus is on the environment, innovation, and development. In Tranås there is a production unit and a competence and development center. The heat pumps we manufacture draw energy from different sources - the mountain, the water, or the air. We work to constantly be at the forefront and contribute to sustainable energy and a better environment with the goal of creating a simplified everyday life for our customers. In short, we create technology that is "Invented for life". About us We support managers and executives in their environmental and working environment responsibilities. We comply with requirements according to laws and certifications as well as directives within the company group and communicate continuously internally. Your contribution to something big Our department drives the company's sustainability work, and your internship work will contribute to the implementation of local activities and initiatives in this area. We also need to strengthen our team with an intern who is interested in environmental technology, has a basic understanding of ISO 14001 or similar standards. The internship includes, among other things, environmental technology, waste management, chemical substances, reporting and project management. We want you to have experience in problem solving, collecting and analyzing data, contributing to the development of training materials and work instructions. Duration of the internship: 6 months, preferably starting February 2027 Location: on-site in our plant in Tranås, Sweden What distinguishes you You are an organizer, happy to take on projects and organize events in the area of sustainability. Our company language is English, but we work on production projects and it would be beneficial if you could also communicate in Swedish, so a basic knowledge of Swedish is an advantage. Ongoing studies in Industrial Engineering and Management, Sustainability Management, Safety & Environmental Engineering, or a related field. Knowledge and experience of Microsoft Office 365 with a special emphasis on Word Excel and PowerPoint. Good communication skills, both verbal and written. Problem solving skills. Please note : Only applications from students that are currently studying are accepted. What we offer you Monetary compensation is included to support you during your internship We can offer free accommodation in Tranås To support your well-being, we provide a wellness contribution for use on fitness, sports, or wellness services We cover your travel costs from your residence to Tranås, making relocation easier for you You gain valuable experience working within an international company with global connections Welcome to Tranås – the heart of Bosch Home Comfort in Sweden Tranås, beautifully located by the idyllic Lake Sommen and surrounded by forests and nature reserves, is home to Bosch Thermotechnology AB in Sweden. Here, more than 600 associates work in manufacturing and research & development of innovative heating solutions for a sustainable future. At Bosch, we care about you, our business, and the environment. We offer more than a job – we help you grow in your career and as a person. Life is about balance, and we support your goals, whether they involve new challenges, development, or time for family and hobbies. Join a workplace that values individuality, openness, and trust, where you can be yourself and be inspired by diverse perspectives from around the globe. Join us in Tranås and be part of shaping tomorrow’s energy solutions – in a workplace where innovation meets quality of life. Here, you’ll find not just a job – but a lifestyle. #LikeABosch

jobs.title: Systems Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Come start your career with some of the brightest and most innovative minds in the country! As a Systems Engineering Intern, you will participate in a comprehensive summer internship program designed to provide hands-on experience in a dynamic aerospace and defense environment. You will work alongside industry experts, contribute to real-world projects, and develop valuable technical and professional skills. This internship offers a unique opportunity for growth through mentoring, cross-functional workshops, and direct involvement in company projects. The ISR (Intelligence, Surveillance & Reconnaissance), Aviation, and Security (IAS) business area is a leader in ISR and aviation, it is a leading prime manned and unmanned aircraft systems integrator for innovative, high-performance ISR and aviation systems. Its end-to-end Command, Control, Computers, Communications and Intelligence, Surveillance & Reconnaissance (C4ISR) capabilities encompass design, integration, test, certification, ground/flight training and complete logistics support. IAS tailors solutions to customer cost, performance, and schedule requirements and designs to consistently exceed expectations – with an unrivaled record of on time and on (or under) budget deliveries. Responsibilities: Participate in actual technical projects and contribute to team objectives by completing assigned tasks. Receive guidance and mentorship from experienced industry professionals in your field. Prepare and maintain technical documentation, reports, and records as required. Assist in collecting, analyzing, and interpreting technical data to support engineering decisions. Attend planning meetings to understand project requirements, timelines, and team goals. Perform hands-on technical work assignments to gain practical experience and build technical skills. Work closely with team members, absorb and learn from their expertise, and apply that learning to ongoing projects. Identify opportunities for process improvements and support the implementation of best practices. Participate in workshops designed to provide a deeper understanding of the business and company culture. Qualifications You Must Have: Must be a Sophomore, Junior, or Senior in college or technical school, with at least 6 months until graduation after end of internship. Currently enrolled in a university or college program pursuing a degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Strong skills in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Visio. Ability to work in a highly collaborative team environment. Strong organization skills and work ethic; detail oriented. The ability to obtain and maintain a Secret U.S. Security Clearance is required Qualifications We Prefer: Prior internship or work experience in a technical or engineering role. Familiarity with the Aerospace and Defense industry. Basic knowledge of engineering software tools (e.g., CAD, MATLAB). Microsoft Access skills. Pursuing a degree in engineering or a related discipline. Essential Functions: Ability to sit at a computer for extended periods. Proficiency with computers and office equipment. Manual dexterity for handling tools and technical equipment. Ability to lift up to 25 lbs occasionally. Ability to work in a laboratory or workshop environment, which may involve exposure to loud noise levels or hazardous conditions. Ability to travel may be required. This posting will be open for application for a minimum of 5 days and may be extended based on business needs. SNC offers a generous benefit package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, 401(k) with 150% match up to 6%, life insurance, 3 weeks paid time off, tuition reimbursement, and more . IMPORTANT NOTICE: This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret U.S. Security Clearance. U.S. Citizenship status is required as this position needs an active U.S. Security Clearance for employment. Non-U.S. citizens may not be eligible to obtain a security clearance. The Department of Defense Consolidated Adjudications Facility (DoD CAF), a federal government agency, handles the adjudicative aspects of the security clearance eligibility process for industry applicants. Adjudicative factors which affect the outcome of the eligibility determination include, but are not limited to, allegiance to the U.S., foreign influence, foreign preference, criminal conduct, security violations and illegal drug use. Learn more about the background check process for Security Clearances. SNC is a global leader in aerospace and national security committed to moving the American Dream forward. We’re known and respected for our mission and execution focus, agility, and disruptive and rapid innovation. We provide leading edge technologies and transformative solutions that support our nation’s most critical security needs. If you are mission-focused, thrive in collaborative environments, and want to make our country stronger with state-of-the-art technologies that safeguard freedom, join our team! SNC is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to an environment free of discrimination. Employment decisions are made based on merit without regard to race, color, age, religion, sex, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran or other characteristics protected by law.

jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite Manufacturing Engineering What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will : ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting ​ Implement new ideas , be constantly challenged, and develop your skills ​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business ​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture ​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. jobs.title: 12-Month Geospatial Intern
jobs.body: The following job descriptions outline common geospatial internship openings for 12 month interns at Trimble. Once interviews are completed, candidates will be matched based on their backgrounds, skills and interests. This hands-on internship empowers you to bridge hardware-software integration, translate user needs into intuitive workflows, and build automated testing frameworks that ensure top-tier product quality. About Us: Trimble Field Systems develops hardware, software and services that connect the site to the office for key industries around the world, including civil construction, surveying, mapping, automotive, marine, utilities and more. Key Exciting Responsibilities Apply survey and GIS knowledge to guide product development and define optimal user workflows. Execute exploratory testing and design test cases using state-of-the-art equipment to ensure high-quality software releases. Build and expand automation testing frameworks by writing code that simulates real-world end-user operations. Track, analyze, and report automated test results from daily runs to optimize performance and customer satisfaction. Essential Skills & Experience Currently pursuing a degree in Land Surveying, Geomatics Engineering, or a related field. Strong foundational understanding of office and field survey workflows. Solid computer skills including experience with test design, databases, Excel, and networking principles. Excellent written and verbal technical communication skills with a collaborative, proactive mindset. Full-time availability for a 12-month commitment starting May or June 2027. Bonus Points For Hands-on practical surveying experience. Familiarity or interest in C# programming and automated testing frameworks. Experience with GIS platforms such as Esri products, ArcGIS, or spatial databases. jobs.title: Technical Innovation Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: POSITION SUMMARY The Technical Innovation Intern will support the Office of the CTO by researching and evaluating emerging technologies that can enhance data center operations and Vertiv’s current and future product offerings. This role is ideal for candidates passionate about innovation and the future of critical digital infrastructure. The intern will also contribute to hands-on AI development and experimentation using local AI computing systems while collaborating with engineering, product, IT, university, and innovation teams. RESPONSIBILITIES • Conduct research on emerging data center technologies, including AC power, air and liquid cooling, energy storage, IoT, advanced materials, AI infrastructure, and digital twins. • Analyze industry reports, academic publications, patents, and market trends to identify innovations applicable to Vertiv’s product lines. • Evaluate technologies from startups, universities, established vendors, and advanced technology providers. • Assess the potential impact of emerging technologies on current and future product offerings. • Prepare technical summaries, reports, presentations, innovation briefs, and recommendations highlighting integration or development opportunities. • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to assess technical feasibility and application potential. • Use local AI computing systems to prototype, test, and document AI and machine-learning workflows. • Support local large language model deployment, inference, evaluation, prompt testing, semantic search, and lightweight fine-tuning experiments. • Assist with Python-based data pipelines, API and RSS integrations, model evaluation, dashboards, and automation workflows. • Help maintain reliable AI computing workloads, including logging, scheduled jobs, backups, startup and recovery processes, and technical documentation. • Follow Vertiv IT, laboratory, access-control, cybersecurity, and responsible-AI requirements when working with AI systems and company information. • Support university partnerships, startup engagement, innovation dashboards, newsletters, and knowledge-management activities. • Present research findings, demonstrations, and recommendations to the Office of the CTO and engineering leadership. QUALIFICATIONS • Pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Statistics, Industrial Engineering, Physics, or a related field. • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. • Demonstrated work ethic, attention to detail, and commitment to high-quality work. • Strong analytical, research, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills. • Ability to learn in a fast-paced innovation environment and manage multiple assignments. • Strong collaboration and teamwork skills across engineering, product, IT, and external partner teams. • Experience with Python and familiarity with Linux or Ubuntu environments is preferred. • Familiarity with machine learning, generative AI, large language models, embeddings, semantic search, or model evaluation is preferred. • Exposure to Git or GitLab, REST APIs, databases, containers, automation, or open-source AI tools is a plus. • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; Power BI or Streamlit experience is a plus. • Ability to troubleshoot software and system issues and maintain clear technical documentation. • Commitment to safe, secure, ethical, and responsible use of AI systems and company information. PHYSICAL & ENVIRONMENTAL DEMANDS • No special physical requirements. • Work may take place in an office or controlled lab environment using desktop AI-computing equipment. TRAVEL REQUIRED • None or minimal travel as required #LI-RB1
